The provisions of the PPN apply to all central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies ('in-scope organisations). The PNN state that in-scope organisations should "take action to apply this PPN when procuring good and/or services and/or works with an anticipated contract value above £5million per annum (excluding VAT) which are subject to the Public Contracts Regulation 2015 save where it would not be related and proportionate to the contract". The PPN further states that in-scope organisations should include a requirement for bidding suppliers to provide a Carbon Reduction Plan, confirming the suppliers commitment to achieving net zero by 2050 in the UK, amongst other provisions, as part of the assessment process in the procurement of goods and services.


Organisations that fall within the scope of the PPN guidelines must apply the PPN's provisions to procurement processes from September 30th, 2021 onwards.

 - The sustainable management of land, water, energy, and raw materials and environmental conditions
 - The conservation of energy and water, as well as climate conditions

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda in Mexico (Estrategia Nacional para la implementación de la Agenda 2030 en México)
DESCRIPTION: Mexico's National Strategy for the 2030 Agenda establishes a framework for sustainable development, placing climate change action as a central pillar. It commits to transitioning towards a low-greenhouse-gas emission development model by 2030, prioritising sustainable natural resource management, clean and renewable energy adoption, and the integration of climate resilience into economic growth. The strategy underscores alignment with international objectives to limit global temperature increase to below 2°C and pursue efforts towards 1.5°C, emphasising the urgency of both mitigating emissions and adapting to climate impacts to safeguard ecosystems, communities, and future prosperity.The policy details specific climate-focused measures, including strengthening ecosystem adaptation through protected area management, reforestation, and community-based adaptation plans; promoting low-carbon technologies and processes across industry, energy, and waste sectors via regulations, incentives, and carbon pricing mechanisms; and consolidating institutional coordination through the National Climate Change System (SINACC) to ensure policy coherence and effective implementation across all government levels. It further stresses inclusivity, integrating gender and human rights perspectives to address disproportionate climate vulnerabilities, and highlights the mobilisation of public and private finance—through strategic investment, insurance mechanisms, and international cooperation—to support mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction efforts.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Minister of Industry Decree No. 27/2020 on Specifications, Development of Roadmaps, and Provisions to Calculate the Domestic Component Standards for Domestic Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV)
DESCRIPTION: This Decree states that based on the roadmap, 4-wheel BEV in 2030 will be 750,000 units, while 2-wheel BEV will be 2,450,000 units.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Zimbabwe National Forestry Policy 2023
DESCRIPTION: The Zimbabwe National Forest Policy 2023 creates the framework for sustainable forest management to maintain biodiversity, productivity, regeneration capacity, and vitality. The policy aims “to enhance the contribution of the forestry sector to development and social equity through active participation of all stakeholders for the benefit of present and future generations.” Regarding climate change, the policy has an objective to “enhance forest carbon sinks and build communities’ resilience to climate change through sustainable forest management.” It proposes policy actions such as promoting land-use plans that recognise forestry at all governance levels, capacity building for sustainable forest management in the context of climate change, maintaining and accounting for carbon sinks with community participation, implementing a carbon credit framework as a guide in forest-based projects and promote gender-sensitive forest-based climate solutions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Power Development Plan 2023-2050
DESCRIPTION: In alignment with the Philippine Energy Plan (PEP) which prioritises the aggressive deployment of renewable energy, this the Power Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2050 coordinates adjustments across the power industry’s sub-sectors - generation, transmission, distribution, and supply - to align with the nation’s medium- to long-term energy goals. The PDP adopts the national renewable energy power generation mix targets of 35% by 2030 and 50% by 2040, while providing a roadmap for stakeholders in the electric power industry. The PDP is also aligned with the PEP's goal to create a resilient, climate-proof energy infrastructure.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decision 428/QD-TTg approving the Revised National Power Development Master Plan for the 2011-2020 Period with the Vision to 2030
DESCRIPTION: This decision notably aims to enhance the installation and use of energy from renewable sources. It also promotes energy efficiency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: iGST submission: Negotiator Briefing: A Needs-Based Approach to Loss and Damage
DESCRIPTION: iGST submission: Negotiator Briefing: A Needs-Based Approach to Loss and Damage, Submission to the Global Stocktake from Climate Equity Reference Project Canada (CERP) in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Risk and Disaster Management 2016-2020
DESCRIPTION: In addition to the introduction, this document is divided into five chapters, including: I. Country Profile; II. Current Situation of Risk Reduction and Disaster Management; III. Components of the Strategy; IV. Conditions for Implementing This Document; and V. Analysis of Risks Associated with the Strategy's Implementation. This policy will be structured around the vision of the General State Policy defined in May 2014, aimed at building a modern and prosperous Malagasy society, respectful of human dignity and human rights, and in which the fight against poverty, vulnerability, and precariousness constitutes the top priority. Thus, in contributing to the achievement of this vision of the State, the vision of this strategy is formulated as follows: "The Malagasy people hope to build a sustainable and prosperous society in which natural and man-made disasters have less impact on their environment, development, and living conditions," with the objective of "increasing the resilience of Madagascar, its national institutions, and local authorities to disasters by 2020, with a view to providing the population with acceptable and secure living conditions." The field of disasters being transversal, the implementation of this strategy, in the spirit of the General Policy of the State, the national strategy of the agriculture-livestock-fishing sector in the face of climate change, the National Program for Adaptation to Climate Change and many other sectoral programs relating to water resources and sanitation, land use planning, forestry, health, cartography and housing, is part of the perspective of the sustainable development of the country.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decision No. 888/QD-TTg on approval for Scheme Setting Out Tasks and Solutions for Implementation of Outcomes of the 26th Conference of the Parties to the Untied Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
DESCRIPTION:
• The Scheme's general objective is to set out the strategy for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 and contribute to global efforts in response to climate change. Its specific objectives are:Setting up a comprehensive legal framework;
  • Reforming strategies in order to be conform with net-zero commitments by 2050;
  • Promoting the reduction of GHG emissions in the sectors of energy, transport, production of building materials, agriculture and waste treatment;
    • By 2030, encourage the use of green energy and electricity in transport, and use of 100% of E5 petrol; decrease greenhouse gas emissions by 32,6% in energy, 43% in agriculture, 70% in forestry and land use sector in which the carbon sequestration capacity is expected to increase by 20%, 60,7% in waste treatment, and 38,3% in industrial processes (compared to the emission reduction stated in the BAU scenario).
  • Identify potential of renewable energy sources;
    • By 2030, increase the ratio of sources of renewable energy, including hydroelectricity, wind power, solar power and biomass to at least 33% of total production of electricity.
  • Develop new zero-emission energy projects and energy storage technologies;
  • Establish carbon credit exchange and offsetting mechanisms, and domestic carbon credit market;
    • By 2030, the domestic carbon market shall be operated and connected with regional and global carbon markets.
  • Undertake climate change adaptation and natural resource and ecosystem restoration consistently and efficiently;
    • Implement UN initiatives accordingly.
  • Establish and participate in partnerships, alliances, and other international initiatives on emissions reduction and energy transition;
  • Promote climate diplomacy; do scientific research; improve capacity and communication activities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree 829 - Tax incentives for non-conventional renewable energies - streamlined procedure
DESCRIPTION: This decree regulates the administrative procedure for access to tax benefits from renewable energy projects, reducing waiting times from 3 months to 45 days

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Environmental Impact Assessment Act (UVPG)
DESCRIPTION: This Act sets out regulations for environmental assessments which comprise the identification, description, and evaluation of the significant effects of a project, plan, or programme on certain protected goods, such as the climate. The act demands that projects/programmes/ plans have to consider risks of incidents, accidents and disasters that are scientifically determined to be caused by climate change and impacts of those on greenhouse gas emissions, changes in the local microclimate.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal Law No. 10.257/2001 on the Cities Statute
DESCRIPTION:
Tihs law establishes general guidelines for urban policy. Article 42 establishes that the Director Plan for municipalities included in the national register of municipalities with areas susceptible to the occurrence of high-impact landslides, sudden floods or related geological or hydrological processes must contain:

I - parameters for land parcelling, use and occupation, to promote a diversity of uses and contribute to the generation of employment and income;                  

II - mapping of areas susceptible to major landslides, sudden floods or related geological or hydrological processes;        

III - planning of preventive intervention actions and relocation of the population from disaster risk areas;      

IV - urban drainage measures needed to prevent and mitigate disaster impacts; and       

V - guidelines for land regularisation of irregular urban settlements, if any, and provision of areas for social housing through the boundary of special social interest zones and other urban policy instruments, where housing use is permitted.      

VI - identification and guidelines for the preservation and occupation of municipal green areas, where appropriate, to reduce the waterproofing of cities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Clean Ambient Air Act, last amendment in 2025
DESCRIPTION:
The Clean Ambient Air Act regulates the limitation of emissions into the air from stationary sources and the quality requirements for liquid fuels - among others the activities directly related to GHG emissions. In addition, since 2008, Article 25 on Common methodology for emissions inventory specifically includes CO2, CH4 and N2O (plus relevant ODS and SF6) among the regulated substances.

It establishes standards for air pollutants, sets monitoring and reporting obligations, and defines the responsibilities of public authorities, businesses, and individuals to prevent air pollution. The law incorporates EU air quality directives and provides mechanisms for environmental inspections, enforcement, and public access to information, aiming to safeguard human health and the environment. The 2025 amendments modernised administrative procedures by reducing paperwork and promoting digital compliance, strengthened enforcement powers by granting inspectors broader access to emission sources, and clarified sanctions, including fines and confiscation of non-compliant fuels.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 24-594 of 26 June 2024 (establishing the National Commission for the Fight against Climate Change)
DESCRIPTION: Decree No. 24-594 of 26 June 2024 establishes the National Commission for the Fight against Climate Change. This body is a national platform for the supervision, guidance, and coordination of activities to combat climate change. The amendment sets out more responsibilities of this Commission, more responsibilities for the Steering Committee and composition of the working unit for developing a taxonomy and disclosure regime.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Brazil's Cross-cutting Strategy for Just Transition and Climate Justice
DESCRIPTION: Brazil's Cross-cutting Strategy for Just Transition and Climate Justice (ETTJ) examines the effects of the transition on vulnerable populations and groups beyond the dimensions of employment and income, proposing national objectives and guidelines that ensure mitigation and adaptation measures not only prevent the exacerbation of inequalities and vulnerabilities but also promote, to the extent possible, their reduction through the equitable distribution of the benefits of climate action. This strategy has as overarching goal to guide the implementation of the Climate Plan by ensuring the promotion of a just transition and climate justice in order to build a more sustainable and equitable society.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Poland’s Recovery and Resilience Plan
DESCRIPTION:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient.The Total value reaches approx. €59.8 billion, which are divided into (i) €25.3 billion in RRF grants and (ii) €34.5 billion in RRF loans.

Poland’s plan strongly supports climate and environment objectives:

• ≈46.6 % of funding goes to green projects.

• Includes investment in renewable energy (offshore onshore wind), energy-efficient building renovations, green hydrogen, and sustainable transport.

• Regulatory changes to facilitate renewable projects and electricity imports.

The plan was approved by the Council on 17 June 2022.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Government Decree 331/2013 on Landfills, last amended by Decree 1030/2021
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of this decree is to support the transition to a circular economy, in particular to ensure a reduction in the disposal of waste suitable for recycling and other recovery in landfills, and to prevent pollution of surface water, groundwater, soil and air, and to combat climate change and other similar large-scale harmful environmental impacts, to guide the planning, establishment, construction, use, management, decommissioning and after-care of landfills and the disposal of waste in them in such a way that they do not pose a risk or harm to health or the environment during the entire life cycle of the landfill.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Renewable Energy Policy (ANREP)
DESCRIPTION:
The National Renewable Energy Policy (ANREP) aims to mainstream renewable energy in the national energy sector planning to deploy them in different capacities and through different projects in the country. The policy aims to provide a direction to the renewable energy (REN) sector. The Policy is aligned to the Power Sector Master Plan (PSMP) and the Afghanistan National Development Strategy (ANDS) to set a framework for deployment of REN and it connects with the Rural Renewable Energy Policy (RREP) to ensure an implementation of the policy guidelines in the rural energy sector. 

The Policy sets the following target : to deploy 350-450 MW of REN capacity by 2032, which is equivalent of 10% of the total energy mix of 3500-4500 MW as per the targets of PSMP. To achieve the target, the policy promote the involvement of the private sector, government and non-government organisations and donors.

The Policy will be implemented in two terms : TERM 1 (2015- 2020) will create the activities for the development of REN sector particularly in the PPP mode; TERM 2 (2021-2032) will deploy REN in full commercialization mode.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agreement on the municipalities' finances for 2013 (climate adaptation)
DESCRIPTION:
On June 10, 2012, the government and the Municipality of Copenhagen reached an agreement on the municipalities' finances for 2013.

The agreement establishes an ambitious effort to address climate change. The municipalities will increase their investments in climate adaptation of the wastewater sector by DKK 2.5 billion in 2013, which will strengthen the drainage and handling of rainwater.

In addition, all Danish municipalities would prepare local climate adaptation plans by the end of 2013. This requirement came after severe cloudbursts and floods, especially in 2011, which focused on the need to protect cities and infrastructure against increasing water levels. The plan is to include a mapping of risks of flooding from rainwater, seawater, watercourses and groundwater and prioritize the efforts. The 2013 agreement marked the beginning of a structured, municipal effort to deal with the consequences of climate change in Denmark.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Expansion and Modernization Programs for the National Transmission Network and the Elements of the General Distribution Networks of the Wholesale Electricity Market (PAMRNT) 2024-2038 [Programas de Ampliación y Modernización de la Red Nacional de Transmisión y de los elementos de las Redes Generales de Distribución del Mercado Eléctrico Mayorista (PAMRNT) 2024 - 2038]
DESCRIPTION: This policy document details programmes for the expansion and modernisation of Mexico's National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD) associated with the Wholesale Electricity Market. It operates within the context of the country's Energy Reform, with the Ministry of Energy (SENER) and the National Energy Control Centre (CENACE) coordinating efforts to ensure the efficiency, quality, reliability, continuity, and security of the National Electricity System (SEN). The overarching aim is to strategically plan and develop grid infrastructure, integrating demand forecasts and generation capacity plans. A key objective is to facilitate the increased integration and utilisation of clean energies, thereby modernising the electricity sector to support national development and meet evolving energy policy objectives.The policy significantly emphasises climate change mitigation and adaptation. It supports Mexico's international commitments, such as the Paris Agreement, by promoting the transition to a higher proportion of clean energy in electricity generation, projected to increase to 61.41% by 2038. This involves planning for new capacity from renewable sources and energy storage, alongside measures aimed at reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through fuel substitution and grid efficiency improvements. The policy also incorporates strategies for enhanced resilience, such as ensuring flexible generation to counter the impact of climate events on variable renewable sources. Furthermore, it acknowledges the influence of climate phenomena, like heat waves, on electricity demand patterns and system reliability, and promotes electromobility as a key strategy for reducing transport sector emissions, integrating considerations for the broader energy transition.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree of 13-5-2020 approving the buildings regulations
DESCRIPTION: This document promotes energy efficiency and renewables in new and old buildings.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Change Policy for the Coffee Subsector of Honduras
DESCRIPTION: This policy aims to ensure the long term climate-resilience of coffee production in Honduras, creating economic benefits and also helping to mitigate net greenhouse emissions through sustainable land use and agroecology. It aims to act through capacity building, enhanced climate early warning systems, agroforestry carbon bond financing, and technological modernisation in plantation maintenance.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Board of Health and Welfare - Action plan for climate adaptation 2022 – 2025
DESCRIPTION:
The National Board of Health and Welfare has analysed the consequences that a changing climate can have on human health and the health and care sector and, based on this, analyzed how the agency can contribute to reducing the negative consequences through its activities. It also sees a need for increased knowledge about the impact of climate change on the health and care sector in order to be able to make the right decisions. The National Board of Health and Welfare also has the opportunity to contribute to increasing knowledge through the dissemination of information.

The National Board of Health and Welfare shall contribute to developing the ability of health and care to counteract the negative effects of climate change on vulnerable groups within health and care.

The goal shall be long-term and is intended to fulfil the National Board of Health and Welfare’s mission as the government’s administrative authority for activities related to health and medical care, dental care and social services, support and service for certain disabled people.

The goal should also be linked to possible and relevant indicators to measure, for example: heat-related mortality, and the proportion of homes with heat wave preparedness plans.

The agency goal for climate adaptation is also divided into two action goals:

1. Climate adaptation is integrated into the agency's work; and

2. The National Board of Health and Welfare has contributed to improving and developing work on climate adaptation in society.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 2024-548 of June 15, 2024 on the implementation of the future climate savings plan
DESCRIPTION: This Decree is on climate insurance; it the securities in which the sums collected by the future climate savings plans can be invested, the principles of savings allocation to which they are subject, the investment strategies they can propose and the fee ceiling in the event of transfer of the plan. This Decree implements the plan provided for in Article 34 of Law No. 2023-973 of October 23, 2023 relating to the green industry.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Lesotho Energy Policy 2015-2025
DESCRIPTION: This Policy aims at providing Lesotho's citizens with an affordable, reliable and environmentally-friendly energy supply. Bioenergy, renewable energy sources, energy efficiency are main objectives laid out by the document, which details how the government intends to foster them.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Decree No. 2011-423 fixing the operating procedures of the Trust Account No. 302-1221 'National Fund for Renewable Energy and Cogeneration'
DESCRIPTION: Amends the operating procedures of the National Fund for Renewable Energy and Cogeneration, first established pursuant to the Finance Act of 2010, to increase the revenue paid into this fund from .5% of oil royalties to 1% of oil royalties, plus any additional contributions. Grants authority to the Minister of Finance to jointly manage expenditures from this fund with the Minister of Energy for the purposes of financing operations and projects for the promotion of renewable energy and cogeneration.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Equatorial Guinea Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC1
DESCRIPTION: Equatorial Guinea First NDC, Nationally Determined Contribution from Equatorial Guinea in 2018

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Growth and Transformation Plan (GTP) II
DESCRIPTION:
The GDP II replaces the initial GDP to cover the period 2015-2020. It sets some targets for energy generation from renewables and biofuels. The Plan focuses on improving the macroeconomic indicators, sectoral economic development plans (e.g. for agriculture and rural transformation, manufacturing, mining, tourism), infrastructure (transport, digital and water supply), human and technology capacity building, good governance and cross cutting issues. New feasible agricultural varieties that are resilient to climate change and have positive contributions for climate resilient green economy development aimed at enhancing agricultural production and productivity will also be identified and disseminated. Other important GTP II goals are protecting forests and re-afforestation including carbon stocks; expanding electricity generation from renewable sources of energy; and leap-frogging to energy efficient technologies in transport, industry and construction.

Building a climate resilient green economy is a pillar of the GTP. The plan notably aims at increase forest coverage from 15.5 % to 20%, thus reducing GHG emissions by 147 Mln/Metric tons.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Cameroon Vision 2035
DESCRIPTION:
This document presents Cameroon's overall policy direction in pursuit of development. General objectives are: reducing poverty to minimal levels; becoming a middle-income country; becoming a newly industrialised country; and consolidating democracy and enhancing national unity. It was prepared by the Ministry of Economy, Planning and Regional Development.

Climate change is identified in Vision 2035 as one of the two major challenges to Cameroon's economy. Over exploitation of natural resources and environmental costs have been warned as it results in climate change threats; Cameroon is partly located in Sahel area with existing harmful effects of climate change: desert encroachment, increased temperatures, irregular seasons, sea level rise, floods, volcanism, landslides rock fall and toxic fumes. The document calls for reduction of greenhouse gases to tackle climate change as a key regional strategy for Cameroon. The Government of Cameroon pledges to seek high growth level while achieving Millennium Development Goals.

Under the tentative implementation schedule of Vision 2035, drafting and implementation of major environmental policy to fight against the climate change impact is planned for the phase one (2010-2019). Climate change control is listed as one of the three specific objectives for the phase two (2020-2027). Specific actions include protecting and ensuring sustainable management of forest ecosystems, fighting desert encroachment and promoting regional projects like the Niger Basin and the Lake Chad Basin.Diversification of energy source and replacement of fossil fuel with clean energy supplies is mentioned in the document without quantitative targets.

DESCRIPTION: Canada National Communication. NC3 from 2002

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Green Deal Action Plan (approved by Presidential Circular 2021/15)
DESCRIPTION: This document was prepared by the Ministry of Trade and provides a strategy for achieving a green shift in all sectors of the economy. It further seeks to put Turkey in line with the EU's Green Deal.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Water Protection Act (GSchG)
DESCRIPTION: The Act is designed to protect the aquatic environment from harmful impacts and to promote its sustainable use, ensuring that water management is approached holistically and coordinated at the international level. Its main objectives include safeguarding the health of humans, animals, and plants; preserving groundwater and spring water in their natural state for drinking and utility purposes; conserving and restoring natural habitats around water bodies for native flora and fauna; and maintaining water as an important element of the landscape. Additionally, the Act implements Directive 2000/60/EC, establishing a framework for water policy at the European level. It comprises 52 articles.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Disaster Risk Management Plan
DESCRIPTION: This National Disaster Risk Management Plan is the guiding document for addressing disaster risk management in Rwanda. The document pursues the mission and goals of disaster management laid down by the National Disaster Management Policy 2012. The plan is to be used by all government and non-government sectors as the basis for developing their own sub-plans, systems and arrangements (health, transport, agriculture, and public works). Main goals are 1) to strengthen the institutional capacity of MIDIMAR and its stakeholders to effectively implement disaster management programmes, 2) to create a programmingframework incorporating Government, Agencies and Departments, Non-Governmental Organizations and the private sector in Rwanda, 3) mitigation of the impact of disasters on livelihoods, property, the environment and economic activity, 4) to perform research that will support an implementation of the plan and upgrading the scope of the plan to respond to the changing risk environment.

DESCRIPTION: Turkmenistan Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1

DESCRIPTION: Côte d'Ivoire National Communication. NC1 from 2000

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Protection of Air from Pollution
DESCRIPTION: This law charges relevant ministries and institutions with implementing measures to protect and improve air quality and the ozone layer. It ensures the right of citizens to live in an environment free of pollution and aims to mitigate climate change, by promoting the use of renewable energy sources and establishing, maintaining, and improving an integrated air quality management system in the country. This law is in line with Kosovo's obligations under international treaties on climate change mitigation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Energy Policy
DESCRIPTION:
This document sets Mali's energy policy. It seeks in particular to foster the production and use of renewable energy sources, and to improve energy efficiency.

The policy further seeks to 1) improve wood burning systems to reduce use, 2) promote the use of natural gas in order to reduce desertification from wood burning, and 3) assess CO2 and other GHG emissions due to the use fossils fuels.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: CO2 Act
DESCRIPTION:
The CO2 Act has been fully revised several times since the 2000 CO2 Act. On 15 March 2024, the National Council and the Council of States agreed on a new legal text that will enter into force on 1 January 2025. 

Article 1 of the CO2 Act states that its purpose is to implement the objectives set out in the Federal Act on Climate Protection Goals, Innovation and Strengthening Energy Security (Switzerland's climate framework law). Article 3 set outs quantified greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets: 50% reduction by 2030 (compared to 1990), and 35% on average betwen 2021 and 2030 (compared to 1990). It also states that the Federal Council may set benchmarks for individual sectors.

Other measures include: vehicle emissions limits and ETS. The Act also provides an exemption for companies for the CO2 levy, if they commit to reducing their greenhouse gases in return. They would need to inform the federal government via an annual report, and submit a decarbonisation plan within three years of the start of the reduction commitment, outlining the measures they will take to significantly reduce GHG emissions from the energy use of fossil fuels by the end of 2040. There is also q requirement to update this plan every three years.

This Act also includes an amendment to the Unfair Competition Act, which now bans statements about climate impact that cannot be substantiated (i.e., there is an obligation to provide evidence of proof of such climate claims).
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Carbon Pricing;Energy Demand;Energy Supply;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;REDD+ And LULUCF;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Agricultura y Desarrollo Rural)
DESCRIPTION: The Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (SADER) establishes a structured framework for advancing sustainable agricultural development in Mexico, emphasising climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, and resource efficiency. Organised into specialised coordinations and directorates (including the Coordinación General de Sustentabilidad y Resiliencia Climática and Dirección General de Sustentabilidad), the policy mandates inter-institutional collaboration to integrate climate adaptation into agricultural planning. Key responsibilities include designing public policies to mitigate climate risks (e.g., droughts, floods), promoting sustainable production systems, and aligning national efforts with international agreements (e.g., Paris Agreement). The policy explicitly addresses climate change. The Coordinación General de Sustentabilidad y Resiliencia Climática oversees initiatives such as promoting agroecological practices, restoring degraded soils, optimising water use, and reducing pesticide reliance. It also emphasises deforestation prevention and the adoption of regenerative livestock systems to curb greenhouse gas emissions. The Dirección General de Sustentabilidad further mandates the development of climate-resilient strategies, including early-warning systems for extreme weather, land-use planning to avoid deforestation, and biodiversity integration into agriculture. Similarly, financing mechanisms under the Dirección General de Financiamiento Verde seek international partnerships to fund sustainable projects, aligning with global climate goals.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Lao People's Democratic Republic Biennial Update Report. BUR1
DESCRIPTION: Lao People's Democratic Republic. Biennial update report (BUR). BUR 1., Biennial Update Report from Lao People's Democratic Republic in 2020

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ministerial Decree 414 of 7 December 2023 concerning identification of an incentive tariff for renewable energy plants, in implementation of Legislative Decree 199/2021
DESCRIPTION:
Ministerial Decree No. 414/2023 is a regulatory framework designed to execute Legislative Decree No. 199/2021 and fulfill a specific green energy investment (Mission 2, Component 2) within Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). Its primary goal is to incentivize the growth of renewable energy through collaborative models, specifically targeting Renewable Energy Communities (CERs) and various collective or individual self-consumption arrangements.

The Decree establishes two cumulative financial benefits for eligible projects:

  • PNRR Capital Grants: A direct, non-repayable contribution covering up to 40% of the initial investment costs. This specific fund is a geographic incentive, reserved for renewable plants built in smaller municipalities (those with 5,000 residents or fewer).
  • Incentive Feed-in Tariffs: A performance-based "premium" paid for the renewable electricity actually produced and shared within the community. Unlike the capital grant, this tariff is available nationwide and is guaranteed for a 20-year period starting from the date the plant begins commercial operations.

Eligibility for the incentives is subject to compliance with the conditions set forth in Article 3 of the Decree. These include: a maximum plant capacity, the prior establishment of the energy community before the plant’s entry into operation, and the requirement that participating enterprises be classified as small or medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Technical Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emission Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects in the Fossil Fuel Power Generation Sector
DESCRIPTION: The Ministry of Ecology and the Environment’s guidelines on the general workflow, content, methodologies and technical requirements for carrying out greenhouse gas emission EIAs for construction projects in the fossil fuel power generation sector, including fossil fuel power generation projects and cogeneration (combined heat and power) projects.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Belize Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1
DESCRIPTION: Belize Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Ecological Transition Strategy
DESCRIPTION: Tunisia's National Ecological Transition Strategy aims to guide sustainable economic development across a wide range of sectors while preserving and restoring natural capital. The strategy underscores the need to adapt to climate change and reduce the carbon intensity of the economy. Among other measures, it promotes: development of climate-specific policies and the formation of government entities to oversee their implementation; creation of a national climate early warning system; intensification of reforestation efforts; substantial waste reductions across the economy; enhanced flood protection; sustainable urban mobility.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: UK Hydrogen Strategy
DESCRIPTION: This document sets the government's strategy to create an integrated low carbon hydrogen sector in the UK. It considers changes to the regulatory framework, aims to assess jobs opportunity, and makes a range of financial commitments and targets, notably: 1) 5GW of low carbon hydrogen production capacity by 2030 (1GW by 2025), 2) provision of £240m for the Net Zero Hydrogen Fund out to 2024/25, 3) deliver hydrogen for heat trials, and 4) provide up to £120 million this year through the Zero Emission Bus Regional Areas (ZEBRA) scheme towards 4,000 new zero emission buses, either hydrogen or battery electric, and infrastructure needed to support them. The strategy also calls for the development of metrics to monitor progress against outcomes and the commitments made, including incorporating data on hydrogen production into the Digest of UK Energy Statistics.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Slovenia’s recovery and resilience plan
DESCRIPTION:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state.The European Commission has given a positive assessment to Slovenia’s €2.5 billion recovery and resilience plan, consisting of €1.8 billion in grants and €705 million in loans. 42% of the plan’s total allocation for reforms and investments supports climate objectives.

  • Energy efficiency and seismic renovation of buildings: financing large-scale renovation programmes to increase the energy efficiency ofpublic buildings, including schools. €230 million
  • Decarbonisation of transport through investments in railway infrastructure: upgrading congested railway lines, refurbishing railway stations, increasing capacity, speed and safety of rail transport and digitalising rail infrastructure to reduce travel time. €292 million
  • Improved drinking water supply and water saving projects: building and renovating ageing drinking water supply systems to reduce water losses by more than 20%. €54 million

Tthere were 4th amendments to the date and the 5th amendment is waiting for the Council's approval.
