PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Powering Up Britain: Overview
DESCRIPTION: The "Powering Up Britain" Joint Overview sets out the UK government's approach to energy security and net zero, and acts as an introduction to the Energy Security Plan and Net Zero Growth Plan.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Clean Energy Industries Sector Plan
DESCRIPTION: The UK Clean Energy Industries Sector Plan is a core part of the UK’s Modern Industrial Strategy, aiming to make the country a global leader in clean energy by 2035. The plan targets frontier industries including offshore and onshore wind, hydrogen, carbon capture, heat pumps, nuclear fission, and nuclear fusion. Its objectives are to double annual private investment in clean energy industries to over £30 billion by 2035, strengthen domestic supply chains, accelerate innovation and deployment, improve energy security, and create high-quality jobs across the UK. The government intends to support growth through infrastructure investment, skills development, regulatory reform, and public-private partnerships while positioning the UK as a major exporter of clean energy technologies and service

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 1447/99, approving the Kyoto Protocol
DESCRIPTION: This Law approves the Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC (1997). The convention was signed by the Republic of Paraguay on 25 August 1998. The full text is reproduced in the law.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Submission by the World Economic Forum, relating to the consideration of outputs component of the global stocktake
DESCRIPTION: Submission by the World Economic Forum, relating to the consideration of outputs component of the global stocktake, Submission to the Global Stocktake from World Economic Forum (WEF) in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program
DESCRIPTION: The Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program (SREPs) is a $4.5-billion program designed to support the deployment of grid modernization, energy storage and renewable energy technologies in every region of Canada, helping to grow the grid in a sustainable, affordable and reliable manner. The program also includes support for transmission and distribution infrastructure, and continues to support Indigenous-led clean energy projects. The program is currently expected to end March 31, 2036.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution CVM 193/2023 on fiduciary duties
DESCRIPTION: It expands the integration of ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) practices in the Brazilian Stock Market, aligning Brazil with the global standards established by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), a body created by the IFRS Foundation. This resolution details how climate-related risks and opportunities must be reported in the corporations’ inventories to assess the impact of climate change on organisations' operations.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: UNDRR Inputs in the First Global Stocktake Technical Dialogue 1.3
DESCRIPTION: UNDRR Inputs in the First Global Stocktake Technical Dialogue 1.3, Submission to the Global Stocktake from United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree-Law 181/2023 containing provisions for energy security, promotion of the use of renewable energy sources, support for energy-intensive businesses, converted, with amendments, by Law 11/2024
DESCRIPTION: TDecree-Law 181/2023 (converted, with amendments, by Law No. 11/2024) introduces urgent measures to strengthen Italy’s energy security and accelerate the energy transition, focusing on promoting renewable energy deployment, particularly through incentives for self-production by energy-intensive industries, and facilitating new generation capacity. It also includes provisions to secure natural gas supply and system flexibility, simplify permitting procedures for renewable and grid infrastructure, and support the development of strategic sectors such as offshore wind, biometane and energy infrastructure, while aligning with PNRR and decarbonisation targets. In addition, the decree provides economic support to energy-intensive companies and includes measures for reconstruction in areas affected by the 2023 floods.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Directive 2008/50/EC on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe
DESCRIPTION:
This Directive lays down measures aimed at the following:

1.defining and establishing objectives for ambient air quality designed to avoid, prevent or reduce harmful effects on human health and the environment as a whole;

2.assessing the ambient air quality in Member States on the basis of common methods and criteria;

3.obtaining information on ambient air quality in order to help combat air pollution and nuisance and to monitor long-term trends and improvements resulting from national and Community measures;

4.ensuring that such information on ambient air quality is made available to the public;

5.maintaining air quality where it is good and improving it in other cases;

6.promoting increased cooperation between the Member States in reducing air pollution.

Pollution limits are provided in the directive annexes.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy to Combat Desertification and Drought 2016-2030, Executive Decree No. 008-2016-MINAM
DESCRIPTION: This decree adopts Peru's National Strategy to Combat Desertification and Drought 2016-2030 into law.Peru's National Strategy to Combat Desertification and Drought 2016-2030 has six specific goals: (1) elaborate and update soil quality baselines to include the causes and consequences of desertification, land degradation and drought based on scientific and technological guidelines, (2) strengthen regulatory frameworks related to desertification, land degradation and drought in affected areas, (3) develop synergistic, multisectoral, intrasectoral, regional and local plans, programs and projects to reduce desertification, land degradation and the impact of drought in affected areas, (4) raise awareness of the problem and actions to mitigate desertification, land degradation and the impact of drought through the media, (5) strengthen management capacities of desertification, land degradation and drought in various interest groups on a scientific-technological basis, and (6) develop scientific research or technological innovations that help sustainable land management by taking advantage of traditional knowledge.There is a specific subsection (1.5.2) dedicated to the relationship between climate change and desertification in Peru.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 28832. Ensures the efficient development of electricity generation (Ley Nº 28832. Asegura el desarrollo eficiente de la generación eléctrica)
DESCRIPTION: This Law for Ensuring Efficient Electrical Generation establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework for the Peruvian electricity sector, focusing on creating mechanisms to secure efficient and opportune electrical supply. The legislation aims to reduce administrative intervention in generation pricing, promote effective market competition, and ensure reliable electricity provision through strategic measures such as long-term supply contracts and public bidding processes. Key objectives include mitigating price volatility risks, facilitating new generation investments, and ensuring competitive electricity tariffs for end consumers, with a particular emphasis on creating a transparent and efficient electricity market governance structure. This Law was modify by the Act No. 32.249 which amendments to the regulatory framework governing electrical generation in Peru, with a primary focus on ensuring secure, reliable, and efficient electricity supply while promoting energy matrix diversification. The modifications encompass multiple dimensions of the electricity sector, including contract mechanisms, bidding processes, and the introduction of complementary services market regulations. Key changes include extending potential contract durations, establishing more flexible procurement strategies, creating a competitive framework for complementary services, and implementing mechanisms to enhance operational efficiency and transparency in electricity generation and distribution.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Republic of North Macedonia Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC1 (Archived)
DESCRIPTION: The Republic of North Macedonia First NDC (Archived), Nationally Determined Contribution from North Macedonia (Republic of North Macedonia) in 2018

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 137 - National Forest Restoration Program 2021 - 2025
DESCRIPTION: This Decree creates the National Forest Restoration Program 2021-2025, which aims to structure and lead the processes to restore national water-producing hydrographic basins, contribute to the recovery of degraded soils, and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. The Program seeks to promote the recovery and valuation of Panama’s forest resources to facilitate their protection, sustainable use and management from a cultural, economic, ecological, social and community perspective.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Brazil's Adaptation Climate Plan: Sectoral Plan for Agriculture and Livestock
DESCRIPTION:
Brazil’s Sectoral Plan for Agriculture and Livestock is part of the Plano Clima Adaptação framework and aims to strengthen the resilience of agricultural and livestock production systems to climate change. The plan focuses on increasing the adaptive capacity of the sector through public policies, promoting sustainable and climate-resilient farming systems that maintain productivity under changing climate conditions, and conserving and sustainably using genetic resources to support the adaptation of agroecosystems. Through these measures, the plan seeks to enhance food security, rural livelihoods, and the long-term sustainability of Brazil’s agricultural sector.

Main objectives are:

  • Increase the adaptive capacity of agricultural and livestock production through public policies.
  • Adapt agricultural systems to climate change while maintaining productivity, sustainability, and resilience.
  • Promote the conservation and sustainable use of genetic resources to improve agroecosystem adaptation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Transport Policy
DESCRIPTION:
This sectoral development policy sets out a strategy for the transport sector, aiming to:

- Ensure that the transport sector competently contributes to enhance the overall economic development and social interaction

- Make the transport sector convenient, efficient, safe and accident free, Information Technology (IT) supported, reliable and accessible

- By guaranteeing the strategic, economic and social benefit for our country, ensure an equitable and efficient transport infrastructure and services operation

- Encourage and expand transport systems operating on renewable energy without compromising the safety of the natural environment by ensuring that the transport sector is environmentally friendly and does not harm the natural environment.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Waste Management Plan 2028
DESCRIPTION:
The National Waste Management Plan 2028 (Krajowy Plan Gospodarki Odpadami 2028) was adopted by the Resolution 96/2023 of the Council of Ministers.

It sets Poland’s strategic framework for waste policy through 2028 with a perspective to 2035, aligning domestic planning with EU waste-management and circular-economy goals.

The National Waste Management Plan 2028 aims to increase recycling and reuse, reduce landfilling, and promote biowaste treatment, which together help lower greenhouse gas emissions from waste and support climate mitigation, while building modern waste infrastructure and fostering a circular economy in Poland.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation No. 12/2024 on the Implementation of NDCs in Climate Change Mitigation
DESCRIPTION:
This Regulation governs the processes for the formulation and implementation of Indonesia's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). Article 3 states that the NDC shall include NDC targets, and efforts to achieve these targets are carried out to move towards low greenhouse gas emissions and climate-resilient development by 2050, and carbon-neutral development by 2060 or sooner.

Articles 5 to 7 outline the implementation strategy, which spans building ownership and commitment through outreach and communication; capacity building; creating enabling conditions in laws and policies; developing implementation guidelines; and monitoring and review, among others. There are also other provisions on what the NDC Roadmap for Climate Change Mitigation should include, and how it should be developed.

This Regulation specifies that climate change mitigation shall be carried out in specified sectors and subsectors, and action plans are to be carried out through the stages of inventorising emissions; preparing an emissions baseline; formulating targets; and establishing an action plan. Adaptation is to be carried out through the stages of planning, implementation and monitoring and evaluation. Each of these stages is detailed in this Regulation.

This Regulation also lays out provisions for the implementation of monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) and the National Climate Change Control Registry System for information on actions and resources for climate change mitigation and adaptation and carbon pricing to enhance transparency; and for stakeholder participation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Strategy 2021-2026
DESCRIPTION:
The National Climate Change Strategy 2021-2026 fully replaces the 2012 version that is described below.

The 2012 National Climate Change Strategy aims to enable Tanzania to effectively adapt to climate change and participate in global efforts to mitigate climate change, whilst also achieving sustainable development.

Adaptation strategies are outlined for water resources, coastal and marine environment, forestry, wildlife, agriculture and food security, human health, tourism, energy (hydropower dams), industry, livestock, and fisheries, infrastructure, human settlements and land use. Mitigation is addressed through low-emission energy technologies, policies to conserve energy usage by industries, improved livestock management and food stuffs, greater efficiency in the transport, mining, agriculture and waste management industries, and afforestation and reforestation policies (including REDD+).

Additionally, cross-cutting programmes seek to implement public awareness programmes, establish research capacity and training institutions for climate change. The Strategy's estimated financial requirements are USD750m per year through to 2030, with the funding to come from international and some domestic support.

The National Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in Climate Change in Tanzania has also been produced as part of this strategy.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;CCGAP;Energy Supply;Gender;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Roadmap for the Implementation of Vietnam's Sustainable Development Goals to 2030
DESCRIPTION:
This Roadmap, approved by Decision 681/QD-TTg, contains climate-related actions, which include the following:

  • In relation to Goal 2.4 on ensuring sustainable food production by 2030, the actions are to:
    • Maintain an annual increase of 10-15% of agricultural cultivation areas that apply safe production processes;
    • Maintain an annual increase of 8% of aquaculture area that apply good and sustainable aquaculture practice process;
  • In relation to Goal 11.9 to significantly increase the number of cities and residential areas applying integrated planning and policies towards inclusiveness, resource efficiency, mitigation and adaptation to climate change, increasing disaster resilience by 2030:
    • Ensure that urban general planning is integrated with green growth and climate change goals progressively;
  • In relation to Goal 13: Respond promptly and effectively to climate change and natural disasters:
    • Ensure that the percentage of centrally-run provinces and cities that develop, promulgate and implement the Action Plan to implement the Paris Agreement on climate change is 100%; and
    • Ensure that the proportion of the population is given knowledge of flood prevention, storm prevention and disaster risk mitigation progressively increases to 90% by 2030.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on strategic environmental impact assessment
DESCRIPTION: This Law contains provisions that the body responsible for evaluating the strategic assessment report shall assess the impact of the project on climate amongst other factors, and the need for a strategic environmental assessment shall depend on the degree to which the plan and programme influence climate and climate change. The strategic assessmnet report should contain possible significant consequences for human health and the environment including climactic factors influencing climate change.

DESCRIPTION: France National Communication. NC2

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Renewable Energy Subsidy Policy 2016
DESCRIPTION:
The Renewable Energy Policy focuses on scaling up the Renewable Energy Technologies (RETs) and achieving the objectices on the UN's 'Sustainable Development Goals' and 'Sustainable Energy for All'. 

The objectives of the policy are to reduce dependence on traditional and imported energy by increasing access to renewable energy for improving the livelihoods of people and create employment opportunities, especially in the rural areas.

The policy establishes the following strategies: 1) to reduce the initial upfront cost thereby increasing the access to the renewable energy services; 2) to maximise service delivery and efficiency in the use of renewable energy resources and technologies in the rural areas; 3) to support development and growth of the renewable energy market by mobilising commercial credit, attracting private sector and entrepreneurs; 4) to encourage public-private sector participation in the renewable energy technologies, etc.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agriculture Sector Plan 2021-2031
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan provides policy guidelines and direction for the agricultural sector to implement programmes to increase agricultural productivity. The goal is resilient food, nutrition and livelihood security of Marshallese in the face of climate change. The seven key outputs to be achieved over the ten years are:1. Minimisation of environmental degradation;2. Development and promotion of sustainable small-livestock production systems developed and promoted3. Development and promotion of sustainable crop production systems; 4. Increased consumption of nutritious locally produced foods;5. Improved biosecurity and marketing;6. Improved capacity of agricultural sector stakeholders; and7. Development of enabling policies/legislations.

To address disaster risk reduction related to climate risks, the strategy at the farm level is to adopt climate-smart practices.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Order on Reduction of Greenhouse Gases from the Transport Sector and Sustainability of Biofuels
DESCRIPTION:
This Order mandates biofuel blending requirements in transport fuels for aviation, shipping and road transport and implements the EU Renewable Energy Directive II (EU RED II), setting out the sustainability criteria for biofuels which apply regardless of their geographical origin. Enterprises shall report to the Danish Energy Agency on how they have complied with their obligations.

The Danish Energy Agency shall charge an annual fee to companies to cover the cost of administration in relation to the reduction of greenhoue gases from the aviation and maritime transport sectors.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree no. 20 - National Forestry Strategy 2018 - 2050
DESCRIPTION: This Decree approves the National Forestry Strategy 2018-20150, which aims to increase forest cover, stimulate the sustainable forestry industry, conserve Panama’s forest heritage as an important basis for ecosystems and mitigate the effects of climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Seychelles’ Protected Areas Policy
DESCRIPTION: The Seychelles’ Protected Areas Policy provides a first national policy framework dedicated to the treatment of protected areas in general, which make up 47% (at time of policy) of the total land area, and seeks to promote a sustainable and balanced but multi-use approach to protected zones. Among the specific objectives of this policy is maintaining ecosystem function and integrity in a way that supports climate change resilience and mitigation of net emissions. It underscores the need to ensure equitable sharing of benefits, alongside these efforts in ecosystem preservation, restoration, monitoring and awareness-raising.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Change Policy for the Public Works, Transport and Housing Sector 2018-2036
DESCRIPTION:
This policy emanates from the Ministry for Public Works and Transport (MOPTVDU) and aims to prevent, care for and reduce the vulnerability of the population towards adverse effects of climate change, with a particular focus on the most affected. The document details key concepts and sets the ministry's strategy to design a multi-sectoral plan within its vested powers. The document also has a mitigation component, in particular with regard to urban and transport actions.

The strategy laid out in the policy focuses on updating the legal and regulatory framework; enhance knowledge creation and sharing; and promote institutional coordination at all levels while involving citizens. The strategy also discusses financial and budgetary matters (alternative financing mechanisms, MOPTVDU budget, taxes, project management involving international actors).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Forestry Policy (2009 - 2019)
DESCRIPTION:
The Forestry Policy embraces medium term strategies for poverty alleviation and growth. It focuses on research and development, programme development, institutional/organisational development, decentralization and synergy. The Policy aims at engaging in partnerships and networking in order to strengthen national resource base. Specific objectives include 1) further integration of Department of Forestry into the medium and long-term national development framework, 2) ensuring that Department of Forestry create multiplier effects on forest resource management and the domestic economy in general, 3) technology transfer to decentralized structures and development of indigenous technology in forest resource management, and 4) promoting efficient and unified systems for forest resource management.


The Department of Forestry will also engage on integrated resource management programming to maintain and develop forest and mangroves, notably to ensure that 75 % of forest lands are managed and protected, to promote national tree planting and encourage urban forestry. The Department will also promote the production and adoption of efficient fuelwood and biomass charcoal briquette end-use appliances which improve the efficiency and reduce the quantities of these household energy source.

DESCRIPTION: Switzerland. 2022 National Inventory Report (NIR), National Inventory Report from Switzerland in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decarbonisation plan
DESCRIPTION:
This plan sets out the government's strategy to decarbonise Costa Rica's economy until 2050. It differentiates between the initial phase (2018-2022), the inflection period (2022-2030), and the "massive deployment" (2031-2050).

The Plan is organised around ten focus areas:
1) Development of a mobility system base on safe, efficient and renewable public transport, and active and shared mobility schemes.
2) Transformation of the light duty vehicle fleet to a zero emissions one, nourished by energy that is renewable and not of fossil origin.
3) Promotion of a freight transport that adopts modalities, technologies and energy sources that emit zero or the lowest possible emissions.
4) Consolidation of the national electric system with the capacity, flexibility, intelligence, and resilience necessary to supply and manage renewable energy at competitive cost.
5) Development of buildings of different uses (commercial, residential, institutional) under high efficiency standards and low emission processes.
6) Modernization of the industrial sector through the application of electrical, efficient, and sustainable processes and technologies of low and zero emissions.
7) Development of an integrated waste management system based on the separation, reuse, revaluation, and final disposal of maximum efficiency and low greenhouse gas emissions.
8) Promotion of highly efficient agricultural food systems that generate low-carbon local consumption and export goods
9) Consolidation of an eco- competitive livestock model based on productive efficiency and reduction of greenhouse gases.
10) Consolidation of a model of management of rural, urban, and coastal territories that facilitates the protection of biodiversity, the increase and maintenance of forest cover and ecosystem services based on nature-based solutions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency 2024-2027 Climate Adaptation Plan
DESCRIPTION: This plan expands the EPA’s efforts to incorporate climate adaptation into the agency’s programs, policies, rules, enforcement activities and operations. The plan builds on work initiated in the 2014 and 2021 EPA Climate Adaptation Plans. This plan promotes climate resilience across the country, with objectives including: fostering a climate-ready workforce, building facility resilience, developing climate-resilient supply chains, applying climate data and tools to decision making, and integrating climate adaptation into rulemaking processes.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Energy Policy
DESCRIPTION: The National Energy Policy aims to ensure universal access to modern energy services in an affordable and sustainable way. It notably encourages the production and use of renewable energy, and energy efficiency, in an effort to drive the country towards it objective of carbon neutrality by 2050.

DESCRIPTION: Uzbekistan First NDC (Updated submission), Nationally Determined Contribution from Uzbekistan in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation on Increasing Efficiency in the Use of Energy Resources and Energy
DESCRIPTION:
The purpose of this Regulation is to regulate the procedures and principles for increasing efficiency in the use of energy resources and energy in order to ensure the efficient use of energy, prevent energy waste, alleviate the burden of energy costs on the economy and protect the environment.

This Regulation covers the procedures and principles regarding the authorization of universities, professional chambers and energy efficiency consulting companies in guiding and disseminating services and studies on energy efficiency, energy management practices, the duties and responsibilities of energy managers and energy management units, training and certification activities related to energy efficiency, studies and projects, support of projects and voluntary agreement applications, demand-side management, increasing energy efficiency in electricity generation, transmission, distribution and consumption, utilization of waste heat from thermal power plants, outdoor lighting, encouraging the use of alternative fuels such as biofuels and hydrogen, and administrative sanctions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Green solutions of the future - Strategy for investments in green research, technology, and innovation
DESCRIPTION:
The strategy sets a clear direction for the Danish green research and innovation effort in order to accelerate the development of technologies and solutions, which can help protect the climate, nature and environment.

The strategy points out four missions that focus on challenges where the need for new solutions and the potential for meeting the green objectives are the largest in Denmark as well as on a global scale. The missions are to be accomplished by green partnerships in which knowledge institutions, businesses, public authorities, and private players join forces in a strategic research and innovation effort over several years.

The goal is to enable greenhouse gas reductions and strengthen the green frontrunner position of Danish industries to the benefit of exports and green jobs in Denmark.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National disaster risk reduction strategy
DESCRIPTION:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (ENRRD) responds to and implements a series of national instruments and policies relevant to implementing the various elements and dimensions of disaster risk reduction. This strategy complies with and respects all the basic principles and provisions of the Constitution and fundamental laws of the Republic of Cape Verde. It is interconnected and supported by other national policies, plans and legislation relevant to disaster risk reduction. Provides the mechanisms to align, validate and strengthen all policies, strategies, regulations and other instruments relevant to disaster risk reduction, such as spatial planning, building codes and standards, sustainable management of natural resources, environmental conservation and protection ecosystems, social protection systems and public health, among others. It provides the motivation (incentives and sanctions) to ensure compliance and reinforce compliance with these instruments designed to reduce exposure and vulnerability.

The policy provides a framework for the systematic and cross-cutting integration of disaster risk reduction into national and sectoral policies and plans and those relating to decentralization, development and local governance. ENRRD wants to encourage reviewing or modifying some of these policies and other instruments to strengthen the integration of disaster risk reduction or give more explicit and practical formalization to disaster risk reduction. For sectors currently in a strategic planning phase, ENRRD aims to demonstrate the relevance of the integration of risk reduction and provides general guidelines for the sector's contribution to the general objectives of disaster risk reduction and resilience of Cape Society Verdiana.

The policy lays the foundation for an efficient cross-sectoral legal framework for disaster risk reduction to be promoted by key sectors and partners and enacted by Parliament to provide the necessary authority for its implementation.

This strategy affirms the government's commitment to the integration of disaster risk reduction and adaptation to climate change in a coherent way in national, sectoral and local development plans and policies, resulting in integration in instruments such as the Strategic Plan of Sustainable Development (PEDS); in fiscal instruments, frameworks and public investment systems; in strategic policies, plans and sectoral programs; and in decentralization frameworks and local development programs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Efficient Use of Energy
DESCRIPTION:
This law regulates the conditions and method of efficient use of energy and energy in the sector of production, transmission, distribution and energy consumption; policy of efficient use of energy; energy management system; labeling the energy efficiency of products that affect energy consumption; minimum requirements for energy efficiency in the production, transmission and distribution of electricity and heat and the supply of natural gas; financing, incentives and other measures in this area, as well as other issues of importance for the rights and obligations of natural and legal persons in relation to efficient use of energy. The basic principles on which energy efficiency is based in the country are energy security, competitiveness, sustainability, energy management and cost effectiveness.

The document lists the legal framework around energy efficiency in Serbia, including the Action Plan for Energy Efficiency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Agricultural Sector Investment Plan 2015-2025 and Plan National D’Investissement dans Le Secteur Agricole (PNISA)
DESCRIPTION: The National Agricultural Sector Investment Plan constitutes Mali's national planning framework for the agricultural sector for a ten year-period from 2015-2025. It is divdied into 5 programs which are expected to be developed through specific actions and activities listed under them. The 5 programs are Capacity Building, Investment, Production and competitiveness of agricultural sector, Training and Research, and Food Security, all of which are aimed objectives such as food and nutritional security, sustainable agriculture, and promoting agriculture as the source of economic growth and propverty reduction. The PNISA also identifies parameters against which the impacts and results of the actions on the agriculture sector are to be measured and evaluated.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Turkmenistan National Communication. NC3
DESCRIPTION: Turkmenistan. National Communication (NC). NC 3., National Communication from Turkmenistan in 2016

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Central Bank of Kenya - Guidance on Climate-Related Risk Management
DESCRIPTION:
In October 2021, the Central Bank of Kenya issued this guidance under section 33(4) of the Banking Act, which empowers the Central Bank of Kenya to guide institutions in order to maintain a stable and efficient banking and financial system.

The guidance recognises that climate change poses a substantial risk and can pose an opportunity for the financial sector and requires banks to:
a)  embed the consideration of the financial risks from climate change in their governance arrangements.
b)  incorporate the financial risks from climate change into their existing financial risk management practice.
c)  develop an approach to disclosure on the financial risks from climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Forest Financing Strategy
DESCRIPTION: Describes different strategies to finance forestry activities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Honduras Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC2.0
DESCRIPTION: Honduras Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC2.0

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act amending the Renewable Energy Sources Act (Solar Package Act I)
DESCRIPTION: Solar Package I (Solarpaket I) is a key legislative package supporting Germany's renewable energy transition by accelerating the deployment of photovoltaic (PV) systems and reducing administrative barriers. Adopted in 2024, it introduces measures to simplify the installation and operation of rooftop, commercial, and utility-scale PV systems, while promoting innovative applications such as agrivoltaics, floating PV, and parking-lot PV. Overall, Solar Package I aims to accelerate progress toward Germany's target of 215 GW of installed solar capacity by 2030 while increasing system flexibility and encouraging broader participation from households, businesses, and citizen energy communities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Food, Nutrition and Climate 2025-2030
DESCRIPTION:
This Strategy aims to guarantee healthy, sustainable, and accessible food for all by 2030, based on an interministerial approach. Its goal is to build a sustainable food system that ensures food security and nutrition for all without compromising the economic, social, and environmental foundations necessary to guarantee food security and nutrition for future generations.

The four key areas are:

  1. Ensuring coordinated governance of policies related to food, health and the environment at all levels and act at the territorial level;
  2. Guaranteeing access for all to quality and sustainable food and nutrition environments;
  3. Supporting sustainable and healthy and environmentally friendly behaviors and diets; and
  4. Developing research, expertise and evaluation for a transition of food systems.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Decree No. 61-2005 - Rural Electrification Policy of Nicaragua (2023)
DESCRIPTION:
This decree outlines the Rural Electrification Policy of Nicaragua, aiming to expand access to electricity in rural areas to promote sustainable development and improve living conditions.

This expansion will be sustainable, have a controlled environmental impact, and prioritize the use of renewable energy sources for areas far from the national grid. The policy also focuses on affordable electricity pricing for rural areas and ensures that distribution companies consider rural electrification needs in their expansion plans.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree no. 2007-291 (approving the statutes of the National Rural Electrification Agency)
DESCRIPTION: This decree approves and specifies the statutes of the National Rural Electrification Agency, including its missions of promoting renewable energy sources and technologies favouring energy efficiency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Green Building Code of Pakistan (GBCP)
DESCRIPTION: The Green Building Code of Pakistan (GBCP) provides detailed standards to promote green construction and renovation of buildings nationally. PRINCIPAL_TITLE: General Regulations of the Fuel Alcohol Law (Reglamento general de la Ley del Alcohol Carburante)
DESCRIPTION:
This regulation establishes the operational framework for Guatemala's Fuel Alcohol Law (Decree-Law No. 17-85), specifically designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the transport sector through mandatory blending of renewable alcohol fuels with gasoline. The regulation updates previous regulatory provisions to align with current technological advances and international climate commitments, particularly Guatemala's Nationally Determined Contributions under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. It establishes comprehensive procedures for the production, storage, handling, use, transport, and commercialisation of fuel alcohol, while creating institutional mechanisms for monitoring greenhouse gas emission reductions and promoting sustainable mobility.

The framework prioritises advanced ethanol with lower carbon intensity, requiring distributors to blend a minimum of sixty percent advanced ethanol in the total alcohol fuel mixture, with flexibility for market disruption circumstances. It establishes technical standards for fuel quality, mandates emission reduction monitoring through internationally recognised methodologies, and creates certification requirements for greenhouse gas emission calculations. The regulation incorporates lifecycle emission assessments, prioritises low-emission fuels, and establishes registration requirements for producers, thereby institutionalising a systematic approach to decarbonising Guatemala's transport sector while aiming to ensure compliance with international environmental obligations and constitutional protections for environmental sustainability.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategy on the Transition of the Republic of Uzbekistan to a "Green" Economy 2019-2030

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy and Action Plan to 2030 (Stratégie nationale de réduction des risques de catastrophe à l’horizon 2030 et plan d‘action)
DESCRIPTION: Tunisia's National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy and Action Plan to 2030 aims to strengthen disaster preparation and response in the long term. It acknowledges climate change as a major threat, and elevates climate adaptation as a key instrument for disaster risk reduction. The action plan contains provisions to: enhance funding and capacity to meteorological monitoring infrastructure and early-warning systems; mainstream climate adaptation in education at all levels; enact governance reforms to improve inter-sectoral co-ordination.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Spatial Development Strategy for Slovenia 2050 (RESPR50)
DESCRIPTION: The Spatial Development Strategy of Slovenia 2050 sets out the country’s long-term strategic objectives and guidelines for the development of activities in the spatial context. The strategy supports the development paradigm of spatial cohesion, which ensures balanced, harmonious and sustainable development of all areas in the country by taking into account and utilizing their endogenous spatial potentials (resources). It highlights the importance of reducing exposure to climate risks (e.g. floods, droughts, heatwaves) through spatial measures such as relocating development away from high-risk areas, improving water retention, and addressing urban heat island effects.Later, Slovenia published the Implementation Plan for the Spatial Development Strategy. The plan sets out a series of activities derived from the strategy's long-term objectives and priority areas. Implementing the proposed activities will enhance the resilience of settlements to climate change, support the preservation of cultural heritage, and improve their overall attractiveness and quality of life. The plan supports the transition to a low-carbon energy system through the spatial integration of renewable energy production, energy infrastructure, and efficient settlement patterns, while also encouraging sustainable mobility and reduced energy demand. All in all it translates national climate-neutrality ambitions into concrete spatial planning actions, ensuring that land-use decisions contribute to decarbonisation, energy efficiency, and climate adaptation goals.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The 2030 National Environmental Policy - Resolution No. 67 of the Council of Ministers
DESCRIPTION:
On 16th July 2019, the Council of Ministers adopted the 2030 National Environmental Policy (PEP2030). PEP2030 became the most important strategic document in the area of the environment and water management. The role of PEP2030 is to ensure Poland's ecological safety and high quality of life for all residents. In the system of strategic documents it specifies the mid-term Strategy for Responsible Development to 2020 with a perspective to 2030.

PEP2030 will be the basis for investing European funds from the financial perspective 2021-2027. PEP2030 also supports the implementation of Poland's objectives and commitments at the international level, including those of the EU and the UN, especially in the context of the EU's climate and energy policy objectives to 2030 and the sustainable development goals (SDGs) included in Agenda 2030.

Detailed objectives will be implemented through the following lines of intervention:

  • sustainable water management, including ensuring access to clean water for society and the economy and achieving good water status,
  • elimination of sources of air pollution emissions or significant reduction of their impact,
  • protection of the earth's surface, including soil,
  • counteracting environmental threats and ensuring biological, nuclear and radiological safety,
  • management of natural and cultural heritage resources, including protection and improvement of biodiversity and landscape,
  • supporting multifunctional and permanently sustainable forest management,
  • waste management towards a circular economy,
  • management of geological resources by developing and implementing the state's raw materials policy,
  • supporting the implementation of eco-innovations and disseminating the best available BAT techniques (they involve determining emission limits for larger industrial plants),
  • combating climate change,
  • adaptation to climate change and disaster risk management,
  • ecological education, including shaping sustainable consumption patterns,
  • improving the environmental protection control and management system and improving the financing system.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Air Pollution;Biodiversity;Climate Change;Climate Protection;Disaster Risk Management;Education;Forests;Soil Erosion;Water Management

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power for Thermal/ Hydro Power Stations
DESCRIPTION:
These Guidelines are the Guidelines for Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power from Grid Connected RE Power Projects for utilisation under the scheme for flexibility in Generation and Scheduling of Thermal/ Hydro Power Stations through bundling with Renewable Energy and Storage Power. The objective of this mechanism is to promote bundling of cheaper Renewable Energy (RE) with costlier Thermal Power and to promote the Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) of Distribution Licensees.

The Guidelines outline the bidding process and standard provisions to be included in the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). The PPA period should not be less than 25 years from the scheduled commissioning date, as the period influences the amount of tariff to be charged. Bids are to be submitted within 22 days, and the PPA is to be signed within 170 days of the release of the bid. The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) presides over arbitration of any tariff-related disputes.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Medium- and long-term plan for the development of the hydrogen energy industry (2021-2035)
DESCRIPTION:
This document sets the government strategy to boost low-carbon hydrogen supply in the country and notably decarbonise high-energy-consuming and high-emission industries.It explicitly favours green hydrogen over grey hydrogen. By 2025, the plan hopes that China will enjoy a relatively complete system and policy environment for the development of the hydrogen energy industry, significant improvements in industrial innovation capability, a mastering of core technologies and manufacturing processes, and a relatively complete supply chain and industrial system. It also sets directional goals to the 2030 and 2035 horizons.

The plan further seeks to:
  • Coordinate and promote the construction of hydrogen energy infrastructure
  • Actively carry out international cooperation in hydrogen energy technology innovation
  • Build a storage and transport system
  • Develop planning of hydrogen refueling network
  • Ppromote the diversified demonstration application of hydrogen energy
  • Promote fuel-cells medium and heavy vehicles
  • Explore alternative applications in the industrial field
  • Accelerate the improvement of hydrogen energy development policies and institutional guarantee systems
  • Establish and improve the hydrogen energy policy system
  • Establish and improve the hydrogen energy industry standard system
  • Promote pilot demonstrations
  • Strengthening fiscal and financial support
  • Carry out the publicity and implementation of safety regulations and safety standards for hydrogen energy production, storage, transmission and use, enhance the safety awareness of the main body of enterprises, and build a solid foundation for the safe utilization of hydrogen energy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Clean Air Policy
DESCRIPTION:
The National Clean Air Policy (NCAP) aims to provide a framework for improving air quality in Pakistan by accelerating progress to reduce air pollutant emissions across all major sectors.


To do so, the NCAP identifies a priority intervention in each of the following five key sectors:

 

·        Transport: Implement Euro-5 and Euro-6 Fuel Quality Standards 

·        Industry: Enforce emission standards for industries 

·        Agriculture: Prevent burning of agricultural residues 

·        Waste: Prevent open burning of municipal solid waste 

·        Households/ Residential: Promote use of low emission cooking technologies 


The full implementation of these interventions under are projected to reduce particle pollution from fine particulates (PM2.5) emissions by 38% in 2030 compared to Pakistan’s current baseline scenario and by 21% compared to 2020 levels. By 2040, these five key interventions are projected to further reduce emissions by 81% in 2040 compared to the baseline scenario and by 70% compared to 2020 levels.

- Stabilise, ensure safety for residents of the cities, regions, particularly the Mekong river delta, the Northern delta and the Central coastal zone

- Ensure food security, maintenance of 3.8m ha of paddy land, of which 3.2m ha with 2 crops per year at least
- Ensure safety of the dike system, civil works, technical and economic infrastructure, that meets the requirements for natural disaster prevention and mitigation
- Keep the sector growth of 20%, poverty reduction rate of 20% and reduction of greenhouse gas emission at 20% in each 10-year period.

The action plan contains seven duties that are to occur, and under each, specifies numerous detailed actions and outputs required.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Policy Framework
DESCRIPTION:
The National Climate Change Policy Framework (NCCPF) sets out the Government's commitments and responsibilities to address climate change. This policy framework will guide the development of adaptation and energy security measures, prepare to manage current climate variability and future climate projections. 

The document sets five priority goals: 1) Strengthen the Enabling Environment for Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, including Sustainable Financing, 2) Adaptation and Reducing Risks for a Climate Resilient Future, 3) Energy Security and Low-Carbon Future, 4) Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery, and 5) Building Education and Awareness, Community Mobilization, whilst being mindful of Culture, Gender and Youth. The National Climate Change Committee (NCCC) will further oversee the development of a Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management National Action Plan. This action plan will identify priority actions needed under each strategic goal, and align these with actions already identified under the National Action Plan for Disaster Risk Management 2008-2018.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Grenada Vision 2030
DESCRIPTION:
Further to the publication of the Grenada National Energy Policy (2011), the 'Grenada Vision 2030' lays down the proposal to establish a 100% renewable energy target for both the electricity and transport sectors for 2030. As a first step to determining the pathway towards this objective, a 100% renewable energy showcase study is to be conducted in co-operation with the German government and a consortium of specialised companies. 

The Grenada Vision 2030 consists of four major projects, three focused on development of utility scale generation from geothermal, wind and waste-to-energy sources, and one on distributed solar. They are expected to require relatively little capital investment, given the small size of the economy and energy demand.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Supreme Decree No. 4 Approving regulations for pollutant emission reduction projects to compensate taxable emissions pursuant to Article 8 of Law No. 20.780
DESCRIPTION:
Supreme Decree No. 4 establishes requirements, obligations, procedures, and records for emission reduction projects and certificates used to compensate taxed emissions on fixed sources introduced by Law No. 20.780.

Mitigation Activity Provisions

  • Taxed emissions compensated limited to implementation of emissions reduction projects targeting the same pollutant. For CO2, reductions must correspond to CO2 or CO2 equivalent.
  • Maximum three-year gap allowed between emission reduction and taxed emission generation years.
  • Taxed emissions of particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, and sulphur dioxide compensated through projects executed in the same or adjacent communes.

Criteria for Ineligible Projects

  • Emission reduction projects from closing activities or establishments due to specified lifespan expiration, administrative sanctions, court judgments, or authority actions.
  • Projects causing increased emissions of other taxed pollutants, unless best available technology is used to minimise impact.
  • Reduction projects in sources subject to the tax.

Further Considerations

  • The Ministry will maintain a public registry including approved methodologies, third-party methodologies, and recognised external certification programs.
  • The criteria from Article 6, paragraph 4, of the Paris Agreement can be applied in establishing, reviewing, and approving methodologies for emission reduction projects.
  • Taxpayers must utilise the compensation mechanism through the designated online platform.
  • The national registry of emission reduction projects will be overseen by the Environmental Superintendence.
  • External auditors providing verification services must be authorised by the Environmental Superintendence.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Norway’s integrated ocean management plans (Meld. St. 21 2023-2024)
DESCRIPTION:
The purpose of the management plans is to provide a framework for value creation through the sustainable use of marine natural resources and ecosystem services and at the same time maintain ecosystem structure, functioning, productivity and diversity. The management plans are thus a tool both for facilitating value creation and food security, and for maintaining the high environmental value of Norway’s seas and oceans.

The plans include the climate and environmental considerations as a basis for marine spatial management; adaptation to climate change and a warmer ocean; and strengthening the knowledge base on oceans and climate change. Norway is considering carbon capture and storage under the seabed, aided by the presence of geological formations suitable for carbon dioxide storage, as an important mitigation measure in climate policy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy 2018-2037
DESCRIPTION: This Strategy is developed in accordance with Section 65 of the Constitution of the Kingdom of Thailand, which stipulates that the State should develop a national strategy in accordance with the principle of goood governance. The National Strategy is (2018-2037) is the country’s first national long-term strategy to ensure that the country achieves its vision of becoming “a developed country with security, prosperity and sustainability in accordance with the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy” with the ultimate goal being all Thai people’s happiness and well-being. The Strategy considers Thailand's national development in the light of unpredictable and abrupt impacts of climate change. It includes solutions such as smart farming; increasing value of a maritime bioeconomy; and promoting climate-friendly growth and infrastructure development.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Biomass Strategy
DESCRIPTION: The Biomass Strategy 2023 sets out the UK Government’s approach to using sustainable biomass as part of the transition to net zero, recognising biomass as a limited resource that should be prioritised where it offers the greatest emissions-reduction potential and where alternatives are limited. The strategy places strong emphasis on strengthening sustainability criteria to ensure biomass delivers genuine greenhouse gas savings, while assessing future domestic and imported biomass availability. It identifies harder-to-decarbonise sectors and, in the longer term, Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) as priority uses, with BECCS expected to provide negative emissions that help balance residual emissions from sectors that are difficult to fully decarbonise. It also considers biomass’s role in renewable power, biomethane, heat, low-carbon transport fuels, industrial decarbonisation and low-carbon hydrogen, while highlighting the need to manage competing demands for sustainable biomass and protect wider environmental objectives.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: UAE Green Growth Strategy 2015
DESCRIPTION: The Green Growth Strategy was announced in 2015. It seeks to make UAE's economy environmentally-friendly and make the country's development sustainable over the long term. The Green Agenda 2015-2030 was announced in 2015 as the implementation framework of the strategy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The National Disaster Response Coordination Plan
DESCRIPTION: The National Disaster Response Coordination Plan (NDRCP) outlines the coordination mechanism and functions to be undertaken to ensure a coherent response to threats and events from hazards impacting Jamaica. It does not replace the National Disaster Plan or plans and standard operating procedures required for managing responses to particular threats.The NDRCP identifies coordinating activities to be taken in the preparedness and response phases by the public, private and voluntary sectors as well as community-based response teams. Coordinating activities, called Emergency Support Functions (ESFs) are led by ministries, departments and agencies of the government, with assistance from their private and voluntary sector partners and community teams.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Norwegian Defence Pledge: Long-term Defence Plan 2025-2036
DESCRIPTION: The Plan involves climate, innovation, and research. The Norwegian government will strengthen research and development, emphasising innovation, and intensifying efforts to reduce emissions. The objective is to emphasise climate-friendly solutions without negatively impacting activity levels and operational capability.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Malaysia HCFC Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP)
DESCRIPTION:
This plan implements the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer. Malaysia successfully eliminated the use of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) by 2010. Building on this milestone, Malaysia has implemented the hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC) Phase Out Management Plan (HPMP) Stage I (2011-2016) and Stage II (2017-2024).

By 2030, Malaysia aims to achieve a full phase-out of HCFCs, accepting a small allowance for the servicing ‘tail’ to 2040. HPMP Stage III will focus to address two subsector plans, the Refrigeration Air Conditioning (RAC) Servicing Sector Plan (HCFC-22) and the Chillers Servicing Sector Plan (HCFC-123). HPMP stage III will further strengthen the regulatory and institutional systems by establishing new bans on the use of HCFCs, and expand customs officers, port authorities and national control and compliance officers’ capacities to control and manage HCFC in trade, use and continue raising awareness to sustain the HCFC phase-out. Implementing HPMP Stage III will reduce Malaysia’s greenhouse gas emissions by up to 8.42 million tonnes CO2-eq.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Technical analysis of the third biennial update report of Brazil submitted on 2 March 2019. Summary report by the team of technical experts
DESCRIPTION: Technical analysis of the third biennial update report of Brazil submitted on 2 March 2019. Summary report by the team of technical experts, Technical Analysis Summary Report from UNFCCC Secretariat in 2020

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Public Utilities - Title 37
DESCRIPTION: This document focuses on strenghtening the generation and transmission of electrical power in the country. Art. 408.n) states that the Palau Public Utilities Corporation shall investigate, research, and implement where feasible and practicable the application of appropriate renewable energy resources including solar power, tidal power and wind generated power.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: General Electricity Law No 64 of 2003
DESCRIPTION:
This law is a general regulatory framework for the generation, distribution and sale of electricity in the Kingdom, and has been updated over the years. The 2003 update includes language that is directly related to climate change despite the fact that the law does not name climate change as an objective. The law states that energy efficiency shall be a national priority, a precursor to the law concerning renewable energy summarised above. In addition, the General Electricity Law grants authority to the Electricity Sector Regulatory Commission to provide incentives (not specified in the law) to encourage improved technological efficiency; and to participate in the regulation of efficiency standards for electric devices officially issued by the Standards and Meteorology Corporation.


Previous additions to the law passed in 2002 allowed private energy companies to access to the electricity grids as well as set guidelines for renewable energy projects. Large-scale projects (above 5MW) would be contracted through competitive tendering (no longer necessary due to the provision in the renewable energy law), small-scale (below 5MW) through direct negotiations and very small scale (below 1MW) for auto-generation and only to be bought during peak demand.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Renewable Energy Certificates Regulations
DESCRIPTION: "The Renewable Energy Certificates Regulations, 2022, came into effect on Dec. 6, 2022, in India, aiming to restructure the local renewable energy certificate (REC) mechanism. The new regulations introduce the concept of REC multipliers by technology, increase the validity of RECs to perpetuity until sold and remove the floor and the ceiling price for REC trading." [SP Global 2023]

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution No. 1447 of 2018
DESCRIPTION:
Resolution 1447 of 2018 aims to regulate the Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) system of mitigation actions at the national level and to establish the National Registry of Greenhouse Gas Emission Reductions [Registro Nacional de Reducción de Emisiones de Gases Efecto Invernadero (RENARE)]. RENARE is a platform of the MRV System designed to manage information at the national level regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation initiatives.

Types of GHG Mitigation Initiatives that can be registered in RENARE

1. GHG mitigation programmes such as Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions (NAMAs), Low Carbon Development Programmes (LCDPs), and REDD+ Programmes.

2. GHG mitigation projects such as Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) projects and programmes of activities, LCDPs, and REDD+ projects.

3. Other mitigation initiatives defined by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change within its GHG mitigation mechanisms, or by the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development [Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible (MADS)].

The accounting rules established in the resolution aim to delineate the following aspects for each type of mitigation initiative:

1. Methodologies used for the formulation of GHG mitigation initiatives.

2. Parameters for constructing baseline emissions.

3. Maximum GHG mitigation potential for REDD+ projects subject to national accounting.

4. Guidelines for establishing GHG mitigation goals for initiatives.

5. Validation and verification criteria.

6. Additionality criteria.

Further Considerations

The specifications for the use of RENARE will be established in the Technical Guide of RENARE, which will be developed and updated by the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Water Policy 2024
DESCRIPTION:
The Policy discusses water security in the context of climate change. It states that groundwater resources offer essential livelihood mechanisms and its strategic importance will probably intensify under climate change and human development (population growth, urbanisation) in the future. Groundwater constitutes the most important buffer and reserve of water during surplus periods as well as a source of water for streams and/or direct withdrawals in times of shortage, and thus is expected to play an essential role in climate change adaptation.

The Policy also states that Zambia faces the issues of inadequate climate resilient water harvesting infrastructure; inadequate framework for rainwater harvesting; and inadequate groundwater exploration and aquifer mapping.

To harness water resources and ensure water security for enhanced access and utilisation, the Policy lists the measure of establishing mechanisms that ensure environmental considerations are included in the design for water resources infrastructure and mitigate the effects of climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Policy on Biological Diversity (Política Nacional de Diversidad Biológica)
DESCRIPTION: This policy establishes Guatemala's comprehensive framework for biodiversity conservation and sustainable use, explicitly recognising the fundamental role of biological diversity in sustainable development, climate change adaptation, human health, reduction of socio-environmental vulnerability, and food security. Developed following Guatemala's recognition as a Megadiverse Country by the Conference of the Parties in Nagoya (2010), the policy responds to the dual challenge of Guatemala's exceptional biological wealth and its classification as one of Latin America's most climate-vulnerable nations. The policy is structured around five thematic axes: knowledge and valuation; conservation and restoration; sustainable utilisation; biodiversity in climate change adaptation; and policy instrumentalisation. The fourth axis specifically addresses climate change, promoting biodiversity as a tool for strengthening adaptation and mitigation mechanisms whilst reducing ecosystem, species and genetic vulnerability. This climate-focused component encompasses research partnerships for conservation strategies that enhance adaptation and mitigation options, integration of traditional and local knowledge in climate response measures, and identification of opportunities for benefit-sharing through mechanisms such as REDD+, payment for ecosystem services, and carbon bonds.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2020-2030
DESCRIPTION: This National Policy for Risk Reduction is in response to the international commitments made by the Chilean State and the need to establish guidelines to strengthen Disaster Risk Management in the country by 2030. It is comprised of a set of principles, cross-cutting approaches, priority axes and strategic objectives, which will be implemented through its respective National Strategic Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction, which will address gaps identified in previous processes and consider the territorial particularities and diversity of communities through the implementation of strategic actions emanating from the guidelines established in this public policy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 3831/2010 on 'Revision of the vehicle taxes regime for vehicles, abolishment of the vehicles recycling measures (scrappage scheme) and measures for tackling atmospheric pollution'
DESCRIPTION: This law regulates traffic taxes for different vehicles. It divides cars into four classes from A (vehicles with the lowest emissions) to D (vehicles with the highest emissions). The revised taxes are based on these four classes and on cylinder capacity. The legislation exempts from annual vehicle taxes privately owned hybrid, electric, and hydrogen passenger cars in classes A and B with capacity lower than 1,929cc. As for A and B class hybrid, electric or hydrogen vehicles with a cylinder capacity higher than 1,929cc, the relevant vehicle taxes are cut by half. Hybrid and low?emission vehicles are also exempt.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Action Plan on the Establishment of a 'Green Energy' Zone in the Liberated Territories 2022-2025
DESCRIPTION: This Plan aims to build wind power plants in the Lachin and Kalbajar regions and a solar power plant in the Jabrayil region, to construct the Azerbaijan-Turkey-Europe energy corridor, to use green technologies for the lighting of streets and roads as well as to install electric vehicles’ charging stations in the territories.

DESCRIPTION: Submission to the UNFCCC ahead of the second Technical Dialogue of the Global Stocktake: submitted by observer organization ClimateWorks Foundation on behalf of the iGST consortium, Submission to the Global Stocktake from ClimateWorks Foundation (CWF) in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 079/CAB/PM
DESCRIPTION: According to Cameroun's second NDC, art. 2 of this document states that the mission of the interministerial committee is to “coordinate and monitor sectoral diligence relating to the implementation of the recommendations of the Paris Agreement on global warming".

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Environmental Impact Assessment Act 2000 (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfungsgesetz, UVP-G)
DESCRIPTION:
The overall objective of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (EIA) is to anticipate the possible effects of projects on the environment, therefore examining them before the realisation of the project. Overall the EIA is centred around:

  • Avoiding the environmental damage beforehand as driven by the precautionary principle
  • Consider environmental impacts from both an integrative and comprehensive perspective, not just focused on sections
  • Achieving better project planning and approval procedures
  • Integrating concerns for the environment in the overall evaluation and decision-making procedure with the same level of attention as to any other concerns
  • Increasing the transparency and comprehensibility of approval procedures for projects by involving the public

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Bangladesh health-national adaptation plan (HNAP)
Inflation Reduction Act
DESCRIPTION:
The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) is a wide-ranging document aiming at reducing inflation, improve healthcare across the country, invest in domestic energy production and manufacturing to increase security of supply and jobs while reducing carbon emissions and focusing on disadvantaged communities. One of the main objective of the Act is to lower energy costs while making cleaner technologies affordable, thus also reducing future costs of climate inaction. It further invests through federal support in a wide range of economic sectors to encourage their decarbonisation efforts. It also aims to increase and resilience among rural areas by supporting climate-smart practices for farmlands and forests.The Act is based on a series of tax credits, grants and subsidies with a $369 billion funding for climate- and energy-related purposes. Prominent incentives contain in the Act aim to boostthe U.S. manufacturing and buying of electric vehicles; U.S. manufacturing of solar panels, wind turbines and batteries; carbon-capture solutions ; green hydrogen production.The Act contains clauses on environmental justice 1) on legacy pollution reduction, 2) on affordable and accessible clean energy for disadvantaged communities, and 3) on better quality of life and good jobs (urban forests, renewable energy, adaptation programs).

In July 2025, Congress passed the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' Act, which repeals section 50262 of IRA and restored earlier legal provisions that had been amended by section 50262. Section 50262 of IRA increased the minimum royalty of gas leases from 12.5% to 16.66%, in addition to increasing the minimum rates for renting and bidding on oil and gas leases.

Furthermore, as of March 2025, the status of some of the other provisions of this entry are likely impacted by the Trump-Vance administration’s regulatory rollback on climate action and ongoing litigation challenging the rollback. To learn more about the rollback, visit the Sabin Center’s Climate Backtracker.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Estonia Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
DESCRIPTION:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030.

Estonia’s long-term objective is to transition to a low-carbon economy, which means gradually reforming the economy and energy system to be resource-efficient, productive and environmentally-friendly in line with the objectives. The use of fossil fuels will be reduced and CO2 emissions will decrease due to energy savings in transport, agriculture, waste management and industrial processes and small-scale power production where energy is produced by facilities with a rated output of less than 20 MWh. To maintain final energy consumption in the period 2021-2030 requires annual energy savings equivalent to 0.8% of the average final energy consumption in the period 2016-2018. Consumption of primary energy is forecast to drop by a quarter in the period 2017-2030. The share of renewables will be increased by changing fossil fuel boilers to renewable fuels, increasing electricity generation from fuel free sources and increased use of biofuels in transport. In the electricity and heating sector, the plan aims at increasing renewable sources.
KEYWORDS: Energy Efficiency;Energy Supply;National Energy And Climate Plans

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: P. 30/Menhut-II/2009 On the implementation of REDD activities
DESCRIPTION: Sets out the regulations for the implementation of REDD+ in Indonesia, including previously unresolved questions over which land classes could be used to develop REDD+ activities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Proclamation creating the Ministry of Environment and Forestry
DESCRIPTION:
The proclamation creates the ‘Ministry of Environment and Forestry'; and amends the designation 'Ministry of Urban Development and Construction' and 'Ministry of Water and Energy'. It considers that to expand farm land and increase forest coverage it is necessary to separate the Forest area from the Ministry of Agriculture. Therefore, the provision gives to the Ministry of Environment and Forest the powers and duties previously given to the Ministry of Agriculture with respect to matters relating to forestry issues.
 
 In its preamble, the proclamation states that industrialised nations will help Ethiopia to decarbonise its economy. It also says the EPA must be elevated to an executive level in order to promote a green economy and climate change resiliency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: OGA Plan on Emissions Reduction
DESCRIPTION: The Plan is a regulatory instrument issued under the NSTA's overarching OGA Strategy, translating that Central Obligation into concrete, binding requirements, including cutting emissions from flaring, venting, and power generation, and supporting CCUS to help the UK meet net zero by 2050. Rather than setting a single interim target or target year, the Plan lays out binding principles and requirements operators must follow, organised under four headings: investment and efficiency, electrification and low-carbon power, flaring and venting, and inventory. Crucially, emissions offsetting does not count toward meeting these obligations, only actual reductions do.
KEYWORDS: Carbon Capture and Storage;Electricity;Energy Efficiency;Net Zero

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Nature Conservancy Act, 2022
DESCRIPTION: The Nature Conservancy Act, 2022, promotes and regulates the creation and operation of protected areas, and is named in the Seychelles' 2025 Biennial Transparency Report as a core recent instrument for ecosystem protection, forest restoration and resulting climate adaptation/resilience. It provides that the responsible minister should appoint a National Advisory Committee, and gives a set of distinct classes of protected area. For these it gives a legal framework for selection, designation, management agreements/planning, entry fees, enforcement powers, definition of fixed-penalty offences and their appeal process.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Amendment to the Law of Superior Education (Decree No.715)
DESCRIPTION: This Amendment to the Law of Superior Education redefines research in institutions of higher learning to include the systematic search and analysis of new knowledge to address the adverse effects of climate change.The Amendment further directs state and private universities to adjust their curriculums in accordance with this amendment.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Presidential Decree 400/2021 on the National Security Strategy of the Russian Federation
DESCRIPTION:
This decree approves a new version of the country's national security strategy (attached to the decree's text). The Russian government has been acknowledging in its security strategy the threats deriving from climate change since 2015 (decree 683/2015, repealed by this document). 

This strategy notably states that climate change is used as a pretext by the world community "for restricting the access of Russian companies to export markets, curbing the development of Russian industry, establishing control over transport routes, and preventing Russia from developing the Arctic." 

In article 25.6, the strategy states that among Russia's national interests and strategic priorities are environmental protection, conservation of natural resources and rational use of natural resources, adaptation to climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Fifth Tourism Master Plan 2023-2027
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan aims to strengthen Maldives’ position as a competitive and sustainable destination, enabling the industry,which has been the driving force in transforming the economy over the last 50 years, to continue leading the country’s growth. One of the goals is to build climate resilience and protect natural assets, which will be implemented through the following strategies:

  1. Improve planning guidelines and concept-approval processes to ensure sustainability is adequately addressed;
  2. Improve the management of common beach resources;
  3. Scale up and improve the quality of management systems to increase the resilience and health of coral reefs;
  4. Develop guidelines to ensure wildlife interactions are sustainable and in line with Maldives’ image and brand;
  5. Improve planning guidelines, knowledge sharing, and access to finance to adapt to climate change and build climate resilience into tourism infrastructure;
  6. Eliminate the use of single-use plastic products in tourist establishments in line with national targets;
  7. Reduce waste and develop and operationalise waste collection and processing infrastructure; and
  8. Develop a framework to renew and rejuvenate coconut palms and native vegetation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Adaptation Plan 2018
DESCRIPTION: This National Adaptation Plan has been endorsed by the Fijian government and has been prepared by national policymakers in coordination with a group of international actors. It contains 160 adaptation measures to be prioritised over five years.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2009
DESCRIPTION: The Barbadian taxation system allows for certain income tax deductions related to the production and use of renewable energy. A deduction of 150 per cent of expenditures on energy audits and electrical retrofitting can be retrieved. For individuals, the deduction cannot exceed BBD $10,000 per year or five years. The deduction is also allowed for training in renewable energy and energy efficient systems for unemployed people under 25 years old.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan 2050
DESCRIPTION: This document sets Hong Kong's climate policy vision until 2050 and details how its net zero emission commitment and other targets should be achieved by then. It follows the Climate Action Plan 2030+ that was released in 2017. The plan emphasises on zero-emission electricity generation, energy savings in buildings, decarbonisation of the transport sector, and a reduction of waste.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Soil Conservation and Land Use
DESCRIPTION: This Law aims to protect Türkiye's soil and ensure for the planned, sustainable use of agricultural land across the country. The Law classifies land and sets minimum parcel sizes, plus additional sizes by province and district, so farmland is not split into plots which are too small to farm viably and sustainably. The Law also requires land-use plans, agricultural land-use plans and soil conservation projects. It also mandates that each province will have a Soil Conservation Board, chaired by the provincial governor. Prime farmland may be used for other purposes, according to the Law, but only in limited cases such as defence, mining, energy, or public-interest projects and only with approval. Violations of the law may lead to fines or the demolition of projects. A subsequent amendment in 2014 further clarified the rules for inherited farmland and the sale of land parcels.
