DESCRIPTION: Mauritius First NDC (Updated submission), Nationally Determined Contribution from Mauritius in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Disaster Risk Management Act (2023-91)
DESCRIPTION:
This Act lays down provisions on the establishment and duties of the National Disaster Council, National Emergency Operations Committee, Recovery Coordination Committee, Disaster Resilience Committee, Clusters, Local government disaster committees, National Disaster Management Office, Disaster Coordinator and the National Emergency Operations Center. It also sets out rules as regards disaster planning at the national and local levels; declaration of state of disaster by executive orders; establishment and utilization of the Disaster Assistance Account; offences and penalties; and public cooperation to successfully prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.

The objectives of this Act are:

  • to establish an institutional structure for the delivery of disaster management and climate and disaster risk reduction measures throughout the Republic, including by promoting cooperation between the government agencies, and with local governments, non-governmental organizations and the private sector;
  • to provide a planning framework for disaster management and for disaster resilience through climate and disaster risk reduction throughout the Republic;
  • to provide arrangements for the effective management and coordination of preparedness for, responses to and recovery from disasters, including arrangements for access to external support;
  • to promote and integrate measures to reduce climate and disaster risk in social, livelihood and development planning and practices throughout the Republic.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Swedish Marine and Water Authority's work on the action plan for climate adaptation
DESCRIPTION:
This action plan aims to adapt operations to a changing climate so that the resilience of ecosystems is strengthened rather than weakened. Other climate adaptation measures will be worked into the action plan gradually.

Measures that contribute to increased resilience to climate change include:

- Effective cooperation between the working areas, marine area protection, green infrastructure, maritime planning, water environment and marine environment management. G

- Green infrastructure: Promoting natural climate adaptation solutions such as restoration of wetlands and floodplains.

- Taking increased action against other environmental pressures such as eutrophication and toxicants to increase the resilience of ecosystems to the effects of a changing climate and ocean acidification. The authority's action work takes into account the effects of a changing climate and links to climate adaptation and limited climate impact.

- Promoting adaptation in collaborations: Working actively for climate adaptation within the framework of the authority's national, European and global collaborations.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: N4C Joint Submission on Recommended Outcomes on Nature-based Solutions for the Global Stocktake
DESCRIPTION: N4C Joint Submission on Recommended Outcomes on Nature-based Solutions for the Global Stocktake, Submission to the Global Stocktake from Conservation International, Nature4Climate coalition in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 25/2022 on circular economy (LEC)
DESCRIPTION: According to article 1, this law aims to promote the transition towards a circular economy, moving from a linear economy to a more efficient and sustainable economic model that optimises the use of natural resources, minimises environmental impacts, promotes efficiency in achieving that products and resources maintain utility and value as long as possible and avoid material emissions and losses. The circular model also promotes responsible and efficient consumption by minimising waste generation and optimising its management, increasing reuse and recycling and reducing less efficient waste management options. It also promotes the awareness of society in the principles of the circular economy.Article 9 of the law states that the Public Administration must intensify the synergies between circularity, the fight against climate change, especially with the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, and the fight against the loss of biodiversity and health protection human through the following actions:a) Analyse how the effects of circularity can be measured in the fight against climate change, adaptation to this phenomenon and the fight against the loss of biodiversity.b) Improve modeling tools to take advantage of the benefits of the circular economy from the point of view of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, linking them to the emission reduction targets established in Law 21/2018, of 13 September, to promote the energy transition and climate change (Litecc) and the mechanisms for the protection of human health.c) Analyse the ecological footprint of the Andorran economic model to improve the circularity of the model.

DESCRIPTION: This document aims at protect Chile's biodiversity from the adverse effects of climate change, raise awareness, improve scientific knowledge and interminiserial coordination.

DESCRIPTION: Nigeria First NDC (Updated submission), Nationally Determined Contribution from Nigeria in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Plan 2050
DESCRIPTION:
The National Climate Change Plan comes in line with the UAE Vision 2021 and the UAE Green Agenda 2015-2030. It seeks to: manage greenhouse emissions while sustaining economic growth; build climate resilience through minimizing risks and increasing capacity for climate adaptation; and advance the country's economic diversification agenda through innovative solutions. According to executive sources, the plan is designed to address the gaps and opportunities for growth in the short, medium and long term. However, the plan has not been published and targets do not seem to have been quantified.

The plan is overseen by the UAE Council on Climate Change and the Environment, which is an inter-ministerial, inter-Emirate governance body. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) will assume the role of the secretariat and take on the primary responsibility for monitoring the progress of the plan. All previous targets and plans of action will now fall under this plan.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Miscellaneous Taxes Act No. 13 of 1963, Chapter 77:01 (Act last amended by Act 46 of 2013)
DESCRIPTION: This Act establishes the Green Fund to financially assist organisations and community groups that are engaged in activities related to remediation, reforestation and conservation of the environment. Effect from 1 January 2001, the 0.1% Green Fund Levy applies on gross sales or receipts of a company carrying on business in Trinidad and Tobago. The Green Fund is the National Environmental Fund of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago. The detailed definition of the relevant activities are as follows:- Remediation: remedying and restoring the functional capacity of an environmental resource damaged by both natural or man-made causes (e.g. wetland or watershed restoration after a storm, land restoration of abandoned oilfields after quarrying or mining)- Reforestation: replanting a previously forested area mainly with seedlings of indigenous forest tree species- Conservation: wise use of natural resources for the benefit of present and future generations (e.g. ecotourism, national parks, renewable energy, reducing pollution (e.g. greenhouse gas emission), sustainable fishery, protecting biodiversity and ecosystems, green technologies and practices)Activities financed by the Green Fund shall be managed by the Minister responsible for finance. The Minister responsible for the environment shall appoint a committee called the Green Fund Advisory Committee to advise on the certification of activities. The Committee comprises of a minimum of five but no more than nine members, selected among persons with experience and relevant qualifications in the areas of finance, environmental management, law or forestry that have demonstrated interest in remediation, reforestation, environmental education and public awareness of environmental issues or conservation. The members of the Committee holds office for two years and renewed by no more than two consecutive terms.All accounts of the Green Fund are kept separately by the Comptroller of Accounts, and shown to Parliament in the general accounts. The Auditor General, in accordance with the Exchequer and Audit Act, audits them annually. The Minister may make Regulations for:- The management and control of the Green Fund- The accounts, books and form to be used in the management of the Green Fund- The projects and other activities which advances are made from the Green Fund- The general operations of the Green Fund.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Energy Sources Development Program
DESCRIPTION:
In 1993, a National Energy Sources Development Programme was implemented to reduce energy imports and obtain maximum benefits from domestic energy sources. 

The document proposed energy efficiency as the first national source of energy and mandates exploration and exploitation of the biomass-based energy generation potential of the country, increase in electricity cogeneration, adoption of efficiency measures in the fisheries and transport sectors, and support to development of hydropower, wind and solar sources especially in isolated areas.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ukraine Adaptation Communication. AC1
DESCRIPTION: Ukraine's Adaptation Communication version 1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Guidelines for Environmental Labelling and Advertising
DESCRIPTION:
These Guidelines are issued in accordance with Article 3 of the Act on Fair Labelling and Advertising, and Article 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act. The Guidelines are subsidiary legislation and are legally binding. 

Under the Guidelines, advertisements relating to the environment must be true, clear, capable of being substantiated and comprehensive. They must not be deceptive or misleading. The guidelines define "environmental properties or efficacy" to include the degree of greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption throughout the product life cycle. 

The Guidelines provide specific case examples to illustrate how claims might be considered. For example, it states that it would be inappropriate for airlines that purchase carbon credits to offset its carbon emissions to claim that its flights contribute to a carbon-neutral future. It also states that it would be misleading for a company to advertise that it had reduced its carbon emissions by 33%, but then state in fineprint "exclusive of transport". Environmental advertising must consider the impact on the natural environment throughout the entire process / life cycle of the product.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Energy Efficency and the Rational Use of Energy
DESCRIPTION: This law aims to create the necessary conditions to improve energy efficiency by implementing and monitoring a functional energy management system. It seeks to reduce the negative impact of energy systems on the environment and limit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Tourism Policy 2015
DESCRIPTION: The Policy includes a section on Environmental Management and Conservation, where the stated policy measure is to promote a “green” environmentally responsible tourism that enhances the country’s natural and cultural resources and addresses environmental threats such as climate change, poaching, over-fishing, deforestation. This includes promoting the increased use of sustainable waste disposal, green packaging and recycling, water and energy conservation, renewable energy, energy monitoring technology, integrated environmental management, social and environmental audits; and developing plans for tourism management and promotion that address environmental sustainability.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Prime Ministerial Decree no. 104/2022
DESCRIPTION: Promote investment incentives under articles 11 of Egypt's Investment Law No. 72/2017 and 10 of its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree no. 2310/2017 including renewable energy projects, agriculture, livestock.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Adaptation to Climate Change in Switzerland: Goals, Challenges and Fields of Action (UD-1055-E) (Swiss National Adaptation Strategy: Part I) and Adaptation to Climate Change in Switzerland: Plan of Action 2014-2019 (1081-F) (Swiss National Adaptation Strategy: Part II)
DESCRIPTION:
The Swiss National Adaptation Strategy aims to serve as framework for the federal offices to adapt a co-ordinated course of action in response to adverse climate effects. It is spilt into two parts. The Strategy describes the goals, challenges and fields of action in adapting to climate change in Switzerland. The overall goal of the strategy is to seize the opportunities provided by climate change, to minimise climate change related risks and to improve the adaptive capacity of society, the environment and the economy.
 
 The first part examines the climate change impacts and identifies the most important fields of action of adaptation to climate change in the following sectors:
 - Natural hazard management
 - Water management
 - Agriculture
 - Forestry
 - Energy
 - Tourism
 - Biodiversity management
 - Health
 - Spatial development.
 
 The second part of the strategy is an action plan to reach the strategy's goals. These measures are co-ordinated between the federal offices in order to address the challenges posed by climate change, i.e., effects of heat waves in urban areas, droughts, floods, increasing slope instabilities in the Alps, decreasing snow cover, adverse effects on water, soil and air quality, changes in biodiversity, and the potential spreading of invasive species, vermin and infectious diseases. The adaptation measures need to be carefully aligned with other cross-cutting strategies of the Federal Council.
 
 12 cross-sectoral challenges are identified, including:
 - Greater heat stress on agglomerations and cities
 - Increasing levels of summer drought
 - Greater risk of flooding
 - Decreasing slope stability and more frequent mass wasting
 - Rising snowline
 - Impaired water, soil and air quality
 - Change in habitats, species, composition and landscapes
 - Spread of harmful organisms, diseases and alien species.
 
 Co-ordinated approach includes the following:
 - Working with the cantons, cities and municipalities
 - In the context of sectoral policies
 - Cross-collaboration and coordination
 - International cooperation on adaptation to climate change
 -International climate negotiations
 - Adapting to climate change in Europe
 - Collaboration with neighbouring countries.

DESCRIPTION: The Heat Pump Investment Roadmap outlines the UK’s strategy to further expand the deployment of heat pumps as a means of advancing climate action and reducing carbon emissions from heating.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Financial Conduct Authority Rules to Enhance Climate-related Disclosures
DESCRIPTION: As of December 2020 the UK's Financial Conduct Authority issued new rules requiring publically listed companies incorporated in the UK to either comply with the recommendations of the Task Force for Climate related Financial Disclosure and include information on climate-related financial disclosures in their annual report or explain the absence of such disclosures.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Malaysia National Communication. NC1
DESCRIPTION: Malaysia National Communication. NC1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Master Plan up to 2030
DESCRIPTION: The Energy Efficiency and Conservation Master Plan (EECMP) is a supreme plan of Bangladesh’s initiative on energy efficiency and conservation.Energy efficiency and Conservation (EEC) potential is defined as a ratio of energy reduction gained by introducing more effective energy management, EE equipment, insulation and solar control for buildings nationwide. EEC potentials were estimated in the agricultural, industrial, Buildings sectors. EEC implementation is a multi-sector issue tackled with the participation of all interested parties including the people and private/public establishments. The EECMP is declined with an action plan containing programs, frameworks and organization structure.

DESCRIPTION: This document was identified in the country's NDC, however no further detail or documentation is available.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Tunisian National strategy and action plan for biodiversity 2018-2030
DESCRIPTION: This updated strategy sets Tunisia's vision to protect its diversity, notably from the adverse effects of climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 17/2015 on the National Civil Protection System
DESCRIPTION: The present Law of the National Civil Protection System aims at civil protection, as an instrument of public security policy, which is the public service that protects people and property by guaranteeing an adequate response to different types of emergencies and disasters originated by natural causes or derived from human action, whether accidental or intentional. Its purpose is to establish the National Civil Protection System as an essential instrument to ensure the coordination, cohesion and effectiveness of public civil protection policies, and regulate the powers of the General State Administration in the matter.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Dam Basins Green Belt Action Plan (2013-2017)
DESCRIPTION: This Action Plan from Türkiye's Ministry of Forestry and Water Affairs aims to create green belts of afforestation and erosion control around dams and ponds. The goal is to reduce the sediment that shortens reservoirs’ lifespans, improve water quality and quantity, and benefit local communities through recreation areas, wildlife habitat, and income-generating tree species to bolster local economies. It targets about 400 of Turkey’s 1,073 dams and ponds, prioritizing potable-water and erosion-sensitive catchments, with work ramping up to 100 sites per year by 2015. Measures include planting species suited to each region, building terraces and check dams, and involving local communities, led by the General Directorate of Forestry with support from the General Directorate of Combating Desertification and Erosion.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Adaptation Plan 1
DESCRIPTION:
Denmark is a flat country with several thousand kilometers of coastline and countless islands, and is particularly vulnerable when sea levels and groundwater rise as a result of climate change.

Climate Adaptation Plan 1 includes, among other things:

  1. Government commitment to vulnerable coastal areas: The state will offer professional help to the municipalities, for example, in choosing a technical solution, developing a payment model, financial calculations or environmental assessments, depending on how far along the municipalities are in the project phase and what they want help with.
  2. Solution to the challenges of high groundwater levels: The government will give municipalities the authority to handle high groundwater levels and make it possible for wastewater companies to create collective solutions in areas where it is profitable for society.
  3. Extension of the coastal protection pool: To speed up climate adaptation, the government will extend the coastal protection pool in 2024 by 150 million kroner. Municipalities can apply for joint coastal protection projects throughout the country and the establishment or reinforcement of dikes in the Wadden Sea.
  4. Protection of Denmark's west coast: It is proposed to allocate more than 1 billion kroner to protect the west coast through sand replenishment and investments in critical lock and coastal facilities in Thorsminde and Hvide Sande.
  5. New advisory committee of civil servants: The government will establish a permanent committee of civil servants at department head level to continuously advise the government on the next steps in Denmark's climate adaptation. The committee may also establish rapid working groups with relevant parties to solve climate adaptation challenges across sectors.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agreement on the implementation of the transition aid from the Green tax reform for industry etc.
DESCRIPTION:
This Agreement establishes the framework for implementing the transition support from the Green Tax Reform for Industry, etc., including the target group, type of support, design of support schemes and requirements for a climate audit in order to receive support. The transition support will be provided on the basis of specific technical transition. In this way, the transition support will contribute to additional CO2 reductions. The parties to the Agreement want to support the various technical transition options that companies in industry and business have. For some companies, the investment cost is the primary barrier to conversion, while the operating cost is the primary barrier to conversion for other companies.

This Agreement follows the Agreement on the Green Tax Reform for industry etc. of 22 June 2022, where the parties agreed to introduce a new and ambitious CO2 tax, which will be phased in from 2025 towards 2030.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB) - climate and vulnerability analysis and action plan for continued work
DESCRIPTION:
This report and its appendices constitute the report on the work of the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB) in accordance with the Ordinance (2018:1428) on the authorities' climate adaptation work in 2019 and the action plan for continued work in 2020-2025. The Swedish government has seen a need to increase work on climate adaptation in Sweden, where this is part of the work. MSB has previously worked on climate adaptation within the authority's entire mission. MSB works to strengthen society's ability to handle stresses across the entire spectrum from accidents to crises and wars. With a changing climate comes more extreme weather events. This means that MSB needs to develop support for stakeholders so that Sweden is better prepared to handle these events. MSB's objectives for the work according to the regulation on authorities' work with climate adaptation have been developed based on the overall vision for MSB:

- A safer society in a changing world

- MSB's work shall contribute to ensuring that the effects of a changing climate do not cause more accidents or social disruptions and thus that damage to the environment, to people's lives or health or to property does not increase.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree on the Quotas for Incentivising the Production of Electricity from Renewable Energy Sources and Highly-Efficient Cogeneration
DESCRIPTION: This document sets quotas for the subsidised production of energy from renewable energy sources and cogeneration.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Plan of priority activities for climate change adaptation and mitigation
DESCRIPTION: This Plan was developed with the support of the Green Climate Fund. It contains sections on national circumstances; the framework for cooperation with the Green Climate Fund; national priority areas and activities and assessment of needs; the need for knowledge and capacity building; consultation; gender equality; and monitoring and evaluation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Development Concept 2050
DESCRIPTION: The National Development Concept 2050 is Poland’s first long-term strategic vision, setting out the country’s development directions through the middle of the 21st century. It uses foresight, forecasting, and scenario analysis to identify potential development pathways and key societal, economic, and environmental challenges. This policy shifts the economic paradigm by treating the natural environment not as an infinite resource, but as a critical form of capital that must be preserved for "generational justice". A primary focus of the concept is a comprehensive energy transformation, which mandates a transition away from fossil fuels toward a zero-emission system powered by renewables and nuclear energy. Beyond power generation, the strategy emphasizes the adoption of a circular economy and a "moderate" consumption model to drastically reduce Poland's overall ecological footprint. To address the physical realities of a warming world, the document prioritizes building national resilience through blue-green infrastructure designed to mitigate the risks of extreme weather events like droughts and floods. Furthermore, it integrates climate action into spatial planning and education, aiming to foster a society that is both environmentally sensitive and structurally prepared for the challenges of the mid-21st century.This Concept was adopted by y the Council of Ministers on 25 July 2025.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution 54/2020 establishing the Climate Change Council
DESCRIPTION:
This resolution creates the Climate Change Council and defines its composition and mission.The resolution was amended 3 times, in 2021, 2023 and 2025 adjusting the members of the Climate Change Council, and the last amendment also brought modifications in the Climate Change Council Statute. The Council is composed of representatives of several Ministries and public authorities. The Council’s core mission is to ensure the efficient implementation of the Paris Agreement. The Council is in charge of: - deliberating on the issues related to the preparation and implementation of the NDC, reviews, recommending and submitting updated NDCs to the Secretariat of the Convention;

- discussing the national system for measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) within the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF), to implement the Paris Agreement in Georgia, and, in case it is approved, shall initiate the decision-making process by the government of Georgia;

- reviewing the national communications of Georgia to the Convention, biennial update reports and the reports on the fulfilment of the nationally determined contribution, and, if those are approved, shall initiate the decision-making process by the government of Georgia;

- reviewing the national program of Georgia prepared for the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and, in case it is approved, shall address the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia with the relevant recommendation;

- reviewing the projects to be submitted to the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Convention Adaptation Fund (AF), Climate Technologies Centre and Network (CTCN) and other financial institutions working on the climate change issues, and, in case the project is approved, shall address the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia with the recommendation to support the projects; - reviewing the national strategies and plans related to climate change and, in case of approval, shall initiate the decision-making process by the government of Georgia;

- establishing and approve the task forces for relevant economic sectors;

- With the view to achieving the objectives of the Council and participating in its activities, the Council can invite representatives from other ministries, government agencies and organisations, private sector, international organisations, as well as other experts and stakeholders.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Iceland National Inventory Report (NIR). 2026
DESCRIPTION: Iceland National Inventory Report (NIR). 2026 - National Inventory Document: Emissions of Greenhouse Gases in Iceland from 1990 to 2024 submitted under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Decree No. 13-2004, establishing the National Energy Policy (2023)
DESCRIPTION: Provides that the National Energy Policy shall promote greenhouse gas emission reduction in energy projects; makes renewable energy and clean technologies a priority.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Emissions Trading Act (EHG)
DESCRIPTION:
This law indends to reduce greenhouse gas emissions within and outside Liechtenstein, and implement the EEA legislation on emissions trading. The targets are similar to EU commitments. The document details permitting rules. Art. 4 states that the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions is primarily pursued through domestic measures, in particular through energy, transport, environmental, forestry, agricultural, economic and financial measures. The share of greenhouse gases that can not be reduced by domestic measures to achieve the reduction targets under para. 1 is covered by participation in project measures abroad or in international emissions trading.

The Emission Trading Act anchors in law a GHG emission reduction target, reducing GHG emissions by 55% compared to the base year 1990. Article 4 outlines a long-term goal to reach climate neutrality by 2050, and an interim target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 45% below 1990 levels by 2030. Reductions are primarily to be achieved domestically, with at least 40% reduced in Liechtenstein. Liechtenstein is also participating in the European Economic Area (EEA) and is obliged to adopt EU legislation considered relevant to the EEA, which is the case for all acts under the EU's Fit for 55 package, and the current version reflects changes in EEA/EU ETS law and updated climate commitments, ensuring the law stays consistent with international obligations and linked registries and market mechanisms.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Mitigation Plan
DESCRIPTION: The Department of Communications, Climate Action and Environment published the National Mitigation Plan in July 2017. The "whole-of-Government" Plan aims at setting Ireland on a decarbonisation pathway to 2050. The Plan further includes 100 actions for various Ministers and public bodies to implement its strategy. The Government recognises that this document does not constitute a "complete roadmap" to achieve the 2050 decarbonisation objective, but develops a medium to long term action. The document outlines the emissions profiles, policy frameworks and strategies to achieve climate change mitigation at the national level, and in each of the following sectors: 1) electricity generation, 2) the built environment, 3) transport, and 4) agriculture, forestry and land use. It further quantifies costs and emissions reductions potentials.
KEYWORDS: Energy Demand;Energy Supply;REDD+ And LULUCF;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 2036/2020 promoting the participation of territorial entities in renewable alternative energy generation projects
DESCRIPTION: Law 2036/2020 authorises the national government to finance the participation of territorial entities in small-scale and distributed generation projects using Non-Conventional Renewable Energy Sources (FNCER). These include biomass, hydroelectric, wind, geothermal, solar, green hydrogen, marine energy, and waste-to-energy technologies. The law allows financing through the General Budget of the Nation projects to prioritise rural areas, align with energy policy guidelines, and support local labour with qualified and unqualified personnel. It aims to promote sustainable energy development, especially in rural areas, through renewable energy sources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Cuba Biennial Update Report. BUR1
DESCRIPTION: Cuba. Biennial update report (BUR). BUR1., Biennial Update Report from Cuba in 2020

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Evaluation of the cost the impact of climate change and adaptation in France
DESCRIPTION:
Second phase report

The interministerial working group on the assessment of the impacts of climate change, the cost of damage and adaptation measures, led by the National Observatory on the Effects of Global Warming (under the Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and the Sea) and the Directorate General of Energy and Climate, has just submitted its second phase report.

Produced with the contribution of the Ministry of Health and Sports, the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Fisheries, and the Interministerial Delegation for Territorial Planning and Competitiveness, this report presents the results of the work on the 10 sectors studied:

  • health;
  • energy;
  • urban planning / built environment/transport infrastructure;
  • biodiversity;
  • tourism;
  • natural risks and insurance;
  • agriculture;
  • forestry;
  • water resources;
  • territories.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Technical analysis of the second biennial update report of Ghana submitted on 19 February 2019. Summary report by the team of technical experts
DESCRIPTION: Technical analysis of the second biennial update report of Ghana submitted on 19 February 2019. Summary report by the team of technical experts, Technical Analysis Summary Report from UNFCCC Secretariat in 2019

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 282/2023 on the energy performance of buildings
DESCRIPTION: Law No. 282/2023 creates a legal framework to promote the energy performance of buildings, implementing existing public policy and establishing minimum buildings energy performance requirements across a range of sectors. It established the responsibilities of national and local governments, and mandates the formation of a Sectoral Strategy for the long-term renovation of the national real estate stock, in order to meet overarching targets to decarbonise the buildings sector.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Supreme Decree No. 019-2009-MINAM, Regulation of Law No. 27446, Law of the National System of Environmental Impact Assessment
DESCRIPTION: The regulation incorporates modifications to the Environmental Management Regulation for the Industry sector. Among the main reforms are the promotion of integrated management of climate change and the inclusion of risk analysis of the effects of climate change in environmental management instruments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law of Socio-Natural and Technological Risks
DESCRIPTION: This general law specifies various risks faced by the country and stipulates how the government is to respond. Climate change and environmental contamination are specified as national priorities. Specifically the law states that a special commission named The National Advisory Board of Sociocultural and Technological Risk Management shall dictate, within one year of promulgation, the terms for the creation of a National Plan of Adaptation to Climate Change. Such a plan is required to include the evaluation of national and regional vulnerabilities to a changing climate, potential effects that climate change will bring to Venezuela, and strategies to adapt to climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree Regulating the Electricity Sector Law (Decreto que expide el Reglamento de la Ley Sector Eléctrico)
DESCRIPTION: Mexico's Regulation of the Electricity Sector Law (2025) implements the Electricity Sector Law by establishing detailed rules for electricity planning, system operation, generation, storage, commercialization, transmission, distribution, and participation in the wholesale electricity market. The regulation strengthens state coordination of the electricity sector through binding planning mechanisms and institutional oversight while providing the operational framework for public and private actors participating in Mexico's reformed electricity market.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategy for Sweden's Support for Democracy, Human Rights and the Environment in Russia (2020-2024)
DESCRIPTION:
This Strategy outlines Sweden's support for democracy, human rights as well as the environment and climate in Russia. 

The Strategy also aims at enhancing climate action in the Baltic sea region. It aims to do so mainly through capacity building for the sustainable management of ecosystems, sustainable management and use of natural resources, conservation of biodiversity and a decrease in emissions in the Baltic Sea. It also seeks to strengthen capacity to contribute to the climate transition and phase out fossil fuel. Lastly, it aims at increasing capacity among civil society actors and other relevant stakeholders.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Biden-⁠Harris Plan to Revitalize American Manufacturing and Secure Critical Supply Chains in 2022
DESCRIPTION:
This plan builds on the conclusions from seven sectoral reports published by federal agencies (linked in the full text). These reports identify key weaknesses in crucial supply chains and set multi-year strategies accordingly. The Biden-Harris plan announces additional measures to enhance long-term resilience of critical supply chains, and formally institutionalises supply chain resilience throughout the Federal government.The administration notably indicates that it will invest in sustainable domestic production and processing of critical minerals, from rare earths serving in electric motors to carbon fibre used for airplanes. In parallel to this document, it announced plans to expand domestic rare earth processing, strengthen the National Defense Stockpile; update mining regulations to ensure sustainable and responsible practices; and issue recommendations for comprehensive reform of mining laws. The plan further charges the Department of Energy to investigate the feasibility of extracting rare-earth from mine waste. As part of the Mining Innovations for Negative Emissions Resources (MINER) Program, the Department is releasing a $44 million funding opportunity "to provide commercial-ready technologies that give the United States a net-zero or net negative emissions pathway toward increased domestic supplies of copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt, rare earth elements, and other critical elements required for a clean energy transition."

As of March 2025, the status of this entry is likely impacted by the Trump-Vance administration’s regulatory rollback on climate action. To learn more about the rollback, visit the Sabin Center’s Climate Backtracker.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Nationwide Climate Change Policy 2009
DESCRIPTION: Nationwide Climate change Policy was approved by the President and became effective on 01/12/2009. Mitigation is the country's first goal. There is no agency to coordinate the implementation but the Office of Environment and Emergency Management is responsible for performing th evaluation with assistance from all sectors. Nationwide Climate Change Policy: 1. To advocate a post Kyoto carbon dioxide emission reduction that will keep temperature rise to less than 1.5 degree celsius by 2020 and beyond, 2. To urgently address the global reduction and/or destruction of GHGs and non-GHG warmers through 'fast action' strategies, 3. Aims to maintain and enhance FSM as a negative carbon country through effective management of our natural sinks, bio-sequestration, promotion of renewable energy and energy efficiency, and other appropriate means.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Integrated Transport Planning Act (ZCPN)
DESCRIPTION: The Integrated Transport Planning Act (ZCPN in Slovenian) establishes a legal framework for coordinated, multi-level transport planning in Slovenia, aiming to ensure the development of a sustainable, efficient, and integrated transport system. It aims to change the structure of transport modes in favour of more sustainable forms of mobility that are more energy efficient, contribute to the economic use of space and cause fewer emissions of greenhouse gases, noise and other pollutants than fossil fuel-powered transport. The act promotes a shift from fragmented, infrastructure-focused planning toward a comprehensive approach that includes public transport, walking, cycling, and intermodal solutions, with the goal of reducing reliance on private motorised transport and improving accessibility.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal water pollution control act (Clean Water Act)
DESCRIPTION:
This document aims to restore and main­tain the chemical, physical, and biological integrity of the United States' waters. It sets the rules against water pollution and water quality goals.

Section 104 on research, investigations, training and information stipulates in clause n.1) that authorities and associated bodies shall conduct and promote comprehensive studies of the effects of pollution. These studies shall notably consider the effect of the exploitation of fossil fuels, flood and ero­sion control.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan, developed by the Ministry of Climate Change (MOCC) and the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN), aims to support policy measures and strengthen institutional processes that enhance women’s participation in climate decision-making and implementation. It was formulated under the first Gender Responsive Readiness Grant of the Green Climate Fund (GCF).

The cross-cutting priority actions are as follows:

  1. Ensure the participation and representation of women at all levels of climate policy, planning and decision making across sectors;
  2. Strengthen coordination and promote institutionalisation to address gender issues and support gender mainstreaming;
  3. Develop gender responsive climate actions through national and provincial policies and programmes;
  4. Collect gender disaggregated data to fill information gaps Invest in context specific research to inform policy making and programming; and
  5. Develop a framework to monitor progress on ccGAP implementation.

This Plan is divided into six sections, covering the priority sectors aligned with the National Climate Change Policy (NCCP) of 2021: disaster risk reduction; agriculture and food security; forests and biodiversity; integrated coastal management; water and sanitation; and energy and transport. Each section covers the gender-related concerns, relevant polciies and institutional frameworks, programmes and projects that focus on women or contain a women-related component; and a sector-specific action plan to strengthen the inclusion and leadership of women in climate action.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Vision 2036: Achieving Prosperity for All
DESCRIPTION: Vision 2036 aims to transform Botswana from an upper middle-income country in 2016 to a high-income country by 2036. The first vision was set in 1996, and also followed a 20-year period, but does not have a climate focus. Vision 2036 aims to further sustainable economic development, human and social development, sustainable environment, as well as governance, peace and security. In particular, it lays a large focus on climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, and a low-carbon future.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Policy Framework for MSMEs
DESCRIPTION:
This document identifies a high potential for micro, small and medium enterprises in powering the country's economic growth. It aims to enable MSMEs to deliver on this potential and expand their share of the GDP, with a focus on 1) Legislative, regulatory and business support framework; 2) Access to finance; 3) Market access, competitiveness and productivity; and, 4) Development of entrepreneurial skills, knowledge and competencies through education and training.

The document notably seeks to facilitate the development of MSMEs in the field of renewable energy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation 65/2024 on the implementation rules for the European Union Cohesion Policy Programme 2021-2027
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation No. 65 establishes the implementation framework for measure 6.1.1.6. "Promoting the use of zero-emission vehicles in municipalities" under specific objective 6.1.1. "Mitigate the economic, social and environmental consequences of the transition to climate neutrality in the regions most affected" of the EU Cohesion Policy. It defines the eligibility requirements for municipalities seeking funding from the Just Transition Fund to acquire zero-emission vehicles, including financial allocations, reporting standards, and the legal responsibilities of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development (VARAM).

The objective is to mitigate the socio-economic impacts of the "green transition" in Latvia's most vulnerable regions. By subsidizing zero-emission transport, the program ensures that autonomous municipal functions, such as education, social assistance, and healthcare access remain stable and environmentally sustainable during the shift to a carbon-neutral economy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Vanuatu National Energy Roadmap
DESCRIPTION:
The National Energy Roadmap, published by the Department of Energy with assistance from the Australian government and the World Bank, proposes a long-term development plan for the energy sector to reduce its reliance on imported petroleum fuels and focuses on five energy sector priorities, each with specified targets and associated strategic directions for action (note that some targets are included in several different areas but are each included here once for brevity):
- Access to secure, reliable and affordable electricity for all citizens by 2030
o Within concession areas; 75% household connected by 2015, 90% by 2020 and 100% by 2030
o Close to concession areas; 33% household connected by 2015, 90% by 2020 and 100% by 2030
o Off-grid grid areas; 100% households having access to modern electricity via individual homes systems and basic power products by 2020
o Public Institutions; 90% having access by 2015 and 100% by 2020
- Reliable, secure and affordable petroleum supply throughout Vanuatu
o Reduce the cost of distributing all petroleum products in Vanuatu by 5% in 2015 and 10% in 2020
o Improvements in Health, Safety and Environmental Standards. All Operators to meet new standards by 2020
- A more affordable and low cost of energy services in Vanuatu
o 40% renewable energy generation by 2015 and 65% by 2020
- An energy secure Vanuatu at all times
o 10% improvement in diesel efficiency by 2015 and 20% by 2020
- Mitigating climate change through renewable energy and energy efficiency
o Comprehensive data collection established to set realistic targets and begin energy efficiency initiatives

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Environmental Quality Decree of the Netherlands (Besluit kwaliteit leefomgeving, Bkl)
DESCRIPTION:
The Environmental Quality Decree of the Netherlands (Bkl) applies to central and local governments and contains:

  • Rules on environmental values, including the state’s environmental values for the protection of health and the environment, with ambient values having been established for the quality of air, water, and bathing sites.
  • Instruction rules for programmes related to water, including flood risk management, the approach to nitrogen reduction both on a national and municipal level, and rules regarding Natura 2000 areas
  • Rules for the monitoring of environmental values and other parameters, the collection of data, and the provision of information. Moreover, it contains rules dealing with monitoring information on climate change mitigation (e.g. monitoring emissions of greenhouse gases, the states of bird species, natural habitats and the animal and plant species, and ambient values of nitrogen deposition)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority Act
DESCRIPTION:
This act, predicated on the aim of increasing energy security, creates an independent authority, the Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority, to promote the development and use of renewable energy. The act specifies 23 responsibilities of the authority, including to:
 - Encourage the use of power and energy efficient equipment and take necessary steps for standardisation and labelling of power and energy using equipment and appliances
 - Assist the government in making and implementation of energy efficient building code
 - Provide technical and financial assistance in research, development, demonstration and training on renewable energy
 - Encourage commercialisation of renewable energy and energy efficiency activities in private sector through implementation of pilot project

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: U.S. National Blueprint for Transportation Decarbonization
DESCRIPTION: This Blueprint is a strategy to cut all greenhouse gas emissions from the transportation sector by 2050 and improve overall transport sector efficiency. The plan covers road, off-road, maritime, aviation, and rail transportation. The decarbonization approach focuses on three areas: 1) increasing convenience with walkability and cycling access, co-ordinated land use and transportation system development; 2) enhancing efficiency-public transportation, modal shift for passengers and freight, and improved efficiency of all vehicles; and 3) promoting clean vehicles-zero-emission vehicle fuels and the infrastructure to support them.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Change Mitigation Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030
DESCRIPTION:
This document aims to present a roadmap on climate response covering the period until 2030 and includes the relevant strategies and action plans in this regard. Built on a scientific basis, it offers a comprehensive approach by bringing together institutional policies, expert views, and GHG reduction needs. It includes 49 strategies and 260 actions covering GHG reduction policies in energy, industry, buildings, transport, waste, agriculture, and land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF) sectors as well as in areas of carbon pricing mechanisms and just transition.

The key sectoral strategies in the Action Plan, which comprises 49 strategies and 260 actions for 7 main mitigation sectors and 2 cross-cutting thematic areas, include:

● Promoting energy efficiency across all sectors,

● Maximising the use of renewable energy,

● Reducing product-based carbon footprint and carbon intensity in industry,

● Promoting sustainability reporting,

● Promoting circular economy and resource efficiency across the manufacturing industry,

● Promoting Nearly Zero Energy buildings,

● Promoting the use of district heating and cooling systems,

● Developing electrification systems in the transport sector,

● Developing integrated transport systems,

● Ensuring transition to zero- or low-emission transport systems,

● Protecting and increasing sink areas for effective climate response,

● Ensuring transition of forestry and agricultural enterprises to circular bioeconomy with high added value,

● Extending eco-friendly agricultural practices,

● Ensuring rational fertiliser use,

● Reducing methane emissions originating from livestock,

● Preventing and reducing waste generation,

● Increasing use of waste as raw material/resource in production,

● Establishing an emissions trading system in Türkiye,

● Conducting infrastructure studies on other carbon pricing mechanisms,

● Developing and promoting clean technologies,

● Achieving digitalization in all sectors,

● Developing incentive and support mechanisms for GHG reduction,

● Developing sustainable investment instruments,

● Planning for transition to a low-carbon economy with the principle of just transition,

● Building capacity for just transition and employment transformation, and

● Integrating Türkiye’s net zero emission target into the education system.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Order on Withdrawal of Agricultural Production from Carbon-Rich Soils (Peatland Restoration)
DESCRIPTION:
This Executive Order establishes a framework for projects that withdraw carbon-rich lowland soils from agricultural operation and, through the interruption of drains, closing of ditches etc., restores natural hydrology to the greatest extent possible (climate lowland projects).

The purpose of climate lowland projects is to achieve a reduction in CO2 emissions and at the same time support other considerations, particularly regarding nature, the environment and climate adaptation.

The Danish Environmental Protection Agency may, in accordance with the rules in this executive order, provide subsidies for climate lowland projects to municipalities, to landowners, to national park funds, and to funds with non-profit nature, environmental or climate purposes. The subsidy includes landowner compensation. The Danish Nature Agency may implement climate lowland projects within the framework of the allocated grant and purpose statement in Implementation may take place by fully or partially purchasing project land, purchasing replacement land, selling these, land distribution and agreeing on landowner compensation in accordance with the rules in this executive order.

DESCRIPTION: Greece National Communication. NC1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation on Supporting Domestic Parts Used in Facilities Producing Electricity from Renewable Energy Sources
DESCRIPTION: This Regulation from the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources sets the conditions and procedures for paying an additional domestic contribution price to licensed renewable electricity generators that use domestically manufactured components, with the aim of encouraging local manufacturing in the renewable energy sector. These components are qualified as domestically manufactured when 55% of their integrated parts are made locally. The Regulation includes the calculations for the domestic contribution price, how manufacturing facilities who wish to participate can apply for a certificate, and the conditions for inspections of energy generation facilities. The Regulation has subsequently been updated in 2020 and in 2021.

DESCRIPTION: Ukraine National Inventory Report (NIR). 2025

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Building Regulations etc. (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2026 ("Future Homes and Buildings Standards")
DESCRIPTION:
These Regulations were introduced by the government as a statutory instrument authorised by the Buildings Act of 1984. They replace the previous Buildings Regulations for 2010 which introduced requirements for energy efficiency in buildings. The 2010 Regulations were subject to amendments in 2013 and 2021.

The 2026 Regulations - often referred to as the Future Homes and Buildings Standards - require all new dwellings in the UK to meet certain standards which would avoid the need to retrofit them once the grid becomes zero carbon. The standards effectively prevent the use of gas boilers in new builds.

The Regulations were laid before parliament on 24th March 2026. However, they do not enter into force until 24 March 2027, with certain provisions for higher risk buildings not coming fully into force under 24 September 2027, subject to transitional provisions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sao Tome and Principe Biennial Update Report. BUR1
DESCRIPTION: Sao Tome and Principe. Biennial update report (BUR). BUR1., Biennial Update Report from Sao Tome and Principe in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Sustainable Constructions (ENCS) 2013-2020
DESCRIPTION: The National Sustainable Construction Strategy (ENCS) was developed by the Government of Chile as an inter-ministerial initiative to incorporate sustainability principles throughout the life cycle of buildings and infrastructure. Led by the Ministries of Housing and Urban Development, Environment, Energy, Public Works, Economy, and Social Development, the strategy provides a framework for advancing environmental, social, and economic sustainability in the construction sector. The goal is to promote sustainable construction practices by improving energy and resource efficiency, minimizing environmental impacts, and enhancing quality of life in urban and rural environments. It aims to guide both public and private sector actors toward a low-carbon, climate-resilient, and socially inclusive built environment.Now it is under revision. A Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) process is underway to update its objectives and scope. The revised strategy is expected to incorporate new policy priorities such as: Climate resilience and disaster risk reduction, Ecosystem and biodiversity protection, Gender equity and social inclusion, Enhanced public engagement and territorial equity.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Iceland National Inventory Report (NIR). 2020
DESCRIPTION: Iceland National Inventory Report (NIR). 2020

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Operational Programme Quality of Environment (2014-2020)
DESCRIPTION: The Operational Programme Quality of Environment (OP QE) of the Slovak Republic for the 2014–2020 programming period focused on sustainable and efficient resource use, environmental protection, climate change adaptation, and the promotion of a low-carbon, energy-efficient economy. Aligned with the Europe 2020 strategy and the Slovak National Reform Programme, the OP QE addressed national and regional challenges through a targeted investment strategy. This strategy incorporated three thematic objectives: shifting to a low-carbon economy, promoting climate change adaptation and risk management, and preserving the environment while enhancing resource efficiency.

DESCRIPTION: Technical analysis of the third biennial update report of Viet Nam submitted on 16 April 2021. Summary report by the team of technical experts, Technical Analysis Summary Report from UNFCCC Secretariat in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Implementation Plan to Accelerate the Comprehensive Utilization of Industrial Resources
DESCRIPTION: To achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this Plan promotes the circular development of industrial parks, strengthens the comprehensive utilisation of bulk solid waste, and improves the resource recycling system.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Colombia National Inventory Report (NIR). 2022
DESCRIPTION: Colombia's National Inventory Report submitted in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 41127 creating the National Measuring System for Climate Change
DESCRIPTION:
This Decree creates the National Climate Change Metric System (SINAMECC) which constitutes the official coordination platform, and institutional and sectoral linkage of the Costa Rican State to facilitate the management and distribution of climate change knowledge and information. SINAMECC will operate as a sub-module of the National Environmental Information System (SINIA) and will be linked to the National Statistics System (SEN). The coordination, operation and execution will be under the responsibility of the Directorate of Climate Change (DCC).

The SINAMECC will allow the compilation and management of the data and information produced by the State on climate change, and where appropriate, of the private sector, academia and civil society, and will guarantee its dissemination, respecting the confidentiality of information that possess that character, of compliance with current regulations.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Royal Decree-Law No. 10/2017 on urgent measures to mitigate the effects caused by drought in certain river basins
DESCRIPTION:
This Royal Decree-Law establishes support measures for the owners of agricultural holdings located in the territorial areas affected by drought in 2017, if they had an endowment less than or equal to 50 percent of the normal, or have suffered losses of gross production in crops of at least 20 percent of normal production in coastal areas, and 30 percent in other areas.

It also establishes measures of support to the owners of the agricultural holdings affected by both the hydrological drought in the previous basins and the meteorological one in the whole national territory.

DESCRIPTION: Lebanon National Adaptation Plan. NAP1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Geological Survey of Sweden - action plan for climate adaptation 2025-2027
DESCRIPTION:
This action plan for climate adaptation applies to 2025–2027, but looks forward to 2030. The action plan is based on the Swedish Geotechnical Institute's (SGI's) mission to reduce the risks of landslides, rock falls and coastal erosion and to contribute to sustainable development in a changing climate. The action goals to achieve this visionary authority goal, which encompasses SGI's entire area of ​​operation, are:

• SGI will develop and disseminate knowledge about climate-driven geotechnical risks within four of the national risk areas,

• SGI will develop and disseminated methods for nature-based solutions to reduce coastal erosion and stabilise slopes,

• SGI will implement advice and recommendations on climate adaptation to support sustainable municipal planning, and

• Physical climate adaptation measures for landslides, avalanches and coastal erosion will be implemented and followed up on.

A changing climate can contribute to an increased spread of PFAS and other pollutants that are already present in the landscape and those that will be added in the future. We see that we have an important role in guiding municipalities in how they can assess and manage these risks. Since SGI is primarily a knowledge-producing authority, continued dialogue and cooperation within the civil engineering sector is essential to achieving our authority goal.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Climate Change Risks;Coastal Erosion;Disaster Risk Management

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Prime Minister Circular 2013/11 establishing Coordination Board on Climate Change and Air Management
DESCRIPTION: The Coordination Board on Climate Change and Air Management (CBCCAM), a public body created by Prime Minister Circular 2013/11, is competent for taking decisions and measures related to climate change and air management. The CBCCAM decisions are the first legal means for the national inventory system.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Restoration and Reforestation Plan
DESCRIPTION: This plan aims to protect and regrow the country's forests.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Nagar Van Yojana (NVY) forestation scheme
DESCRIPTION: This urban forest scheme intends to create 400 ‘Nagar Vans’ and 200 Nagar Vatikas in the vicinity of urban areas under the National Fund of CAMPA.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Order 232/1999 on CO2 emissions
DESCRIPTION: This document was prepared by the Ministry of Natural resources and Environmental Protection to implement a regulation on the method of calculation of emission of carbon dioxide to the atmosphere from thermal power plants and boiler plants.
