PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resources Methane Abatement Fund
DESCRIPTION:
This Fund is for the development, prototype verification, validation, and demonstration-level projects of methane abatement technologies related to coal and gas industries. Funding is between AU$1 and 5 million for universities, publicly funded research organisations and non-profit research organisations to:

  • accelerate the development and deployment of methane abatement technologies;
  • reduce costs of abatement technologies;
  • reduce Australia’s methane emissions;
  • complement the Safeguard Mechanism reforms; and
  • support the Government’s commitments to the Global Methane Pledge.

The Fund is also intended to support opportunities for First Nations’ researchers to be involved in technology development.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: St. Kitts Agricultural Development Strategy (ADS) 2013 - 2016)
DESCRIPTION:
The Agricultural Development Strategy was published in February 2013 by the Department of Agriculture to provide a framework to improve the production and marketing of national agricultural products over the period 2013 to 2016. The document acknowledges the criticality of climate change and resource scarcity and the subsequent need to adopt a sustainable agriculture agenda.

The Strategy first states the national agriculture situation, then develops a vision and development goals, establishes the Planning for Implementation Network, and details the Institutional Development Plan. Development goals include: 1) to provide safe, affordable food and nutrition security, 2) to create sustainable resilient farming systems in oder to support effective land, water and biodiversity management, and 3) to create resilient farming systems capable of adapting to hazards of a changing climate. The Core Program on Agricultural Risk Management and Climate Change Adaptation shall be activated to reach this latter goal.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Electric System Development Program 2021-2035 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2021-2035)
DESCRIPTION: The Programa para el Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) 2021-2035 is a key planning instrument for Mexico’s National Electric System (SEN), outlining a fifteen-year strategy for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution, in alignment with the National Development Plan. It integrates various planning tools, such as the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE) and programmes for the expansion and modernisation of the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN aims to ensure a reliable electricity supply for over 120 million users across two million square kilometres, while addressing the growing demand, reducing electricity costs, and enhancing system reliability. A core objective is to strengthen the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation and transmission, including the reactivation of combined-cycle plants and the modernisation of hydroelectric facilities, to support national energy sovereignty and economic development.In relation to climate change and energy transition, the PRODESEN explicitly incorporates Mexico’s international commitments under frameworks such as the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Protocol, the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It emphasises the reduction of GHG emissions, targeting a limit of 139 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030, as part of Mexico’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The programme promotes the orderly integration of clean and renewable energy sources into the national energy mix, with a significant focus on distributed generation, particularly solar photovoltaic systems, which are projected to grow substantially by 2035. Additionally, it underscores energy efficiency measures and the expansion of electricity access to rural communities, aligning energy policy with sustainable development goals and environmental protection.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change 2023-2030
DESCRIPTION:
This Strategy is a planning document for all actions in the field of gender and climate change. It defines the Central African Republic's vision on gender issues related to climate change, in line with the guidelines of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It is jointly led by the National Climate Coordinator of the Ministry of the Environment and Sustainable Development, and the Directorate-General for Gender Promotion of the Ministry for the Promotion of Gender and the Protection of Women, Families and Children. The Strategy covers the strategic framework, the action plan, and the framework for implementation, monitoring, evaluation and financing.

The strategic areas are:

  1. Governance, coordination and climate finance;
  2. Specific actions in priority sectors for combating climate change;
  3. Capacity-building and knowledge transfer;
  4. Information, awareness-raising and communication; and
  5. Empowerment and climate leadership of women and vulnerable groups in a secure environment.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National climate change policy guidelines
DESCRIPTION:
The policy guideline aims to identify the strategies required to consolidate the national capacity necessary to respond to the potential threats of climate change.

It proposes implementing a mechanism for clean development concerning the reduction of emissions. The diagnosis considers the implications for Colombia of being a country Party to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and its Kyoto Protocol in terms of the commitments made and the opportunities they represent.

The objective is to identify the strategies required to consolidate the national capacity necessary to respond to the potential threats of climate change, respond to the provisions of the Convention and the Kyoto Protocol to maximise the opportunities derived from the financial mechanisms and comply with the established commitments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Resources Regulations (Testing Energy Efficiency of Pumping Installations) 2004
DESCRIPTION: The regulations set energy efficiency standards for induction motors, preventing the manufacturing, sale, import, marketing or exhibition of Pumps (installations composed of an electrical motor and water pump with an electrical consumption of 150,000 KWH per year or more), if they fail to meet the standards set in the regulations.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Zimbabwe Vision 2030
DESCRIPTION: Zimbabwe Vision 2030 embodies the aspirations towards a Prosperous Upper Middle-Income Nation by 2030, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and African Union Agenda 2063. It provides for plans to partner with development partners to “broaden climate change mitigation and adaptation activities to include critical elements such as water management and harvesting measures to mitigate the effects of drought, respect for biodiversity and wetland management issues.”

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan
DESCRIPTION:
The Plan contains seven main areas:

■ Infrastructure: Integrate adaptive flood control and flood management measures. Enhance the ability of transportation systems to carry out decision-making, withstand and recover from disruptions, and detect and respond to challenges. Bolster the ability of public works to resist climate shocks. ■ Water resources: Guarantee a stable water supply by developing a diverse range of new water resources, eliminating public water pipe leakages, conserving water and adopting smart technologies for water resource management. ■ Land use: Promote rational land use, such as by advancing nature-based solutions in holistic planning of rural areas, and encouraging water retention landscape design in urban renewal projects. ■ Oceans and coasts: Adopt nature-based solutions to strengthen the adaptability of coastal environments and maintain a dynamic ecological equilibrium. ■ Energy supply and industries: Raise awareness among industries regarding climate change adaptation. Help companies identify and evaluate the extent of risks to their infrastructure from climate hazards such as flooding and high winds. Provide companies with guidance on adaptation strategy planning. ■ Agricultural production and biodiversity: Improve agricultural risk management and lower agricultural losses by administering climate change impact assessments. Bolster ecological resilience by advancing nature-based solutions. ■ Health: Strengthen emergency medical services, disease control systems and occupational health and safety protections. Improve long-term environmental monitoring, risk identification and pollution control measures. Heighten public preparedness by establishing warning systems for extreme temperatures and other awareness mechanisms.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agreement announcing the North Pacific Marine and Regional Ecological Management Program (Acuerdo que da a conocer el Programa de Ordenamiento Ecológico Marino y Regional del Pacífico Norte)
DESCRIPTION: This policy establishes the Marine and Regional Ecological Zoning Programme for Mexico's Northern Pacific, mandating integrated spatial planning to align coastal and marine development with constitutional mandates for environmental protection and sustainable development. The programme employs systems dynamics modelling to forecast environmental conflicts across sectors (including tourism, fisheries, aquaculture, and agriculture) designating Environmental Management Units (UGAs) to regulate land and sea use. It prioritises biodiversity conservation (e.g., whale habitats, turtle nesting grounds) while promoting sustainable economic activities, emphasising intergovernmental coordination between federal agencies, state governments, and local authorities to balance ecological preservation with socioeconomic objectives.The policy addresses climate change through vulnerability assessments and adaptive spatial planning. It identifies low-lying sandy zones and coastal lagoons as highly exposed to sea-level rise, erosion, and extreme weather events, projecting impacts such as habitat loss and water scarcity. Key adaptation measures include restricting development below 5m elevation, protecting coastal ecosystems (mangroves, dunes, seagrasses) as natural buffers, mandating wastewater treatment to maintain water quality, and implementing sustainable water resource management to mitigate aquifer depletion.

DESCRIPTION: The decree establishes the legal architecture to ensure that Italy can meet the deadlines and goals imposed by the European Commission vis-à-vis the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2021/241 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2021, by the National Plan for complementary investments, Legislative Decree no. 59 of 6 May 2021, as well as by the NECP 2030. The Title I of Part 2 brings the Ecological Transition and acceleration of ecological landscape procedures that establishes the "PNRR-PNIEC Technical Commission" for fast-tracked environmental approvals of green energy projects (article 17). It also introduces simplified permitting for renewable plants (solar, wind, biogas), energy storage systems, and EV charging infrastructure (article 30-32) and includes critical reforms to the "Superbonus" for building energy efficiency (article 33).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation on Exhaust Gas Emission Control and Gasoline and Diesel Oil Quality
DESCRIPTION: This Regulation aims to protect public health and the environment by reducing the air pollution from motor vehicle exhaust and to set environmental quality standards for the gasoline and diesel sold for road use. Cars must be tested every two years, and other motor vehicles every year after the first, at authorized stations that check emissions against set limits. Vehicles that pass get a stamp on their emission certificate, while those that fail must be repaired and retested within thirty days. Stations that break the rules can lose their authorization, and owners who skip testing or exceed the limits may face administrative fines. The energy regulator enforces the fuel standards, including a maximum sulfur content.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards
DESCRIPTION: In December 2021, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalized revised national greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions standards for passenger cars and light trucks for Model Years 2023- 2026. In this final action, the EPA is establishing revised, more stringent national GHG emissions standards for passenger cars and light trucks under section 202(a) of the Clean Air Act (CAA), 42 U.S.C. 7521(a).Section 202(a) requires EPA to establish standards for emissions of air pollutants from new motor vehicles which, in the Administrator’s judgment, cause or contribute to air pollution which may reasonably be anticipated to endanger public health or welfare. The emissions standards aim for a fleet average of 52 miles per gallon (mpg) by 2026.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Adaptation Program
DESCRIPTION:
As part of the implementation of the  National Climate Change Plan 2050 , the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) launched the National Climate Change Adaptation Program. The Program aims to carry out a systematic and participatory risk assessment as a basis for planning adaptation measures in four priority sectors: public health, energy, infrastructure, and the environment. It is geared towards increasing climate resilience by minimising risks and improving adaptive capacity, particularly among vulnerable groups, such as women, the elderly, persons living with disabilities, and young people who will inherit the increasing impacts of climate change. The Program entails the following:

  • risk and vulnerability assessment, and adoption of immediate low-cost measures;
  • mainstreaming of adaptation planning in development policies; and
  • monitoring and evaluation to ensure implementation of evidence-based adaptation measures.

This information is based on the United Arab Emirates' Updated Second Nationally Determined Contribution.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Kosovo's Law on Climate Change
DESCRIPTION:
This law determines Kosovo's mitigation and adaptation measures to climate change in line with binding international agreements, and its commitments to sustainable development and the transition to a carbon-neutral economy. It further establishes a monitoring, reporting, and verification system and defines the obligations and responsibilities of relevant state authorities.

The objectives of the law include 1) the reduction of anthropogenic emissions, 2) the strengthening of adaptation capacities, 3) the conservation and growth of carbon sinks, and 4) the promotion of economic development and job creation through the sustainable management of natural resources. To oversee the implementation of these objectives, the law establishes the Council of Climate Change, an inter-ministerial body, and the Scientific Advisory Board. To monitor, report, and verify greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, it relies on the National Inventory System, the Greenhouse Gas Inventory, and the Information System on Climate Change.

This law further aims to develop the Long-term Strategy for Decarbonization, and the Strategy and Action on Adaptation to Climate Change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction 2025-2029 (PNRRD)
DESCRIPTION:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction Plan (PNRRD) 2025-2029 guides public policies on comprehensive risk management. It outlines the goals and objectives of programs, as well as actions aimed at reducing existing risks in order to protect people and their property. Its formulation involves the identification, analysis, and management of the causal factors of emergencies and disasters, with the objective of reducing exposure to hazards, decreasing the vulnerability of the population, and improving preparedness for adverse events. It establishes the multi-year strategic guidelines and goals that govern the National System for Comprehensive Risk Management and Civil Protection (SINAGIR), created by Law No. 27,287.

The priorities of the PNRRD 2025-2029 are:

  • Understanding disaster risk.
  • Strengthen governance of disaster risk management.
  • Increase disaster preparedness in order to provide an effective response.
  • Recovery, rehabilitation and resilient reconstruction.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sudan National Forestry Policy Statement
DESCRIPTION: This document was prepared with the support of the Food and Agricultural Organisation support to update the Sudan's forestry policy. The Policy notably seeks to create a "greener Sudan", by countering deforestation and degradation of forest cover caused by illegal cutting, misuse and mismanagement of cutting permits, agricultural expansion, and demand for fuel energy. This goal is meant to reverse the trend of forest cover loss by facing and dealing with the deforestation, desertification and environmental degradation problems. The Sudan will in particular aim at identifying the detailed reasons of forest loss, formulate and implement programs supported by the mid and long term national development and investment plans.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree 211/015 - Energy Efficiency National Plan
DESCRIPTION:
Uruguay's growing economy has led to an increased demand for energy across all sectors. The challenge is to manage this growth in an environmentally sustainable, ethical way that also considers future generations.

To address this, Law No. 18.597, passed in 2009, establishes a framework for energy efficiency, promoting the reduction of energy use through various mechanisms. The National Energy Efficiency Plan, outlined in the law, includes a target to avoid 1,690 kTep of energy between 2015 and 2024. This goal focuses on optimizing energy use by combining general strategies with sector-specific actions, targeting consumers based on their usage patterns.

The plan emphasises the need to both increase energy supply responsibly and reduce energy demand efficiently through integrated policies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law of Georgia on Energy Efficiency
DESCRIPTION: This law aims to increase energy savings, security of supply, eliminate barriers to energy efficiency improvements in the energy market. It sets the legal framework on measures promoting and implementing energy efficiency to achieve the goals set out in the Protocol on the Accession of Georgia to the Treaty establishing the Energy Community. It also establishes 1) a procedure to develop a national energy efficiency target, 2) a procedure for adopting an energy efficiency action plan, 3) an energy efficiency commitment scheme, and 4) aims to implement an energy efficiency policy including MRV.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Zero Waste Masterplan 2019
DESCRIPTION: The Masterplan lays out Singapore's strategies to build climate, resource and economic resilience by moving away from the linear 'take-make-dispose model to a circular one that reuses resources endlessly. Climate resilience is explained as doing Singapore's part to mitigate climate change and protecting Singapore from its effects. In a resource- and carbon-constrained world, Singapore needs to adopt a circular economy approach, where scarce resources are valued and kept in use for as long as possible. By conserving resources, Singapore can also reduce greenhouse gas emissions from production and the incineration of waste, which will help to mitigate climate change.The Masterplan sets a target to reduce the amount of waste per capita sent to landfill by 30% by 2030, which is in addition to the existing target to achieve a 70% overall recycling rate by 2030. The strategies include reducing food waste; encouraging e-waste recycling among households; extending the mandatory waste reporting scheme; closing the waste loop with innovative solutions; exploring alternative uses for treated incineration bottom ash and waste treatment residues; turning waste into resources; and exploring the chemical recycling of plastic waste.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate and Nature Fund Bill
DESCRIPTION:
The creation of the Climate and Nature Fund is part of a strategic vision focused on the urgent need to conserve the environment and natural resources for the benefit of both current and future generations. This fund also presents an opportunity to strengthen Uruguay’s international commercial strategy and attract non-repayable investments and resources, based on the country’s progress in environmental sustainability in recent decades.

The fund will help channel potential benefits (such as lower interest rates or reduced capital) and co-benefits (such as donations) derived from sustainable debt instruments into concrete actions at the national level.

The Climate and Nature Fund will be used to finance actions that contribute to achieving the indicators outlined in sustainable sovereign financing instruments. The fund will be managed by the Executive Power, with the establishment of an Advisory Committee for the fund under the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The committee will be composed of representatives from the Ministry of Economy and Finance (which will also chair the committee), the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Industry, Energy, and Mining, the Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture, and Fisheries, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Environment Policy of Guinea
DESCRIPTION: This document notably 1) sets adaptation to climate change as a prominent goal, 2) promotes research in areas related to climate change, biological diversity and the fight against desertification, particularly in sectors related to agrofuels, non-wood forest products and forestry, and 3) promotes measures towards soil restoration and carbon sequestration.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Master Plan for 2021-2030, vision to 2050
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan, approved by Resolution No. 81/2023/QH by the National Assembly, sets out Vietnam's vision to develop as a prosperous country and to organise development effectively. The vision to 2050 is to be a developed, high-income country, with a modern socialist-oriented market economy, a fair, democratic and civilised society; and a digital society.

It contains actions to protect the environment and adapt to climate change, including adapting to rising sea levels through a modern infrastructure system and suitable urban architecture.

Actions include:

  • Improving the ability to forecast, warn and monitor climate change impacts and manage natural disaster risks to be equivalent to that of developed countries;
  • Reducing the impact of industrial development on climate change;
  • Proactively and activley participating in international agreements on climate change and taking advantage of the international support available for responding to climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 20,283 on Recuperation of Native Forest and Forestal Promotion
DESCRIPTION:
The Chilean Law of Recuperation of Native Forest and Forestal Promotion (Law 20.283) aims to promote the protection, recovery and improvement of native forests in order to promote forest sustainability.

DESCRIPTION: This ordinance creates the Center for Strategic Thinking on Climate Change ("Núcleo de Pensamento Estratégico em Mudança do Clima"). It aims to contribute to the reflection on climate change and long-term planning, supporting the Secretariat for Strategic Affairs in strategic planning and the integration of public policies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Transformation, Recovery and Resilience Plan (PTRR)
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan is the plan to rebuild and recover from the losses caused by storms, to prepare the country to face climate events and other extreme risks, and to improve emergency response capabilities and support for the community at these moments. 

This plan allocates an overall sum of 22.6 billion euros, between national public funding, (37%), private funding (34%), and European funds (19%). Measures include a mandatory home insurance scheme linked to a national natural catastrophe and earthquake fund, upgrades to the emergency communications system, direct mobile phone alerts, and investments in energy, water, cybersecurity, and emergency accommodation infrastructure. There will also be a A new Calamity Law to regulate support in instances of emergency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Power Industry, No 588-II
DESCRIPTION:
This legislation contains broad directives about managing the country's power resources, distribution of power and energy priorities. It establishes a list of priorities for future regulation and policy related to the power industry. Included in those priorities are the development of renewable energy sources and the rational and efficient use of current sources (thus reducing the amount of energy consumed). It also explains that regulation includes passing of technological standards to increase efficiency.

It grants the government the authority and obligation to develop and implement policy along the framework established in this law; thus facilitating the implementation of climate change policies without legislative debate and approval.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Saudi Green Initiative
DESCRIPTION:
SGI unites environmental protection, energy transition and sustainability programs with the overarching aims of offsetting and reducing emissions, increasing afforestation and land restoration, and protecting the Kingdom’s land and sea. Three overarching targets guide SGI’s work - emissions reduction, afforestation and land regeneration, and land and sea protection. SGI targets:

  1. To reduce carbon emissions by 278 mtpa by 2030 and net-zero in 2060.
  2. To grow 10 billion trees across Saudi Arabia
  3. To protect 30% of Saudi Arabia’s land and sea

DESCRIPTION: The Law of 31 July 2023 on product standards for integrating energy from renewable sources into fossil motor fuels for the transport sector establishes Belgium’s framework for increasing the use of renewable energy in transport fuels and aligning national rules with updated EU renewable energy and decarbonisation objectives. The law introduces product standards and obligations to ensure that suppliers progressively incorporate renewable energy and low-carbon fuels into fuels used in the transport sector, helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions from mobility. In addition, the law amends the

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ministry of Education Climate Change Action Plan 2022
DESCRIPTION:
The Climate Change Action Plan, published in 2022 by the Ministry of National Education, identifies climate change education as a critical area for emission reduction and climate crisis adaptation policies. The objectives of climate change education are stated as follows:

Climate change education has started to form its own identity at every level of education, from preschool to higher education. In this context, the fundamental task of climate change education is to train environmentally conscious individuals who understand the basic principles of the climate system, can evaluate scientifically reliable climate information, can minimize the effects of climate change, can make conscious decisions, and can contribute to the formation of sustainable communities by developing environmental attitudes and behaviours.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: A plan for jobs
DESCRIPTION: This document is the UK's policy response to the COVID-19-induced economic crisis. It outlines a number of stimulus measures, including a "green homes grant" scheme budgeted at 2 billion pounds aimed at enhancing energy efficiency, and a 1.1 billion pound plan to decarbonise the public sector and social housing. The Green Homes Grant scheme introduced as part of this policy response was discontinued in March 2021.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Specific Guidelines and Criteria for the Evaluation of the National Climate Change Policy (Lineamientos y Criterios Específicos para la Evaluación de la Política Nacional de Cambio Climático)
DESCRIPTION: The Guidelines and Specific Criteria for the Evaluation of the National Climate Change Policy set the framework for the systematic and periodic assessment of Mexico’s climate policy in accordance with the General Law on Climate Change. The process, led by the Evaluation Coordination (composed of the head of the National Institute of Ecology and Climate Change and six social advisers) aims to ensure that national mitigation and adaptation objectives are regularly reviewed, potentially leading to their modification, addition, or reorientation. The guidelines establish an obligatory procedure for federal agencies, state and municipal governments involved in the evaluation process, with assessments prioritised according to strategic relevance, resource allocation, feasibility, utility, and quality of available information.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law no 002/2014 on sustainable development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: 6th Five Year Plan (FY 2011-FY 2015)
DESCRIPTION:
The current Five Year Plan, produced by the Ministry of Planning, and focusing on ‘accelerating growth and reducing poverty' contains numerous policy initiatives that relate to climate change, including the following topics:

Energy:

- A target to increase energy efficiency by 10%

- Improve railways and waterways as energy efficient multi-modal transport system to reduce carbon emissions

- Optimising domestic production of primary energy resources including renewable energy

Environmental sustainability:

- Increase productive forest coverage by 2 percentage points

- 500 metre-wide permanent green belt established and protected along the coast

- Environmental, climate change and disaster risk reduction considerations are integrated into project design, budgetary allocations and implementation process

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
DESCRIPTION:
This Act, also known as the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, aims to modernise the United States' infrastructure and boost competitiveness. It specifically aims to upgrade roads, bridges and rails, expand access to clean drinking water, ensure universal access to high-speed internet, tackle the climate crisis, advance environmental justice, and invest in vulnerable communities.According to the White House, the following notable transport and energy climate-related actions are enable by this Act:

  • Invest $110 billion in additional funding to repair and rebuild roads, bridges and transformational projects with a focus on climate change mitigation, resilience, equity, and safety for all users. The legislation also includes the Safe Streets and Roads for All program to support projects to reduce traffic fatalities.
  • Improve transport options for all citizens while reducing greenhouse emissions. The document includes $39 billion of new investment into public transport, representing more than 24,000 buses, 5,000 rail cars, 200 stations, and thousands of miles of track, signals, and power systems in need of replacement. In total, the new investments and reauthorisation in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Deal provide $89.9 billion in guaranteed funding for public transit over the next five years.
  • Invest $66 billion in additional funding into passenger rail to eliminate the Amtrak maintenance backlog, modernize the Northeast Corridor, and bring world-class rail service to areas outside the northeast and mid-Atlantic. The Act also seeks to improve the infrastructure for freight rail.
  • Invest $7.5 billion to build a national network of electric vehicle chargers. The legislation will provide funding for deployment of EV chargers along highway corridors to facilitate long-distance travel and within communities to provide convenient charging where people live, work, and shop. This will support the President's goal to get a network of 500,000 EV chargers.
  • Invest $65 billion to upgrade the power infrastructure to deliver clean, reliable energy across the country and deploy cutting-edge energy technology to achieve a zero-emissions future. This should allow to fund new programs to support zero-carbon solutions, and to build resilient transmission lines to facilitate the expansion of renewables and clean energy, while lowering costs.

The Act further:

  • establishes new research agencies and initiatives within the Department of Transport with new funding schemes.
  • aims to improve the electricity grid's resilience and help mitigate potential risk to cause wildfire and to create stronger grid to adapt to other natural disasters including hurricanes. Grants will be given to states or tribes based on project proposals that align with policy goals.
  • seeks to make the country's infrastructure resilient against the impacts of climate change, cyber-attacks, and extreme weather events, by investing over $50 billion to protect against droughts, heat, floods and wildfires, in addition to a major investment in weatherisation.
  • reinstates the chemical excise taxes and invests resources in environmental remediation at Superfund sites to address the legacy pollution threatening local public health.
  • The Department of Energy established the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations after the passing of the law overseeing $20 Billion Federal Investment to Stand Up Clean Energy Projects.

As of March 2025, the status of this entry is likely impacted by the Trump-Vance administration’s regulatory rollback on climate action and ongoing litigation challenging the rollback. To learn more about the rollback, visit the Sabin Center’s Climate Backtracker.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Hydropower Development Policy
DESCRIPTION:
This Policy revised the original policy document of 1992. The objectives of hydropower development are to generate electricity at low cost and provide reliable and qualitative electric service for both own country and exportable commodity. Connecting electrification with economic activities and extend rural electrification are also the goals of this Policy.

The strategies to accomplish these objectives include extension of hydropower services to the rural economy, implementation of small, medium, large and storage projects for hydropower development, attracting investment from both private and governmental sectors (as necessary through public-private joint ventures) and minimising the potential risks in hydropower projects with a joint effort of government and private sector. Key implementation policies for these include development of electric systems for domestic use and storage projects, provision of appropriate incentives and transparent processes, contribution to environmental protection by developing hydropower as an alternative to biomass and thermal energy, restructuring institutions in the public sector to create a competitive environment and fixing electricity tariffs in rational and transparent manner.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electricity Act 2010
DESCRIPTION: This Act provides for a new legislative framework for regulating the electricity sector, the establishment of the post of the Electricity Regulator and the Office of the Regulator. PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Agricultural and Rural Development (NSARD/SNDAR) for the years 2023-2030

This should notably be done by increasing the use of renewable energy resources in the sector, and by reducing the vulnerability of crop productions to climate change.

Moldova's NSARD for 2023-2030 also emphasises the importance of climate change adaptation and mitigation, with measures for capacity building, impact/vulnerability reporting systems and technological modernisation in the agricultural sector.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Targets (Alineación de la Estrategia Nacional sobre Biodiversidad de México y Plan de Acción 2030 con las Metas del Marco Mundial de Biodiversidad de Kunming-Montreal)
DESCRIPTION: Mexico began aligning its National Biodiversity Strategy (ENBioMex) with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework through a national process led by CONABIO. As a result, the Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy (ENBioMex) and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Targets recognises climate change as a critical driver of biodiversity loss, embedding it explicitly in Target 8, which calls for minimising climate and ocean acidification impacts on biodiversity through mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction. PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage Act 2025
DESCRIPTION:
Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage Act 2025 (the "CCUS Act") applies to Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territory of Labuan only, and does not extend to the East Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak. The CCUS Act permits the transportation or importing for permanent storage at designated offshore or onshore sites in Malaysia of carbon dioxide captured both within and outside of Malaysia. At each stage of the CCUS value chain (capture, transport/import, storage assessment, and permanent storage), compliance is required with prescribed technical and environmental standards, and relevant certificates and permits from the CCUS Agency must be obtained.

The CCUS Agency supports implementation of the CCUS Act 2025, overseeing, regulating, and promoting CCUS activities across the value chain, issuing permits, managing resources and funding mechanisms, advising the government, and ensuring compliance with the CCUS Act 2025.

A Post-Closure Stewardship Fund has been established to cover post-closure monitoring and remediation costs of the carbon dioxide storage sites and is financed through government allocations, injection levies collected from offshore storage operators, and earnings from investments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Germany's Roadmap for Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels
DESCRIPTION:
This Roadmap outlines Germany's commitment to transition away from fossil fuels no later than 2045. It was developed in the context of the Paris Agreement, Decision 1/CMA.5 of the first Global Stocktake, which calls for a just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems to reach net zero by 2050, and European Union commitments, including the binding 90% emissions reduction target for 2040 under the European Climate Law. It is anchored in the Federal Climate Action Act, which sets legally binding reductions of at least 65% by 2030 and 88% by 2040 and net greenhouse gas neutrality by 2045, and in the 2026 Climate Action Programme, whose 67 measures underpin the sectoral strategies. These cover energy, transport, buildings and industry, supported by carbon pricing, research and innovation, social measures and international cooperation.

The Roadmap sets out how Germany will reduce its dependence on imported fossil fuels through the rapid expansion of renewables (at least 80% of electricity by 2030), electrification, and the use of climate-neutral fuels where direct electrification is not yet viable. It confirms the legal phase-out of coal-fired power generation by 2038, with 2035 under consideration. It also provides for hydrogen-ready gas plants operating climate-neutrally by 2045, a switch to climate-neutral heating fuels from 2045, and EU emissions trading covering about 85% of national emissions. Internationally, Germany supports the transition through the Powering Past Coal Alliance, Just Energy Transition Partnerships, bilateral energy partnerships and €11.8 billion in climate finance in 2024. The Roadmap does not set separate end dates for oil and gas, and it recognises that fossil fuels will remain in use during a transitional period

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Decree No. 19-280 establishing the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Commission (20 October 2019)
DESCRIPTION:
The Executive Decree No. 19-280 of 21 Safar 1441, corresponding to 20 October 2019, establishes the creation, organisation, and operation of the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Commission. This Commission reports to the Prime Minister and is develops renewable energy and energy efficiency measures, to provide energy security in economic development, environmental preservation, and the fight against climate change.

The Commission is also responsible for ensuring, in liaison with the reelvant secotrs, the implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Algeria's commitments under international conventions and agreements in the areas of combatting the effects of climate change and achieving sustainable development goals.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Third National Adaptation Programme (NAP3) and the Fourth Strategy for Climate Adaptation Reporting
DESCRIPTION: This Programme consolidates policies and actions to address the climate change risks and opportunities identified in the third Climate Change Risk Assessment (CCRA3), as section 58 of the Climate Change Act 2008 requires. This programme covers England and non-devolved functions across the UK. It emphasises climate action in key areas, such as: infrastructure; natural environment; health, communities and built environment; business and industry; international impacts; adaptation reporting power and supporting evidence. The programme is organised around the themes of "action", "information", and "coordination" to provide for a comprehensive approach to adapt to climate change by ensuring that government actions are more targeted, informed, and well-coordinated over the five-year NAP period.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Amendment of the Energy Conservation and Production Act (2011)
DESCRIPTION: Section 305 of the Energy Conservation and Production Act (ECPA), as amended, brought modifications to the Building Energy Codes. ECPA requires to establish building energy efficiency standards for all new Federal buildings (42 U.S.C. 6834(a)(1)). The established standards must contain: (i)energy savings, (ii) efficient use of water, energy, and (iii) use renewable energy sources. The aim is to meet or exceed the energy savings and renewable energy specifications of the referenced voluntary consensus energy codes. (42 U.S.C. 6834(a)(1)-(3)). Another provision is that the Federal building energy efficiency performance standards for new Federal buildings must require that such buildings be designed to achieve energy consumption levels that are at least 30 percent below the levels established in the referenced codes, if life-cycle cost-effective.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Food Strategy 2040: A land of happy food
DESCRIPTION: Finland's National Food Strategy 2040 sets a long-term vision for Finland to become a global leader in sustainable food systems, developed through extensive stakeholder consultation (600+ participants) in response to climate change, geopolitical instability, and biodiversity loss. It is built around four strategic goals: profitability and fairness (raising value-added, fairer income distribution, tripling export value by 2040), security of supply (resilience in critical inputs like nutrients, energy, seeds, and protein feed), nature's carrying capacity (emissions reductions toward carbon neutrality, including peat field emissions, biodiversity restoration, and reduced nutrient runoff), and food culture and wellbeing (healthier diets, food education, sustainable public procurement). Implementation happens through rolling four-year action plans, supported by five cross-cutting capabilities: innovation/technology, skills development, investment capacity, cross-sector cooperation, and a shift toward more enabling public administration — aiming to balance economic competitiveness, ecological limits, and public health by 2040.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree n° 2022-1085 regarding ways of aiding the acquisition or rental of low-polluting vehicles
DESCRIPTION: This Decree modifies the eligibility threshold for the "ecological bonus" (a purchase grant) for plug-in hybrid vehicles stipulated in the Energy Code (articles D. 251-1, D. 251-7 and D. 251-8).  It also introduces a transitional period during which heavy vehicles ordered up until December 31, 2022 (or invoiced up until June 30, 2023) will be able to benefit from the ecological bonus.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Opinions on Accelerating Comprehensive Green Transformation of Economic and Social Development
DESCRIPTION:
The Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Accelerating Comprehensive Green Transformation of Economic and Social Development was issued in July 2024. The opinions include the following:

  • Promote the green transformation in the urban and rural areas, including the construction of climate-adapted cities and enhance the climate resilience of urban and rural areas;
  • Participate in leading the global green transformation process, including actively participating in the formulation of international rules in dealing with climate change, marine pollution control, biodiversity protection, plastic pollution control and other fields, and promoting the construction of a fair, reasonable and win-win global environmental climate governance system; and
  • Study and formulate special laws to deal with climate change and carbon peaking.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sectoral Planning Guidelines for Climate Change Adaptation
DESCRIPTION:
To support these key national sectors in planning for climate change adaptation and achieving resilience by 2050, sectoral adaptation guidelines published by the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications (DECC) in 2018 have been updated to account for national adaptation progress and to reflect the evolving landscape of international policy and best practice. These guidelines aim to ensure that a coherent and consistent approach to adaptation planning is adopted at national and sectoral levels. The new guidelines draw on the most up-to-date national approaches to change risk assessment (such as the National Climate Change Risk Assessment (NCCRA)) and sources of climate and adaptation information (such as the Irish Climate Change Assessment Report (ICCA), the National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS), and Climate Ireland).

Sectors preparing sectoral adaptation plans under the NAF are required to prepare their plans in line with the process described within these guidelines, while also being aware of the overall requirements regarding the development of sectoral adaptation plans in Sections 5 and 6 of the Climate Action and Low Carbon Development Acts 2015 to 2021 (Climate Act) and the NAF (particularly Chapters 2 and 3). In addition, when preparing sectoral adaptation plans, sectors should consult and take account of the recommendations of the NCCRA Technical Guidance for Sectoral Risk Assessments (EPA, 2024c), and the national and sectoral priorities and targets (such as those related to emissions reductions). The Technical Guidance will ensure that all sectors plan for common and well-accepted climate scenarios, as well as a common understanding of the future climate.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 2/2011, of March 4, of Sustainable Economics
DESCRIPTION:
This Law aims to make the economy more competitive by promoting environmental sustainability in sectors such as energy, transport and sustainable mobility, and housing.

The Law has four sections. The first is dedicated to improving the economic environment. The second addresses competitiveness and the third, environmental sustainability. The fourth deals with how to implement and evaluate the Law.

The major principles of environmental sustainability are the guarantee of economic efficiency, respect for the environment, national objectives for 2020 on energy saving and efficiency and on the use of renewable energy. Energy policy should promote renewable energy, strengthen predictability and efficiency in energy policy decisions - especially as regards the incentives framework - and cut back the contribution of energies with higher CO2 emission potential.

The law establishes a national target of 20% of energy consumption to come from renewable energy by 2020 for both homes and commercial buildings.

It also creates the Carbon Fund for a Sustainable Economy (FES - CO2), which will help to reduce GHG emissions by buying carbon credits.

The purpose Royal Decree 1.007/2015 is to regulate the specific procedure for the acquisition of carbon credits, within the framework of the PIMA Company Plan, to companies that carry out actions that meet the requirements established in this standard, by the Carbon Fund to a Sustainable Economy (FES-CO2) provided for in the Sustainable Economy Law 2/2011.

Lithuanian Agriculture and Rural Development 2023-2027 strategic plan
DESCRIPTION: The Agriculture and Rural Development 2023-2027 strategic plan aims to achieve stable development of Lithuania's food production and rural land, guiding the deployment of domestic policy and EU funding, and names contributing to climate goals among its main priorities. Climate adaptation measures in the plan emphasise the importance of widespread efficiency improvements to irrigation systems. The plan also contains significant measures for forest restoration; reconfiguration of crop systems to reverse declines in agricultural soil carbon storage across Lithuania; biogas installation and development; and funding for research, innovation and more general capacity-building.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2023-053 establishing Ecuador's greenhouse gas emissions compensation scheme
DESCRIPTION:
Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2023-053 aims to establish and issue the scheme, guidelines, and technical criteria for the compensation of greenhouse gas emissions in Ecuador. This technical standard applies to voluntary mitigation initiatives for the reduction and/or removal of greenhouse gas emissions, whether public, private, community-based, or mixed, developed within the national territory, to be used as compensation for greenhouse gas emissions by national or foreign proponents.

The National Environmental Authority [Autoridad Ambiental Nacional (AAN)] will gradually enable the following compensation mechanisms:

  • Compensation without transferring greenhouse gas emissions to another nationally determined contributions (NDC) or transferring ownership of Equivalent Carbon Units [Unidades de Carbono Equivalentes (UCE)] to a proponent. This pathway rewards initiatives in the land-use, land-use change, and forestry (LULUCF) sector, and all mitigation sectors within the compensation portfolio that generate verified emissions reductions or removals.
  • Compensation without transferring greenhouse gas emissions to another NDC, with the transfer of ownership of UCE to a proponent. Applicable to the energy, agriculture, waste, and industrial processes sectors meeting AAN-approved certification standards.
  • Compensation with the transfer of greenhouse gas emissions to another NDC, with or without the transfer of ownership of a UCE to a proponent. This mechanism will be defined by the AAN considering national capacity development and the provisions established in the Article 6 rulebook of the Paris Agreement.

Mitigation activities falling under the following categories may enter the compensation portfolio:

  • LULUCF sector
  • Other mitigation sectors (Energy, Waste, Industrial Processes, Agriculture)

Further Considerations

  • Compensation will be carried out by a proponent who has previously made efforts to decarbonise their processes.
  • The AAN will approve GHG certification programs to be used, defining the evaluation methodology.
  • The National Compensation Registry will maintain traceability of mitigation initiatives and UCE generated, registered, and rewarded under the scheme.
  • For initiatives in the LULUCF sector, the AAN will retain 10% of the UCE from each mitigation initiative for the UCE Reserve Account.
  • Conformity assessment bodies, those responsible of the validation and verification processes, must be accredited, registered, designated, or recognised by the competent authority.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012 (S.I. 1976 of 2012)
DESCRIPTION:
The Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012 (S.I. 2012/1976) govern the administrative framework and enforcement rules for the UK Climate Change Agreement (CCA) scheme. The regulations designate the Environment Agency as the scheme administrator and establish provisions for setting up umbrella and underlying agreements, maintaining the official CCA electronic register and monitoring progress against target periods.

Over time, the regulations have been amended to extend scheme target periods, update financial buyout fees, and adjust reporting rules:

  • S.I. 2020/958: Established Target Period 5 (2021–2022), increased the buy-out fee price per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent, and reopened the scheme to new applicants.
  • S.I. 2023/1226: Introduced Target Period 6 (2024), adjusted target reporting deadlines, and updated buy-out fee rates for underlying agreement non-compliance.
  • S.I. 2025/813: Extended the CCA scheme by establishing Target Periods 7, 8, and 9 (spanning 2026 through 2030) to underpin the operation of the long-term Climate Change Agreement scheme.
  • S.I. 2026/826: Adjusts administrative procedures, fee calculation factors, and operational rules for governing those facilities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Integrated Coastal Zone Management of Montenegro 2015–2030
DESCRIPTION:
This Strategy develops the vision of the coastal area as resilient, healthy, attractive, diverse, productive and recognisably unique. This vision is to be realised through: more efficient protection of nature and landscapes; significant improvements in the efficacy in the management of protected natural assets, ecologically valuable habitats, and coastal zone ecosystems; improvements to the environmental status of marine ecosystems; improvements to the spatial planning system; remediation of pollution due to the inadequate disposal and treatment of solid waste; stimulation of green mobility and development of green infrastructure; and protection and improvement of coastal area resources.

Measures include mitigation of climate change impacts (e.g. through afforestation and reduced use of carbon intensive materials and fuels, using various biomaterials that absorb carbon dioxide, expanding municipal green areas as to mitigate effects of micro-climate events in urban areas, particularly those resulting from the impacts of heat waves); adjustment of the existing infrastructure to be able to bear burdens shown by the latest data on climate extremes and storm waves; and development of an approach for climate change risk analyses (e.g. coast vulnerability index). The targets include Projects on mitigating the impacts of coastal erosion, seismic hazard, climate change, and meteorological hazards that are implemented in the coastal zone municipalities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Prevention and Reduction (SNPRRC) of the Republic of Congo
DESCRIPTION: This strategy aims to address the current situation and optimize the implementation of disaster risk management in the Republic of Congo. The strategy constitutes the main instrument for implementing the country's vision and priorities for disaster risk management within the framework of a comprehensive and comprehensive approach, covering all its components, which are simultaneously objectives, modalities, and components or phases of disaster risk management. This document contains seven strategic areas of intervention, comprising several fields of intervention, namely: Promoting the effectiveness of disaster risk management at the decentralized and local community levels (populations). Building institutional (technical and material) capacities at all levels and among the public for disaster risk management. Strengthening national coordination of disaster risk management and its key mechanisms. Optimizing preparedness and strengthening disaster response capacity at all levels. Strengthening risk assessment and monitoring, as well as early warning and risk information systems, at the national level. Optimizing the implementation and practice of risk prevention and reduction of all origins, at all levels. Strengthening regional, subregional, and international cooperation. For each area, this policy discloses expected results and key performance indicators. In addition, the document contains an implementation and monitoring framework.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Royal Decree 525/2014, on the subsidization of the Incentives Programme for Efficient Vehicles (PIVE-6)
DESCRIPTION:
The Decree considers that renewing the transport fleet is one of the most efficient ways to reduce energy consumption, as well as improve road safety and the general environment. The Decree extends the PIVE programme, with the aim of replacing 450,000 old vehicles.

In its sixth edition, the government decided to provide EUR175m (USD216m) to continue the Programme. This Decree introduces an obligation on car dealers or outlets within the Programme to inform beneficiaries about efficient driving when they sell new vehicles.
KEYWORDS: Energy Demand;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Commission (Energy Efficiency Standards and Labelling) (Clothes Washing Machines) Regulations, 2022
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of these Regulations is to promote the efficient use and conservation of energy in Ghana and mitigate climate change by providing for the minimum energy performance standards, the labelling of and supplementary product information on electric mains-operated clothes washing machines, and the registration of models of such machines. The manufacture, importation, offer for sale, sale, storage, donation, disposable or installation or use of a clothes washing machine that does not meet the stipulated minimum energy performance standards.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Consumer Energy Resources (CER) Roadmap
DESCRIPTION: In July 2024, the Energy and Climate Change Ministerial Council (ECMC) endorsed the National Consumer Energy Resources Roadmap (CER Roadmap) which sets out an overarching vision and Implementation Plan to unlock the benefits of CER for all Australians and the electricity system. The National CER Roadmap aims for a consistent approach across Australia while ensuring fair access to Consumer Energy Resources (CER) and stronger protections for consumers.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 94-20 on Environmental Education and Communication
DESCRIPTION:
This law aims to include environmental education into all levels of the country's schooling and academic system.

Its stated goals are, amongst others, to build skills and values ​​that lead to sustainable development, based on equity, social justice and respect for biological diversity; promote the implementation of policies and measures for adaptation to climate change and the management of climate risks; and foster the development of an environmental awareness. The law also proposes to encourage the extension of practices and sustainable ways of life in the different territorial contexts of the Dominican Republic, based on the rational and supportive use of resources, as well as on the respectful enjoyment of the environment. It also proposes the development of an environmental education and communication programme (that includes risk management elements) to develop a culture of resilience aimed at minimizing the effects of climate change-related natural disasters. This would lead to a decrease in adverse effects of these threats and prepare appropriate and immediate responses. The law proposes to encourage the mass media to acquire specialized, appropriate technical knowledge related to environmental conservation, in order to adequately disseminate it to the population; and to develop an ethical awareness towards environmental values through environmental education.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Kyrgyzstan National Communication. NC1
DESCRIPTION: Kyrgyzstan National Communication. NC1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree 9.172/2017 (National Emissions Registration System - Sirene)
DESCRIPTION:
Establishes the National Emissions Registration System - Sirene, provides for the instruments of the National Policy on Climate Change referred to in item XIII of the caput of art. 6 of Law No. 12,187, of December 29, 2009, and amends Decree No. 7,390, of December 9, 2010, which regulates said Policy.

Related to this, normative instruction 12/2010 stipulates in art 2 that the IBAMA Licensing Board evaluates, in the process of licensing activities capable of emitting greenhouse gases, the measures proposed by the entrepreneur with the objective of mitigating these environmental impacts, in compliance with the commitments assumed by Brazil in the Convention- United Nations Framework on Climate Change. Art 3 states that the Terms of Reference, prepared by IBAMA, to guide the Environmental Impact Studies for the licensing of projects capable of emitting greenhouse gases, include measures to mitigate or compensate for these environmental impacts in line with the National Plan on Climate Change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Department of Justice Climate Action Plan
DESCRIPTION:
The Department of Justice Climate Action Plan was published according to Executive Order 14008 and contains a number of provisions for improving adaptation and increasing resilience to climate change.

As of March 2025, the status of this entry is likely impacted by the Trump-Vance administration’s regulatory rollback on climate action. To learn more about the rollback, visit the Sabin Center’s Climate Backtracker.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
DESCRIPTION: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority published the Hong one Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to set out guidance on green and sustainable finance and to facilitate financial flows towards green activities, with the objective of contributing to global efforts to combat climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Policy for Sustainable Urban Mobility of Ecuador (PNMUS) 2023–2030
DESCRIPTION: The National Policy for Sustainable Urban Mobility (PNMUS) 2023–2030 provides a strategic framework to address the environmental, economic, and social challenges of current mobility systems in Ecuador. Guided by the Constitution, the Organic Law on Land Transport, Traffic, and Road Safety, and international commitments such as the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the policy aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve accessibility, and promote sustainable urban planning.On climate change, the plan incorporates three climate-focused approaches to enhance urban resilience and reduce environmental impacts: (1) promoting sustainable and efficient mobility modes, such as public transport and active transportation, to reduce private vehicle reliance; (2) developing resilient infrastructure to adapt to climate change, including climate-proof urban spaces and facilities; and (3) mitigating the effects of urban heat waves through nature-based solutions, such as green streets, shaded spaces, and microclimates. These approaches align with the policy's broader goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and fostering climate-resilient cities.The PNMUS serves as a comprehensive guide for local governments, supporting the implementation of Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (PMUS) and providing technical and financial resources for cities to transition toward low-carbon and inclusive mobility systems.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Submission by IDDRI on behalf of the Adaptation Without Borders global partnership, relating to the 3rd Technical Dialogue of the UNFCCC Global Stocktake - Accounting for transboundary climate risks in the Global Stocktake to drive regional and global cooperation on adaptation
DESCRIPTION: Submission by IDDRI on behalf of the Adaptation Without Borders global partnership, relating to the 3rd Technical Dialogue of the UNFCCC Global Stocktake - Accounting for transboundary climate risks in the Global Stocktake to drive regional and global cooperation on adaptation, Submission to the Global Stocktake from Institute for Sustainable Development and International Relations (IDDRI), External organization authors in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: System Development Strategy 2024
DESCRIPTION: The System Development Strategy 2024 (Systementwicklungsstrategie, SES 2024) provides Germany's first integrated, cross-sectoral framework for planning the transition to a climate-neutral energy system by 2045. Published by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK), the strategy coordinates the long-term development of the electricity, hydrogen, natural gas, and heat sectors to ensure a coherent and cost-efficient transformation. It identifies the large-scale expansion of renewable energy, widespread electrification of transport, buildings, and industry, the establishment of a nationwide hydrogen infrastructure, and increased system flexibility through energy storage, demand-side management, and sector coupling as the key pillars of the future energy system. The SES also emphasizes integrated infrastructure planning, European energy market integration, and the coordinated development of transmission, distribution, and hydrogen networks. As an adaptive planning framework, the strategy serves as the basis for future network development plans and will be periodically updated to reflect technological, economic, and policy developments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Greening Finance: A Roadmap to Sustainable Investing
DESCRIPTION: This document details Sustainability Disclosure Requirements to help businesses prepare for what they will have to report and by when (chapter 1), details the UK Green Taxonomy (chapter 2),  Highlight the importance of investor stewardship in green finance and set out the government’s expectations (chapter 3), and reiterates the UK's commitment to international leadership on green finance.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National climate change adaptation plan
DESCRIPTION: The National Plan for Climate Change Adaptation's objectives are to increase knowledge of the potential risks and opportunities associated with climate change and climate variability, to incorporate climate risk management in territorial and sectoral planning and to mitigate the climate change vulnerability of ecological and socio-economic systems. It promotes a planned, territorial environmental development compatible to Climate Change variability through sort, medium and long term actions.  This Plan seeks the mainstreaming of climate variables and projections into environmental, territorial and sectoral planning, effectively decreasing the vulnerability of populations, ecosystems and productive sectors, and increasing the social, economic and ecosystems capacities to answer to climate events. The plan needs to be an instrument to establish strategic guidelines and bring effective tools to prioritise adaptations measures, as well as to guide sectors and territories in the development of strategies and adaptation plans to reduce their vulnerability and associated risks.  The implementation of the plan is divided into four phases. Beginning in 2012, the first two stages were conceptual and methodological, followed by the detailing of specific sectoral and regional plans. Phase four, implementation of measures, began in 2013, while monitoring and reporting, the final phase, began in 2014.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Towards a climate-resilient society in 2050 - Federal adaptation measures 2023-2026
DESCRIPTION:
This adaptation report contains a set of federal adaptation measures, aimed at limiting the negative impacts of climate change as much as possible. It discusses the possible climate scenarios for Belgium and the future impacts of climate change. The document includes 28 federal adaptation measures, divided into 8 domains for action 

  1. Research 
  2. Biodiversity 
  3. Infrastructure 
  4. Natural resources 
  5. Public health 
  6. Disaster and crisis management 
  7. International cooperation 
  8. Awareness
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Biodiversity;Climate Change Risks;Disaster Risk Management;Health;Infrastructure;Natural Resources;Research And Development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Environmental Policy Guidelines for 2021-2027
DESCRIPTION:
The Environmental Policy Guidelines for 2021-2027 (EPGs 2027), adopted by the Cabinet Order 583/2022, are a medium-term policy planning document for the environmental sector.

They have been developed in accordance with the priorities set out in the Latvia 2030, Latvian NDP for 2021-2027 and the strategic objectives of the European Green Course and provide for:

  • achieving the 2030 greenhouse gas reduction target and achieve climate neutrality by 2050;
  • improving adaptability, strengthening resilience and reducing vulnerability to climate change;
  • making progress towards a renewable growth model by decoupling economic growth from resource use and environmental depletion and acceleration of the transition to a circular economy;
  • aiming for zero pollution in the environment free of toxic substances, including air, water and soil, and thus also protecting the health and well-being of Europeans;
  • protecting, preserving and restoring biodiversity and increasing natural capital, in particular air, water, soil, and forest, freshwater, wetland and marine ecosystems; and
  • promoting environmental sustainability and reducing environmental and climate pressures related to production and consumption, in the fields of energy, industrial development, buildings and infrastructure, mobility and food systems.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: A UK government food strategy for England, considering the wider UK food system
DESCRIPTION: The UK government's food strategy for England (Defra) argues that the current food system is harming health, the environment and resilience, through a "junk food cycle" driving obesity, environmental costs that markets ignore, and growing exposure to climate and geopolitical shocks. On climate and nature, it notes that the food system (including imports) accounts for about 38% of UK greenhouse gas emissions, with agriculture alone at 11.7%, and that farming and fisheries are leading drivers of biodiversity loss, with around 40% of inland water bodies affected by agricultural and rural pollution. It describes a "vicious cycle" in which farming contributes to climate change, which in turn threatens food supply, and argues that unpriced environmental damage gives harmful practices a competitive edge. Its vision is a healthier, more affordable, sustainable and resilient system that also supports economic growth. It is a high-level framework rather than a detailed delivery plan.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 298/2006  (Finance Law 2007)
DESCRIPTION: This law provides for various fiscal incentives and financial measures to improve energy efficiency and to abate emissions.It also established an obligation for all traditional fuel producers to supply, each year, a minimum quota of biofuels determined as a percentage of the previous year's total supply volume. The initial quota was 1% for 2007; subsequently it was increased to 2% for 2008 and 3% for 2009. Non-compliance with the quota is subject to penalties. The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry is responsible for verifying the fulfilment of this obligation.The Law introduced tax allowances for purchase or installation of high-efficiency electric motors and for high-efficiency fridges and freezers. It also promotes the reduction of duty for biofuels used for transportation and fiscal incentives for enhancing energy efficiency and use of renewable energy in buildings.The Law also established the Revolving fund for Kyoto: it provides EUR 200 million (USD 272 million) for financing measures to promote GHG emission reductions for 2010-2012 and to achieve the targets. It finances, for instance, a high-performance micro-cogeneration plant.
KEYWORDS: Carbon Pricing;Energy Demand;Energy Supply;Fossil Fuels;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;REDD+ And LULUCF;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree 19 February 2007 on new Feed-In premium for photovoltaic systems
DESCRIPTION: This decree establishes the criteria and procedures for incentivizing the production of electricity from solar photovoltaic systems, in implementation of Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 387 of December 29, 2003 . It introduced a new version of the feed-in premium scheme applied to photovoltaic plants connected to the grid by individuals, registered companies, condominiums and public bodies, with a nominal capacity higher than 1 kWp (output power achieved by a Solar module under full solar radiation).The decree provides a set of tariffs, valid for a period of 20 years, with a bonus in cases of a high degree of photovoltaic integration in the buildings.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No.08/L-072 on Agriculture and Rural Development
DESCRIPTION: This law regulates the drafting and implementation of national policies for agriculture and rural development. It seeks to create a competitive agricultural and agri-food sector that contributes to food security and to establish a sustainable food supply. It aims to address climate challenges by protecting natural and environmental resources against negative effects of agricultural production, as well as to ensure improved quality of life and increased employment opportunities in the sector.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Thailand Power Development Plan (PDP) 2018-2037
DESCRIPTION:
The PDP 2015 was revised, and the Thailand Power Development Plan 2018-2037 (PDP 2018) was passed. Key highlights include:

  1. The power generation system, power transmission system and power distribution system are stable by area to create a balance. Electrical systems by region;
  2. Appropriate level of security of the power plants and increasing flexibility of the electrical system (Grid Flexibility);
  3. Promote low-cost electricity generation;
  4. Prepare the electrical system to enable competition in power generation, and thus, increase efficiency of electricity production;
  5. Reduce environmental impact;
  6. Promote the production of electricity from renewable energy and increase the efficiency of the electrical system, both in terms of electricity generation and electricity consumption.
  7. Develop a smart grid power network system (Smartgrid) to support the changing trend of electricity users like Prosumer.

In addition, the PDP2018 places emphasis on Stakeholder participation by creating participation of the public sector.

Due to an increase in the proportion of electricity generation using natural gas instead of coal, carbon dioxide emissions will be lower than in PDP 2015.

  • Amount of carbon dioxide emission per unit (kgCO2/kWh): 2022 - 0.368; 2027 - 0.339; 2030 - 0.326; 2032 - 0.291; and 2037 - 0.283;
  • Amount of carbon dioxide emission per annum (thousand tons of CO2): 2022 - 88,947; 2027 - 94,007; 2030 - 98,743; 2032 - 93,357; and 2037 - 103,845.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act 587/2011, last amended by Act 827/2025 (Water Act)
DESCRIPTION: The Water Act (587/2011) provides the main legal framework for the sustainable use, management and protection of Finland’s water resources and aquatic environment. Its objectives include promoting socially, economically and ecologically sustainable use of water resources, preventing and reducing harm caused by water use, and improving the condition of water resources and the aquatic environment. The Act regulates water resources management projects and permitting, including activities affecting water bodies, groundwater, water levels and flows, hydropower, water abstraction and structures in waterways.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Natura 2000 Management Programme for the 2023-2028
DESCRIPTION:
The Natura 2000 Management Programme (PUN) for the 2023–2028 period is prepared in accordance with the Decree on Natura 2000 areas and covers both Special Protection Areas (SPA) for birds and Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) for habitats.The programme consists:

  • Detailed Conservation Objectives: Specific targets for zones, species, and habitat types to be maintained in a favorable state.
  • Management Measures: A diverse toolkit including direct nature conservation, adapted use of natural resources, adjusted agricultural practices (farming), and water management.
  • Monitoring and Indicators: Specific metrics to track the effectiveness of measures, including deadlines and funding sources.
  • Ecological Connectivity: Activities to ensure the European ecological network remains linked.
  • Research: Basic and applied science to improve the understanding of species ecology.

It also brings specialized Annexes to facilitate implementation across different sectors. The management programme is important also in the climate perspective due to future trends in emissions and removals in the sector will also be shaped by the restoration or enhancement of carbon-rich natural ecosystems. This includes the restoration of ecosystems such as peatlands, wetlands, shrublands, grasslands, and forest habitat types. The measure is aligned with the Natura 2000 Management Programme for the 2023-2028 period.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Energy Efficiency No. 139/2018
DESCRIPTION: This law implements the EU Directive 2012/27/EU in Moldova. It creates the legal framework for regulation of energy efficiency in both energy supply and use.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Government Decree on Flood Risk Management (659/2010)
DESCRIPTION:
Government Decree on Flood Risk Management (659/2010) provides detailed rules for implementing the Flood Risk Management Act (620/2010). It specifies the requirements and procedures for the preliminary assessment of flood risks, including the identification of areas where significant flood risks may occur, and sets requirements for the preparation and content of flood hazard and flood risk maps. It also establishes more detailed requirements for flood risk management plans, including their objectives, measures, monitoring and coordination with river basin management planning.

All in all the Decree provides the detailed regulatory framework needed to implement the Flood Risk Management Act.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Presidential Decree No. 46/14 approving the National Action Programme to fight Desertification
DESCRIPTION: This Presidential Decree, consisting of 4 articles and 1 Annex, approves the National Action Programme against Desertification (PANCOD). The Program is included in the Annex and consists of 11 sections, providing a broad introduction and background of the desertification issues, objectives and principles of the Program and its main lines of action. It is in line with the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), which was ratified by Angola in 1997.The program aims to be a social participatory process, including different stakeholders in the definition of objectives and actions, to deepen the knowledge of desertification processes and droughts in order to develop guidelines and strategies for their prevention and control. It presents three main lines of action: 1) Reduction of poverty and social inequality; 2) Increasing productivity of dry areas vulnerable to desertification through conservation and preservation of natural resources; 3) Institutional capacity building.
