DESCRIPTION: Togo. Biennial update report (BUR). BUR 2., Biennial Update Report from Togo in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on National Committee to Reduce Destructive Impacts of Natural Disasters
DESCRIPTION: This law requires the National Committee to Reduce Destructive Impacts of Natural Disasters to conduct research on and manage information about disasters. It requires the Minister of the Interior to establish local equivalents and report on research results every six months.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ethiopia Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1
DESCRIPTION: Ethiopia Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Consumer Energy Resources Roadmap
DESCRIPTION: This Roadmap sets out the vision to provide secure, affordable and sustainable future electricity systems, delivering benefits and equitable outcomes to all consumers through efficient use which smooths the transition, rewards participation and lower emissions. It contains four workstreams relating to consumers, technology, markets and power system operations. An in-depth review of the Roadmap will occur in 2027.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Biological Diversity to 2050 (Estrategia Nacional de Diversidad Biológica al 2050)
DESCRIPTION: Peru’s National Strategy for Biological Diversity to 2050 establishes a long-term framework to address biodiversity loss through integrated, participatory governance aligned with climate resilience and sustainable development. Central to the strategy are five strategic objectives targeting land-use change, climate impacts, pollution, invasive species, and institutional weaknesses. These objectives operationalise principles such as the precautionary principle (Rio Declaration, Principle 15), intercultural equity, and human rights-based approaches, ensuring alignment with international obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Paris Agreement. The strategy mandates ecosystem-based adaptation, including restoring 10% of degraded ecosystems and species affected by climate change, while integrating traditional ecological knowledge to strengthen adaptive capacity. The strategy’s implementation relies on institutional reforms, such as strengthening multi-level governance and integrating biodiversity metrics (e.g., the Lista Roja de Ecosistemas) into national reporting frameworks, including the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. It addresses climate-biodiversity linkages by prioritising mitigation of climate-driven threats (e.g., deforestation, water pollution) and promoting nature-based solutions, such as community-led water harvesting projects. The "Enfoque Territorial" (territorial approach) ensures localised, context-specific actions, while the Enfoque "Una Salud" (One Health) links ecosystem health to human and animal well-being.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Pact with the Municipalities
DESCRIPTION:
The Climate Pact with the Municipalities consists of a 2012 law, amended on March 29th, 2016, that aims at encouraging greenhouse gases emissions mitigation at the municipality level. The law authorises the State to subsidy, from 2013 to 2020, the municipalities committed via the signature of a Climate Pact to apply a mitigation programme. Such a programme must comprise a quality assessment ending up in a «European Energy Award®» certificate and quantified measures.
 
 Several types of subsidies are elaborated to encourage municipalities to adopt and seriously commit to the Pact. These subsidies are modified in the 2016 amendment.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Efficiency Action Plan 2019-2021
DESCRIPTION: This Action Plan is based on the newer and stricter requirements from the European Union in the field of energy efficiency, and Montenegro's obligation under the Energy Community Treaty. It sets out measures to improve energy efficiency across sectors, and in the building, household, public, industry/commercial services and transport sectors, and energy transformation, transmission and distribution. Part of the measures include strengthening institutional capacities in the fields of climate change and energy and the creation of the first National Energy and Climate Plan, in close cooperation with the Secretariat of the Energy Community.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings Project
DESCRIPTION: This project, undertaken by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change, aims to renovate 500-700 public buildings in Türkiye as part of a broader national strategic goal to transition to a low-carbon economy and reduce carbon emissions. Funded by the World Bank, the project is implemented by the Ministry from 2019-2025, with the stated goals of lowering energy consumption in public buildings, developing institutional mechanisms for sustainable financing, and supporting the country's overall energy transition. The Project focuses on buildings like hospitals, schools, university campuses, government buildings, and more. It also aims to advocate for and improve legislation on energy efficiency in Türkiye's public sector as well as supporting technical assistance/capacity on the sustainability of such measures.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Liberia Adaptation Communication. AC1
DESCRIPTION: Liberia's Adaptation communication, Adaptation Communication from Liberia in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The National Climate Plan
DESCRIPTION: The National Climate Plan presents an agenda both in terms of mitigation and adaptation, aims to realize sustained economic growth and inclusive social development, while taking due account of climate change related challenges. It provides an overview of climate change vulnerabilities in Algeria and proposes over 70 action measures, including: - adoption of cleaner energy consumption model by substituting liquid fuels by natural gas and liquefied propane; - achieving 35,000 hectares of forests and developing another 175,000 hectares; -waste recovery (13.5 million tonnes / year), - electrification of railway transport and intensification of urban public transport (including constructing the Algiers metro and tramway infrastructure in several cities). The Plan further promotes uptake of renewable energies and sets a target of installing of 22,000 MW of renewable power capacity between 2011 and 2030, divided between 12, 000 MW to be dedicated to cover the national demand for electricity and 10,000 MW for export.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: German strategy to strengthen resilience to disasters: Implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030) - Germany's contribution 2022-2030
DESCRIPTION:
The Federal Government's strategy for strengthening resilience to disasters (resilience strategy for short) will make Germany more resilient to crises in the long term. The Federal Government is pursuing a holistic strategic approach in order to invest in prevention and to better cope with and recover from disasters and crises: The resilience strategy shows what efforts are already being made to this end and where overarching action is required in five specific fields of action:

  • Understanding disaster risk.
  • Strengthen intuitions to manage disaster risk.
  • Invest in disaster risk reduction to strengthen resilience.
  • Improve disaster preparedness and enable better recovery.
  • International cooperation

Crises and disasters have accompanied mankind since time immemorial. However, our recent past, our present and a look into the future show that crises and disasters present us with new and changing challenges. In Germany, risk and crisis management are national tasks and an integral part of our security architecture. Security is a fundamental human need for which the state bears a special responsibility. We must therefore place people at the centre of our initiatives to strengthen resilience to disasters.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Indicative expansion plan for the generation system 2022-2052
DESCRIPTION:
This plan was approved by the Ministerial Agreement no 09-2022. It sets the government's energy supply strategy for the next thirty years, and notably seeks to boost the production of energy from renewable sources.

It was approved alongside the Expansion Plan of the power transport system 2022-2052 (not in scope).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Environmental Impact Assessment 2012
DESCRIPTION: The Law on Environmental Impact Assessment regulates the implementation of the EIA, centred around protecting the environment, preventing the loss of environmental balance caused by human activities, exploiting the mineral resources with minimal adverse impact on the environment, and assessing the environmental impact of policies to be governed, and any plans, programmes, and project to be implemented at the regional and sectoral level. The Law also contains a discussion of the compensation of damages caused by incorrect performance or violation of the assessment, and implementation of projects without conducting the EIA.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation on the Monitoring of Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Policies and Mitigation Measures in the Republic of Croatia (Official Gazette 5/17)
DESCRIPTION: The regulation establishes a national system for calculating and reporting anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and removals. It assigns ministerial responsibilities, defines implementation reporting structures (including to the UNFCCC via national and biennial reports), and gives the key types of statistics to be included in the overall emissions reporting.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Maldives Energy Efficiency Guideline for Buildings
DESCRIPTION:
Energy efficiency and conservation are crucial for the Maldives to mitigate climate change risks and achieve energy security. Maldives has a high dependence on fossil fuels to meet all of its domestic energy demand, and the use of fossil fuels has resulted in huge greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and its associated climate change risks. Maldives is also vulnerable to global oil price shocks due to dependence on imported fossil fuels. This Guideline mainstreams energy efficiency in building design practices to achieve a substantial reduction of energy consumption from buildings.

Actions include encouraging energy efficiency both at the construction stage and during the lifetime of the building, e.g. by climate-sensitive design which takes account of the orientation and surrounding features to control wind effects while optimising sunlight, daylight, and solar gain benefits.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Greece National Inventory Report (NIR). 2019
DESCRIPTION: Greece National Inventory Report (NIR). 2019

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ordinance on Methodologies for Setting National Energy Savings Targets and Verification of Energy Efficiency Measures (SG 27/2009, last amended SG 88/2011)
DESCRIPTION: The Ordinance on Methodologies for Setting National Energy Savings Targets and Verification of Energy Efficiency Measures (SG 27/2009, last amended SG 88/2011) establishes the framework for implementing the Energy Efficiency Act in Bulgaria. It defines how national energy savings targets are calculated and allocated to obligated parties under Article 10, sets the eligible energy efficiency measures, and specifies the methodologies for assessing and verifying achieved energy savings. Additionally, it regulates the approval of the tariff for fees collected by the Energy Efficiency Agency when issuing energy savings certificates under Article 51. The ordinance ensures transparent accounting of energy savings, facilitates compliance with national and EU energy efficiency obligations, and supports reporting under EU directives.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Deductions for carbon sink forest expenses
DESCRIPTION: Businesses can claim a deduction for expenses incurred establishing trees in a carbon sink forest, which is a forest established for the primary and principal purpose of carbon sequestration. To be eligible, businesses must hold the interest or rights in the land or trees that is most specific to the carbon sequestration activities, and use the land and the forest for the primary and principal purpose of carbon sequestration by the trees.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Environment Act of 2024
DESCRIPTION: The Environment Act of 2024 sets a range of regulatory and administrative frameworks around environmental protection, of which it considers climate action to be a subset. It establishes a National Network for Sustainable Development, with the partial purpose of recommending climate adaptation and mitigation actions. The act also integrates climate into environmental impact assessments, and establishes a National Environment and Climate Change Fund. Lastly, the Ports Act (1998) is amended to stipulate that master plans for port development should include climate adaptation and mitigation assessments and provisions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Latvia’s Strategy to achieve climate neutrality by 2050
DESCRIPTION:
The Strategy is a long-term policy planning document designed to increase the economic competitiveness of the Latvian economy at the same time as limiting and reducing climate change, as well as to ensure a safe living environment for the people of Latvia. It is designed to support the European Union's overall climate-neutrality target by 2050. This document was released alongside the National Energy and Climate Plan 2021-2030 that is a mandatory communication to the EU.

The document details the government's overarching goals and lines of action, examines and sets the emissions reduction low-carbon objectives across the economy's main sectors.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulations of the Law on Incentives for the Development of Renewable Energy Projects (Reglamento de la Ley de Incentivos para el Desarrollo de Proyectos de Energía Renovable)
DESCRIPTION:
This Government Agreement No. 211-2005 establishes the regulatory framework for implementing Guatemala's Law on Incentives for Renewable Energy Projects, providing detailed procedural mechanisms for accessing fiscal, economic, and administrative benefits. The regulation specifies comprehensive application requirements for individuals, legal entities, municipalities, and the National Electrification Institute, mandating submission of detailed project documentation including pre-feasibility studies, technical and financial analyses, and itemised lists of required machinery, equipment, and materials with tariff classifications and intended utilisation.

The framework establishes a two-tier administrative process involving technical evaluation by the competent directorate within twenty days, followed by ministerial resolution within ten days, whilst providing mechanisms for requesting additional information and granting extensions where justified. It creates ongoing compliance obligations including semi-annual progress reporting, archaeological discovery notification, tax payment verification for equipment sales, and project suspension reporting. The regulation establishes detailed supervision and verification mechanisms permitting ministerial, directorate, and tax authority personnel access to project areas, whilst mandating cooperation with tax auditors conducting fiscal verification to ensure proper application of incentives in accordance with the Tax Code and preventing misuse of tax exemptions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Order TED/989/2022 on the remuneration of energy production from renewable energy sources, cogeneration and waste
DESCRIPTION: The object of this order is the establishment of new standard facilities in order to accommodate the facilities to which the maintenance of the remuneration established in Order TED/171/2020, of February 24, which updates the parameters, is applicable. remuneration of the standard installations applicable to certain installations for the production of electricity from renewable energy sources, cogeneration and waste, for the purposes of its application to the regulatory period that begins on January 1, 2020, in accordance with the application of the provisions of article 4 of Order TED/260/2021, of March 18, which adopts accompanying measures for facilities whose operating costs depend essentially on the price of fuel during the period of validity of the state of alarm due to the health crisis situation caused by COVID-19.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Master Plan for Urban Nature: Federal Government Action Programme for a Vibrant City
DESCRIPTION:
The Masterplan Stadtnatur translates the strategic vision of the White Paper on Urban Green into a concrete programme of measures. While the White Paper defines the overall goals for greener, healthier, and more resilient cities, the Masterplan specifies 14 actions that the federal government will implement to increase biodiversity, strengthen urban green infrastructure, and support municipalities. It puts biodiversity, nature-based solutions and integrated planning at the core for climate adaptation.

The Masterplan adopts a broad definition of urban nature, including parks, gardens, urban forests, rivers, wetlands, street trees, green roofs and façades, brownfields, and habitats for wildlife within the built environment. Its objective is to strengthen these elements through coordinated planning, funding, research, education, and policy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Amendment to Act Concerning Energy Tax (a component of the climate and energy package) within the 2013 National Budget Bill
DESCRIPTION:
The law aims to support the uptake of biofuels through the establishment of the following tax incentives:
- All biofuels are exempted from the carbon tax
- Fuels that contain hydrogenated vegetable and animal fats and oils (HVO) in blends of up to 15% are exempt from the fuel tax
- E85 and other high-blend biofuels continue to be exempt from the fuel tax; and
- Low-blend biofuels are subject to a reduction of the fuel tax.

DESCRIPTION: Germany National Communication. NC6

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Tunisia National Communication. NC4
Fuel-Consumption Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles
DESCRIPTION:
India initially introduced fuel consumption standards for diesel vehicles weighing 12 tonnes or more in 2017, implementing them in two phases. Phase 1 began on April 1, 2018, and Phase 2 was scheduled for April 1, 2021. In 2019, the standards were expanded to include diesel vehicles weighing 3.5 tonnes or more, with enforcement set for April 2020. However, in September 2020—just months before Phase 2 was to begin—the government scrapped the Phase 2 standards entirely and postponed the Phase 1 compliance deadline to January 1, 2021.

The regulations are aimed at reducing fuel consumption and greenhouse-gas emissions from diesel-powered trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight of 12 tonnes or greater. Indian HDVs greater than 12 tonnes represent about 60% of total fuel use and GHG emissions from the entire HDV fleet." (ICCT 2017)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Namibia's Sixth National Development Plan (NDP6) 2025/26-2029/30
DESCRIPTION: The Sixth National Development Plan (NDP6) for 2025/26-2029/30 aims to set long and medium term overarching guidance on social and economic development in Namibia. The plan underscores the necessity of a green transition, and promotes climate adaptation and mitigation interventions across a range of sectors. It promotes the research and development of hydrogen fuel production, and the use of climate-smart agricultural enhancements in crop breeding, irrigation and cold-storage of products. In the fossil fuel sector it aims to mitigate the climate impacts of recent oil and gas discoveries by implementing carbon capture and storage. The plan calls for more general mainstreaming of climate adaptation across all sectors, including the diversification of water source exploitation to maintain aquifer resilience. Downstream of these various efforts, it aims to reduce the proportion of the population vulnerable to climate change from 65% to 45% by 2030, and more than double the funds available for climate change resilience.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Comprehensive Plan for Reconstruction with Changes (Plan Integral para la Reconstrucción con Cambios)
DESCRIPTION: The Comprehensive Plan for Reconstruction with Changes (Plan Integral de Reconstrucción con Cambios "PIRCC") addresses the aftermath of El Niño Costero, a climatic phenomenon that caused widespread damage to infrastructure, livelihoods, and communities in Peru. Its primary objective is to rehabilitate and reconstruct public infrastructure—such as roads, schools, health facilities, and water systems—while prioritizing the recovery of vulnerable populations displaced by floods, landslides, and other disasters. The plan emphasizes climate-resilient reconstruction and disaster risk reduction, integrating adaptive measures to prevent future vulnerabilities. The PIRCC outlines two core intervention types: (1) rehabilitation and replacement of damaged infrastructure to restore essential services, and (2) preventive measures such as river desilting, flood barriers, and urban planning reforms to reduce exposure to climate-related hazards. It incorporates sustainable construction standards, including climate-resilient materials, energy-efficient systems, and disaster-safe housing, ensuring long-term resilience. The plan also prioritizes territorial ordering and sustainable land use, addressing the root causes of vulnerability linked to unregulated urban growth.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sectoral Adaptation Plan - Agriculture, Forestry and Seafood
DESCRIPTION:
The 2024 National Adaptation Framework (NAF) requires the development of Sectoral Adaptation Plans (SAPs) for 13 key sectors. The SAPs were developed applying a six-step adaptation planning process described in Sectoral Planning Guidelines for Climate Change Adaptation to prepare the ground, conduct a climate impact screening, prioritise impacts, conduct a detailed climate risk assessment, develop goals, objectives and actions, and establish governance and implementation frameworks.

The goals of the Agriculture, Forestry and Seafood Climate Change Sectoral Adaptation Plan are to:

  • Establish a cohesive framework for governance, collaboration and cross sector resilience in agriculture, forestry, and seafood;
  • Promote sustainable agricultural practices that enhance resilience and safeguard the natural environment;
  • Promote sustainable forest management that enhances resilience and safeguards the natural environment; and
  • Maintain sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and enhance resilience of the seafood sector.

Examples of actions include:

  • Strategically investing in and facilitating targeted climate adaptation research and innovation across agriculture, forestry, and seafood sectors, leveraging the expertise of key national research bodies;
  • Encouraging farm diversification to improve the resilience of the agri-food sector;
  • Developing a facility for forest research and innovation with a strong focus on sustainability, circular economy and value creation; and
  • Supporting a resilient, climate smart, environmentally sustainable and profitable Irish seafood sector in order to maximise its contribution to jobs and growth and maintaining the economic and social activities of our most vibrant and sustainable coastal communities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Albania National Adaptation Plan. NAP1
DESCRIPTION: Albania National Adaptation Plan. NAP1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act of 15 May 2015 on substances that deplete the ozone layer and on certain fluorinated greenhouse gases, last amended by Act of 21 November 2025
DESCRIPTION: The Act of 15 May 2015 establishes Poland’s national legal framework for implementing EU and international regulations on ozone-depleting substances (ODS) and fluorinated greenhouse gases (F-gases), ensuring compliance with key EU instruments such as Regulation (UE) No 517/2014 on F-gases and Regulation (WE) No 1005/2009 on ODS.The Act also defines certification requirements for personnel and businesses handling such substances, establishes control and enforcement powers for authorities, and provides for administrative sanctions for non-compliance. The 2025 amendment to the Act of 15 May 2015 primarily updates Poland’s legal framework to align with the revised EU regulations on fluorinated greenhouse gases and ozone-depleting substances, ensuring continued compliance with strengthened EU phase-down, control, and reporting requirements. It also adjusts administrative and financial provisions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for REDD+ 2017-2030 (ENAREDD+)
DESCRIPTION: Mexico's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a voluntary framework for climate change mitigation developed under the UNFCCC, with a focus on the challenges faced by developing countries.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Master Plan for Major Projects on the Protection and Restoration of Key Ecosystems Nationwide (2021-2035)
DESCRIPTION: This Plan defines the national ecological security barrier system based on the "Three Zones and FourBelts", and sets out the major ecological protection and restoration tasks by 2035. The tasks include improving the monitoring, evaluation and warning systems; prevention measures for wildfires and sandstorms; eliminating threats to endangered species; and improving technology for weather modification, to tackle extreme weather events and climate change impacts that will affect ecological systems.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Joint National Action Plan on Climate Change Adaptation and Disaster Risk Management 2010-2015
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan defines six objectives and a subsequent implementation strategy: 1) Improved good governance for climate change adaptation and disaster risk management (mainstreaming, decision making, organizational and institutional policy frameworks), 2) Improved good governance for climate change adaptation and disaster risk management (mainstreaming, decision making, organizational and institutional policy frameworks), 3) Analysis and assessments of vulnerability to climate change impacts and disaster risks, 4) Enhanced community preparedness and resilience to impacts of all disasters, 5) Technically reliable, economically affordable and environmentally sound energy to support the sustainable development of the Kingdom, and 6) strong partnerships, cooperation and collaboration within government agencies and with Civil Societies, Non Government Organisations and the Private Sectors. 

The development of this Joint Action Plan on Climate Change Adaptation and Disaster Risks Management complies with Tonga's National Strategic Development Framework 2009-2014, the Pacific Islands Framework of Action on Climate Change 2006-2015, the Pacific Disaster Risk Reduction and Disaster Management Framework for Action 2005-2015, the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction (IDNDR), the Yokohama Plan for Action and the Hyogo Framework for Action 2005-2015, and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

DESCRIPTION: Monaco Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Lithuanian Transport Development Strategy until 2050
DESCRIPTION: The Transport Development Strategy aims to guide the long term development of transport in Lithuania, accounting for the need to mitigate and adapt to emerging challenges such as climate change. The strategy promotes general expansion of low carbon transport, calling for the establishment of a sustainable mobility fund, and the use of tax incentives to guide development. Recommendations include electric vehicle promotion, rail electrification and improvements in monitoring administration. It also acknowledges threats to existing transport infrastructure by flooding and extreme weather, as they increase in frequency under climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation on Renewable Energy Designated Areas (YEKA)
DESCRIPTION:
The objectives of the Regulation can be regarded as:

• forming large-scale Renewable Energy Designated Areas ("REDAs") on either property belonging to public / treasury, or privately owned property, in order to make effective and efficient use of renewable energy sources,

• Rapidly completing investment projects by assigning these areas to investors, and enabling high-tech equipment used in the generation facilities to be domestically manufactured or supplied and contribute to technology transfer.

(source: British Chamber of Commerce Turkey)

In order to procure the production of renewable energy on ‘Renewable Energy Designated Areas’ which are deemed most suitable for energy generation, this Regulation introduced a tender process. The process requires developers to include domestic businesses, establish domestic factories, create employment for the local labour force and invest in RD.

(source: Climate Action Tracker)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Power Development Master Plan 2022-2040
DESCRIPTION: The PDP outlines a comprehensive long-term plan for Cambodia's power sector that includes forecasts of demand, expansion of generation, and a plan for transmission and distribution from 2022 until 2040. The plan will oversee a rapid expansion of renewable energy resources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Kiribati Joint Implementation Plans for Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management 2014-2023 and 2019-2028
DESCRIPTION:
The Kiribati joint Implementation Plan For Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management 2019-2028 aims to increase resilience through sustainable climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction.The KJIP formalises the role of the Kiribati National Expert Group on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management ( to become the main advisory body and coordination mechanism as well as the entry point for climate change and disaster risk management initiatives.

The 2014-2023 document aims at identifying an integrated set of specific actions and measures to increase the country's resilience to climate change and associated risks in different sectors. It is designed to complement the National Disaster Risk Management Plan and the National Framework for Climate Change and Climate Change Adaptation. By identifying tangible, on-the-ground actions for resilience and measures that enable the Government to facilitate these, the plan will guide the implementation of these complementary policies in an integrated approach.

The government hopes that such a systematic approach will maximise the efficiency and effectiveness of existing capacities and resources as well as ensuring the success of new initiatives. The specific goals of the policy are: 1) strengthening good governance, policies, strategies and legislation, 2) improving knowledge and information generation, management and sharing, 3) strengthening and greening the private sector, including small-scale business, 4) increasing water and food security with integrated and sector-specific approaches and promoting healthy and resilient ecosystems, 5) strengthening health service delivery to address climate change impacts, 6) promoting sound and reliable infrastructure development and land management, 7) delivering appropriate education, training and awareness programs, 8) increasing effectiveness and efficiency of early warnings and disaster and emergency management, 9) promoting the use of sustainable, renewable sources of energy and energy efficiency, 10) strengthening capacity to access finance, monitor expenditures and maintain strong partnerships, 11) maintaining the existing sovereignty and unique identity of Kiribati, and 12) enhancing the participation and resilience of vulnerable groups. The document further examines administrative and governance factors, as well as financial resources needed for implementing such an approach.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Supreme Decree No. 012-2021-MINAM. Adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 012-2021-MINAM. Adecúa la Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático)
DESCRIPTION:
The Decree Supreme No. 012-2021-MINAM adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático) to the legal framework established by Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, and its implementing regulations. The instrument formalises the Commission as a permanent, multisectoral body under the technical supervision of the Ministry of Environment, with the primary function of monitoring the implementation of national climate policies and international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Commission is designed as a consultative and oversight mechanism that facilitates coordination between state institutions and civil society actors across all levels of government. Its mandate includes tracking compliance with national climate objectives, evaluating policy effectiveness, and generating technical recommendations for decision-making at both institutional and governmental levels.

The Commission’s composition reflects a structured approach to inclusive governance: it comprises 22 state representatives (designated from key ministries, regional and municipal associations, and intergovernmental bodies) and 22 non-state representatives drawn from diverse civil society groups, including Indigenous organisations (PPICC), Afro-Peruvian networks, environmental NGOs, youth collectives, women’s coalitions, trade unions, academic institutions, professional colleges, and private-sector associations. All members, whether state or non-state, possess equal voting rights, reinforcing principles of participatory legitimacy. The Secretariat Technical is housed within the Ministry of Environment and provides administrative and analytical support, while the Commission may convene specialised technical working groups and seek expert input from affiliated public institutions such as SENAMHI, CONCYTEC, SERFOR, SERNANP, OEFA, and CEPLAN. The body operates under an internal regulation that governs procedural matters, including quorum requirements, voting procedures, and meeting schedules. By institutionalising multi-stakeholder engagement and establishing clear mechanisms for information exchange, reporting, and accountability, the decree aims to strength Peru’s domestic climate governance architecture, ensuring alignment with international obligations, particularly those related to transparency, periodic NDC reporting, and the integration of subnational inputs into national climate planning.

As a result of administrative reorganisations, the Supreme Decree N° 005-2023-MINAM modifies the composition of the High-Level Climate Change Commission (CANCC), expanding its membership to include five additional ministries: Defense, Interior, Justice and Human Rights, Labor and Employment Promotion, and Foreign Trade and Tourism. This modification aims to enhance inter-ministerial coordination and strengthen Peru's national climate change response strategy by broadening governmental participation in climate action planning and implementation. The decree seeks to create a more comprehensive and integrated approach to developing and executing national climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, reflecting a whole-of-government strategy in addressing climate challenges.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National plan for civil protection, prevention and mitigation of disasters
DESCRIPTION:
The Civil Protection, Prevention and Mitigation of Disasters Law, LPC, in article 20, defines that the Civil Protection, Prevention and Mitigation of Disasters Plan, PNPC, aims to define the actions of the State and civil society for the management of risks, the study of existing vulnerabilities and their mitigation, as well as preparations for care and recovery in the event of disasters.

The PNPC has planned results for the public administration period 2014-2019 based on the Five-Year Development Plan and expected results until 2030 based on the international commitments to implement the 2030 Agenda, The Paris Agreement, COP 21, and the Sendai Framework, these international commitments are country commitments and the following public administrations must take up their implementation in their five-year planning cycles.

The approach used in planning for the GIRRD is intersectoral, interinstitutional and multidisciplinary. It includes prevention, mitigation, response, and post-disaster recovery in its design, and its actions indicate that all public entities, the private sector, and civil society are involved in its execution. The premise of the planning is that to the extent that the risk is known, the person will be better prepared to prevent, mitigate and confront them in a timely and effective manner for recovery.

The PNPC is divided into five chapters: the first addresses the national and international regulatory legal framework that regulates the PNPC; the second the institutional framework that, due to its intersectoral nature, is needed to execute the PNPC; The third chapter interrelates the PNPC with the Sendai Framework, the SDGs and the Five-Year Development Plan 2014-2019 of El Salvador; The fourth articulates the conceptualization of the prevention, mitigation, response and post-disaster recovery components. The fifth chapter develops the strategic framework of planning, its philosophy and executive direction by establishing the mission, vision, objectives, priorities and strategic lines of action; finally, the sixth chapter defines the guidelines for post-disaster recovery.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 27345 Approving the Law for the Promotion of Efficient Energy Use
DESCRIPTION:
The Law declares the promotion of energy efficiency a matter of national interest. The motivations listed in the bill are to ensure a stable energy supply, protect the consumer, improve competitiveness of the national market and to reduce environmental damage caused by energy consumption. The Law requires the Ministry of Energy and Mining to promote a culture of energy efficiency and to design and fund energy efficiency projects. However, the legislation is vague on details and activities to be realised. The one exception is the labelling of electronic appliances and machines of energy consumption information within 90 days after the law has taken into affect.

The Executive Decree details how the Ministry of Energy and Mining is to realise the mandates of the corresponding law.

In order to encourage a culture of energy efficiency, the Ministry is to co-ordinate education programmes for the general public and in primary and secondary schools, as well as co-ordinate the establishment of undergraduate and graduate degree programmes in energy efficiency. Additionally, 21 October is celebrated as National Energy Saving Day.

The Ministry will encourage energy efficiency in homes and residences with publicity campaigns meant to change consumption behaviour; promote the financing of energy efficient electrical systems appliances; and encourage the use of energy efficient technologies in remote areas.

In the service and private industry sectors the Ministry will promote the creation of an 'energy efficiency market'; create standards of energy efficiency for private enterprises; create minimum standards of energy efficiency depending on the type of productive activity; co-ordinate the financing of small and medium enterprises to establish pilot projects meant to make energy use more efficient; and coordinate with the National Commission on Climate Change and the National Environmental Fund to facilitate international financing through the Clean Development Mechanisms.

In the public sector the Ministry will audit the use of energy by public entities that use more than a pre-established amount of energy units; co-ordinate efficient lighting systems; and co-ordinate the conversion of public sector vehicles to run on natural gas.

In the transport sector, the Ministry will co-ordinate with the appropriate public entities to encourage efficient use of public transport systems and optimise traffic systems to mitigate idle use of fuels.

The Ministry should co-ordinate the replication of successful projects at the Regional Government level.

It also considers raising awareness, building capacity and making the case for local government action and proposes a framework for action.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electricity Demand Side Management Measures
DESCRIPTION:
These Measures apply to the demand-side management of electricity within China. The Measures were introduced to "implement the major strategic decisions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on carbon peaking and achieving carbon neutrality..." (Article 1).

Article 14 includes a target for "demand response capability". By 2025, the capacity of each province to respond to demand will reach 3%-5% of the maximum electricity load, with provinces with an annual peak valley difference rate of over 40% reaching 5% or more.

The Measures were introduced in accordance with existing laws and regulations, including the Electric Power Law, the Energy Conservation Law, the Regulations on the Supply and Use of Electric Power.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: NDC Implementation Plan of Nepal, 2023
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan lays out a detailed roadmap for achieving the country’s emission reduction targets, aligning with its broader climate goals. It focuses on both mitigation and adaptation measures. For mitigation, the plan prioritises the expansion of renewable energy sources, particularly hydropower, solar, and wind power, as well as improving energy efficiency in various sectors. To adapt to climate change, the plan emphasises building climate resilience in agriculture, water resources, and infrastructure. Additionally, it prioritises disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, and community-based adaptation measures. The implementation plan aims to mobilise domestic and international resources, strengthen institutional capacity, and promote public awareness to ensure its successful execution.

The Plan highlights the importance of policy support and financial incentives to accelerate the shift towards low-emission technologies. This includes access to climate finance, government subsidies for cleaner technologies, and public-private partnerships to drive innovation. It also sets out a framework for capacity building, aiming to enhance the technical skills and knowledge of industry stakeholders and strengthen the regulatory environment to enforce compliance with emission reduction targets.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategic framework for climate change adaptation
DESCRIPTION: This strategic framework aims at making Slovenia, by 2050, a society adapted and resilient to climate change impacts and characterised by a high quality of life and a high degree of safety of life, while taking full advantage of the changed climate on the basis of sustainable development. This document presents the measures to strengthen capacities for climate change adaptation, management of risks and for taking advantage of eventual opportunities brought by a changing climate.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Policy 2012-2017
DESCRIPTION: This document sets the Solomon Islands' Climate Change Policy for the period 2012-2017. Its seeks to enhance mitigation and adaptation efforts, improve related governance, integrate climate issues to development policies, enhance the people's resilience to climate change, and promote renewable energy and energy efficiency. The document further addresses disaster risk management and financing issues.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/955 (recast) (Energy Efficiency Directive or EED)
DESCRIPTION: Part of the EU's 'Fit for 55' package, a legislative package that aims to align the EU's climate, energy, land use, transport, and taxation policies with a GhG emissions reduction target of 55% by 2030 (compared with 1990 levels), this revised Directive require Member States to integrate the ‘energy efficiency first’ principle into all planning, policy and major investment decisions, with a view to meeting an increased EU target of no more than 1,023 Mt of oil equivalent (Mtoe) to be used in 2030. Annual energy savings by Member States will reach 1.5% by 2030, on average. The Directive obliges the public sector to reduce its final energy consumption by 1.9% each year (with the option to exclude public transport and armed forces). Member states are also obliged to ensure that at least 3% of publicly owned buildings are renovated each year to a net-zero/ zero-emissions standard.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Organic Agriculture 2025-2032
DESCRIPTION: As climate and environmental challenges have increased, this Strategy promotes organic farming to contribute to adaptation to a changing climate, reduction of biodiversity loss and carbon storage through soil. DESCRIPTION: The Papua New Guinea Fisheries Strategic Plan 2021-2030 is an overarching framework to align strategic purposes, priorities, actions and outcomes for the fisheries sector. The negative impacts of climate change on the fisheries sector can be devastating, including the rising sea temperatures and sea levels which in turn impacts the oceans, ecosystems and fish stocks. This increases the importance to consider ways to climate proof the sector, focusing on adaptive management approaches, mitigation, and resilient strategies. These include the rising sea temperatures and sea levels which in turn impacts the oceans, ecosystems and fish stocks.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Special Tax Law on Production and Services (carbon tax and credits)
DESCRIPTION:
The 2012 amendments to the Special Tax Law introduced Mexico's carbon tax. It covers fossil fuel sales and imports by manufacturers, producers, and importers and is capped at 3% of the sales price of the fuel. Rather than imposing a levy on the full carbon content of fuels, it taxes the additional amount of emissions that are generated compared to if natural gas (not currently subject to tax) was used instead. Companies may also choose to pay the tax with credits from local CDM projects, which support the development of carbon trading schemes within Mexico. The carbon tax is updated yearly and announced in December to be implemented on January 1st each year.

The 2013 amendments also introduced carbon credits. These credits are a translation into Mexican Law of the Kyoto Protocol and the subsequent UNFCCC texts. They are meant to allow for projects being undertaken in Mexico under the scope of the UNFCCC to pay taxes via the credits, based on market carbon price. The allocation and price mechanisms of carbon credits will be determined in accordance to the rules edited by the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit.

DESCRIPTION: This Plan determines how Samoa plan to meet their SDG targets regarding the natural environment and its links to human activities, which include agriculture, water and sanitation, infrastructure, energy and tourism. It distinguishes between eight types of environments, such as upland, lowland, coastal and protected habitats. One key objective of the plan is to implement ecosystem-based strategies to support climate change mitigation and adaptation. It also identifies the following ways to adapt to climate change impacts: 1) implement sustainable plans for improving the protection of critical catchment areas, 2) assign priority to securing the full protection of the entire Apia, Vaisigano and Tafitoala catchment areas, 3) promote and support the replanting of catchment and erosion prone areas, 4) promote and support the replanting of mangrove forests and exposed coastal areas, 5) encourage and facilitate the relocation of households away from high risk flood-prone areas, 6) promote the growing of food crops that are not vulnerable to wind damage, 7) support the full implementation of Samoa's NAPA, 8) encourage the implementation of natural solutions to enhance coastal resilience to climate change, 9) promote efforts to rehabilitate all degraded land areas through the replanting of appropriate tree species and the use of sustainable soil management techniques, and 10) develop and promote sustainable models of future climate for project sites based on a range of climate change scenarios.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: ASIC Regulatory Guide 280 (RG 280) Sustainability reporting
DESCRIPTION:
This guide is for entities required to prepare a sustainability report under Ch 2M of the Corporations Act (reporting entities). This may include companies (including registered corporations under the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act 2007), registered schemes, registrable superannuation entities and retail corporate collective investment vehicles.

It explains how the Australian Securities Investments Commission (ASIC) will exercise specific powers under legislation (primarily the Corporations Act), how ASIC interprets the law and the principles underlying ASIC’s approach. It also provides practical guidance to entities about complying with their sustainability reporting obligations. Reporting entities may ask for information from entities within their value chain, including small businesses and farmers.

The sustainability report requires climate-related content, including statements of no material financial risks or opportunities relating to climate if applicable, statements with forward-looking climate information based on reasonable grounds, if any, and the use of a minimum of two climate scenarios that are referable to temperature increases set out in the Climate Change Act 2022 (Climate Change Act) in assessing their climate resilience, and material financial risks and opportunities relating to climate.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 4612 establishing the Presidential Commission for Climate Change (Decreto No. 4612 que establece la Comisión Presidencial para el Cambio Climático)
DESCRIPTION: Venezuela established a permanent Presidential Commission for Climate Change through Decree No. 4.612. This commission serves as an advisory body to the President on climate change matters and comprises representatives from five ministries: ecosocialism (presiding), planning, foreign relations, industries and national production, and science and technology. The commission operates under a technical secretariat exercised by the Ministry of Popular Power for Ecosocialism and may convene additional government bodies and subject matter experts as required.The commission's primary functions encompass advising the President on climate change issues, developing proposals for national climate change regulations, and coordinating the creation of the National Climate Change Strategy alongside National Adaptation and Mitigation Plans for presidential approval. Additional responsibilities include ensuring effective technical, administrative and financial information management; strengthening state, regional and municipal monitoring, reporting and verification capacities for climate adaptation and mitigation; and promoting risk management measures to address climate change vulnerabilities and impacts. The commission is empowered to establish working groups for specific topics and must develop its internal operating regulations within ninety days of the decree's publication.

It focuses on six key technological areas: electrification/efficiency/renewables; carbon capture and storage; low-carbon hydrogen; battery storage; clean cooking; and BECCS (bioenergy with carbon capture and storage). The budget also includes plans for a new National Infrastructure Bank with £22 billion of financing and for the issuance of the UK's first green government bond or gilt.As policy decisions it states that the e new UK Infrastructure Bank will provide financing support to private sector and local authority infrastructure projects across the UK, to help meetgovernment objectives on climate change and regional economic growth. Also, the government will offer a green retail savings product through NSI in the summer of 2021. PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The First National Greenhouse Gas Mitigation Plan and Government decision 2508
DESCRIPTION:
The National Plan for the Reduction of Greenhouse Gas Emissions aims to reduce emissions by 20% compared to a business-as-usual scenario by 2020.
 
 The main strategies relate to energy efficiency, green building, and transport. A key element was a government-sponsored programme of subsidies administered jointly by the Ministry of Environmental Protection and the Investment Centre in the Ministry of Economy, aimed at encouraging investments in energy efficiency and GHG reduction projects and at advancing new Israeli technologies. The Chief Scientist in the Ministry of Economy grants additional assistance (ILS40 million, USD10.4 million) to approved projects, based on new Israeli technologies (first installation).
 
 Key elements of the National Plan included:
  • Reducing residential energy consumption - (responsibility of Ministry of Energy and Water Resources)
  • Support for investments in GHG emissions reductions (responsibility of Ministry of Environmental Protection)
  • Support for Israeli technologies and green innovation (responsibility of Ministry of Economy)
  • Pilot projects for green building and green building teaching and training (responsibility of Ministry of Environmental Protection)
  • Pilot project for retrofits ((responsibility of Ministry of Construction and Housing)
  • Education and awareness (responsibility of Ministries of Environmental Protection and Transport)
  • Promotion of energy efficiency (responsibility of Ministries of Environmental Protection and Economy)
  • Setting standards for energy efficiency (responsibility of Ministry of Energy and Water Resources)
  • Transport (responsibility of Transport Ministry) - including energy efficient components in imported cars and eco-driving education
 
 The approved budget for the implementation of the plan was ILS2.2 billion (USD573 million) until 2020. During 2011-2012 ILS106 million (USD27.6 million) were allocated to 208 projects, with a reduction potential of ~ 450,000 tons of CO2eq per year and a savings potential of approximately ILS100 million (USD26 million) per year in electricity and fuel costs. The programme leveraged investments of more than ILS 550 million (USD143 million) by industries, businesses and municipalities during those first two years.
 
 The inter-ministerial committee was set to begin to examine additional reduction measures for the years 2013-2014, including renewable energies. In July 2013, however, the National Plan for the Reduction of GHG Emissions was frozen for three years by the Ministry of Finance, with the passage of the 2013 budget. This meant the cessation of many of the GHG mitigation programs. Only those that were already funded in previous budgets or that could be funded via other means will continue.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Circular No. 01/VBHN-BNNPTNT - Regulations on Sustainable Forest Management

The plan shall take into account the management of forest carbon reserves, assessing the impact of forestry activities on the environment. Forest owners are to encourage the implementation of measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions; management measures to enhance the absorption and preservation of forest carbon, and the effective use of resources in forestry activities.

It also imposes on the inter-ministerial committee to formulate by 1.7.2022 a methodology for examining the possible effects on meeting the national targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions set forth in this proposed resolution, which stems from government policy and its decisions.

It determines that the Cabinet Ministers of the Ministries of Environmental Protection, Energy, Transport and Road Safety, Economy and Industry and the Interior report to the Government, each year.

It finally instructs the Minister of Environmental Protection, in consultation with the Minister of Economy and Industry, to formulate a voluntary mechanism for reporting and publishing information on the impact on the climate and greenhouse gas emissions of products and services manufactured in Israel and imported into it.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Seychelles Climate Change Policy
DESCRIPTION:
The policy aims at making the country climate resilient, sustainable and low-carbon. Its objective is to facilitate a coordinated, coherent, proactive and effective response to the local, regional and global challenges and opportunities presented by climate change.

Specific objectives of the policy are as following: 1) advance understanding of Climate Change and its impacts on Seychelles, 2) to strengthen capacity and social empowerment at all levels to adequately respond to Climate Change, 3) mainstream and integrate Climate Change considerations into all relevant sectors and all levels of government, 4) achieve transition to a low carbon economy, 5) put in place measures to adapt, build resilience and minimise vulnerability to the impacts of Climate Change, and 6) contribute effectively to regional and global negotiations on Climate Change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal Government Charging Infrastructure Master Plan I, II and III
DESCRIPTION:
It is the Federal Government Charging Infrastructure Master Plan 2030, which is Germany’s national roadmap for expanding and improving EV charging infrastructure through 2030. It focues on shifting from simply increasing charger numbers to reliability, accessibility, affordability, transparency, and user experience. It contains 41 measures across five priorities:

  1. Increase EV charging demand and private investment.
  2. Accelerate charging infrastructure deployment and simplify permitting.
  3. Strengthen competition and improve charging-price transparency.
  4. Integrate charging infrastructure with the electricity grid and enable smart/bidirectional charging.
  5. Improve convenience, accessibility, cybersecurity, and overall user experience.

Its priority areas include (i) residential/apartment charging, workplaces, motorway fast charging, and charging for electric trucks and buses; (ii) grid capacity and faster grid connections; (iii) reduction of administrative barriers and make public land and suitable sites more readily available. The overall objective is to establish a reliable, competitive, user-friendly and scalable charging ecosystem capable of supporting widespread EV adoption by 2030.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 2019-027/MESUDD implementing Law No. 2018-28, establishing the principles of Environmental Assessment
DESCRIPTION: The Decree n° 2019-027/PRN/MESU/DD provides the detailed application principles for the Law 2018-28, establishing the fundamental principles of Environmental Assessment (EA) in Niger, designating the Bureau National d’Évaluations Environnementales (BNEE) as the primary responsible body. The decree specifies four assessment types, with the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (EIES) for projects and the Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (EESS) for public policies, plans, and programs being the central tools for assessing climate change impacts. Through the EIES, the decree ensures that individual projects are evaluated for their vulnerability to climate risks (such as increased flooding or drought) and their contribution to environmental degradation or mitigation efforts. The EESS, on the other hand, guarantees that new government policies, plans, and programs integrate climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies at a high, strategic level.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Accord for Sustainable Growth (Energieakkoord)
DESCRIPTION:
The National Climate Agreement (2019) builds on, and replaces the Energy Accord of 2013. Rather than focusing solely on energy policy, the National Climate Agreement addresses all greenhouse gas emissions.

The Energy Agreement for sustainable growth (Energieakkoord) included agreements on energy efficiency, more renewable energy and more jobs. The government has made these agreements including employers, unions and environmental organisations. The government sees the agreement as an important step towards 100% renewable energy. The Dutch Energieakkoord replaced the Clean and Efficient Programme.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: GB 3095 - Air Quality Standards
DESCRIPTION: These standards are phased-in beginning in 2012 for some cities and by 2016 for all cities nationwide. Class 1 applies to special regions (including national parks) and Class 2 applies to all other areas. The standards state maximum levels for different gases, amid them SO2 and NOx, which are GHG-relevant gases.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution No. 1279 on the establishment of a Parliamentary Research Committee to cope with the impacts of climate change and drought and ensure efficient use of water resources.
DESCRIPTION: Resolution no. 1279, published in the Official Gazette No. 31411, sets outs a provision for the creation of a Parliamentary Research Committee that will help to produce measures that mitigate the negative impacts of climate change and drought and ensure the efficient use of water resources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Planned Relocation Guidelines - A framework to undertake climate change related relocation
DESCRIPTION: This document provides guidance for the Government of the Republic of Fiji and all other stakeholders present in Fiji to consider planned relocation solutions for the affected communities as part of their adaptation strategies in relation to environmental change, and disasters due to climate change related slow-onset events occurring on the territory of Fiji.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Green Taxonomy Regulation
DESCRIPTION:
This Regulation regulates the procedures and principles of the Green Taxonomy in order to support economic activities compatible with sustainable development goals, to encourage the flow of financing to sustainable investments and to prevent greenwashing in the market. To qualify as a compatible economic activity, it must meet the significant contribution criteria of one of the environmental targets:

a) Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions,

b) Adaptation to climate change,

C) Sustainable use and protection of water and sea resources,

ç) Transition to circular economy,

d) Prevention and control of pollution,

E) Protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems.

The Regulation also establishes the responsibilities of the President, the Green Taxonomy Committee and the technical expert group, and sets up an online taxonomy management system. Technical screening criteria are to be published on the website of the Presidency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electricity Market Law
DESCRIPTION: The Electricity Market Law aims to ensure that all energy users are supplied with electricity, promote energy independence of the country and also promote electricity production using renewable energy resources,The law establishes promotional measures for the production of electricity using renewable energy resources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Medium Term National Development Plan 2021 - 2025
DESCRIPTION: This plan succeeds to the Economic Recovery and Growth Plan (2017-2020) in order to implement the government's 2050 agenda over the period 2021-2025. It focuses on economic growth and development, infrastructure, public administration, human capital development, social development and regional development. It notably seeks to increase awareness to climate issues, boost the production and use of renewable energy sources, and generally create the conditions for making the economy sustainable.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2021/1056 establishing the Just Transition Fund, amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/795 and Regulation (EU) 2025/1914
DESCRIPTION:
This regulation establishes the Just Transition Fund (JTF) to provide support to the people, economies and environment of territories which face serious socio-economic challenges deriving from the transition process towards the Union’s 2030 targets for energy and climate as defined in Article 2.11 of Regulation 2018/1999 and a climate-neutral economy of the Union by 2050.It lays down the specific objective of the JTF, its geographical coverage and resources, the scope of its support with regard to the Investment for jobs and growth goal referred to in point (a) of Article 5(2) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060, as well as specific provisions for programming and indicators necessary for monitoring.

Amendments dispose that the JTF may also support investments contributing to the objectives of the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP) referred to in Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/795 and about investments in smart and sustainable local mobility, including the decarbonisation of the local transport sector and its infrastructure, as well as the deployment of recharging infrastructure referred in Regulation (EU) 2025/1914.

DESCRIPTION:
This Resolution outlines the responsibilities of the Environment Agency, belonging to the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment, in disaster risk management. The Environment Agency has the following functions and powers:

a) To prepare proposals for regulatory and methodological documents for the conduct of hazard, vulnerability, and risk studies and environmental impact assessments;

DESCRIPTION: This regulation introduces a Ministry of Environment duty to review applications for activities and developments affecting the environment, using a new 4-category classification scheme. Preliminary environmental impact assessment studies for 'high risk' (category 1) activities are mandated to include a section on both their impact on the climate and their vulnerability to climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Policy on Green Growth 2013-2030
DESCRIPTION:
The National Policy on Green Growth aims at enhancing the well-being and livelihood of all people on harmonization with ecological safety through green development growth, basing on green economy, blue economy, environment protection, social safety nets system and uphold of national cultural identity.

The main objectives of the policy are : 1) developing an economy in balance with environment, society and culture; 2) effective management of access to water resources management and sanitation, access to food security and food safety, access to development, access to renewable energy and energy efficiency; 3) to enhance education and training on green growth; 4) To strengthen information exchange, knowledge, technology and investment relation to green growth; 4) to stimulate green growth cooperation at a national and subnational level, region and the world.

This document replaces the 2009 version.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: United States of America: The President's climate action plan
DESCRIPTION:
This broad-based plan focuses on cutting the carbon pollution that causes climate change and affects public health.
It has three key pillars:

Cut carbon pollution in America: the plan (i) directs EPA to work closely with stakeholders to establish carbon pollution standards for both new and existing power plants; (ii) provides for loan guarantees for investments in innovative technologies; (iii) includes provisions for expanding on renewable energy projects; (iii) expands the President’s Better Building Challenge; (iv) sets a goal to reduce carbon pollution by at least 3 billion metric tons cumulatively by 2030; among other measures.
Prepare the United States for the impacts of climate change: The plan (i) directs agencies to support local climate-resilient investment by removing barriers or counterproductive policies and modernizing programs; and establishes a short-term task force of state, local, and tribal officials to advise on key actions the Federal government can take to help strengthen communities on the ground; (ii) pilots innovative strategies in the Hurricane Sandy-affected region to strengthen communities against future extreme weather and other climate impacts; and building on a new, consistent flood risk reduction standard established for the Sandy-affected region, agencies will update flood-risk reduction standards for all federally funded projects; (iii) launches an effort to create sustainable and resilient hospitals in the face of climate change through a public-private partnership with the healthcare industry; (iv) maintains agricultural productivity by delivering tailored, science-based knowledge to farmers, ranchers, and landowners; and helps communities prepare for drought and wildfire by launching a National Drought Resilience Partnership and by expanding and prioritizing forest- and rangeland- restoration efforts to make areas less vulnerable to catastrophic fire; and (v) provides climate preparedness tools and information needed by state, local, and private-sector leaders through a centralized “toolkit” and a new Climate Data Initiative.
Lead international efforts to combat global climate change and prepare for its impacts: one of the objectives is to strengthen global resilience to climate change by expanding government and local community planning and response capacities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ministerial Decree No. 9.719 on the institutional framework of the Project for the Development of Resilience to Recurrent Food Insecurity in the Sahel
DESCRIPTION: This decree creates within the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Equipment, a Project Management Unit (PMU) responsible for the implementation of the Food Insecurity Resilience Development Project. This applies to the Sahel in the regions of Fatick, Matam, Saint-Louis, Tambacounda and Ziguinchor (DRIARS Senegal). The aim of the project is to contribute to the reduction of food insecurity and to the development of the resilience of vulnerable populations in Senegal by targeting five (5) vulnerable regions of the country subjected to climate variability and hazards, in accordance with the objectives of the National Plan for Agricultural Investment (PNIA).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Green Affordable Housing Program (IGAHP)
DESCRIPTION: This program provides housing for low-income communities, applying the Green Building principle to achieve climate change targets by reducing carbon emissions. The program aims to build 100,000 green affordable housing units by 2024, build and retrofit one million units by 2030 (with a potential emissions reduction of 19-36 MtCO2), and achieve 100% net-zero housing by 2050 (PUPR, 2023). The program was launched by the Ministry of Public Works and Housing (PUPR: Kementerian Pekerjaan Umum dan Perumahan Rakyat). The IGAHP program is expected to save at least 20% water, save at least 20% energy, and reduce greenhouse gas effects by 29%.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Bangladesh Delta Plan 100
DESCRIPTION: This plan aims at fostering economic growth while eliminating poverty. It notably seeks to ensure safety from floods and climate disasters, sustainable water management, and preserve wetlands.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate adaptation strategy for transport
DESCRIPTION: The Climate Adaptation Strategy for Transport sets out how the transport sector will prepare for the impacts of climate change, built around three themes: a systems-based approach, mainstreaming adaptation into decisions, and building a stronger evidence base. It focuses on England and is a direction of travel rather than a full set of solutions. On climate, the strategy stresses that extreme weather is already disrupting transport, with rails buckling in heat, roads washed out by heavy rain, and ports and airports facing rising disruption. As of 2024, 38% of roads and 37% of railways in England are at risk of flooding, projected to rise to 46% and 54% by 2050. Weather-related incidents cost Network Rail over £1bn in compensation between 2006 and 2021. The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates climate damage could cut GDP by 3.2% to 7.8% by 2074, while adaptation measures can return £2 to £10 of benefits per £1 invested.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Forests (No. 011/24-1259/2-01)
DESCRIPTION:
This Law regulates the cultivation, protection, preservation and improvement of forests, planning, methods and conditions of forest use, construction and maintenance of forest roads, forest monitoring, as well as other issues of importance for forests, forest land and forestry. It also applies to the protection, preservation and use of forest trees located outside forests.

This Law contains provisions on protecting the ecological functions of forests, which include the sequestration of carbon from the air, and on forest monitoring. Forest monitoring is carried out for the purpose of preservation, restoration and sustainable use of forest ecosystems and their services, to increase the resilience of forests and enable the protection of the multifunctionality of forests, with a special emphasis on adaptation and mitigation of climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 14.995/2024 on the Eco Invest Brasil Programme and other provisions
DESCRIPTION:
The law establishes the Foreign Private Capital Mobilisation and Exchange Protection Programme (Eco Invest Brasil Programme), within the scope of the National Climate Change Fund (FNMC), established by Law No. 12,114 of 9 December 2009, with the following objectives:

I - to foster and encourage investments in projects that promote ecological transformation, especially in the areas of transition to sustainable practices and technologies, technological densification, bioeconomy, circular economy, energy transition and infrastructure and adaptation to climate change, among others;

II - to attract foreign investment to the country;

III - to make capital market operations feasible for companies, investors and financial institutions based in the country to raise funds abroad to finance projects that comply with the provisions of item I of this article;

IV - to support the development, liquidity and efficiency of the long-term foreign currency hedge market in the country.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act 393/2013 on sustainability criteria for certain fuels, last amended by Act 549/2026 and accompanying Decree 6/2021
DESCRIPTION:
Act on Sustainability Criteria for Certain Fuels (393/2013) establishes sustainability requirements and verification procedures for biofuels, bioliquids, biomass fuels and renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBOs). Its main objective is to ensure that renewable fuels used in energy and transport deliver genuine greenhouse-gas emission reductions and are produced from sustainable sources. The Act requires operators in specified cases to demonstrate compliance with sustainability criteria, including lifecycle greenhouse-gas emission savings and requirements concerning the origin of agricultural and forest biomass, biodiversity, land use, carbon stocks and sinks. It also establishes sustainability verification systems, including traceability and mass-balance requirements, and sets additional efficiency and emission requirements for biomass-based energy production.

The Government Decree 6/2021 brings further provisions and details.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Chad's national rural sector investment plan 2016-2022 (PNISR)
DESCRIPTION: This document sets Chad's strategy to reach sustainable development goals and increase resilience in the country's rural areas. It identifies adverse climate events as a major cause of food insecurity and malnutrition. The five objectives of this plan are as following: 1) Promote sustainable development of the rural world through the improvement of the living environment of rural producers, rational management of natural resources and judicious adaptation of local economies to climatic hazards.2) Develop rural infrastructure for the optimal development of land and water resources and improved access to markets, materials, equipment and financing.3) Sustainably develop the agro-sylvo-pastoral, fisheries and wildlife sectors to bring more added value to Chadian products and make them more competitive.4) Sustainably improve the food and nutritional security of rural populations, better integrate young people and women into production systems and strengthen the resilience of rural households.5) Create favorable conditions for the development of the rural sector by improving governance and strengthening research, training, extension and effective participation of all stakeholders.

The plan offers subsidies of up to 60% for systems up to 2kW and 40% for 2-3kW systems. The programme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2024. PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Seychelles Sustainable Development Strategy 2012-2020
DESCRIPTION:
The Seychelles Sustainable Development Strategy (SSDS) 2012-2020 is a national instrument which incorporates national priorities for sustainable development and lays out a roadmap for the implementation of those priorities. The Strategy aims at contributing to the realisation of the nation's economic, social and cultural potential through an innovative, knowledge-led approach, while being mindful of the need to conserve the integrity of the Seychelles natural environment and heritage for present and future generations.

The Strategy notably insists on the importance to foster adaptation efforts and investments in renewable energy. Resources needed for such goals, as well as protecting biodiversity, are estimated.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Action Plan for Climate Change Adaptation
DESCRIPTION:
The National Adaptation Action Plan (PANA) was prepared and led by the Ministry of Fisheries and Environment, with the help of UNDP and closely followed the guidelines of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) processes. ) related to the development of PANA.

The priority adaptation activities have been selected as follows:

  • Promotion of adaptation in the energy sector through monitoring precipitation and encouraging the development of other sustainable energies to guarantee energy security.
  • Promoting the development of climate-resistant urban and rural infrastructure in Equatorial Guinea, especially in vulnerable areas.
  • Improving resilience to climate change in the fishing sector towards better food security and livelihoods.
  • Promotion of sustainable management of water resources to improve access to water in urban and rural areas affected by poverty.
  • Sustainable management of the forests of Equatorial Guinea to maintain the integrity of the ecosystem and guarantee food security.
  • Catalyzing innovative financing in extractive industries towards long-term investments and approaches based on ecosystem adaptation in Equatorial Guinea.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Vision Djibouti 2035
DESCRIPTION:
In order to put in place the bases for controlled and controlled development, the Government is committed to developing a long-term vision for 2035, called "Djibouti 2035". The development of the Vision comes in the wake of the Economic Orientation Law 2001-2010 which helped to guide the Strategic Framework for Growth and Poverty Alleviation (PRSP) 2004-2006 and the National Initiative for Sustainable Development. Social Development (INDS) 2008-2012. It aims to provide the country with a generation planning tool for the next generation, which will now include strategic planning and sustainable development policies and strategies.


The document states that in 2035, Djibouti should be a "100 % green" country, using renewable energies for its supply, sustainably managing water, and adapting to climate change and related risks. Anti desertification measures are notable parts of the adaptation efforts that the document is formulating.
