PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Policy and Strategy on Disaster Risk Management
DESCRIPTION: The National Policy and Strategy on Disaster Risk Management aims to reduce disaster risks and potential damage caused by a disaster through a comprehensive and coordinated Disaster Risk Management System in the context of sustainable development. The policy focuses on ten directives, which include the Disaster Risk Management System, and Early Warning System, Official Disaster Declaration System, Resource mobilisation, Information and communication, among other directives. It recommends the creation of a Disaster Risk Management Council to lead the implementation of the policy, and of a Disaster Risk Management Coordination to support this task by coordinating different stakeholders. In addition, the Policy recognises as one of the cross-cutting issues the vulnerability caused by climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Report 2016
DESCRIPTION:
This report follows the previous 2011 Energy Report and focuses on the period beyond 2023 and how to achieve a carbon neutral energy supply system by 2050.


The energy policy is drafted on the basis of three main principles: 1) focus on CO2 reduction; 2) make the most of the economic opportunities that the energy transition offers and 3) integrate energy in spatial planning policy.


The Energy Report also announced the Energy Dialogue, an extensive public consultation in early 2016, to provide the opportunity for parties to share their views on the future energy system and to contribute to the design of the policy agenda. The Energy Dialogue also aimed to foster awareness of the energy transition in the Netherlands.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Supreme Decree No. 006-2020-MINAM. Establishes the High-Level Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 006-2020-MINAM. Crea Comisión de Alto Nivel de Cambio Climático)
DESCRIPTION:
The Decree Supreme establishing the Permanent Multisectoral Commission known as the High-Level Commission on Climate Change (CANCC) creates a formal, institutional mechanism for coordinating national climate policy in Peru. The instrument is grounded in constitutional provisions affirming the right to an adequate and balanced environment (Article 2, inciso 22 of the Constitution), as well as Peru’s international obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The creation of the CANCC responds directly to the mandate contained in Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, which establishes the need for a high-level intergovernmental body to support the formulation, review, and reporting of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) in alignment with international commitments. As a permanent body, the CANCC operates under the technical oversight of the Ministry of Environment and is presided over by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, reflecting its central role in cross-sectoral governance.

The Commission’s primary functions are defined in Article 3 and include: (i) proposing adaptation and mitigation measures within the framework of the National Strategy on Climate Change; (ii) supervising the development and updating of methodologies for greenhouse gas (GHG) emission projections; (iii) formulating recommendations for inclusion in the NDCs; (iv) assessing proposals from regional and local governments to inform progressive strengthening of national targets; (v) preparing and submitting technical reports on the NDCs every five years to the UNFCCC focal point; and (vi) evaluating recommendations from the National Commission on Climate Change (CNCC) and the Indigenous Peoples’ Platform for Climate Change, with a view to their implementation. The structure of the Commission ensures multisectoral representation, including government institutions, civil society, scientific bodies, and Indigenous organisations, thereby embedding principles of participatory governance, transparency, and accountability into the national climate policy architecture.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategic Roadmap for the Production and Processing of Agricultural Products
DESCRIPTION: This roadmap determines a strategic vision for the development of Azerbaijan’s agricultural sector. One of the nine strategic goals outlined in the strategy is the creation of mechanisms for the sustainable use of agricultural resources through the development of adequate adaptation and mitigation measures to prevent negative impacts of climate change on agriculture, and of performance indicators that meet environmental standards. This strategy further aims to reduce carbon emissions in the agricultural sector, create protective forest belts, and develop the production of environmentally friendly agricultural products.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Drought Plan. Together building resilience 2021-2025
DESCRIPTION:
The National Drought Plan - Together building resilience (“PNS”) of Ecuador provides a strategic framework to address the growing challenges of drought, which severely impact the country's agricultural production, hydroelectric power generation, and water and sanitation systems. Developed by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition (MAATE) in collaboration with the National Risk and Emergency Management Service (SNGRE), the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG), and the CIIFEN (International Research Center on El Niño Phenomenon) through the Euroclima+ project, the PNS aims to mitigate drought risks while enhancing resilience at the national level.

The plan highlights the devastating effects of drought, including crop and livestock losses, water shortages, and ecosystem imbalances, which exacerbate economic losses, food insecurity, and health issues. With a long-term perspective, it prioritises reducing drought risk through integrated planning, intersectoral coordination, and leveraging climate data to establish effective monitoring systems. By focusing on sectors like territorial planning, agriculture, water resources, risk management, and the environment, the plan addresses gaps in information and capacity, promoting evidence-based strategies and collaboration among public and private stakeholders, academia, and civil society.

The PNS aligns national policies with global frameworks and emphasises the development of innovative programs for risk reduction, response, and recovery. It sets objectives to strengthen the adaptive capacity of vulnerable communities, minimise economic losses, enhance drought monitoring, and generate evidence of the impacts of drought under current and future climate scenarios.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Climate Change Risks;Disaster Risk Management;Water Management

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Electrification Strategy
DESCRIPTION: This Strategy builds a secure, competitive and sustainable electricity supply for a historic climate transition. It lists 67 actions to achieve this result, including the following action: The guidance on backup power shall be reviewed and complemented with the possibility of using all fossil-free and renewable alternatives, such as biogas and fossil-free hydrogen in fuel cells or gas turbines.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution No. 136/09 on Technical regulation of energy efficiency in electrical equipment
DESCRIPTION: The Resolution promotes a rational and efficient use of electricity by laying down provisions for establishment and regular inspections of energy efficiency standards for electrical appliances and equipment. It sets out the details of the procedure for obtaining required energy labels and defines penalties for importing appliances not respecting the established standards, including potential prohibition of import of such appliances. The Annexes detail the requirements for energy efficiency of refrigerators, electrical ventilators, fluorescent lamps, electrical cooking appliances, microwaves, washing machines and air-conditioning systems.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: 2030 emissions reduction plan - Canada’s Next Steps for Clean Air and a Strong Economy
DESCRIPTION:
This plan is the first developed under the Canadian Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act. It develops sectoral projections of emissions reductions to 2030 with a view on achieving net-zero by 2050, details the government's low-carbon strategy and announces $9.1 billion in new federal investments. The government notably states its objective of reducing methane emissions from the fossil fuel industry. Progress under the plan will be reviewed in 2023, 2025, and 2027. Additional targets and plans will be developed for 2035 through to 2050.

Sectoral goals, funding and measures laid out in the document include the following: 

  • Homes and buildings: develop a $150 million Canada Green Buildings Strategy and provide $458.5 million of new investment to the Canada Greener Homes Loan program in order to reduce energy costs
  • Indigenous climate action: the Low Carbon Economy Fund is renewed ($2.2 billion funding) and include a dedicated $180 million Indigenous Leadership Fund
  • Energy systems: support regional growth, jobs and transformation of energy systems with a $25 million investment in Regional Strategic Initiatives
  • Electricity grid: aim of establishing a Pan-Canadian Grid Council to promote clean electricity infrastructure investments in coordination with provinces and utilities. Investment of $600 million in the Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program and $250 million to support predevelopment work for large clean electricity projects
  • Clean transport: reduction of emissions from light, and heavy vehicles. provision of $1.7 billion to extend the Incentives for Zero-Emission Vehicles (iZEV). $400 million in additional funding for zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) charging stations. The Canada Infrastructure Bank will also invest $500 million in ZEV charging and refueling infrastructure. Sales mandate to be put in place to ensure thresholds of clean vehicles sales. Development of a MHDV ZEV (medium- and heavy-duty zero emission vehicles) regulation. 
  • Industry: developing a carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) strategy, introducing an investment tax credit to incentivize the development and adoption of this important technology, and investing $194 million to expand the Industrial Energy Management System to support ISO 50001 certification, energy managers, cohort- based training, audits, and energy efficiency-focused retrofits for key small-to-moderate projects.
  • Agriculture: help the sector to adopt sustainable practices thanks to an investment of $470 million in the Agricultural Climate Solutions: On-Farm Climate Action Fund. Further to this, there will be a tripling of investment of the funding for the Agricultural Clean Technology Program (to $330 million) to support the purchase of energy-efficient equipment. $100 million will also be invested on science to support a sectoral transition to net-zero by 2050.
  • Environment: promote nature-based emissions reductions through an additional provision of $780 million for the Nature Smart Climate Solutions Fund.
  • carbon pricing: develop strategy to "guarantee the price of pollution", using legislative approaches and investment approaches, like carbon contracts for differences. Aims to see carbon price rising by $15 a year in order to reach $170/tonne by 2030.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the water sector (Water SASAP) 2018-2028
DESCRIPTION:
Saint Lucia’s Sectoral Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan for the Water Sector (Water SASAP) 2018-2028 seeks to reduce water-related risks induced by climate change and climate variability. The plan also aims to build the capacities of relevant actors for ensuring the sustainable management of water resources and services under current and future climatic conditions. The Water SASAP, funded with the support of the United Nations Development Programme’s (UNDP) Japan-Caribbean Climate Change Partnership (J-CCCP), builds on previous efforts and projects, and is the product of an in-depth contextual analysis and search for potential effective solutions to the country’s water-related challenges under a changing climate.
The plan consists of 70 adaptation measures deemed critical for improving water resource and service management, and for reducing water-mediated climate change impacts in the country. The measures, endorsed by relevant stakeholders, offer solutions to information, technical, institutional, financial, regulatory and policy limitations hampering adaptation in the water sector. In the Water SASAP, the adaptation measures are grouped under 13 strategic objectives and contribute to these four major expected outcomes:

- An enhanced enabling environment and improved behaviour for water-related climate adaptation action
- Increased water access, availability and quality 
- Increased water efficiency and conservation
- Strengthened preparedness to climate variability and extremes

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI
DESCRIPTION:
This strategy aims to create jobs, improve livelihoods and encourage balanced diets for the Japanese population. To do so, it aims to create smart food value chains, boost human development, boost research and development, and encourage innovation, notably in rural areas. It also sets specific measures to decarbonise the food sector and make it more resilient.

The document also 1) encourages circular economy with increased use of local resources, 2) aims to contribute to the 2050 goal of carbon neutrality via a reduction in the use of chemical pesticides/fertilisers, , and 3) seeks to disseminate energy saving/precision technologies.

On top of a sectoral carbon neutral target, the strategy sets the following goals by 2050:
- 50% reduction in risk-weighted use of chemical pesticides by dissemination of the Integrated Pest Management and newly-developed alternatives
- 30% reduction in chemical fertilizer use 
- Increase in organic farming to 1Mha
- At least 30% enhancement in productivity of food manufacturers (by 2030)
- Sustainable sourcing for import materials (by2030)
- 90% and more superior varieties and F1 plus trees in forestry seedling
- 100% of artificial seedling rates in aquaculture of Japanese eel, Pacific bluefin tuna, etc.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Infrastructure Investment Plan (NIIP)
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan consolidates and prioritises public infrastructure projects across sectors, evaluating their alignment with national strategic objectives, economic viability, and climate change adaptation. It covers covers infrastructure projects equal to or larger than $500,000 in value. This Plan covers the overall context in the Marshall Islands; the multi-criteria analysis and screening process for infrastructure projects; findings; funding assessment; and a roadmap for implementation. It consolidates the status of relevant projects.

Two out of 12 impact criteria in the multi-criteria analyse relate to environment and climate-change resilience priorities (namely, improve climate change adaptation and resilience, and strengthen disaster risk management and resilience).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation no. 70/2013; amended by no. 823/2013 (Regulation of Emissions Permits for Operators working in the EU Emission Trading System)
DESCRIPTION: The objective of this Regulation is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to ensure that operators of establishments within the scope of the EU Emissions Trading Scheme meet the conditions for participation in the system. This Regulation applies to the licensing allowance of operators falling within the scope of the EU trading system with allowances pursuant to Art. Act no. 70/2012 on climate, ie. on the conditions for issuing an emission permit, form and substance of a permit to issue, a procedure for issuing a permit to issue and changes to a permit to discharge. This Regulation was amended in September 2013 for operational reasons.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate change strategic plan for water resources and meteorology 2013-2017
DESCRIPTION: The Kingdom of Cambodia is considered one of the most water-abundant countries in the region. But climate change is expected to increase water management challenges, with less rainfall during the dry season and more during the wet season. Subsequently, this document establishes two distinct climate change strategic plans for water resources and for meteorology.Concerning the former, the plan seeks to ensure the sustainable use of water resources in adapting to climate change. Meanwhile, delivering timely and trusted weather and climatic information is the goal of the meteorological element. The plan also addresses cross-sectoral issues between water and climate change, and identifies climate change responses and risks in relation to water resources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Green Building Action Plan
DESCRIPTION: Under China’s 2013 Green Building Action Plan, "20% of all new buildings have to be green and that all newly built public buildings and affordable housing financed by the state have to be green certified" by 2015. "The 2-star and 3-star buildings will be eligible for state subsidies and local planning priorities. The local governments are required to develop their own action plans to at least be compatible with that of the central government." (Zhou, 2015)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Active Transport Fund
DESCRIPTION:
This Fund aims to encourage an increase in active transport through the upgrade of existing and construction of new bicycle and walking pathways across Australia. The intention is to increase road safety, reduce transport emissions, and build active and liveable communities. AU$100 million is available in funding.

Projects that reduce transport emissions are standalone projects which would enable people to choose active transport, or a combination of public and active transport, over private vehicle journeys. This supports the Australian Government’s commitment to achieving net zero by 2050. Examples of costs covered include re-alignment of pathways to improve safety, labour costs, and land acquisition costs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Environmental Foundation
DESCRIPTION:
The Environmental Foundation is a joint project, initiated by the Federal Ministry for Climate Protection, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology, along with the Ministry of Labour and social partners. This project aims to train at least 1000 workers in the field of environmental and climate protection in three years time.

The foundation began operations in April 2022, and aims to provide training to primarily unemployed people who do not have sufficient qualifications to find employment. This project aims to provide these job seekers with the required qualifications and training around the clean energy sector, e.g. installing PV panels, constructing wind turbines, and switching to modern heating systems.

The project has a total cost of EUR 17.5 million, of which EUR 10 million will come from the government’s labour budget and EUR 7.5 million will be supplied by companies. The educational foundation follows the 2021 Job.ReAct pilot programme in Austria, which offered jobs in ecological and sustainable sectors to unemployed people, co-funded by the European Union’s European Social Fund.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National regulation on subsidies (Regeling nationale EZK- en LNV-subsidies)
DESCRIPTION:
This document defines the legal framework to grant subsidies for technology policy, SME policy, and spatial economic policy, including with regard to renewable energy projects. It incorporates the mission of the Climate Accord for climate and energy for raw materials, products, and processes in industry to be climate neutral, and at least 80 per cent circular by 2050. This includes multi-year mission driven innovation programmes with subsidy schemes for research, innovative developments, in relation to the following programmes: 

  1. MMIP 6 - Closing industrial value chains, with a particular focus on investments in industrial chains that include waste streams. The three sub programmes are 1) circular plastics 2) bio-based raw materials for products and fueling transport 3) circular non-ferrous metals 
  2. MMIP 7 - A CO2-free industrial heat system
  3. MMIP 8 - Maximum electrification and radically renewed processes (aims to develop knowledge and cost-effective innovations for climate-neutral production by 2050)
  4. CCUS - Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage, in which capturing, transporting, reusing and permanent storage of CO is central
  5. Other CO2 reduction measures, including studies that cover CO2 reducing measures in industry other than those listed in programme 1 to 4
  6. Hydrogen and green chemistry (GreenPowerNL)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 82/2015/QH13 on Natural Resources and Environment of Sea and Islands
DESCRIPTION:
Pursuant to article 1, this Law regulates general management of natural resources and environment rights, obligations and responsibilities of agencies, organisations and individuals in general management and protection of natural resources and the environment.

The Law comprises 10 Chapters:
  1. General Provisions
  2. Strategy;
  3. Fundamental investigation and scientific research;
  4. General planning;
  5. Management;
  6. Control of pollution, coping with spill of oil, toxic chemicals and sea dumping;
  7. General monitoring and supervision, information and database system;
  8. International cooperation;
  9. Responsibilities for general management; and 
  10. Implementary provisions.

Notably, the Law includes several references to climate change.

For instance, article 4(3) advances increasing efficiency in coordination with pollution control, prevention and coping with sea and island environment problems, climate change and rising sea levels. 

Furthermore, articles 9(1)(b) and 9(2)(a) mention as principles and foundations for the formulation of the strategy for exploitation and sustainable use of natural resources and environment coping with climate change and rising sea levels.

Chapter III; Chapter IV; and Chapter V all consider adaptation to climate change and rising sea levels in various provisions.

Lastly, pursuant to article 72(1)(dd), Vietnam shall seek international cooperation regarding these two issues.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Circular Spatial and Building Management Development Programme for the period 2021-2030
DESCRIPTION: The Circular Spatial and Building Management Development Programme recognises climate change mitigation and adaptation as major challenges for Croatia, and aims to mainstream circular principles in building management and spatial development up to 2030. Goals include greater energy efficiency, integration of renewable energy sources, greater use of recycled material, reduced building waste, increased building lifespans, and revitalisation of unused buildings, among others. The programme calls for stronger data collection infrastructure, improved public awareness of circularity, and general capacity building in the construction sector and others.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electrify Africa Act
DESCRIPTION: The law legislates the US initiative and goal to provide access to power for at least 50 million people in sub-Saharan Africa by 2020, and to enable the installation of an additional 20,000 megawatts of electricity capacity by 2020.The law supports a broad variety of power generation options, including oil, coal and natural gas, hydroelectric power, wind, solar, geothermal and other renewable sources of power, as well as energy efficiency and distribution and transmission systems upgrades. The Electricity Africa Act however particularly promotes renewable energy projects, as the law requires the U.S. government to promote the spread of distributed renewable energy in sub-Saharan Africa, including off-grid lighting and power. The priority given to off-grid generation is an endorsement of existing efforts, already carried out by a sub-initiative of Power Africa Initiative (see below).To create lasting infrastructures, the law seeks to promote policies to facilitate private financing and public-private partnerships, allow independent producers' participation in electricity markets, and encourage other regulatory reforms in the power sector. The law calls on the US to partner with sub-Saharan African countries, international and regional financial institutions and the private sector to meet the above goals and implement a strong monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.The Electricity Africa Act does not allocate new funds to the US agencies, but builds on and backs the Power Africa Initiative, launched in 2013 with a goal of doubling access to electricity across sub-Saharan Africa. The Initiative commits the US to US$7 billion support to the energy sector in sub-Saharan Africa.The law requires the President of the U.S. to submit to the US Senate, within 6 months of the law's enactment, a report outlining a multiyear strategy for reaching the objectives of the law.The Electricity Africa Act also directs U.S. government agencies, such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), the US Trade and Development Agency, the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC), and the Millennium Challenge Corporation, to prioritize loans, grants and technical support for power generation and transmission projects in sub-Saharan Africa. The President of the U.S. is allowed by the law to establish an interagency working group to coordinate efforts among the agencies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution 1156/04 on National Programme for Biofuels
DESCRIPTION: In 2004, the Ministry of Agriculture created the National Programme for Biofuels (Resolution1156/04), which defines objectives to promote the use of biofuels as an alternative to fossil fuels. A central part of the programme is to support rural development in the execution of biofuels projects (biodiesel and bioethanol).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Bulgaria's electricity transmission network development plan for 2023-2032
DESCRIPTION: The Bulgartransgaz TYNDP 2023–2032 supports the integration of renewable energy and decarbonisation by preparing the gas transmission system for a gradual transition from natural gas to low-carbon and renewable gases. The plan foresees infrastructure investments that enable the transport of hydrogen and hydrogen–natural gas blends, and support the role of gas networks as a balancing and backup solution for variable renewable electricity (especially solar and wind). It also aligns network development with national and EU climate targets.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act of 17 December 2020 on the promotion of electricity production in marine wind farms, last amended by Act of 9 October 2025 (Offshore Wind Act)
DESCRIPTION: The Act of 17 December 2020 on promoting electricity generation in offshore wind farms aims to boost the production of renewable energy from wind in the Baltic sea, in accordance with EU regulations.The Amendment brought by the Act of 9 October 2025 aims to "unblock" the second phase of Polish offshore development. By removing rigid administrative bottlenecks (like the 50m placement rule) and adding the intervention auction fail-safe, the government aimed to ensure that Poland meets its target of 5.9 GW by 2030 and 18 GW by 2040.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Technical analysis of the first biennial update report of Belize submitted on 5 May 2021. Summary report by the team of technical experts
DESCRIPTION: Technical analysis of the first biennial update report of Belize submitted on 5 May 2021. Summary report by the team of technical experts, Technical Analysis Summary Report from UNFCCC Secretariat in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Honduras Biogas Roadmap
DESCRIPTION: The Honduras Biogas Roadmap promotes biogas development nationally as a tool to promote energy security and contribute to net emissions mitigation goals. It also notes synergies across sectors, including biogas production slurry as a fertiliser contributing to climate resilience in agriculture.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation on the adoption of the Plan for the air protection, protection of the ozone layer and climate change mitigation in the Republic of Croatia for the period 2013-2017
DESCRIPTION: This regulation adopts the Plan for Airspace, Ozone Layer and Mitigation of the Climate Change in the Republic of Croatia for the Period 2013 - 2017. This Plan defines the objectives and priorities for the protection of air, ozone layer and mitigation of climate change in the Republic of Croatia in a five year period. This document describes into detail the purpose of the plan and its legal and economic implications.
KEYWORDS: Carbon Pricing;Energy Demand;Energy Supply;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
DESCRIPTION: The current Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela was passed in 1999. The National Electoral Council reported tonight that 71% of votes were in favor of the new charter while 28.79 percent were against it. The turnout was 44.4% of Venezuela's 11 million registered voters; this low turnout was attributed to a certain extent to torrential rains around the period that the referendum took place. This Constitution has since been amended once, in 2009. In 2017, Maduro’s government started moving towards creating a new Constitution, although this caused widespread objection objections and it still has not led to a new charter to replace the 1999 Constitution. Within the current Constitution’s environmental rights chapter, Chapter IX, develops a right to sustainable development and establishes that the State shall protect a series of environmental areas. Moreover, article 127 establishes a fundamental duty of the State to ensure a pollution-free environment where climate, among other environmental topics, receives special protection. This provision states the following: “It is the right and duty of each generation to protect and maintain the environment for its own benefit and that of the world of the future. Everyone has the right, individually and collectively, to enjoy a safe, healthful and ecologically balanced life and environment. The State shall protect the environment, biological and genetic diversity, ecological processes, national parks and natural monuments, and other areas of particular ecological importance. The genome of a living being shall not be patentable, and the field shall be regulated by the law relating to the principles of bioethics. It is a fundamental duty of the State, with the active participation of society, to ensure that the populace develops in a pollution-free environment in which air, water, soil, coasts, climate, the ozone layer and living species receive special protection, in accordance with law.”

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 2010-22 Regulating the Biofuels Industry
DESCRIPTION:
The Law aims to develop the biofuels sector, establishing norms and conditions for the production and exploitation of biofuels in the national territory as well as for international co-operation. More broadly, the law aims to contribute to environmental protection and increase the value of forest and agricultural resources. Overall, the law expects to increase access to energy, promoting economic growth and social welfare. The law covers all components of biofuels sector, from production to processing, storage to transport and distribution.
 
 It grants biofuels the fiscal benefits established under the Great Agricultural Offensive for Food and Abundance Programme. Thus, revenues generated from biofuel activities are exempted from taxation for a period of five years. The purchase of seeds and equipment for the production and export of biofuels are exempted from value added taxes for an indeterminate period of time.
 
 According to the new law, biofuels projects are eligible to certifications under the CDM. The ownership over these carbon credits should be negotiated between the State and the 'promoters'.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law prohibiting coal in electricity production (Wet verbod op kolen)
DESCRIPTION:
In order to meet the 2030 climate targets, the Netherlands must emit less CO2. For this reason, on December 22, 2021, the Dutch cabinet restricted emissions from coal-fired power stations by limiting their operations to no more than 35% of their maximum capacity. The government estimates it will result in a reduction in CO2 emissions at coal-fired power stations of approximately 6-7 megatons "in the short term". The amendment to the Coal Act came into effect on 1 January, 2022 and will apply until the end of 2024.

This law implements rules relating to the generation of electricity using coal, in order to organise an effective coal phase out by 2030. Article 2 states that it is prohibited to generate electricity in a production installation using coal. Coal-fired power plants do not have to close down. Instead, they are allowed to switch to other, cleaner fuels to generate electricity, such as biomass, biofuels, and hydrogen. The ban applies to all 4 coal-fired power plants in the Netherlands, but the transition period differs.

  • The Amer power plant in Geertruidenberg is subject to the ban from 1 January, 2025. This power plant is more polluting than the 3 other modern power plants, as it produces less electricity with the same amount of coal and thus has a lower output. At the same time, this coal-fired power plant already runs largely on biomass.
  • For the other three, more modern power plants at Eemshaven and Maasvlakte, the ban applies from 1 January, 2030.
KEYWORDS: Coal;Coal Phase Out;Fossil Fuels Curbing Measures;Limits On Fossil Fuels

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law n. 87/ 2015 - Electricity Law
DESCRIPTION:
The Electricity Law provides for a reform and opening of the Egyptian electricity market, and restructures the role of the Electricity Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency. The Agency is now, among others matters, responsible for regulating the development and encouragement of renewable energy production and use, and increased electricity use efficiency, as well as issuing renewable source certificates that could be traded upon issuance of regulations detailing the process.
The Law also contributes to increased competitiveness of the electricity market and opening up for distributed (including clean energy) production, by:






  1. allowing for private sector participation in electricity generation and distribution;

  2. setting out the framework for market liberalisation through de-monopolising generation and distribution activities;

  3. restructuring the roles of the Egyptian Electric Utility & Consumer Protection Agency and the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company, in particular in relation to ensuring freedom of competition in the power sector market; and

  4. codifying the fundamentals of permitting and licensing, including for renewable electricity production.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Uganda Biennial update report. BUR1
DESCRIPTION: Uganda. Biennial update report (BUR). BUR 1., Biennial Update Report from Uganda in 2019

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree No. 2016-0006 P-RM instituting the National Mechanism for Early Warning and Security Risk Response
DESCRIPTION: This decree establishes the National Early Warning and Security Risk Response Mechanism. The National Early Warning and Response Mechanism's mission is to collect information and data on threats, good governance, security and peace in Mali, to alert the Government, to suggest appropriate responses for the identified threats, to monitor and / or coordinate the implementation of the responses agreed to by the Government.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Marine Transport (Emissions Control) Act, 2024-25
DESCRIPTION:
This Act contains provisions on the prevention of air pollution from shipping activities; energy efficiency for ships; nomination of surveyors and certifying of certificates; emissions reduction measures for vessels; fuel options and fuel compliance; national level maritime energy governance; marine diesel engines; engine international air pollution prevention certificates; and exhaust gas cleaning systems operations.

The Barbados Maritime Transport Administration has the duty to keep abrest of activities of the IMO on shipping and climate change and adopt appropriate programmes, strategies and initiatives to promote IMO led activities at the national level.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National action plan of the Republic of Tajikistan on prevention and mitigation of the impact caused by sand and dust storms (SDS) for 2022-2030
DESCRIPTION: The overall goal of the National Action Plan is to reduce the existing and prevent the emergence of sand and dust storm risks, associated with the sand and dust storms through building national capacities for their management.The most important challenge related to sand and dust storms is desertification, based on the reasons for its formation and further development of the process, it would be possible to address the issues and problems related to sand and dust storms.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Onshore Wind Energy Strategy
DESCRIPTION:
The strategy aims to accelerate deployment of onshore wind energy in Germany and includes measures at the federal, state, and local levels including:

  • simplifying and accelerating consenting processes for projects,
  • improving the profitability of plants at locations with less potential,
  • increasing tender volumes and expansion paths, and
  • making it clear that renewables are in the overriding public interest and serve public safety.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 007/2014 of August 1, 2014 relating to the protection of the environment in the Gabonese Republic
DESCRIPTION: Law No. 007/2014 aims to harmonise sustainable social and economic development with environmental protection, enshrining elements of environmental protection in law and providing clear responsibilities for the Ministry of Environment. It establishes the role of climate change mitigation within environmental impact assessments, creates a greenhouse gas inventory system and enforces energy efficiency standards.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Forestry Code (Law No. 331/2024)
DESCRIPTION:
One of the principles of sustainable forest management stated in this Code is strengthening the resilience of forests and increasing their contribution to limiting the effects of climate change. The Code mandates that forest status indicators must include resilience to climate change.

There is a section on limiting the effects of climate change, which allows the owner to implement specific forest management measures to increase the amount of carbon dioxide sequestered by stands in forests for which there is a valid forest management plan. The relevant authority shall finance national programmes aimed at increasing the amount of carbon sequestered through the use of wood in the construction and furniture industries.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Minerals Strategy
DESCRIPTION: In 2025, the government launched the Minerals Strategy for New Zealand, and a Critical Minerals List that includes 37 minerals to guide the development of New Zealand's minerals sector until 2040.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: GX Promotion Strategy (Strategy to Promote the Transition to a Decarbonized Growth-Oriented Economic Structure)
DESCRIPTION: The GX Strategy is based on the aspects of resolving the energy security challenges that Japan faces and the pursuit of efforts to limit the average global temperature increase to 1.5°C following the Paris Agreement. The Strategy was release following the enactment of the GX Promotion Act and the GX Decarbonization Power Supply Act. The GX Promotion Strategy approved by the Cabinet in July 2023 classified the main government initiatives into the following two categories: (1) GX initiatives based on the basic premise of securing a stable energy supply and energy self-sufficiency including using renewable energy and nuclear power; and (2) the realisation and implementation of the "Growth-Oriented Carbon Pricing Concept", including bold upfront investment support through "GX Economic Transition Bonds" and other means, upfront GX investment incentives through carbon pricing, and the use of new financial instruments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Senegal National Communication. NC3
DESCRIPTION: Senegal. National Communication (NC). NC 3., National Communication from Senegal in 2016

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Risk Management Strategy for Security Threats of the Slovak Republic
DESCRIPTION:
The vision of the Strategy is to consolidate the civil protection and crisis management system as a tool based on an integrated approach to risk management and multi-sectoral cooperation. It gives priority to the protection of life and health of persons, property, the environment, natural heritage and social values, and the associated need for society to adapt to the negative effects of climate change. Preventive measures, planning and use of modern technologies, training, comprehensive rescue and search equipment and crisis communication, as well as information sharing and quality education in this area, create the preconditions for reducing vulnerability and increasing resilience of the population and the territory of the Slovak. The strategy aims to improve the institutional, professional, knowledge, technological, competence and legislative framework as a tool for achieving resilience and better coordination of risk management, targeted accountability of actors, diversified funding, early warning and public information, including an adequate response to climate change, as well as the subsequent use of lessons learned from emergencies and crisis situations in planning for reducing the impact of hazards.

To effectively build environmental and socio-economic resilience to climate change at the regional level, a proactive approach and long-term integrated planning are needed that addresses existing aspects of sustainable development, taking into account increased vulnerability, and leads to the economic development of the region. Key risk reduction activities are the assessment and analysis of damages and the related investments and subsequent forms of financing, including lump sum budget measures to ensure prevention and preparedness in each municipality, the establishment of special fees, taxes or tax disincentives in relation to regional development, climate change or energy.

Since specific financial proposals for the allocation of resources for prevention and adaptation to the risks of security threats associated with climate change can only be implemented on the basis of damage assessments and long-term estimates of potential damage due to ongoing trends of disasters, crisis situations and emergencies, it is important to ensure a methodology for damage assessment also in cooperation with rural and municipal authorities. To this end, the introduction of a unified damage planning system is envisaged. In addition, we plan to involve scientific research capacities in the assessment of potential damage, with a view to planning long-term investments in reducing the risk of security threats associated with climate change.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Climate Security;Disaster Risk Management;Finance;National Security;Research And Development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Disaster Risk Management Strategy 2016-2030
DESCRIPTION: The National Strategy for Risk and Disaster Management (SNGRC) is applicable during the 2016-2030 period. Its vision is a nation resilient to shocks, protected from all damage, in its social, cultural dimension , economic and environmental for sustainable development. The overall objective of the document is to make risk and disaster management a pillar of sustainable development. The strategy also aims to eliminate hunger, food insecurity and malnutrition. The goal is to make food production and livelihood systems more resilient to promote food and nutrition security for communities in the face of climate hazards.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Statement by the Russian Federation on the components of the Global Stocktake outcomes
DESCRIPTION: Submission to the Global Stocktake from Russian Federation in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree of 15-03-2017 approving the Regulation of financial aid for electric mobility and for the improvement of energy efficiency and safety of the national car park
DESCRIPTION: This decree approves the regulation on financial aid for electric mobility and for the improvement of energy efficiency and safety of the national car park. It establishes and regulates the criteria, requirements and procedures necessary to access financial aid for electric mobility, the improvement of energy efficiency and the safety of the car fleet, in order to promote a reduction in energy consumption.This document was amended by decrees 19-6-2019 and 11-3-2020.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution No. 33/2015 of the Council of Ministers on the Maritime Policy of the Republic of Poland until 2020 (with a perspective until 2030)
DESCRIPTION: The Maritime Policy of the Republic of Poland until 2020 (with a perspective to 2030) integrates environmental protection and climate action into the strategic development of the maritime sector. A central focus is the promotion of maritime transport as one of the most eco-friendly ways to move cargo, with specific goals to develop "green ships" featuring ecological propulsion systems. The policy emphasizes the expansion of offshore renewable energy, specifically targeting the development of offshore wind farms, wave energy, and current power to diversify the national energy mix. For instance, it set an objective for offshore wind farms to reach a capacity of 500 MW by 2020. To address the physical impacts of climate change, the policy outlines rigorous coastal protection measures, including the stabilization of the coastline and the enhancement of flood defense systems for coastal areas.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 18.621/2019 creating the Public and Permanent National Emergency System
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of this law is to establish a National Emergency System, which is a permanent public system aimed at protecting people, significant assets, and the environment in the event of potential or actual disasters. This is achieved through the joint coordination of the State and the proper use of available public and private resources, in order to foster conditions for sustainable national development. The Decree 65/020 approved its regulation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Marshall Islands Resilience and Trust Fund Act 2022
DESCRIPTION:
This Act provides for the creation, governance, management, legal and financial provisions for a Marshall Islands Resilience and Trust Fund, to ensure that the Marshall Islands adapts and builds resilience to the impacts of climate change and endures and survives as a viable and recognised people, Government and nation into the future. This Fund is focused on collecting, catalysing and growing financial resources dedicated solely to adaptation and resilience.

The initial contribution by the Government is USD 3,000,000 (USD is the currency used in the Marshall Islands), with a target date of end-2026 to reach the minimum amount of USD 20,000,000 in the Fund's capitalisation phase. The Government and Fund Board shall pursue new and innovative financing mechanisms and ventures with diplomatic and development partners.

The Board shall develop and approve a Reinvestment and Distribution Policy, specifying the amount to be distributed to the Government at the end of each financial year for the following financial year, to finance priority adaptation- and resilience-related investments and initiatives. The Advisory Committee shall advise the Board on distribution decisions and the progress of adaptation and resilience-building efforts supported by the Fund.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Combined Heat and Power Act (KWKG)
DESCRIPTION: The law on cogeneration revises the 2002 Combined Heat and Power Act to encourage combined heat and power (CHP) generation plants using renewable energies, district heating, heat and cold storage, and reduce CHP from hard coal and brown coal unless necessary. It details how the financial support for existing and new installations, which was increased from €750 million to €1.5 billion, will be used.Subsidies are limited in time and added to market-based electricity price. Net electricity from cogeneration plants should increase to 110 TW/h by 2020 and 120 TW/h by 2025. Projects concerned by the scheme are newly constructed and "modernised" plants with a focus on increased energy efficiency. Subsidies focus on plants feeding the national supply grid, but there are exceptions for sites with a capacity under 100 kW and installations used by industrial consumers. Additional incentives are granted to plants subject to the Greenhouse Gas Emission Trading Law, and projects which disposed of coal or lignite receive a bonus of €0.6 cents/kWh over the entire funding period.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
DESCRIPTION: This plan (Plan Sectorial de Mitigación y Adaptación de Energía) outlines the mitigation measures needed for Chile’s energy sector to meet its NDC and other sectoral targets, namely the 80% of electricity generation from renewables by 2030 and 2040 coal phase-out for the energy sector. It identifies policy measures across electricity generation, electrification, and energy efficiency. It estimates energy efficiency measures to contribute to around 7% of Chile’s cumulative emissions reductions by 2050. The plan also emphasises developing Chile’s green hydrogen economy and includes a target for green hydrogen to make up 15% of final non-electric energy consumption by 2035 and 70% by 2050.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National intelligent transport system (ITS) action plan
DESCRIPTION: The national ITS action plan identifies the national priorities until 2017. It analyses the state of the Art of ITS deployment in Italy and identifies strategies and policies to be undertaken, for each of the priority areas included in the EU Directive. It is currently under discussion by all the involved stakeholder in order to identify and launch concrete action for the deployment of the Action Plan.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: PM Decision 46/2014 providing for Natural Disaster Forecasting, Warning and Communication
DESCRIPTION: The PM Decision No.46/2014 provides for natural disaster forecasting, warning and communication in service of prevention, response and remedy of natural disasters. The natural disasters concerned are storms, tropical depression, floods on the rivers in the territory of Vietnam, earthquakes, tsunamis, heavy rains, flash floods and landslides,etc.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Plan for Disaster Risk Management and Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector 2016-2022
DESCRIPTION: This document seeks to develop Paraguay's capacity to adapt to climate change and react to natural disasters over the period 2016-2022. Its objective is to reduce the vulnerability of the agricultural sector to disaster risks exacerbated by climate variability and climate change by strengthening the institutionalisation of risk management in the sector, improving information mechanisms and monitoring of agro-climatic risk, the implementation of risk prevention and mitigation actions and preparation for an effective response.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Millennium Challenge Corporation Climate Action Plan
DESCRIPTION:
The Millennium Challenge Corporation Climate Action Plan was published according to Executive Order 14008 and contains a number of provisions for improving adaptation and increasing resilience to climate change.

As of March 2025, the status of this entry is likely impacted by the Trump-Vance administration’s regulatory rollback on climate action. To learn more about the rollback, visit the Sabin Center’s Climate Backtracker.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution E 202/2016 (renewable energy projects)
DESCRIPTION: This Resolution sets out a new framework for renewable energy projects, retaining selected conditions of particular previous projects while introducing new conditions. The projects must commit a minimum level of energy supply defines the prices of electricity in relation to supply contracts, to adjust the prices to the reality of the market.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Kyrgyzstan National Communication. NC4
DESCRIPTION: Kyrgyzstan National Communication. NC4

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution 355/2021 - Comprehensive Climate Change Management Plan for the Agricultural Sector (PIGCCS)
DESCRIPTION:
The objective of the Comprehensive Climate Change Management Plan for the Agricultural Sector (PIGCCS) is to identify, coordinate, and guide the implementation of measures that the agricultural sector must develop to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and reduce its vulnerability to climate change. Additionally, this plan aims to increase sector productivity, contribute to food security, improve the well-being of rural populations, and preserve the natural resources that sustain it.

This document consists of eight chapters. The general objective is to align the sector's efforts to mitigate GHG emissions while enhancing productivity, ensuring food security, supporting rural well-being, and protecting the natural foundation of agriculture.

The strategic topics defined for the plan’s development include:

  • Scientific data and traditional knowledge for decision-making.
  • Transitioning agricultural production toward sustainability.
  • Integrating disaster risk management with climate change adaptation.
  • Developing climate financing mechanisms and recognizing the differentiated impacts of climate change on men and women.
  • Strengthening and creating new leadership at national and local levels.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act 1093/1996 (Forest Act), last amended by Act 448/2026
DESCRIPTION: Forest Act (1093/1996) establishes the framework for the economically, ecologically and socially sustainable management and use of forests in Finland, while ensuring sustainable timber production and the conservation of forest biodiversity. It sets requirements for forest regeneration and management, regulates felling and related notifications, and protects biologically important habitats and their characteristics.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: New energy consumption subsidy scheme
DESCRIPTION:
Argentina has introduced a new, targeted energy subsidy system that replaces the previous income-based segmentation with a unified scheme aimed at households requiring assistance to cover essential energy consumption. The system provides a baseline subsidy of around 50% on a limited “basic consumption block” of electricity and gas, with any consumption above that threshold charged at full cost.

For electricity, the subsidy applies year-round but only up to a capped level of monthly consumption (higher in peak-demand months and lower in milder seasons). For natural gas, subsidies are seasonal, concentrated in winter months (April–September), with no support during periods of low demand.

The scheme also introduces a temporary additional subsidy (up to 25%) during 2026, which gradually declines over the year to ease the transition to higher tariffs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Walking and cycling promotion program
DESCRIPTION: This program aims to boost walking and cycling's modal shares in the country.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Technical analysis of the first biennial update report of Panama submitted on 14 December 2018. Summary report by the team of technical experts
DESCRIPTION: Technical analysis of the first biennial update report of Panama submitted on 14 December 2018. Summary report by the team of technical experts, Technical Analysis Summary Report from UNFCCC Secretariat in 2019

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Petroleum and Other Minerals Development (Prohibition of Onshore Hydraulic Fracturing) Act 15/2017
DESCRIPTION:
This document amends the Petroleum and Other Minerals Development Act 1960 to prohibit the exploration for and extraction of onshore petroleum by means of hydraulic fracturing. The decision is notably motivated by climate change mitigation motivations.

The Climate Action and Low Carbon Development (Amendment) Bill of 2021 extends the ban to all licences for new oil and natural gas exploration.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Presidential Decree establishing the Department of Climate Change (No. 85 of 2021)
DESCRIPTION:
This Decree renames the Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation to the "Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change" and establishes the Department of Climate Change to adopt measures relating to climate change and the depletion of the ozone layer, determine policies for green development, conduct negotiations, and ensure coordination with other organisations. It sets out the organisation structure, duties, powers and responsibilities of the Department of Climate Change.

The Coordination Council, composed of various Ministers and Presidents of stakeholder organisations such as business associations, is responsible for determining, monitoring, and evaluating plans, policies, strategies, and actions related to climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Order No. 2014-0229-MEA-SG
DESCRIPTION: This Order establishes within the Ministry of the Environment a Steering Committee of the Natural Resources Management Project in the Context of Climate Change in Mali. It sets the terms of reference, powers, composition and operating methods of the Steering Committee.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Strategy 2050
DESCRIPTION: This strategy aims to implement the new goals set out in the Energy Act's 2018 revision. It seeks to reduce energy consumption per capita, decarbonise the supply and improve energy efficiency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for the Blue Economy
DESCRIPTION:
This Strategy covers the management of the national maritime space and its resources and sustainable socio-economic development, creating the conditions for attracting public and private investment. It covers maritime and coastal activities, including fishing and aquaculture, maritime transport, port activities, coastal tourism, energy, shipbuilding and repair, seawater desalination, water treatment, non-economic telecommunications, including the protection of natural heritage, surveillance and monitoring of the marine and coastal environment, surveillance, control, and monitoring of marine activities, as well as scientific research.

This Strategy contains actions to respond to the climate challenge, in the marine areas and coastal infrastructures, and in reducing atmospheric emissions from maritime transport.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Côte d'Ivoire National Communication. NC2
DESCRIPTION: Côte d'Ivoire National Communication. NC2 from 2010

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 12.587/2012 establishing the guidelines of the National Urban Mobility Policy
DESCRIPTION: This law establishes the guidelines of the National Urban Mobility Policy in line with broad principles of sustainable development, and takes other measures.Art 23.VII states that the federative entities may use, among other instruments for the management of the transport system and urban mobility, monitoring and control of local and greenhouse gas emissions from motorized transport modes, allowing access to certain roads to be restricted due to the criticality of pollution emission indices;

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategic Plan for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development 2025-2030
DESCRIPTION: The Strategic Plan for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development 2025-2030 provides a five-year vision to guide urban development efforts in Eswatini. The plan aims to modernise housing systems, urban governance and emergency preparedness while promoting sustainability and inclusivity. It enshrines climate resilience as a core principle of urban development going forward, using green building practices and building capacity to identify the areas most in need of climate-adaptive infrastructure.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Multimodal Electric Mobility Master Plan for Urban Public Transport and Logistics
DESCRIPTION:
In 2023, the Multimodal Electric Mobility Master Plan for Urban Public Transport and Logistics in Paraguay was developed. This is a public policy tool complementary to the National Electromobility Strategy and will establish general and specific guidelines for a transition to the electrification of public transport and logistics in Paraguay. This comes as a commitment to supporting international efforts to reduce GHG emissions on the planet by replacing hydrocarbons with a clean energy source. At the same time, this transformation will allow Paraguay to take advantage of its 100% renewable generation matrix, reducing its dependence on petroleum derivatives.

The master plan has a vision to put Paraguay as a regional benchmark in promoting and driving electric mobility, with a sustainable, circular and comprehensive model, with 100% electric vehicles in public transport systems and 50% electric vehicles in logistics transport by 2040.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: European Union National Inventory Report (NIR). 2026
DESCRIPTION: European Union National Inventory Report (NIR). 2026 - (Annual European Union greenhouse gas inventory 1990-2024 and inventory document 2026)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategy on Climate Change and Health Adaptation 2018 – 2025 and action plan 2018 – 2020
DESCRIPTION: This document has been identified in Lao's updated NDC, however no further documentation is available.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: 2050 Climate Strategy
DESCRIPTION:
The Tile Til Eo 2050 Climate Strategy "Lighting the way" makes a number of recommendations to achieve the country's objectives of net zero emissions by 2050 and 100 % renewable energy. These include periodic revision of GHG emissions reductions, specific goals such as in the waste sector, and a planning of new climate policies to adopt, such as a National Adaptation Plan by the end of 2019. This Strategy shall be periodically reviewed by the authorities over the period.

The document further promotes 1) the use of public transport, 2) efforts to phase out the use of kerosene for lighting and strengthen existing institutional arrangements to reduce GHGs from cooking and lighting, 3) the establishment of a long-term finance strategy to implement this strategy, 4) the prioritisation of capacity-building in all sectors, and 5) the inclusion of health considerations in the National Adaptation Plan.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Protection from the Negative Impacts of Climate Change
DESCRIPTION: This law sets the legal framework for adaptation and mitigation actions in the country, as well with regard to the protection of the ozone layer. It further lays out a strategy for low-carbon development and a climate change adaptation plan.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ordinance on Climate Disclosures, made under the Swiss Code of Obligations
DESCRIPTION:
This Ordinance specifies the reporting obligations of section six of title thirty-two of the Swiss Code of Obligations with regard to climate issues on the basis of the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). 

Public companies, banks and insurance companies with 500 or more employees and at least CHF 20 million in total assets or more than CHF 40 million in turnover are obliged to report publicly on climate issues. Public reporting involves disclosures not only on the financial risk that a company incurs as a result of climate-related activities, but also on the impact of the company's business activities on the climate. In addition, the company has to describe the reduction targets it has set for its direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions, as well as how it plans to implement them.

The Ordinance enters into force on 1 January 2024.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ministerial Order 2020-916 On the Establishment of an National Inventory for Atmospheric Pollutants
DESCRIPTION: The order establishes and regulates a national inventory for atmospheric pollutants, including greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide. It assigns ministerial responsibilities and defines a basic recording framework to guide operation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act on the Creation and Facilitation of Use of Smart Grids
DESCRIPTION: The Act aims to create smart grids and to facilitate them to create green growth and to deal with climate change. The government is to develop and implement a 5-year plan for creating and facilitating the use of smart grids. Research and development resources are to be provided for. The Act also details requirements to establish smart grids, and deals with information use and protection. The Act is Supported by a presidential decree from 2011 (Enforcement Decree of Act on the Creation and Facilitation of Use of Smart Grids).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Philippine Disaster Reduction and Management Act (RA 10121)
DESCRIPTION:
The Act shifted the policy environment and the way the country deals with disasters from mere response to preparedness. RA 10121 provides a comprehensive, all-hazard, multi-sectoral, inter-agency, and community-based approach to disaster risk management through the formulation of the National Disaster Risk Management Framework.
 
 A National Disaster Risk Management Plan (NDRMP) is being formulated, developed, and implemented as the master plan that will provide the strategies, organisation, tasks of concerned agencies and local government units, and other guidelines in dealing with disasters or emergencies. Through this plan, a coherent, integrated, efficient, and responsive disaster risk management at all levels will hopefully be achieved.
 
 The law also promotes the development of capacities in disaster management at the individual, organisational, and institutional levels. A very important feature of this law is its call for the mainstreaming of disaster risk reduction in physical and land-use planning, budget, infrastructure, education, health, environment, housing, and other sectors.
 
 RA 10121 also recognises local risk patterns and trends and decentralisation of resources and responsibilities and thus encourages the participation of NGOs, private sectors, community-based organisations, and community members in disaster management. It inhibits the full participation of the Local Government Units (LGUs) and communities in governance. The approach tends to be 'response-oriented' or 'reactive.' This is evidenced by the widespread emphasis on post-disaster relief and short-term preparedness, such as forecasting and evacuation, rather than on mitigation and post- disaster support for economic recovery.
 
 Moreover, the Act mandates the establishment of a Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (DRRMO) in every province, city and municipality, and a Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committee (BDRRMC) in every barangay.
 
 The Strategic National Action Plan on Disaster Risk Reduction for 2009-2019 aims to enhance the capacities of Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Councils.
 
 Finally, RA10121 provides for the calamity fund to be used in support of disaster risk reduction or mitigation, prevention, and preparedness activities for the potential occurrence of disasters and not just for response, relief, and rehabilitation efforts.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Slovakia Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
DESCRIPTION:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes the following goals: 1) to build a competitive, low-carbon economy by the optimal use of renewable energy sources, nuclear energy, decarbonised gases and new technologies; 2) to promote energy efficiency, using low-energy manufacturing processes and enhanced thermal efficiency in buildings; 3) to support an efficient energy architecture which creates the conditions for energy security by strengthening domestic sources; 4) the deployment of smart energy systems and electricity storage systems to ensure an integrated energy market; 5) to implement RD programmes such as domestic geothermal exploration and enhanced energy storage technology. Key targets for 2030 include a 64.3% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions relative to 2005, excluding the LULUCF sector, and a 25% renewable share in domestic energy production.

Against this background, FI believes that financial companies need to increase their transparency regarding the exposures they have to both physical climate risks and transition risks. The overall objective of the authority for FI's climate adaptation work in accordance with the Climate Adaptation Regulation should be that the financial system contributes to sustainable development and that companies falling within FI's area of ​​responsibility should report and manage the risks that arise as a result of climate change in an adequate manner. FI assesses that it is not practically possible to specify a measurable target.

This action plan applies to the period 2021-2026 and consists of three measures that FI intends to take, or is already taking, in order to achieve the government's goal that the financial system should contribute to sustainable development and that Swedish financial companies should manage the risks arising from climate change in an adequate manner. The three measures are:

  1. FI shall promote understandable and comparable sustainability-related information.
  2. FI shall develop methods for measuring climate-related risks.
  3. FI shall work to ensure that financial companies integrate physical risks and the effects of climate adaptation into their operations.

DESCRIPTION:
The Law of 27 April 2022, n. 34, which converted with amendments the Decree-Law of 1 March 2022, n. 17 (widely known as the "Decreto Bollette" or "Energy Decree"), represents a strategic legislative pillar in Italy’s response to the 2022 global energy crisis. Its goal is to accelerate Italy’s energy sovereignty by removing bureaucratic barriers to renewable energy production and reducing fossil fuel dependency.

It liberalises rooftop solar installation as "ordinary maintenance" (Art. 9), defines fast-track "Suitable Areas" for renewables (Art. 12 20), and promotes agrivoltaics (Art. 11). PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Climate Change Levy (General) Regulations 2001 (S.I. No.838 of 2001)
DESCRIPTION:
The Climate Change Levy (General) Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/838) establish the operational and administrative framework for the UK’s energy tax on commercial electricity, gas, and solid fuels. The regulations cover registration, quarterly returns, record-keeping, and procedures for claiming exemptions or reduced rates (e.g., via Climate Change Agreements and CHP scheme certifications). Over time, key amendments introduced the Carbon Price Floor mechanism, revised CHP relief formulas, updated exemption certification rules, and removed legacy renewable supply exemptions.The regulation has been updated through several key statutory amendments:

  • S.I. 2003/604: Revised relief formulas and calculations for Combined Heat and Power (CHP) stations and electricity generation.
  • S.I. 2007/2903: Removed the legacy half-rate relief for electricity supplied to energy-intensive industries.
  • S.I. 2010/643: Updated CHP relief calculation formulas for full-member and scheme-certified facilities.
  • S.I. 2011/684: Revised renewable energy source exemption definitions, specifically affecting auto-generators and Climate Change Agreements (CCAs).
  • S.I. 2012/943: Removed the CCL exemption previously granted to indirect supplies of electricity generated from renewable sources.
  • S.I. 2012/3049: Extended CCL tax reliefs and exemptions to carbon capture and storage (CCS) activities.
  • S.I. 2013/713: Established operational rules and relief mechanisms for the Carbon Price Floor (CPF) / Carbon Price Support (CPS) rates.
  • S.I. 2013/1716: Streamlined exemption certificates and supplier declarations for lower-rate and exempt supplies.
  • S.I. 2018/118: Updated Combined Heat and Power Quality Assurance (CHPQA) scheme definitions and calculation methodologies.
  • S.I. 2020/1499 S.I. 2021/675: Modernized administrative rules and rate tables to reflect post-Brexit tax adjustments and scheduled rate increases.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act No. 5346 on Utilization of Renewable Energy Sources for the Purposes of Generating Electrical Energy (Renewable Energy Law)
DESCRIPTION:
This Act (also known as the Renewable Energy Law) encourages the use of renewable energy. This law encompasses the procedures and principles of the conservation of renewable energy resource areas, certification of the energy generated from these sources, and use of these sources. The measurable objective is to increase the amount of electricity produced by renewable sources by 30% by 2023. The Act governs the principles for the conservation of renewable resource areas and introduces incentives for domestic energy projects, providing feed-in tariffs for electricity from renewable energy sources. The legal entity holding a generation licence is granted a \Renewable Energy Resource Certificate\ (RES Certificate) by the Electricity Markets Regulation Authority (EMRA) to identify and monitor the resource type in purchasing and sale of the electrical energy generated from renewable energy resources in the domestic and international markets. It creates a broad basis for an emerging domestic renewable energy market. Grid operators are obliged to provide access to the grid for renewable energy generators, and independent power producers can benefit from the feed-in tariff. Holders of energy retail licences are obliged to purchase a percentage of their total uptake from licensed generation companies holding a RES Certificate. The price of the electricity to be purchased under the Act should be the nationwide average of the electricity wholesale price of the previous year (determined by the EMRA). However a producer can sell the electrical energy generated for a higher price in the market if they are able to. Some highlights of the law include: - The reduction or cancellation of service fees as an incentive for those willing to build energy generation facilities to meet their own energy consumption needs. - Further incentives are available through a Council of Minister's Decree, such as investments for energy generation facilities, procurement of electro-mechanic systems within the country, research, development and production investments concerning solar energy units, and research and development investments for biomass energy. - Where there are sufficient geothermal energy resources, demand will be primarily met by geothermal and solar thermal energy resources. - In the event that the forests and the lands under private ownership of the Treasury or under the control or disposal of the State are used to generate electricity from renewable energy resources, these areas are leased to or right of way is given to the relevant parties. Any fees required for using this land is reduced by 85%. The law also stipulates that development plans that might have a negative impact on the use and efficiency of renewable energy resource areas can no longer be created on public land.The Act was amended in March 2020 by articles 26 and 27 of law 7226 to enable the Ministry of energy and renewable resources to ease the expropriation of private properties to build renewable capacity. Furthermore, it amends the procedures and principles regarding the evaluation of tariffs applied to support electricity production based on renewable energy sources and other revenues within the scope of the RES Support Mechanism, to grant the Ministry the power to regulate them. The Presidential Decree 2949 (17 September 2020) sets out: 1) the prices in Schedule I in the Law will be applied until December 31, 2030 for Renewable Energy Resources (RER) certified production license holders that initiate their operations under the RER support mechanism between January 1, 2021 and June 30, 2021; 2) if the mechanical and/or electro-mechanical parts used in the RER-certified production facilities that initiate their operations between January 1, 2021 and June 30, 2021 are manufactued domestically, the prices in Schedule II in the Law will be applied to the prices in Schedule I, for additional five years from the date os operation of the production facility for the electrical energy produced.

\Law No. 7257, which was published in the Official Gazette No. 3122 of 2 December 2020, establishes a new renewable energy support mechanism in force 1 July 2021.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Government's action plan for green shipping
DESCRIPTION:
This action plan presents the Government’s policy for cutting domestic greenhouse gas emissions, strengthening the Norwegian maritime industry and playing a part in the global technological developments needed for the world to achieve the targets of the Paris Agreement. Measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions result in cuts in emissions of other pollutants as well, for example sulphur (SOx) and nitrogen (NOx) emissions.

This action plan is divided into five main parts. The first describes important elements of the general framework including Norway’s climate targets, developments in the maritime industry and IMO’s climate ambitions. The second discusses relevant technologies and solutions and introduces a ‘green barometer’ for monitoring the transition in the maritime sector. The third part contains an account of the different vessel categories and describes how the Government intends to accelerate the development of low- and zero-emission solutions. The fourth part discusses infrastructure for green shipping, and the fifth and final part gives an account of the Government’s policy instruments for promoting green shipping.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Spatial Planning Act (ROG)
DESCRIPTION:
The Spatial Planning Act (ROG) incorporates climate considerations as one of its guiding principles. It provides that land is to be developed, safeguarded, and restored in a way that preserves its significance for the climate. The Act requires spatial planning authorities to take the requirements of both climate change mitigation and climate adaptation into account. To this end, it promotes the creation of spatial conditions for the expansion of renewable energy, efficient energy use, and the preservation and enhancement of natural carbon sinks.

The Act also requires an environmental assessment to be carried out during the preparation of spatial development plans. As part of this assessment, the competent authority must evaluate the likely significant effects of the proposed plan on the climate, alongside its impacts on other environmental factors.

The Spatial Planning Act was substantially amended in 2023 through the Raumordnungsnovelle to modernise, simplify, and accelerate spatial planning procedures and spatial impact assessments, particularly in support of the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure. Subsequent amendments, including technical revisions in 2025, have not materially altered the Act's core climate objectives or planning framework.
