PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate impact and risk assessment for Germany (KWRA 2021)
DESCRIPTION:
Commissioned by the federal government as part of the German Strategy for Adaptation to Climate (DAS), this is the second edition of Germany's national climate risk assessment.

The study combines climate projections (showing Germany warming faster than the global average, with more heat days, heavier rainfall events, and shifting seasonal precipitation patterns) with socioeconomic scenarios to estimate risk levels for the mid- and end of this century, both with and without adaptation measures. For each policy area (biodiversity and agriculture, energy, transport, tourism, and public health) the report identifies where climate risks are highest, how much adaptation could reduce them, and where urgent action is needed. It closes with an integrated analysis highlighting priority risks, spatial patterns of vulnerability, and remaining research gaps, aimed primarily at federal ministries but also useful for state and local governments, businesses, and researchers.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Adaptation Strategy to Address Climate Change in the Agriculture Sector of Belize
DESCRIPTION: Undertaken by the government and contracted out to consultants from the Belize Enterprise for Sustainable Technology (BEST) with help from the Caribbean Community Climate Change Centre, this Strategy seeks to promulgate efficient and effective water resource management policy recommendations. The goal is to simultaneously reduce the vulnerability of Belize's water resources to climate change impacts and meet its obligations under the Millennium Development Goals.Policy recommendations presented include: (i) establish an agency to oversee integrated water resource management; (ii) strengthen human resource capabilities; (iii) formalise a legal mandate for the National Climate Change Committee; (iv) strengthen trans-boundary co-ordination of climate change efforts; and (v) increase public awareness and education on climate change. Outlines a 10-year policy implementation schedule (between 2009 and 2019).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Environmental Building Reporting Program
DESCRIPTION: The program mandates housing suppliers that provide a total of 20,000 metres squared or more floor area a year in Tokyo to ensure thermal insulation and high energy efficiency performance and install renewable energy equipment (solar power generation equipment) at small and medium-sized new buildings, including houses, with a total floor area of less than 2,000 metres squared. This policy impacts about 50 companies. The city government will also provide subsidies to encourage the installation of solar panels on existing buildings. This new regulation is expected to be impactful, as half of existing buildings will be replaced with new ones before 2050. This program mandates maintenance/operation of renewable energy equipment.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Transition Mechanism Country Platform (ETMCP)

The ETMCP coordinates various energy transition activities, channels fiscal support where necessary, and supports just transition at the community, regional, and national levels. This program was launched through the Ministry of Finance. The government will invest USD 4.6 billion through the ETMCP to expedite the retirement of 2 GW of coal-fired power plants (CFPP) and replace them with renewable sources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Pan-Canadian Framework on Clean Growth and Climate Change
DESCRIPTION:
The Pan-Canadian Framework on Clean Growth and Climate Change is an extensive document that has been developed by the Canadian government in association with the ten provinces to lay out a mitigation strategy as well as a pathway towards a clean economy. The plan details a number of national orientations over 1) the objective of meeting, or exceed, Canada's 2030 target of a 30 percent reduction below 2005 levels of greenhouse gases emissions, 2) adaptation, 3) and mentions province-wide projects happening in different provinces, such as the "community-based energy generation" scheme of New Brunswick or the efforts towards electrification of transport in Quebec. Specific policies include:

  • carbon pricing, with a federal benchmark calling a price starting at $10/tonne in 2018 and a $10/year increase until it reaches $50/tonne in 2022.
  • efforts to support clean technologies at early stage and their implementation at industrial scale. The plan seeks an increase of renewables in the electricity mix (currently at 80 %), a reduction in the reliance on diesel in local communities power generation, energy efficiency in new buildings and retrofitting. The objectives of mitigation and adaptation are meant to be combined with jobs creation and economic growth.
  • Increased stored carbon in forests, use of wood for construction, bioenergy and bio products.
  • Adaptation - focusing on vulnerable regions and especially the Arctic, to translate scientific information and traditional knowledge into action, building regional adaptation capacity expertise, resilient infrastructure and standards, address climate-related health risks, support communities and respecting the rights of Indigenous people.
  • Federal and province level yearly reporting on greenhouse emissions, to determine whether the country's progression is in line with the set out pathway of greenhouse gases emissions reductions by 2030.

The updated benchmark replaces the 2018-2022 benchmark and associated guidance and will apply for the 2023-2030 period. Canada’s minimum national price on carbon pollution for explicit price-based systems (i.e., systems that directly set a price on emissions) is $65 per tonne of GHG emissionsFootnote3 calculated in carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) in 2023, and increases by $15 per year to $170 per tonne CO2e in 2030.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act no. 100/2001 Coll., on the Environmental Impact Assessment
DESCRIPTION:
The law establishes the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) procedure in the Czech Republic, requiring that certain projects likely to significantly affect the environment — such as industrial facilities, energy plants, infrastructure, and large constructions — are evaluated before approval. It ensures that decision-makers consider potential effects on air, water, soil, ecosystems, and human health, enabling mitigation or modification of projects to protect the environment and support sustainable development. In SEAs, the impact evaluation on the climate or climate change is a part of a comprehensive assessment of the PP impacts on the environment. The quality of the climate change impact assessment should be at the same level as impact assessment of other components of the environment. If this is not the case, the competent authority can return the SEA report to the applicant for completion.

Law amended 25 times.

It also suggests ways to increase renewable energy use in other sectors. Beyond 2028, exploring additional renewable energy technologies will be crucial. These initiatives aim to enhance energy security, create jobs, stimulate economic growth, and mitigate climate change, showcasing the Maldivian government's commitment to sustainable development and carbon neutrality.

The Maldives Energy Road Map outlines 15 flagship interventions fulfilling the 25 strategies defined by the Energy Policy and Strategy 2024-2029 and the guidelines of the Electricity Act 2021:

  1. Accelerating the uptake of rooftop renewable energy;
  2. Evaluating maximum potential for renewable energy integration into the grid;
  3. Decarbonising transport;
  4. Leapfrogging solarisation of islands;
  5. Mainstreaming efficient consumption;
  6. Setting up a fair and cost-reflective electricity tariff and replacing the indirect subsidy mechanism with a targeted subsidy;
  7. Transitioning to cleaner fuels in Greater Male;
  8. Erecting and integrating waste-to-energy plants;
  9. Preparing smart, flexible and reliable grids;
  10. Exploring interconnection possibilities of island clusters and extending access to electricity services;
  11. Interconnecting power systems of Greater Male;
  12. Strengthening regulatory framework;
  13. Accessing and collecting reliable energy data;
  14. Developing institutional capacity; and
  15. Unleashing the potential of marine renewable energy and exploring Green Hydrogen options.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 on guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network
DESCRIPTION: Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 establishes updated guidelines for developing the Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T), creating a strategic framework to connect Europe through efficient, sustainable, and resilient transport infrastructure. It divides the network into three layers — the core network to be completed by 2030, the extended core network by 2040, and the comprehensive network by 2050 — to ensure phased progress toward an integrated system. The regulation requires that all new and upgraded infrastructure support low- and zero-emission mobility, incorporate alternative fuels infrastructure in line with Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, and promotes a shift toward greener transport modes such as rail, inland waterways, and short-sea shipping.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decision No 1386/2013/EU on a General Union Environment Action Programme to 2020 'Living well, within the limits of our planet'
DESCRIPTION: The Decision no 1386/2013/EU sets up the General Union Environment Action Programme to 2020 ‘Living well, within the limits of our planet'. It adopts the '7th Environment Action programme' or ‘7th EAP'. The priority objectives of the 7th EAP are: (a) to protect, conserve and enhance the Union's natural capital; (b) to turn the Union into a resource-efficient, green and competitive low-carbon economy; (c) to safeguard the Union's citizens from environment-related pressures and risks to health and well-being; (d) to maximise the benefits of Union environment legislation by improving implementation; (e) to improve the knowledge and evidence base for Union environment policy; (f) to secure investment for environment and climate policy and address environmental externalities; (g) to improve environmental integration and policy coherence; (h) to enhance the sustainability of the Union's cities; (i) to increase the Union's effectiveness in addressing inter­ national environmental and climate-related challenges.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Energy Demand;Energy Supply;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;REDD+ And LULUCF;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Guideline B-15: Climate Risk Management
DESCRIPTION:
This guideline is a product of the 2022 budget commitments of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). It outlines climate-related risks to federally-regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) and the broader financial system, and OSFI’s expectations regarding the management of these risks. The recognized climate-related risks are:

  • Physical risks which pertain to financial risks related to the climate-related extremes and events, gradual shifts, and indirect effects of climate change.
  • Transition risks which pertain to financial risks related to the transition to a low-emission economy, including risks from current and future policies, legislations, and regulations.

This guideline requires FRFIs to build financial and operational resilience against these risks through addressing, managing, and monitoring vulnerabilities in their business models and strategies, operations, and accounting procedures. It further seeks that FRFIs create adequate and robust governance and risk management practices through the improvement of their data quality and risk measurement methodologies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Hungary National Communication. NC5
DESCRIPTION: Hungary National Communication. NC5

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electricity Sector Outlook 2017-2031 (Prospectiva del Sector Eléctrico 2017-2031)
DESCRIPTION: The Mexican Electricity Sector Outlook 2017-2031 outlines Mexico's energy policy, highlighting the modernization of its electricity sector through energy reforms and increased private investment. These reforms have facilitated a rise in clean energy generation, from under 18% to an estimated 30% in the coming years, driven by the Ley de Transición Energética (LTE). The document emphasizes the successful completion of long-term electricity auctions, projecting substantial investments in new clean energy generation capacity and the establishment of a fund to provide electricity access to impoverished communities, reinforcing Mexico's leadership in combating climate change through a diversified and cleaner energy matrix.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Jamaica Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC1 (Updated submission)
DESCRIPTION: Jamaica First NDC (Updated submission), Nationally Determined Contribution from Jamaica in 2020

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Implementation Plan for the Philippines NDC 2020-2030
DESCRIPTION: The NDC Implementation Plan (NDCIP) 2020-2030 outlines key actions, phasing, costs, and implementation arrangements for delivering the Philippines’ Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the identified policies and measures in the transport, energy, waste, industry, and agriculture sectors. The NDCIP also contains sections on financing the NDC and measurement, reporting and verification. Implementation is overseen by four sector departments: the Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), and Department of Transportation (DOTr).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Debt Guarantee Order on Renewable Energy Investment, S.I. 86 of 2025
DESCRIPTION: The Debt Guarantee Order on Renewable Energy Investment, S.I. 86 of 2025, makes the Seychelles government guarantor for a a development loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to the Seychelles Public Utilities Corporation, the main parastatal electricity provider, promoting a USD $8,000,000 investment in grid upgrades for significant expansion of renewable energy generation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Armenia Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy. LT-LEDS1
DESCRIPTION: Armenia Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy. LT-LEDS1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Research Innovation Plan for the Forestry and Timber Sector (2025)
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan strengthens the research-development-innovation (RDI) continuum to strengthen the competitiveness of the forestry and timber sector and improve its overall economic, environmental, and social performance. The forestry and timber sector is both a major carbon sink and affected by climate change.

This contains actions on increasing the overall sector performance through systems approaches, developing timber uses from a bioeconomic perspective and adapting the forest and preparing the forest resources for the future. Examples of actions are promoting the digital transition for forestry and timber mobilisation and logistics; modernising and adapting the industrial appatus in primary and secondary porcessing; strengtehning resilience to climate change and renewing French forests; sustainably improving production; and monitoring forestry biodiversity.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Saint Lucia Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC1 (Archived)
DESCRIPTION: Saint Lucia First NDC (Archived), Nationally Determined Contribution from Saint Lucia in 2016

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Environment Decree of the Netherlands (Omgevingsbesluit)
DESCRIPTION:
The Environment Decree of the Netherlands (Omgevingsbesluit) contains rules on who is the competent authority for environmental permits, which procedure applies, enforcement and implementation, and how environmental impact assessment takes place. It also contains the Digital System for the Environment Act (DSO). Overall this Decree applies to all parties active in the physical environment - citizens, businesses, and government. The Decree also applies in the exclusive economic zone (the Dutch part of the North Sea). 

It contains rules on the content and monitoring of Environmental Impact Assessment (Chapter 11) for plans, projects, and programmes, including a description of “the impact of the project on the climate and the vulnerability of the project to climate change” (11.18 f). The Decree also includes rules regarding transboundary environmental effects (11.3), and details around the advisory bodies and advisors for environmental assessment. Furthermore, Chapter 9 contains rules concerning damage.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act on the Use of Denmark's Subsoil
DESCRIPTION:
The Act aims to ensure the appropriate use and exploitation of Denmark's subsoil and its natural resources, in the context of carbon capture and storage. The Minister for Climate, Energy and Utilities may grant a permit for a period of up to 3 years to carry out certain types of preliminary studies for the purpose of exploration and extraction of the raw materials covered by the Act or for the purpose of storing CO2 of 100 kt or more, storing CO2 of less than 100 kt for purposes other than research, development or testing of new products and processes, storage other than storage of CO2 and use of the subsoil for purposes other than extraction of raw materials.

The Executive Orders contain provisions on assessing permits, the operation of CO2 storage site, criteria and procedures for receiving CO2 streams and closure of the sites.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Indicative Expansion Plan of the Generation System 2020-2050 (Plan de expansión indicativo del Sistema de Generación 2020-2050)
DESCRIPTION:
TheIndicative Expansion Plan of the Generation System 2020-2050, developed by the Ministry of Energy and Mines through its Unidad de Planeación Energético Minera, establishes the long-term vision for Guatemala’s electricity generation system, ensuring national energy security while advancing the objectives of the national legal and policy framework. Structured in two parts, the plan first analyses the socio-economic, macroeconomic, hydrological, and emissions context of the energy sector, and then projects demand growth, resource availability, and investment requirements under ten modelled scenarios up to 2050. From a total of 60 candidate plants (2758 MW) considered—of which over 80 per cent rely on renewable resources—the scenarios assess expansion costs ($4.8–6.8 billion), the role of fossil and renewable sources, and the impact on diversification, system reliability, and greenhouse gas emissions.

The plan concludes that existing capacity is sufficient to cover demand until 2030, yet highlights the need to periodically reassess hydrological models and climate impacts. Opportunities for renewable development emerge across successive periods: geothermal, hydroelectric and biogas (2020–2025); solar (2024–2027); and wind (2027–2035). Key objectives include diversifying the generation matrix, prioritising renewable technologies with firm capacity, gradually substituting fossil fuels through geothermal and natural gas opportunities, and ensuring transmission infrastructure to integrate new capacity. A further emphasis is placed on expanding generation in high-demand areas or those with future growth potential to stimulate economic development and job creation. Recommendations highlight the importance of regional interconnections (notably with Mexico), state or public-private investment in geothermal and solar projects, and continuous monitoring of demand scenarios, particularly in the context of energy-intensive industries and dry-season hydrological variability
KEYWORDS: Energy Transition;Infrastructure;National Energy And Climate Plans;Public Private;Renewables

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategic Plan of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry 2024-2028
DESCRIPTION:
This Strategic Plan sets out the objectives, targets, and performance indicators for the protection of agriculture, forestry, and water resources, along with natural ecosystems. The objective related to climate change is to enhance adaptation capacity and resilience to climate change. The relevant targets are:

  • Enhancing capacity for adaptation to climate change;
  • Increasing greenhouse gas emission reduction capacity and promoting the use of renewable energy;
  • Enhancing capacity to combat agricultural drought; and
  • Mitigating the adverse effects of floods and waterlogging.

A regulatory analysis was also conducted for the Strategic Plan. The following needs were identified:

  • The preparation of an overarching regulation covering all sectors to harmonise water efficiency policy within the framework of adaptation to climate change;
  • Increasing education and awareness activities on climate change, drought, and desertification were needed; and
  • Planning production in a manner that adapts to water scarcity and climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agriculture Sector Plan 2016 – 2020
DESCRIPTION: This plan sets the government's vision to increase food, nutrition and income security in Samoa. It notably seeks to ensure an environmentally sustainable, climate and disaster resilient agricultural sector.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Storm And Flood Insurance Act
DESCRIPTION: This law establishes a national flood and storm insurance program under the National Emergency Management Agency, defines legal providers of flood and storm insurance, allows national and local governments to subsidize premiums, outlines procedures for the insurance process, such as the length of coverage allowed and the methodology for calculating premium rates, empowers the government to compel people to buy flood and storm insurance, requires the government to establish an information network for administering the insurance scheme, and requires the government to conduct a risk assessment and create hazard maps.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Brazil's Mitigation Climate Plan: Sectoral Plan for Land-Use Change in Public Areas and Collective Territories
DESCRIPTION:
Brazil’s Sectoral Plan for Land-Use Change in Public Areas and Collective Territories is part of the Mitigation Climate Plan framework and plays a central role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions from land-use change while also increasing carbon removals by eliminating illegal deforestation, strengthening territorial protection and governance, expanding ecosystem restoration, and conserving native vegetation across public and collective lands. The main objectives are:

  • Eliminate illegal deforestation and reduce forest degradation, illegal logging, and vegetation fires.
  • Strengthen the protection, management, and governance of public lands, Indigenous territories, protected areas, and collective territories.
  • Expand and improve territorial monitoring, enforcement, and land regularization mechanisms.
  • Restore and recover native vegetation to increase carbon sequestration and ecosystem resilience.
  • Reduce land-use change emissions while contributing to biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.
  • Support climate mitigation through integrated land management, conservation, and restoration policies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate ready Scotland: Scottish climate change adaptation programme (2014)
Green Shipping Corridor Program
DESCRIPTION:
The Green Shipping Corridor Program (GSCP) provides funding for projects that contribute to the establishment of green shipping corridors and the decarbonization of the marine sector along the Great Lakes, the St. Lawrence Seaway as well as Canada’s East and West Coasts by:

  • removing barriers to the adoption of emission-reducing equipment and infrastructure
  • incentivising industry-led partnerships and investments to accelerate the adoption of greenhouse gas (GHG) emission-reduction technologies and infrastructure
  • de-risking investments to increase the technology-readiness level of low-carbon and zero-emission ship technology and marine fuels for the domestic vessel fleet
  • building capacity among Canadian vessel owner/operators with respect to their ability to identify, plan and implement next generation low carbon and zero-emission ship technology and marine fuels into their vessel operations.

Funding is through two streams: 1) Clean Ports Stream; and 2) Clean Vessel Demonstration Stream. The Clean Ports Stream is providing up to $127.2M in contribution funding over 4 years from 2024 to 2028. The Clean Vessel Demonstration Stream is providing up to $22.5M in grant and contribution funding over 5 years from 2023 to 2028.

GSCP supports goals under the Federal Sustainable Development Strategy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electricity Act, No. 13 of 2023
DESCRIPTION: The Seychelles' Electricity Act, No. 13 of 2023, promotes and regulates near and long term electricity sector planning, and focuses partly on building a framework for small and independent generators, regulating their licensing and governance by a national commission. It explicitly promotes the expansion of renewable energy supply and its supporting grid infrastructure, naming this as a duty for all transmission and distribution operators, and it enables the minister responsible for the sector to prescribe the proportion of renewable energy delivered to consumers, within the bounds of generation capacity at the time. The act allows the responsible commission to introduce net metering and feed-in tariff systems, and to propose tax and other incentives for renewable energy generation, including the creation of dedicated investment funds. It also notes that the responsible minister may launch public awareness campaigns to educate producers and consumers on the advantages of renewables.

DESCRIPTION: North Macedonia National Communication. NC1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decision 08/2020/QD-TTg On amending and supplementing several articles of the Prime Minister’s Decision No. 24/2014/QD-TTg dated 24 March 2014 on support mechanisms for the development of biomass power projects
DESCRIPTION: On 5 March 2020, the Prime Minister of Vietnam officially issued Decision No. 08 amending Decision No. 24/2014/QD-TTg dated 24 April 2014 ("Decision No. 24") on support mechanisms for the development of biomass power projects in Vietnam. Effective from 25 April 2020, Decision No. 08, among other revisions, increase Feed-in-Tariffs ("FiT") for biomass power projects.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Key matters relating to the guidelines to be established by the competent minister in accordance with the provisions of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (Public Notification No. 63 of 2012)
DESCRIPTION: This document sets out the foundational rules governing the guidelines that competent ministers must establish under Japan's Environmental Impact Assessment Act, covering six areas: the selection of items for early-stage environmental consideration; procedures for seeking opinions from related administrative bodies and the public at the planning stage; criteria for classifying projects as Class-2 (which require a full EIA); the selection of items and methods for full environmental impact assessments; guidelines for environmental conservation measures; and requirements for post-completion reporting. Across these areas, the document specifies the categories of environmental impact criteria to be assessed, including impacts on air and water quality, biodiversity, and greenhouse gas emissions, and sets out general principles for how impact evaluation and conservation measures should be designed, documented, and conducted by project proponents. Greenhouse gas emissions are specifically addressed in Section 1(2)(4) (on early-stage environmental consideration) and Section 4(2)(4) (on the full EIA process).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Natural Resources Tax Law
DESCRIPTION: In 2006, Latvia introduced it a Natural Resources Tax Law that contains provisions for a carbon tax on CO2 emissions. The tax is applied across many industrial sectors, including "power and heat generation, oil refineries, steel works and production of iron, aluminium, metals, cement, lime, glass, ceramics, pulp, paper, cardboard, acids, and bulk organic chemicals". Operators of stationary technological installation and aircraft operators who are included in the scheme for emission allowance trading within the European Union are exempted from paying the carbon tax. Other exemptions include electric vehicles and rapeseed oil (if it is used as a fuel source or if a biofuel is made solely from rapeseed oil).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Turkish Atomic Energy Authority
DESCRIPTION: This act establishes the Turkey Atomic Energy Agency and requires it to create a national atomic energy plan, conduct research and development related to nuclear energy, and oversee all aspects of atomic energy producing, including licensing and design and construction of facilities. It also requires the agency to collect and manage data and information about atomic energy, as well as to educate and train relevant government staff.
KEYWORDS: Energy Supply;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: PLANAVEG National Native Vegetation Recovery Plan 2025-2028
DESCRIPTION: The "PLANAVEG National Native Vegetation Recovery Plan 2025-2028" was adopted following its renewal at COP16 in October 2024 and aims to restore 12 million hectares of native vegetation in Brazil by 2030. The plan focuses on expanding and strengthening public policies, investment, and coordination among federal, state, and private actors to achieve this restoration target, particularly in compliance with Brazil’s environmental laws and international biodiversity commitments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: United States’ Submission on the Third Technical Dialogue of the First Global Stocktake - April 2023
DESCRIPTION: United States’ Submission on the Third Technical Dialogue of the First Global Stocktake - April 2023, Submission to the Global Stocktake from United States of America in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agriculture and Rural Development Strategy 2021-2027
DESCRIPTION: The strategy aims to diversify and develop economic opportunities in rural areas, improve social condition and quality of life. It lays out three strategic goals: 1) increase competitiveness of agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, 2) sustainable usage of natural resources, retaining the eco-system, adaptation to climate change, and 3) Effective systems of food/feed safety, veterinary and plant protection.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Legislative Decree 656/2020, decree 362/2019 and agreement 617/2019
DESCRIPTION: Concerns the Financial Cooperation Agreement with the Federal Republic of Germany, for the Project called: "Urban Adaptation to Climate Change in Central America (El Salvador Component)" according to Legislative Decree No. 362 dated June 27, 2019, published in the Official Gazette No. 134, Volume No. 424 of July 18 of the same year, which has allowed the execution of mitigation works in different human settlements in urban, peri-urban and rural areas.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy to Combat Short-Lived Climate Pollutants (PCCV)
DESCRIPTION:
The National Strategy to Combat Short-Lived Climate Pollutants (PCCV) is driven by a vision for the Central African Republic (CAR) to integrate into a dynamic of sustained, equitable, and durable socio-economic development by 2030 to improve the well-being of the population. The global objective is to increase the capacity of the CAR, its national institutions, and local communities in the fight against air pollution, ensuring the population benefits from acceptable and secure living conditions. The strategy is built on five key pillars, including developing managerial and operational capacities, creating a robust regulatory and economic framework, promoting ecologically rational technologies, and establishing a national air pollution monitoring system.

The strategy emphasises that this work is a contribution to the global climate change combat strategy of the CAR and was conducted in a participatory and inclusive manner and concludes with the necessity of improving and strengthening the national framework at all levels to effectively meet the challenges posed by PCCVs and the wider fight against climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 9786 to Combat Plastic Pollution and Protect the Environment
DESCRIPTION: The Law to Combat Plastic Pollution and Protect the Environment in Costa Rica, approved in 2019 and implemented in August 2024, targets single-use plastics by prohibiting the commercialization and free delivery of plastic straws and bags, and requiring importers, producers, marketers, and distributors of plastic bottles to implement comprehensive compliance plans. The law also bans state institutions from purchasing single-use plastic items such as cutlery, crockery, or food containers, and mandates the use of recycled resin in plastic bottles, along with the implementation of effective waste recovery and recycling programs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy and Climate Roadmap 2050
DESCRIPTION: Finland’s long-term objective was to achieve a carbon-neutral society, with particular attention to the energy sector, which accounted for around 80% of greenhouse gas emissions when transport was included. The Energy and Climate Roadmap 2050, prepared by a parliamentary committee, provided strategic guidance towards this goal while also emphasising energy security, competitiveness, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and the development of clean technologies. Rather than establishing a fixed pathway to 2050, the roadmap assessed different emission-reduction options and their implications for Finland’s economy and energy system. It highlighted the need for substantial decarbonisation across all sectors, including an almost emissions-free energy system and the potential use of carbon capture and storage for residual industrial emissions. It was subsequently superseded by Finland's Long-Term Strategy, which established the longer-term emissions pathway towards 2050.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Trinidad and Tobago National Adaptation Plan. NAP1
DESCRIPTION: Trinidad and Tobago National Adaptation Plan. NAP1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Value Added Tax (VAT) Act No. 58 of 2009
DESCRIPTION: Under the previous VAT Act of 1969, zero VAT rating for the supply and import of electric vehicles was adopted by the Norwegian Parliament in 2001. In 2013, the Norwegian Parliament adopted amendments to the current VAT Act and the VAT Regulation concerning electric vehicles, which involve an extension of the zero rating to the leasing of electric vehicles and to the sale and import of batteries for electric vehicles.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Concept for the development of hydrogen energy in the Republic of Kazakhstan until 2040
DESCRIPTION: National policy framework for developing Kazakhstan's long-term hydrogen economy vision to 2040 through targeted investments and technology deployment. It sets indicative targets for hydrogen production, including a 10 GW electrolyser target, up to KZT 5 trillion (USD 11.3 billion) in investments, and at least a 20% share of domestic technology supply.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Socio-economic development plan for 2022
DESCRIPTION:
• Climate-related clauses from the Socio-Economic Development Plan for 2022 include the following: invest in urban infrastructure in coastal economic zones. Develop agricultural and rural infrastructure systems, especially irrigation works, fishing ports, large fishing centers, and storm shelters, climate change adaptation projects against landslides.
  • Continue to implement master plans, plans, and projects on urban development to respond to climate change, green cities, and smart cities
  • Ensure the planning and construction progress of key power source and grid projects, especially works for green energy conversion and carbon emission reduction.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation 31761 Amending the Planned Areas Zoning Regulation
DESCRIPTION: The Regulation Amending the Planned Areas Zoning Regulation was published in the Official Gazette on February 25, 2022, in Turkey, introducing significant changes to promote sustainability and combat climate change. It includes measures such as facilitating the installation of solar panels on roofs, implementing water-saving systems, and requiring waste storage areas in architectural projects.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Forest Programme
DESCRIPTION:
The government has established a vision for the forest program: "The forest, the green gold, will contribute to jobs and sustainable growth throughout the country and to the development of a growing bioeconomy". Sweden needs forests and forestry in a transition to a sustainable and fossil-free society and to create jobs and growth throughout the country.

A long-term forest program is needed to promote sustainable, competitive and bio-based industries based in the forest.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Argentina Biennial Update Report. BUR2
DESCRIPTION: Argentina Biennial Update Report. BUR2

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Action Plan for the reduction of CO2 emissions by civil aircraft operators of the Republic of Belarus
DESCRIPTION: The action plan implements a series of recommendations derived from Belarus' participation in CORSIA (Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation) since 2019, aiming to mitigate emissions from the aviation sector. Its provisions include general fleet modernisation (for efficiency gains), long-term incorporation of biofuels, 1% reductions in flight time through route optimisation, improvements to airfield layouts, participation in EU emissions trading schemes, and the creation of a central environmental monitoring organisation for aviation. The action plan is approved by the Council of Ministers through Resolution No. 112, 2022.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Livestock Policy
DESCRIPTION:
The broad objective of the Livestock Policy is to utilize livestock resources for food and nutrition security and improved livelihoods while safeguarding the environment. The Policy aims to address diminishing availability of rangeland resources by proposing measures to address overgrazing, invasive plant species, pests, declining soil health, changing climate patterns, competing land use for settlement and crop development and inadequate supply of forage planting materials. The government will:

  • Facilitate the implementation of legislation and action plans relating to climate change.
  • Develop capacities and technologies to enhance adaptation and mitigation to effects of climate change.
  • Support programs to improve resilience of livestock keepers to effects of climate change.
  • Establish a contingency fund for disaster mitigation and emergencies.
  • Strengthen early warning systems and disaster preparedness.
  • Promote selection and development of appropriate livestock breeds and forage varieties.
  • Promote sustainable land management and green growth practices.
  • Promote climate financing and broaden mechanisms to attract investments in climate-smart agricultural practices along the commodity product value chain. Support adoption of insurance to mitigate climate risks.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Adapting civil security to climate challenges by 2050
DESCRIPTION: A strategy for adapting the Civil Security response to 2050 has been implemented in light of the profound transformations underway linked to climate change. This innovative approach reflects the paradigm shift undertaken by Civil Security: orienting its preparation towards the future through anticipation rather than anchoring itself solely in a learning approach based on feedback. A major upheaval of our time, global climate change will permanently alter the risk map facing France. Responsible for protecting and rescuing populations, Civil Security actors find themselves on the front line when it comes to these changes. They must therefore prepare and anticipate them.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Technical analysis of the fourth biennial update report of Chile submitted on 18 January 2021. Summary report by the team of technical experts
DESCRIPTION: Technical analysis of the fourth biennial update report of Chile submitted on 18 January 2021. Summary report by the team of technical experts, Technical Analysis Summary Report from UNFCCC Secretariat in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: To meet the larger vision of achieving Zero Carbon Emission Goal, Ministry of Ports, Shipping Waterways has launched ‘Harit Sagar’ the Green Port Guidelines. They aim to reduce carbon emissions per ton of cargo by 30% by 2030, and by 70% by 2047.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Antigua and Barbuda National Communication. NC2
DESCRIPTION: Antigua and Barbuda National Communication. NC2 from 2009

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Reform Programme of the Slovak Republic 2024
DESCRIPTION: The Slovak Republic’s National Reform Programme 2024 frames climate and energy policy as closely intertwined with economic resilience and energy security, particularly in response to the geopolitical impacts of the war in Ukraine. It prioritises reducing dependence on fossil fuel imports, especially from Russia, while accelerating the deployment of renewable energy. A strong emphasis is placed on improving energy efficiency, particularly in buildings, as a cost-effective means of lowering emissions and demand. The programme also highlights the need to modernise electricity grids to accommodate a growing share of renewables and to strengthen system resilience. In the transport sector, efforts focus on decarbonisation through the expansion of low- and zero-emission mobility, although progress is constrained by delays in rail infrastructure projects. Challenges remain, including slow permitting processes, gaps in renewable energy uptake and recycling performance, and the absence of a fully adopted national Climate Act to anchor long-term policy commitments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Hydrogen Strategy and the Action Plan 2023-2030
DESCRIPTION:
The vision of the National Hydrogen Strategy (NHS) and the Action Plan for Romania is to develop a hydrogen economy, with a focus on renewable hydrogen but with attention to low-carbon hydrogen at an affordable price, with a view of reducing emissions and sustainable and competitive economic and technological development, through the development of the following strategic directions for 2030:

  1. Decarbonisation of the economy through the use of renewable hydrogen in difficult sectors decarbonised by other methods (e.g. direct electrification impossible)
  2. Economic growth through sustainable development of technologies for industries difficult to decarbonise and focus on creating new jobs
  3. Technological development to ensure long-term mobilisation of the economyeconomy and to support the attraction of investment into the economy
  4. Energy security, through the use of hydrogen and Power-to-X solutions for optimising the integration of renewable energy sources and to achieve sectoral integration.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
DESCRIPTION: The overall of this Plan is to operationalise gender concerns in climate change efforts to enhance implementation and contribute to the promotion of gender equality in Nepal. There are six priority sectors: : (i) Agriculture and Food Security; (ii) Forests and REDD; (iii) Water, (iv) Energy, (v) Health and (vi) Urbanisation. This Plan is a catalyst for further action to be taken through the inclusion of gender in national climate change processes, policy development, decision-making and project development and implementation.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action
DESCRIPTION: The 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action sets out measures the government plans to use to meet international climate change targets and international biodiversity targets to half and revise biodiversity loss by 2030. The Framework outlines a vision to halve global emissions, halt and reverse nature loss and build resilience to climate impacts and identified six global challenges that must be overcome in order to meet commitments made in the Paris Agreement, the Glasgow Climate Pact, and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Input to the first Global Stocktake (GST): A satellite-based, highly spatially resolved gridded greenhouse gas (GHG) emission inventory product in support of national emission reporting and climate mitigation monitoring
DESCRIPTION: Input to the first Global Stocktake (GST): A satellite-based, highly spatially resolved gridded greenhouse gas (GHG) emission inventory product in support of national emission reporting and climate mitigation monitoring, Submission to the Global Stocktake from Universities Space Research Association (USRA) in 2023

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Mozambique National Communication. NC2
DESCRIPTION: Mozambique. National Communication (NC). NC 2., National Communication from Mozambique in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: DRC: National adaptation plan to climate change (2022-2026)
DESCRIPTION: This national adaptation plan demonstrates the DRC’s commitment to the Paris Agreement and will help bring responses to the impacts of climate change. Strengthening climate resilience will enable the country to contribute to the objectives of the SDGs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Italy Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
DESCRIPTION:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes key objectives: 1) to accelerate the transition from traditional fuels to renewable sources by promoting the gradual phasing out of coal for electricity generation in favour of an electricity mix based on a growing share of renewables; 2) to implement policies and measures in order to reduce greenhouse gases (phase out of coal, higher CO2 price, acceleration of renewables and energy efficiency in manufacturing); 3) to use a mix of fiscal, economic, regulatory and policy instruments to enhance energy efficiency; 4) to reduce dependence on imports by increasing renewable sources and energy efficiency and to diversify sources of supply through the use of natural gas, including liquefied natural gas (LNG); 5) to ensure a greater degree of market integration and the development of processes, products and knowledge for the use of renewables, energy efficiency and network technology. In the updated final plan, some general targets have been slightly reduced (i.e. the non-ETS emissions reduction target decreased from 30% to a 29.3% reduction) due to the COVID-19 pandemic and energy supply shocks.
KEYWORDS: Energy Supply;National Energy And Climate Plans

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agreement on follow-up to the evaluation of the Planning Act (2022)
DESCRIPTION:
This is an Agreement between the government (Social Democracy), the Liberal Party, the Danish People's Party and the Conservative People's Party on the follow-up to the evaluation of the Planning Act, etc. dated 15 June 2022.

As follow-up to the agreement Denmark in better balance – Better framework for municipalities, citizens and businesses throughout the country, the rules of the Nature Protection Act on beach protection, dune conservation and the sea and river protection line were changed, and new appeal boards were established in the planning area and the environment. The parties also agreed that an evaluation should be carried out.

This Agreement follows up on the evaluation and implement a number of changes to the Planning Act and other relevant legislation.

The agreement covers the following main themes:

1. Climate, green transition and nature

2. Urban development, etc.

3. New development opportunities on the coasts and for tourism

4. Mobile coverage throughout the country

5. Simplification, administrative relief and digitalization

6. The complaints system

7. Changes to other rules

8. Køge Bugt Strandpark - modernisation and climate protection

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Development Plan 2013-2017
DESCRIPTION: The National Development Plan includes in its environmental objectives the development of national programmes on climate change, the promotion of the use of clean energy, and the adoption of environmental technologies in the oil, gas and petrochemical industries.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Policy
DESCRIPTION:
As the document outlines, 'the goal of the policy is to ensure a harmonised and co-ordinated approach towards a climate- resilient and low-carbon development path for sustainable development in Uganda'. The policy notes that the level of knowledge on climate change and its impacts remains low in Uganda. Therefore, it seeks to raise awareness of climate change, targeting sectorial weaknesses (to be determined by different governmental agencies and ministries) in the short term but providing information for a wide variety of stakeholders in the long term.
To this end, the Policy adopts a comprehensive approach to address climate change, identifying as priority concerns: adaptation, mitigation, monitoring, and research. To address these concerns, the Policy promotes the implementation of activities relating to: education and increased awareness; gender issues; promoting and diffusing research; monitoring and transferring knowledge; and institutional capacity building.
The policy calls for the adoption and implementation of a Transport Policy with emphasis on reducing GHG emissions from this sector, especially through the promotion of the use of less carbon intensive fuels. It also stresses the importance of the implementation of the 2007 Renewable Energy Policy and other measures that promote the use and the production of renewables.
The adoption of climate change strategies that address the impact of climate change and promote sustainable activities in the sectors of agriculture and livestock, fishery production, water management, forestry, wetland, biodiversity and ecosystem services and tourism are identified are important needs to develop Uganda's approach to adaption to climate change.
Moreover, the Policy also seeks to implement the basic institutional structure required to finance this awareness raising campaign and to develop a performance measurement framework for each ministry and agency involved. The policy also strengthens the Climate Change Unit, upgrading it to a National Climate Change Commission with a more advanced legal and institutional framework that can co-ordinate climate change policy across sectors and regions. The Policy Committee on Environment is also strengthened to help guide climate change policy implementation.
As annex to the Climate Change Policy, the Cost Implementation Strategy provides a more detailed account on the implementation of the Policy, including an indicative costing for the programmes and activities to be developed. Thus, according to the document, the total cost for the implementation of the Climate Change Policy is estimated in approximately 3.9 billion dollars over a 15-year period.

DESCRIPTION:

d) The execution of risk transfer mechanisms, in particular the development of insurance

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Consumption Labelling Act (EnVKG)
DESCRIPTION: The Energy Consumption Labelling Act (EnVKG) establishes the legal framework for the energy labelling of energy-related products, passenger cars, and tyres in Germany. It requires manufacturers and retailers to provide standardized information on energy consumption, CO₂ emissions, and other relevant resource consumption to enable consumers to make informed purchasing decisions. The Act also provides for market surveillance and enforcement measures to ensure compliance with national and EU energy labelling requirements, thereby promoting energy efficiency and reducing environmental impacts.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Action Program to Combat Desertification
DESCRIPTION: This document sets Chad's strategy to combat desertification, notably to put it in line with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Among other goals, the programme seeks to protect and develop forests, notably to store carbon.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Shading and cooling of the urban space using street trees as part of preparing for climate change (Decree 1022)
DESCRIPTION: This Decree determines the main points of the inter-ministerial team's recommendations regarding urban forestation, determining goals for shading and cooling the urban area by planting trees in urban streets, to help Israeli cities prepare for the impacts of climate change.

DESCRIPTION: This strategy was approved by the governmental Order 482/2019. It lays out a risk assessment of the sudden and prolonged adverse effects of climate change in the country, with a particular focus on agriculture and land use. The document details sectoral adaptation actions to undertake.

DESCRIPTION: This document sets the EU Commission's strategy to enable the transport sector to lower its emissions. The document notably calls for 1) an update of the regulatory framework, 2) optimisation of the transport system and enhancing its efficiency through digital mobility solutions, fair pricing and the promotion of multi-modality, 3) scaling-up the use of low-carbon solutions and the roll-out of infrastructure for alternative fuels, interoperability and standardisation for electro-mobility, 4) improvement in vehicle testing, 5) rethinking the links between transport and energy systems, 6) strengthening research and development.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2024-2035
DESCRIPTION:
The aim of the National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction (SNRRD) is to provide a comprehensive framework to mobilise the various public and private actors involved to stimulate and accelerate efforts to increase Romania's disaster resilience.

The priority areas are: Understanding disaster risk; strengthening risk governance for disaster risk reduction and management; investing in disaster risk reduction to increase resilience; improving disaster preparedness for effective response; and implementing of the Build Back Better (BBB) ​​concept in rehabilitation and reconstruction.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Reef 2050 Plan
DESCRIPTION:
This document describes government's overarching plan to protect the Great Barrier Reef from the impacts of climate change. It was updated and expanded in 2018.

Among its core functions are:

Creating an Independent Expert Panel and Reef Advisory Committee to evaluate health of Great Barrier Reef and advise the government
Supporting scientific research on climate change impact on the reef
Setting quantitative targets for improving water quality around the Great Barrier Reef
Creating the Clean Energy Finance Corporation Reef Funding Program to make funds available for financing projects that implement the plan's goal
Supporting indigenous peoples in managing the Great Barrier Reef
Controlling and reducing pollution, as well as conserving and restoring the Great Barrier Reef
Promoting capacity building and cooperation among government
Supporting education and awareness raising of the importance of the Great Barrier Reef among Australians

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal Decree No. 9.841/2019 on the National Climate Risk Zoning Programme
DESCRIPTION: The National Climate Risk Zoning Programme - ZARC aims to improve the quality and availability of data and information on agro-climatic risks in Brazil, with an emphasis on supporting the development, improvement and operationalisation of public management programmes and policies. It establishes agro-climatic zoning, which consists of the quantification and delimitation of agro-climatic risk in time and space, normally used to identify regions and times of lower risk to agricultural production and to define the most suitable species, cultivars and production systems.

DESCRIPTION: The 2050 Agenda is the long-term plan for the economic transformation of Nigeria to meet the challenges of development, including climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Water Strategy (2016-2025)
DESCRIPTION: Jordan's National Water Strategy (2016-2025) is the third in the series and has been adapted to the post-Millenium Development Goals era, in tune with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. It identifies priorities for the water sector from 2016-2025, including but not limited to resilience, access to clean water, efficient integrated water resource management and a climate change adaptation plan. The areas of water management covered by the Strategy include sustainability of overexploited groundwater resources, technological developments for decentralised wastewater management, and reuse of treated wastewater, among other things. An important issue addressed by the Strategy is the water-energy-food nexus, identifying the input-usage relationship between these three sectors. The Strategy aims to monitor progress through specific targets and indicators that have been set along 4 parameters, namely Financial Sustainability, Enhancement of services of Water and Wastewater, Supply of Water to meet the Demand and Protection and Sustainability of Water Resources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Green Hydrogen / Green Ammonia Policy
DESCRIPTION: Building on the National Hydrogen Mission released by the Prime Minister in August 2021, this document sets India's strategy to meet its goal of becoming a global green hydrogen hub. It identifies the production of hydrogen and ammonia from unconsumed renewable power and connectivity to the grid as priorities. The policy sets the framework so that hydrogen / ammonia manufacturers can purchase and use unconsumed renewable power. Waiver of inter-state transmission charges for a period of 25 years will be allowed to the manufacturers for projects commissioned before 30th June 2025. The manufacturers of Green Hydrogen / Ammonia and the renewable energy plant shall be given connectivity to the grid on priority basis to avoid any procedural delays.The document also seeks to develop bunkers near ports for storage and export or direct use by ships. The land for the storage for this purpose shall be provided by the respective Port Authorities at applicable charges.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Methodological Guide for Incorporating Climate Change Adaptation Considerations into the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Process of the Dominican Republic
DESCRIPTION: This Methodological Guide aims to help integrate climate change adaptation into every stage of the Dominican Republic's EIA process, fulfilling the requirements of Resolution No. 0025-2025, which made climate adaptation considerations a mandatory requirement in environmental impact assessments.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The Energy Regulations Act (Chapter 436)
DESCRIPTION: This Act establishes an Energy Regulation Board and define its functions and powers. It provides for the licensing of undertakings for the production of energy or the production or handling of certain fuels. It repeals the National Energy Council Act and the Zambia Electricity Supply Act. The board is notably in charge of formulating measures to minimise the environmental impact of energy systems. Nuclear, solar and wind resources are taken into account.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Korean Green Bond Framework
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, the Korean Development Bank (KDB) produced the KDB Green Bond Framework (Framework). The guidelines state that proceeds from Green Bonds are to be used to finance green projects, which must accord with the eligibility criteria set out in the Framework. The eligibility criteria fall under two overarching thematic areas for projects - renewable energy (such as solar, wind, and hydro, amongst others) and low carbon emissions technology (such as carbon capture and storage).

DESCRIPTION: Presidential Regulation No. 22/2017 on National Energy Grand Plan mandates the target of 23% New Renewable Energy (NRE) in national energy mix by 2025 and 1% reduction in energy intensity per year.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Act 2021
DESCRIPTION:
The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Act 2021 (OEI Act) sets out a licensing and regulatory framework for the construction, installation, operation, maintenance and decommissioning of offshore renewable energy and offshore electricity transmission infrastructure.  The OEI Act framework applies to offshore locations from three nautical miles from the coast to the boundary of Australia’s exclusive economic zone (coastal waters remain the responsibility of the adjacent state and Northern Territory governments). The OEI Act framework operates under the principle of shared use of the offshore marine environment, recognising all users and balancing competing interests.

Under the OEI Act framework, the Minister for Energy makes all licensing decisions, including declaring areas suitable for offshore renewable energy infrastructure, both at a commercial scale and for research and development of new and emerging technologies. The declaration of an offshore area is informed through consultation with stakeholders including existing marine users, state and territory governments and Federal Government agencies with responsibilities in the marine area and the community.

In deciding whether an area is suitable for offshore renewable energy infrastructure, the Minister must have regard to the following:

(a) the potential impacts of the construction, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance or decommissioning of offshore renewable energy infrastructure in the area on other marine users and interests;

(b) any submissions received in accordance with particular notice of proposal from the Minister;

(c) any advice received as a result of a designated consultation;

(d) Australia’s international obligations in relation to the area;

(e) Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: General Appropriations Act (RA 12116)
DESCRIPTION:
The General Appropriations Act (Republic Act No. 12116) for Fiscal Year 2025 contains several provisions on climate change mitigation and adaptation, including on:

  1. providing support to all Agrarian Reform Communities (ARCs) to strengthen their climate resilience, including the conduct of climate and disaster risk assessments, provision of capacity-building on value-adding activities and non-farm livelihood options, enhancing access to innovative agricultural insurance coverage such as weather index-based insurance, and enhancing their capacity to adopt climate-resilient technologies;
  2. ensuring that the laws in the protection of the environment, climate change adaptation and mitigation, and disaster risk reduction and management are integrated in the regular subjects in both public and private schools;
  3. promoting and enhancing protected areas through sustainable management and ecotourism development, mapping and inventory of the biodiversity of the province, and accelerating climate change adaptation and mitigation;
  4. establishing and maintaining a Climate Change Information Management System and Network, including climate change risks, activities and investments; and
  5. enhancing Local Government Unit capacity to effectively implement disaster prevention and risk reduction measures through the strengthening of communities and people's capacity to anticipate, cope with, and recover from disasters.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Order No. 2014-0668-MEA-SG establishing the composition, and operating procedures of the Steering Committee of the Mali Climate Fund
DESCRIPTION: This Order creates the Steering Committee of the Mali Climate Fund. It regulates the Committee's composition and functions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sustainability Principles Compliance Framework
DESCRIPTION: In 2020, the Sustainability Principles Compliance Framework was established. It mandates companies that issue securities to disclose their sustainability metrics in their annual reports, including reporting on scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, their strategies and actions to combat the climate crisis and reduce environmental impacts, amongst others.

DESCRIPTION: This policy replaces Chile's previous renewable energy targets, setting a target of 80% for 2030 and 100% for 2050.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Policy for Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique (2017-2021)
DESCRIPTION:
The policy objectives for 2017 – 2021 are to;
1) Strengthen institutional structure to support coordination, mainstreaming and implementation of climate change adaptation and mitigation action, along with the systematic integration of climate change adaptation into development policies, plans, programmes, projects, budgets and processes.
2) Build climate resilience in the following priority thematic areas: water supply and sewage management; ‘agriculture, agri-business and food security’39; biodiversity and ecosystems; human health and coastal zone management.
3) Facilitate climate smart (low carbon, climate resilient) infrastructure location, planning, design and maintenance, sustainable land management and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the electricity, transport, waste and forestry sectors.
4) Integrate disaster risk management and climate change adaptation, and support funding applications for disaster risk management activities.
5) Strengthen institutional arrangements for the collection, storage, analysis, sharing and use of climate, GHG emission and pollutant/chemical data and information to inform evidence-based decision making.
6) Improve citizens’ awareness of the causes, impacts and appropriate responses to climate change, so that they are in a better position to take independent action and support relevant public policies, and state and non-state activities.
7) Access climate technologies for mitigation and adaption along with capacity building. Increase external climate finance support to Grenada’s adaptation and mitigation process.
8) Advocate for international action on climate change through foreign policy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Agreement on green aviation in Denmark
DESCRIPTION:
This Agreement sets out the commitment to allocate funds to establish fully electric domestic aviation routes from 2025, and to ensure that all domestic air travel is electric by 2030 at the latest. Subsidies will be offered for the additional cost of purcashing electric powered aircraft.

In addition, funds will be provided to smaller regional airports to finance green infrastructure and for the restructuring of aviation, for instance in supporting the blending of sustainable aviation fuels such as Power-to-X fuels or other propellants (such as electricity and hydrogen), and the reduction of aromatic hydrocarbons in aviation fuel to reduce environmental impact.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: 13th Ocean Energy Development Five Year Plan (2016-2020)
DESCRIPTION: This Plan aims to achieve a total installed ocean energy capacity exceeding 50,000 kW by 2020, with China leading internationally in ocean energy. The plan lays out key development areas, including the construction of supporting platforms; research and development; construction, operations, maintenance; and upstream and downstream phases of ocean energy developments. The development will occur in the Bohai and Yellow Sea, East China Sea, South China Sea and coastal islands.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023-2027
DESCRIPTION:
The National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023 – 2027 is the third five-year plan that presents the detailed priority actions that Kenya will embark on to address climate change in the medium-term planning period and contribute to the achievement of our NDC under the Paris Agreement. Its development has involved deliberate consultations with the youth and children’s representatives.

NCCAP 2023–2027 proposes priority actions for implementation over the five-year period. These actions are classified in eight (8) Climate Change Priority Areas: Disaster Risk Management; Food Security and Nutrition; Water, Fisheries and the Blue Economy; Forestry, Wildlife and Tourism; Health and Human Settlements; Manufacturing; Energy and Transport; and Children and the Youth. The priority actions, building on achievements from the 2018–2022 period, propose adaptation and mitigation interventions, as well as enabling actions to facilitate their implementation. An implementation matrix has been prepared for each priority area, with an estimated budget that will guide execution. Each Climate Change Priority Area has a set of discrete National Indicators, as well as Key Performance Indicators to enable tracking and reporting of progress over the 2023–2027 period.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal Law on Environmental Protection No. 7-FZ
DESCRIPTION:
The law requires payment for pollution, including emissions into the atmosphere. The law makes clear that payment of these "pollution fees" does not protect an activity from other liability for environmental harm. (Art. 16)

The government shall set limits on emissions and dumping based on the norms of admissible human load on the environment, the norms of environmental quality and also technological norms, and use this in permits for the polluting activities. (Art. 23)

The construction and operation of oil and gas production, processing, transport, storage, and sales facilities shall comply with this law. These facilities may be held liable for compensation of environmental damages, and permitting should be conditioned on a showing of financial ability to restore the site once the activity ceases. (Art. 46)

Source: IEA, 2020

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Integrated Infrastructure Master Plan
DESCRIPTION: This document is Nigeria's blueprint for infrastructure development. It notably seeks to make the country's infrastructures resilient to the adverse impacts of climate change, enable a low carbon development of the transport sector, and prepare the country to natural disasters.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Guyana National Land Use Plan (2013)
DESCRIPTION: Guyana's National Land Use Plan provides a long-term strategic framework to guide land development nationally. Rather than designating specific zones for particular uses, it aims to provide a range of comprehensive viable and sustainable options. The plan names climate change adaptation as a key motivating factor, emphasising the need to develop away from the coastal plain, where flood risks will increase over time and rainfall patterns will shift. It also acknowledges the national and global importance of Guyana's forests and their carbon stock for climate change mitigation, and aims to ensure that new developments do not contribute to deforestation where possible.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Annex Volume II of Federal Law 14.822/2024 on the Annual Budget
DESCRIPTION:
Federal Law 14.822/2024 on the Annual Budget estimates the federal government's revenues and sets out its expenditures for the financial year 2024.

Annex Volume II of the law establishes the federal budget for addressing the climate emergency.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: A roadmap for multi-hazard, impact-based early warning 2023-2030
DESCRIPTION: Ethiopia’s early warning systems, developed over a 50-year span, faced challenges such as fragmentation, inadequate funding, and a lack of proactive measures. The focus on crisis management, rather than anticipatory actions, led to inefficient resource allocation. To address these issues, the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC) and stakeholders propose transforming the early warning system into a comprehensive Multi-Hazard, Impact-Based Early Warning and Early Action System (MH-IB-EW-EAS).This integrated approach encompasses hazard monitoring, forecasting, risk assessment, communication, and preparedness. Aligned with the Sendai Framework’s four pathways - disaster risk knowledge; monitoring, observation, and forecasting; warning communication; and early action and response – the MH-IB-EW-EAS aims to foster resilient communities through proactive measures and effective response strategies. The implementation of the roadmap requires the participation and contribution of multiple stakeholders from the federal to the community level.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Strategy for Agricultural Development (2016-2025)
DESCRIPTION: This document notably seeks to improve resilience for farmers and agricultural areas in general. It aims to maintain biodiversity, reduce desertification, spread drought-resistant plants, enhance forest protection measures and green belts, better manage water and soil, protect grassland and grazing.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: French Strategy for Energy and Climate
DESCRIPTION: This strategy aims at achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 through sectoral policies to enhance energy efficiency, reduction of final energy use and a reinforcement of production from renewable sources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Agreement 2012-2020
DESCRIPTION:
Comprehensive agreement passed by a majority in the parliament that aims at reducing emissions via energy efficiency and increasing the share of renewable energies towards a green socio-economic transition. The overall objective is to shift energy supply to have a share of 35% renewable energy in final energy consumption by 2020 and 100% renewable energy by 2050 expected to reduce GHG emissions by approximately 34% by 2020 over 1990. It proposes a 7.6% reduction of gross energy consumption in 2020 in comparison to 2010.

It contains a number of key elements that contribute to the overall target. Energy companies must realise specific energy savings beyond current standards. It also includes development of a comprehensive strategy to improve energy efficiency standards in buildings, expansion of wind power from 25% (2012) to 50% (2020), demonstration and use of new renewable energy technologies (wave, solar, geothermal), amendment to the Heating Supply Act to increase attractiveness of shifting from coal to biomass, phasing-out of oil-fired boilers via encouraging shifts to natural gas boilers and electrical heat pumps using ambient heat in existing buildings and subsidies to promote investment in energy efficient use of renewable energy in industrial production processes, calls to draw up strategy on establishing smart grids, improving opportunities for using biogas (provision, financial support), facilitating a shift in transport sector from fossil fuels to electricity and biofuels via subsidies for car recharging stations as well as the implementation of the 10% target for renewable energies in transport by 2020 and the implementation of efficiency improvements in the energy sector.

DESCRIPTION: Kiribati National Communication. NC3 - (Third National Communication (NC3) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change )

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Forestry Act 2010 and Forestry Regulations 2014
DESCRIPTION:
The Forestry Act was enacted by the Bahamian Parliament in 2010 to provide the conservation and control of forests. It establishes a Forestry Unit under the authority of the Ministry of the Environment and Housing to regulate activities such as wood exploitation, to declare and manage forest reserves, and monitor protected trees. Reserves should be declared according to environmental conservation objectives, in particular to protect wildlife and prevent fires. The Act also regulates activities held on privately-held lands. Every five year, a Forest Management Plans must be developed.


In 2014, Forestry Regulations updated and precise the applicability of the original Act, notably in order to include carbon sequestration and reforestation within the possible objectives of Forest Management Plans. Private land-owners are equally encouraged to prepare such plans. Forest roads cannot be used as public highways unless a special governmental authorisation is priorly issued. The Regulations require that 20% of the land cover shall be designated into either a forest reserve, a protected forest or a conservation forest.
KEYWORDS: Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;REDD+ And LULUCF;Research And Development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law of the State Public Enterprise, Petróleos Mexicanos (Ley de la Empresa Pública del Estado, Petróleos Mexicanos)
DESCRIPTION: This Act provides the regulatory framework governing Petróleos Mexicanos (PEMEX) as a State-owned public enterprise, established under Articles 25, 27, and 28 of the Mexican Constitution. It affirms PEMEX's legal personality, operational and management autonomy, and special regulatory regime. The law mandates that PEMEX’s core functions encompass the exploration, transformation, and commercialisation of hydrocarbons and their derivatives, as well as the development of alternative energy sources, all in service of national sovereignty, energy security, sustainability, self-sufficiency, and energy justice.Crucially, the law integrates principles of sustainability and energy transition into PEMEX’s strategic governance. It requires a five-year Development Programme to be updated annually, detailing objectives, clean energy use, and transition planning in line with international obligations. Articles 16 and 49 establish institutional mechanisms to align corporate governance with sustainability, mandating a Sustainability Plan approved by the Board and overseen by a Sustainability Committee chaired by an independent director and comprising key ministries. The law obliges PEMEX to reduce GHG emissions and promote a low-carbon economy through targeted programmes, while ensuring transparency and accountability according to national and international standards.
