Foundation actions are: accelerate electrification and increase energy performance; ensure a fair and equitable transition; support consumers to make informed decisions; continue collaboration with states and territories; support materials efficiency; innovate to expand emissions reduction; and create a resilient built environment.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Policy on Green Procurement
DESCRIPTION:
In 2018, the Canadian government modified its existing Policy on Green Procurement to include provisions on integrating sustainable development and climate change mitigation and adaptation considerations into the federal government's procurement processes, and improving the resiliency of Canadian assets to climate change. The government expects that in introducing its Policy on Green Procurement, it will contribute to reducing greenhouse has emissions and supporting biodiversity, amongst other expected outcomes.

Deputy heads are required to ensure that the objectives of the Policy are achieved and are responsible for establishing the management processes and controls to identify environmental risks and mitigation and adaptation strategies as appropriate in the frameworks around procurement planning, the identification and definition of requirements in the procurement, the acquisition, operation and maintenance of assets, as well as in the disposal of goods or closure activities of services.

The Standard on Embodied Carbon in Construction establishes requirements to disclose and reduce the embodied carbon footprint of construction projects in accordance with the commitments in this Strategy.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 125-01: General electricity law
DESCRIPTION: This Law establishes a tax on electricity production from fossil fuels. The tax 'is specifically allocated to be spent on programmes and projects for the development of renewable sources of energy at a national level, and for national energy efficiency programmes.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Kazakhstan National Communication. NC1
DESCRIPTION: Kazakhstan National Communication. NC1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: The National Biofuel Policy
DESCRIPTION:
This Policy focuses on the use of biofuels in transportation, industry, technology, export and for a cleaner environment. The main objectives of this Policy are:

- supplementing the depleting supply of fossil fuels with renewable resources;- mobilising local resources for biofuels- exploiting local technology to generate energy for the transportation and industrial sectors;- paving the way for exports of biofuels; and- benefiting from the spin-off effect of more stable prices for palm oil.

Actions include establishing standards for B5 diesel (mixed with biofuel), mandating the use of B5 diesel, increasing the proportion of processed palm oil in the diesel blend and a greater uptake of biofuels technology by Malaysian companies and foreign companies abroad

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National plan for coastal protection of Denmark (Climate Adaptation Plan II)
DESCRIPTION:
With the Climate Adaptation Plan II, the government will take greater responsibility for coastal protection in Denmark. The government will create an investment plan for coastal protection that will ensure a strategic and cross-cutting prioritization of coastal protection projects, so that Denmark is better equipped against the threat from the sea. The government will allocate DKK 14.9 billion for the investment plan up to 2040. With that money, Denmark can build dikes, high water walls and other protection along coasts throughout the country, where there is a significant risk of flooding. With the investment plan, the government proposes a new financing model, where the state will assume a significantly greater responsibility for financing and thus support the municipalities' prioritization of coastal protection.

As part of the further work, a decision must be made on how large a share of the state expenses that landowners will subsequently be charged. The government has set up an expert group to distribute a possible financial contribution to the construction of coastal protection between the landowners, including citizens, businesses and infrastructure owners who obtain protection for the projects. At the same time, the state will take the initiative to initiate feasibility studies as a supplement to municipal feasibility studies. This work has already begun with the acceleration package, where feasibility studies will be carried out for Esbjerg, Kerteminde, Korsør, Vejle and the section from Risskov to Egå near Aarhus in 2026.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate protection programme 2026 (Klimaschutzprogramm 2026)
DESCRIPTION:
The Federal Government of Germany introduced the 2023 Climate Protection Programme to address a significant climate protection gap of 1.1 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalents by 2030, with a reduction target of 65% of all greenhouse gases compared to 1990 levels. The program encompasses various legislative amendments aimed at achieving these goals. These amendments collectively aimed to bridge the climate protection gap by up to 80%, aligning with Germany's climate targets and commitments under international agreements like the Paris Agreement. However, the German court upheld the lawsuit against the Federal Republic of Germany and determined that the Climate Protection Program must contain all measures necessary to achieve the 2030 climate protection target. The 2023 program does not meet these requirements because, firstly, the forecasts of the greenhouse gas reduction effect of the proposed measures are flawed, and secondly, there is a gap of 200 million tons of CO₂ equivalents that must be closed to achieve the 2030 target.

As a result, in March 2026, the Federal Government adopted the Climate Protection Programme 2026. The programme comprises 90 measures overall aimed at achieving climate neutrality in Germany, 67 of which are targeted at the energy, industry, buildings, transport, and agriculture sectors, with a further 23 measures addressing land use, land-use change, and forestry (LULUCF). Together these measures are projected to cut CO2 emissions by more than 25 million tonnes by 2030, intended to close the gap toward Germany's national 2030 climate target under the Bundes-Klimaschutzgesetz (KSG) and its longer-term 2045 climate-neutrality goal. Eight billion euros in additional funding is earmarked for implementation between 2027 and 2030.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Rational Use of Energy Efficiency Law (UREE)
DESCRIPTION: The Rational Use of Energy Efficiency Law (UREE), promulgated by Decree No.36-2024, establishes legal duties promoting energy efficiency across a range of sectors, reducing deadweight costs and the carbon intensity of the economy. It introduces energy labelling standards for consumer and commercial products, begins the formation of a national energy efficiency strategy, establishes energy audits, assigns departmental responsibilities, and promotes the development of tax incentives for industrial energy efficiency. It also promotes the development and expansion of low-emission transport systems, and for broader energy efficiency efforts to complement renewable energy development.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ireland Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1
DESCRIPTION: Ireland Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Electric System Development Outlook 2016-2030 (Prospectiva del Sector Eléctrico 2016-2030)
DESCRIPTION: The Mexican Electricity Sector Outlook 2016-2030 outlines policy frameworks and regulations aimed at transitioning the electricity sector towards greater sustainability and reduced greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Key to this is the introduction of competitive market actors following energy reforms, incentivising a shift from reliance on fossil fuels to cleaner energy sources. This transition is driven by international agreements on climate change, specifically COP 21, and is enshrined in Mexican law through the Electricity Industry Law (LIE) and the Energy Transition Law (LTE). These legal frameworks provide the basis for increasing the participation and regulation of clean energy sources in electricity generation, alongside the integration of the Mexican electricity sector with the North American grid.The document emphasizes international collaboration, particularly within North America, to achieve climate goals. It highlights recommendations from the Canadian Electricity Association (CEA) for increased integration across Canada, the US, and Mexico, including enhanced trade of clean electricity, promotion of transport electrification, streamlined permitting for cross-border transmission lines, joint innovation in clean energy research, and support for remote electrification with renewable resources. Furthermore, the policy underscores the importance of energy efficiency measures in buildings, such as widespread adoption of energy conservation codes, financial support for equipment upgrades, and mandatory energy labelling of buildings, as well as the modernisation of the electric grid to better integrate renewable energies and facilitate the transition to a cleaner energy mix and a reduction in energy intensity.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: 2023 National Security Strategy of Moldova
DESCRIPTION: The 2023 National Security Strategy of Moldova defines national security objectives, and acts as an orientation document to motivate actions addressing each of the areas it lists. The strategy acknowledges climate change as a significant threat to national security, emphasising the importance of increased resilience and alignment with the adaptation and mitigation measures of the EU.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ordinance 65/2014 approving the Regulations for crop insurance and loss compensation, integrated into the Integrated System of Protection against adverse climate events
DESCRIPTION: This ordinance approves tegulations on crop insurance and loss compensation, integrated into the Integrated System for the Protection against adverse climate events (SIPAC), approved by Decree-Law no. 23/2000, of 2 March.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Belarus National Communication. NC1
DESCRIPTION: Belarus National Communication. NC1 from 2003

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Royal Decree 650/2017 Setting a Quota of 3000 MW of Installed Capacity for New Plants of Electricity Production from RES Located in the Mainland Electricity System, Which Can Receive the Specific Compensation Regime
DESCRIPTION:
This Royal Decree establishes a power quota and the rules for a new call for the granting of specific remuneration to new installations for the production of electricity from wind and photovoltaic technologies in the peninsular electricity system of Spain. The greater growth potential of such technologies was witnessed through the capacity of such technologies to compete with conventional technologies in price and in terms of the high volume of power offered, through a previous auction called.
Under this Decree, the allocation of this specific remuneration scheme and the standard value of the initial investment shall be determined by means of a competitive competition procedure.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA)
DESCRIPTION: The Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) establishes a framework for improving energy conservation and efficiency. It authorises the Department of Energy to set mandatory minimum energy standards for consumer products and commercial and industrial equipment to be sold in the US. It also provides the basis for the Corprorate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards regulating the fuel efficiency of passenger vehicles and light-duty trucks. Other provisions of the EPCA includes energy conservation programmes and building strategic petroleum reserves. Over the years, the EPCA has been amended to expand the scope and stringency of standards, but since the start of 2025 the Trump Administration has weakened or rescinded several appliance efficiency standards and decreased the scope of products covered under the EPCA. Rules on certification, labelling, and enforcement have also been overturned by Congress.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Electricity Strategy 2019 - 2035
DESCRIPTION:
This strategy plans to increase electricity coverage from 32% to 100% by the end of 2035.

It also aims at reducing the cost of operation by focusing on projects to produce electricity from renewable energy, especially solar and wind energies, as well as the distribution networks.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Feed-In-Tariffs Policy On Renewable Energy Resource Generated Electricity (Small hydro, Biomass And Biogas)
DESCRIPTION: The Feed-in-Tariffs (FiT)Policy is an instrument for promoting generation of electricity from renewable energy sources. FiT allows power producers to sell renewable energy generated electricity to an Off-taker at a pre-determined tariff for a given period of time. The 2021 FiT Policy expressly states that it applies to RE power plants not exceeding 20MW in biomass, biogas and small hydro technologies. All solar and wind projects as well as other RE projects larger than 20MW will be procured under the Renewable Energy Auctions Policy

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: United States of America. Biennial Report. BR3, BR4; National Communication. NC7
DESCRIPTION: United States of America. Biennial Reports (BR). BR3. BR4. National Communication (NC). NC 7., National Communication,Biennial Report from United States of America in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Executive Decree No. 40615 creating the Scientific Council on Climate Change
DESCRIPTION:
This Decree creates the Scientific Council on Climate Change (hereinafter 4C), as an independent, consultative body, made up of academics, researchers and experts to advise the Government of Costa Rica on scientific research and technological development in the area of climate change . This Council will be attached to the Directorate of Climate Change of the Ministry of Environment and Energy (MINAE).

The Council will prepare the reports requested by the Minister of MINAE on the issues that it considers necessary and may also voluntarily express itself on those matters relevant to the purpose for which it was created.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Sector Development Plan 2035
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan contains goals and actions to ensure energy security in the transition to climate-neutral energy generation with a competitive price by 2050.

The transition to clean energy is one of the sub-goals of the development plan. The ambition to reach 100% renewable electricity consumption remains, but this will be achieved on a market-based basis at a time when production technologies are competitive without operating subsidies, which is projected to happen in the 2030+ period. The Plan leaves open, among other things, the possibility of introducing nuclear energy in the future.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decision 21/QD-BCT 2023 on Transitional Power Generation Price Framework For Solar And Wind Power Plant
DESCRIPTION: Under the Ministry of Industry and Trade's Decision 21 dated January 7, 2023 that came into force the same day, the maximum purchase price for "transitional" solar power projects is now VND1,185-1,508 (5.0-6.4 U.S. cents) per kWh, depending on the type and excluding VAT.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Forest Fund Act
DESCRIPTION:
Pursuant to section 1, the objectives of this Act are to compensate forest owners for damage caused by climate change, particularly bark beetle proliferation; to reduce the infestation of Austrian forests by bark beetles; to develop climate-smart forests and strengthen biodiversity; and to strengthen the use of wood as a raw material in order to actively contribute to climate protection.

To reach these objectives, section 2 sets up a forest fund for which 350 million euros shall be made available from federal funds.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Spanish strategy for International Climate Finance
DESCRIPTION: The Spanish Strategy for International Climate Finance outlines Spain’s commitment to supporting global climate action through a coordinated framework aligned with the Paris Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goals. Mandated by the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law (Law 7/2021), the strategy focuses on enhancing climate-resilient, low-carbon development by aligning funding with their national climate priorities. It excludes support for unabated fossil fuel projects except in limited, clearly defined cases consistent with the 1.5°C target. Principles guiding the strategy include coherence with EU taxonomy, gender equality, human rights, and fostering public-private collaboration.Key objectives include fulfilling Spain’s international commitments by scaling up climate finance to €1.35 billion by 2025, integrating climate goals into development cooperation, and leveraging investment to advance ecological transitions. The strategy prioritises renewable energy, green transitions, and sustainable development projects while enhancing accountability and alignment with recipient countries’ climate plans.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy code
DESCRIPTION: The Energy Code establishes attribution criteria for the subsidy under the Bicycle Bonus Scheme.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Agriculture Policy Framework 2018-2030
DESCRIPTION: This document aims to modernise the country's agricultural sector, enable investments and a switch to sustainable production. It seeks to improve farmer resilience and promote sustainable agricultural practices in response to climate change.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law on Hydrometeorology
DESCRIPTION:
This Law stipulates hydrometerological activities including managing and exploiting the station network; forecasting and warning; information and data; providing hydrometeorological services; climate change monitoring; impact on weather and state management; rights, responsibilities and obligations of agencies, organizations and individuals participating in hydrometeorological activities.

The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment is responsible for regularly organising forms of dissemination, legal education, propaganda and raising awareness of hydrometeorology and climate change, focusing on people in mountainous areas, coastal fishermen, islands, ethnic minority areas and areas with particularly difficult socio-economic conditions; developing, organising and implementing projects to disseminate, legal education, propaganda and raise awareness of hydrometeorology and climate change.Vietnam News Agency, Voice of Vietnam, Vietnam Television and press agencies are responsible for organising the transmission and distribution of hydrometeorological forecasts and warnings, information on climate change in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the law on the press.

The Law also specifies the contents of climate change monitoring; the contents of the national climate assessment; the need to integrate the results of climate change monitoring into strategies and plans; and the contents of international cooperation on hydrometeorological activities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2022-2030 (Plan Nacional de Gestión de Riesgo de Desastres 2022 - 2030)
DESCRIPTION: The National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2022-2030 (PLANAGERD) establishes a comprehensive framework for reducing disaster risks in Peru, aligning with the Marco de Sendai 2015–2030 and the Act No. 29.664 (Ley N° 29664). It prioritises systemic risk reduction through six key objectives: (1) enhancing disaster risk understanding via integrated data systems and climate change considerations; (2) improving land use and occupation to mitigate vulnerabilities; (3) strengthening coordinated governance across sectors and levels of government; (4) integrating disaster risk into public and private investments; (5) ensuring timely and effective emergency response; and (6) promoting inclusive recovery for affected populations. The PLANAGERD underscores the critical role of data-driven risk assessment and interoperable digital platforms (e.g., SIGRID, GEOIDEP) to enhance preparedness and decision-making. It addresses vulnerabilities from informal land use and climate-driven disasters, advocating for sustainable infrastructure and resilient livelihoods. The plan also highlights the need to embed disaster risk management in public and private investments, ensuring that development projects avoid exacerbating risks.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Governmental Decree No.2019 of 2008 adopting the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan
DESCRIPTION:
This Decree adopts the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP). The first NEEAP outlined the existing planned energy efficiency measures to decrease the energy consumption by 1% annually during the nine years between 2008 and 2016. The objectives of the NEEAP I are as follows: alignment of Hungary's energy policy initiatives with those of the EU; finding the most cost-effective solutions for utilization of energy-saving potential; shaping consumer awareness and influencing the market in order to achieve long-term energy efficiency; informing market players of the structure and time frame of the plans; realization of the EU's energy efficiency expectations of member states; and consideration of climate protection aspects. According to the NEEAP and the Governmental decree No.64 of 2009, the Ministry of National Development (former Ministry of Transport, Telecommunication and Energy) is responsible for the preparation of NEEAPs. Co-ordination of the implementation of NEEAP and the verification of its progress falls under the responsibility of the Energy Centre, a government-owned energy efficiency, environment and energy information agency non-profit company. It is the national agency responsible for energy efficiency and renewable energy.

The Plan also notes that actions including the following could further save energy:extension of state aid to upgrade household appliances and lightbulbs; state aid to develop energy saving awareness activities; making the use of energy efficient office equipment obligatory; promotion of the dissemination of energy-saving building technologies; and strengthening the energy aspect of environmental and traffic safety considerations in connection with the import of used vehicles.

The NEEAP was modified in 2010 under the Governmental Decision No.1076 of 2010 on the Modified National Energy Efficiency Action Plan of Hungary (MNEEAP) and the second NEEAP (NEEAP II) was adopted under the Governmental Decision No.1374 of 2011. The NEEAP II includes shortcomings and an action plan aiming to solve them, national energy saving targets and measures in energy end-use, sectoral measures for energy saving and institutions responsible for implementation and monitoring. Identified shortcomings includes the lack of following: overarching, nationwide demand forecast based on reliable fuel and electricity demand forecast; sufficient monitoring of implementation of the measures in NEEAP I; reliable information on opportunities for energy savings in industry; energy data of dwelling houses; and reliable data about the energy consumption of public buildings.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Council Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2020/2093 laying down the multiannual financial framework for the years 2021 to 2027, last amended by Council Regulation (EU,Euratom) 2024/765 (MFF 2021-2027)
DESCRIPTION:
The Regulation sets the EU’s seven‑year budgetary framework (the MFF) for 2021‑2027, establishing the maximum annual ceilings for commitments and payments across the major spending headings and ensuring predictability for medium‑term investments. It obliges the EU institutions to comply with these ceilings when preparing and implementing the annual budgets.

The Regulation has been amended to respond to evolving circumstances—including support for Ukraine and adjustments for “new own resources”— through Council Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2022/2496 and Council Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/765, which modify the ceilings and flexibilities within the MFF to reflect changing financial and geopolitical priorities.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Preparing Israel to Adapt to Climate Change: implementing the recommendations to the government for a national strategy and action plan (Decree 4079)
DESCRIPTION:
This Decree acknowledges the need to ensure Israel is prepared for climate change. It established the National adaptation Administration ("The Secretariat"), an entity overseen by the MoEP, with the aim of overseeing and executing the National Adaptation Plan.

The Decree also mandates the National Emergency Authority, to formulate national emergency plans in light of extreme weather events. It is also responsible for leading the Emergency Subcommittee, who in collaboration with meteorological services evaluate reference scenarios for fires, floods, and other extreme events.

In 2022, Decree 4079 was amended by Decree 1902 to set a final date for the preparation and submission of adaptation plans by ministries for the end of 2023.

DESCRIPTION: Trinidad and Tobago. National Communication (NC). NC 3., National Communication from Trinidad and Tobago in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Carbon Emissions Trading Management Regulations
DESCRIPTION: These regulations apply to the supervision and management of national carbon emissions trading and related activities. The ETS focuses on the power sector.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Thermal Regulation 2012 (RT 2012)
DESCRIPTION:
• The Regulation replaces the Thermal Regulations 2000 and 2005, introducing more stringent regulations of thermal insulation and heating systems.

    RT 2005 required 15% improvement of thermal efficiency (compared to a building constructed following the guidelines of RT2000) and applied to new buildings. It also created a labelling system to identify energy efficient buildings and introduces measures to discourage air-conditioned buildings in France. Calculations now include natural lighting and renewable energy sources. RT 2012 strengthens the existing requirements (and lays down the following main requirements:Minimum energy efficiency requirement for the 'bioclimatic need' - 'Biomax' of the building (isolation, efficiency of heating and lighting systems)
  • Maximum average primary energy consumption of the building below 50 kWh/m²/year - 'Cmax'
  • Summer comfort requirement (maximum interior temperature for 5 consecutive summer days) to encourage bioclimatic architecture

 
Additional requirements and guidelines are set for: the general building quality, living comfort, preference for renewable energies, good energy use of the building, potential for energy production beyond self-sufficient production.

Overall, the RT 2012 aims at reducing the primary energy consumption in buildings by 150bn kWh between 2013 and 2020 and reducing the CO2 emissions by 13m-35m tonnes of CO2 (depending on the method) between 2013 and 2020.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Sustainable Forestry Development Program for Wellbeing
DESCRIPTION: The "Sustainable Forestry Development Program for Wellbeing 2025" in Mexico, adopted in 2025, aims to address deforestation and environmental degradation through conservation strategies, sustainable development, and active community engagement. The policy targets the protection and sustainable use of Mexico’s forests by promoting community-based management and operational programs designed to halt deforestation and promote forest restoration. It includes the Environmental Compensation Program for Land Use Change in Forest Areas, which mandates restoration activities such as reforestation and soil recovery to offset environmental impacts.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Forest Plan
DESCRIPTION: The National Forest Plan aims to implement the Forest Act as revised in 2005. It was originally planned to review the Plan every five years from 2005 onwards. The Plan notably sets protection and reforestation targets, and mentions carbon trading as a financial mean for environmental action.
KEYWORDS: Adaptation;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;REDD+ And LULUCF;Research And Development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ordinance (2022:225) on State aid for the production of biogas upgraded to biomethane
DESCRIPTION: This regulation provides companies who produce biogas the possibility to apply for the production support for biogas that is upgraded to biomethane in gas or liquid form with such quality that is required for gas grids. The Swedish Energy Agency is responsible for administrating the grant.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Renewable Energy & Energy Efficiency Law, No. 13 of 2012
DESCRIPTION:
The renewable energy and energy efficiency law provides the legislative framework to encourage exploitation of enable energy sources, further supply-side energy efficiency and streamline private sector investment through incentives. It states that to achieve the objectives the government will focus on: Increasing investment in renewable energy extraction, thereby increasing the proportion of renewables in the energy mix; Working towards sustainable development through environment-friendly energy extraction; and pursuing rational and efficient energy extraction.

The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources is in charge of enacting the law, and a first order of business was the identification of geographic areas for renewable energy exploitation. These areas, co-ordinated with the Ministry's Energy Master Plan, will be prioritised for development in a Land Use List, approved by the Council of Ministers. Areas identified for exploitation that are 'treasury land' (owned by the state) shall be allocated to renewable energy projects. Lands owned by individuals shall be purchased based on existing legislative authority, if approved by the Council of Ministers. In addition to hosting a competitive bidding processes to develop projects on lands prioritised on the Land Use List, individuals or projects may approach the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources with a specific proposal to develop an extraction site on any lands in the country (already identified on the Land Use List or not) which have not already been allocated by a public tender. The law outlines the requirements for such proposals and a general outline for the decision making process. The law specifies the purchasing arrangements of the electricity from bulk suppliers; much of this framework is pre-existing in the General Electricity Law. Under the renewable energy law, individual homes may also produce their own renewable electricity, selling any surplus energy back to the grid with the price set by the purchase tariff specified in the Bulk Supply Licensees or the Retail Supply Licensees. On an institutional level this law establishes the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Fund, which shall be administratively and financially independent. The Fund is overseen by the Board of Directors of the Fund, composed of the vice-chairman of the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources; the secretaries-general of the Ministries of Environment, Planning and International Co-operation, and Finance; a commissioner nominated by the Chairman of the Board of Commissioners of the Commission, and three representatives of the private sector appointed by the Council of Ministers. The Fund draws resources from: government allocations from the general budget, returns on investments, aid or gifts from national or international donors.

DESCRIPTION: "Matters Relating to the Global Stocktake referred to in Article 14 of the Paris Agreement": Submission by India – On behalf of the LMDC Group, Submission to the Global Stocktake from India,Like-minded Developing Countries (LMDC) in 2022

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 laying down common provisions on a range of support funds, amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/955
DESCRIPTION:
This Regulation lays down financial rules for:

  • the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF),
  • the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+),
  • the Cohesion Fund,
  • the Just Transition Fund (JTF),
  • the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF),
  • the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF),
  • the Internal Security Fund (ISF), and
  • the Instrument for Financial Support for Border Management and Visa Policy (BMVI).

The Regulation also establishes common provisions applicable to the ERDF, the ESF+, the Cohesion Fund, the JTF and the EMFAF.

The ERDF, the ESF+, the Cohesion Fund and the EMFAF shall support the following policy objectives:

  1. a more competitive and smarter Europe by promoting innovative and smart economic transformation and regional ICT connectivity;
  2. a greener, low-carbon transitioning towards a net zero carbon economy and resilient Europe by promoting clean and fair energy transition, green and blue investment, the circular economy, climate change mitigation and adaptation, risk prevention and management, and sustainable urban mobility;
  3. a more connected Europe by enhancing mobility;
  4. a more social and inclusive Europe implementing the European Pillar of Social Rights;
  5. a Europe closer to citizens by fostering the sustainable and integrated development of all types of territories and local initiatives.

The JTF shall support the specific objective of enabling regions and people to address the social, employment, economic and environmental impacts of the transition towards the Union’s 2030 targets for energy and climate and a climate-neutral economy of the Union by 2050, based on the Paris Agreement.

Article 6 on climate targets and climate adjustment mechanism states that:

  1. Member States shall provide information on support for environment and climate objectives by using a methodology based on types of intervention for each of the Funds. That methodology shall consist of assigning a specific weighting to the support provided at a level which reflects the extent to which such support makes a contribution to environmental objectives and to climate objectives. In the case of the ERDF, the ESF+ and the Cohesion Fund, weightings shall be attached to dimensions and codes for the types of intervention established in Annex I. The ERDF and the Cohesion Fund shall contribute with 30 % and 37 % respectively of the Union contribution to expenditure supported for the achievement of the climate objectives set for the Union budget.
  2. The climate contribution target for each Member State shall be established as a percentage of its total ERDF and Cohesion Fund allocation and included in programmes as a result of the types of intervention and the indicative financial breakdown pursuant to point (d)(viii) of Article 22(3). As provided for in Article 11(1), the preliminary climate contribution target shall be established in the Partnership Agreement.
  3. The Member State and the Commission shall regularly monitor respect of the climate contribution targets, based on the total eligible expenditure declared by the beneficiaries to the managing authority as broken down by types of intervention in accordance with Article 42 and on data submitted by the Member State. Where the monitoring shows insufficient progress towards reaching the climate contribution target, the Member State and the Commission shall agree on remedial measures in the annual review meeting.
  4. Where there is insufficient progress towards reaching the climate contribution target at national level by 31 December 2024, the Member State shall take this into account in its mid-term review in accordance with Article 18(1).

This Regulation was amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/955 which establishes the Social Climate Fund for the period from 2026 to 2032.

The Social Climate Fund shall provide financial support to Member States for the measures and investments included in their Social Climate Plans. Each Member State should submit to the Commission a Social Climate Plan by 30 June 2025.

The measures and investments supported by the Social Climate Fund shall benefit households, micro-enterprises and transport users, which are vulnerable and particularly affected by the inclusion of greenhouse gas emissions from buildings and road transport within the scope of Directive 2003/87/EC (EU emissions trading scheme), in particular households in energy poverty or households in transport poverty.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: CONAMA Resolution 403/2008 that establishes Motor Vehicle Pollution Control
DESCRIPTION: This resolution provides for the new phase of the Air Pollution Control Program Control of Air Pollution by Motor Vehicles (PROCONVE) for new heavy-duty vehicles (Phase P-7) and makes other provisions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Environmental Improvement Plan 2025
DESCRIPTION:
The Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025 is a strategic framework for improving England’s natural environment up to 2043, containing interim targets for the statutory Environment Act 2021 targets. It sets out how the government will work alongside individuals, communities and businesses to achieve England's nature ambitions in the context of nature depletion.

The EIP contains 10 goals on: the restoration of nature; the improvement of environmental quality through goals on air, water, chemicals and pesticides; driving forward a circular economy through goals on waste and resources; the achievement of environmental security through goals on climate, hazards and biosecurity; and increase to access to nature.

There is a focus on actions and investment to:

  • enhance the quantity and state of our critical natural capital assets;
  • capture more of the benefits from natural assets; and
  • reduce the pressures on our natural capital assets from direct use and respond to external threats.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Alternative Energy Development Plan 2015-2036
DESCRIPTION:
The Alternative Energy Development plan (AEDP), developed by the Ministry of Energy has developed the Thailand Integrated Energy Blueprint (TIEB) focuses on three key areas:

  1. Energy security - in relation to energy supply

  2. Economy - regards to controlling energy and fuel costs while promoting efficiency

  3. Ecology - increasing domestic renewable energy production to reduce impact on environment


The AEDP defines overall goals for the increase of renewable energy from the current 7,300 MW to almost 20,000 MW by 2036, and to achieve 20 % of net national electrical energy demand being supplied by renewable energy sources by 2036.
The following capacities are envisaged for the respective sectors:

  • Waste-to-energy: 550 MW (currently approx. 65 MW)

  • Biomass: 5,570 MW (currently approx. 2,500 MW)

  • Biogas from waste /wastewater: 600 MW (currently approx. 300 MW)

  • Biogas from plants: 680 MW

  • Wind energy: 3,002 MW (currently approx. 225 MW)

  • Solar energy: 6,000 MW (currently 1,300 MW)

  • Hydropower (small): 376 MW (currently 142 MW)

  • Hydropower (large): unchanged (currently approx. 3,000 MW)

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Capacity Building Action Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction, Emergency Preparedness and Response 2015-2020
DESCRIPTION: This document lays out Chad's vision to reinforce its capacities to prevent and face disasters, including climate-related events.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal Decree-Law No. (11) of 2024 on the Reduction of Climate Change Effects
DESCRIPTION:
This Federal Decree confers powers and obligations on Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (“the Ministry”) and the local authorities in the UAE to manage greenhouse gas emissions to achieve climate neutrality, and strengthen adaptation. The Decree also sets out the obligations of public and private legal persons to reduce and measure emissions, with penalties for non-compliance.

For mitigation, the Decree mandates that the Cabinet determine annual targets for emission reduction for all sectors, while local authorities shall develop the plans and procedures for each sector to achieve the target. For adaptation, the Ministry shall issue a resolution regarding the development of adaptation plans, while local authorities shall develop and implement adaptation plans.

The Decree also contains provisions on contributing to climate science and research; international cooperation mechanisms; carbon offsetting mechanisms including establishing the National Carbon Credit Registry; approving and periodically reviewing Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs); and preparing international reports. The law will come into effect on 30 May 2025.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Ministerial Resolution No. 196-2021-MINAM. Methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Local Climate Change Plans (Resolución Ministerial Nº196-2021-MINAM. Lineamientos metodológicos para la formulación y la actualización de los Planes Locales de Cambio Climático)
DESCRIPTION: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N° 152-2021-MINAM establishes methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (ERCC), positioning them as mandatory instruments that operationalise climate action at the subnational level. These strategies, aligned with Peru's National Climate Change Strategy and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), must incorporate both adaptation and mitigation measures across five mitigation sectors (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, land use and forestry, and waste) and seven adaptation areas (water, agriculture, forests, health, fisheries and aquaculture, tourism, and transport). The guidelines mandate that regional governments integrate climate measures into their Regional Development Plans, Strategic Institutional Plans, Operational Plans, budget programmes, and investment projects.The resolution outlines a structured five-phase methodology comprising Organisation, Territory Analysis, Planning, Implementation, and Monitoring and Evaluation, emphasising participatory processes that ensure effective engagement with state and non-state actors, particularly indigenous peoples. Regional governments must establish working groups within their Regional Environmental Commissions to lead strategy development, ensuring climate risk analysis, identification of greenhouse gas emission sources, and determination of adaptation and mitigation measures with enabling conditions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law (Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria)
DESCRIPTION: The Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law is a piece of legislation governing the management of public finances in Mexico. It sets out the legal framework for programming, budgeting, approving, executing, controlling, and evaluating federal public income and expenditures, ensuring that public resources are managed with principles of legality, efficiency, transparency, and accountability. Among its key provisions, the law establishes guidelines for the distribution of funds, including allocations for energy transition and climate change initiatives. The law outlines the operation of the Mexican Petroleum Fund (Fondo Mexicano del Petróleo), which serves to manage revenues from oil and gas activities and directs part of these funds toward energy sustainability and climate change-related projects.In terms of climate change and energy transition, the law mandates that part of the resources from the Mexican Petroleum Fund be dedicated to research and innovation in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and clean technologies. Article 88 of the law specifies that a significant portion of these funds (65%) should support scientific and technological initiatives focused on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and clean technology, as well as energy diversification. Additionally, the law directs the Ministry of Energy and the National Council of Science and Technology to collaborate on projects that advance Mexico's energy transition in line with its international commitments to mitigate climate change. Through these provisions, the law seeks to align Mexico's fiscal management with its environmental and energy goals.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree establishing the Inter-ministerial Commission on Climate Change (CIMGC) and related resolutions
DESCRIPTION:
This Decree establishes the Inter-ministerial Commission on Climate Change (CIMGC), composed of nine ministries and headed by the Ministry of Science and Technology, for the purpose of co-ordinating discussions on climate change and integrating the government's policies in these ministries. The CIMGC provides input on the government's involvement with the UNFCCC and sets criteria and makes decisions on Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) projects.

Order 533, of 29 August 2000, established the by-laws of the CIMGC.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Decree n° 2015-1491 on the national carbon budgets and the national low-carbon strategy
DESCRIPTION:
This decree modifies the Environment Code in order to define and set carbon budgets. 


The decree further adopts the National Low-Carbon Strategy (SNBC), which was replaced in April 2020 through Decree No. 2020-457.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Georgia’s 2030 Climate Strategy and Action Plan 2021-2023
DESCRIPTION: This document was prepared in accordance with government's Ordinance no 629/2019 on the “Approval of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation of Policy Documents.” It consists of a strategy to 2030 and an action plan covering the period 2021-2023. It identifies mitigation measures capable of translating into action the objectives set out in Georgia's existing NDCs, therefore of meeting the country's international commitments, but also to determine the future level of ambition. The document sets specific GHG emissions reductions targets against the projection of a reference scenario.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Fifteenth Development Plan (2019/20–2023/24)
DESCRIPTION:
This Plan sets the target to ensure that there are 460 localities that have prepared and implemented a climate change adaptation plan by FY 2023/24. One of the national objectives is to implement strategies of climate change adaptability and disaster risk reduction, mainstreaming disaster management into the development process through institutional and structural reforms at the federation, province, and local levels for preparedness, rescue and relief, and rehabilitation.

A section covers the strategies for climate change adaptation and mitigation, and accessing international finance and technologies, including forest management, green development, and electric vehicles.

There are also sectoral goals that are climate-relevant. For instance, the goal for the agricultural sector is to acheive inclusive and sustainable economic growth through the transformation of the agricultural sector into a competitive, climate-resilient, self-reliant and export-oriented industry, by developing climate-adaptive and resilient organic farming. For tourism, sensitive tourist destinations and cultural heritage sites vulnerable to climate risks will be identified and protected. For water, the objective is to ensure climate change-resilient and disaster management-friendly drinking-water and sanitation services.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: GX2040 Vision: A revised Strategy for Promoting the Transition to a Decarbonized Growth-Oriented Economic Structure
DESCRIPTION: The GX2040 Vision, approved by the Japanese Cabinet in February 2025, sets out Japan's long-term strategy for achieving a "Green Transformation" (GX). Japan's GX2040 Vision is a national green industrial transformation strategy that provides a long-term framework for achieving economic growth, energy security, and decarbonization simultaneously. The strategy promotes investment in clean technologies, industrial decarbonization, carbon-pricing mechanisms, low-carbon energy systems, and the development of competitive green industries, while supporting a just transition for affected workers and regions.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Resolution No. 70-NQ/TW - Resolution of the Politburo on ensuring national security to 2030, vision to 2045
DESCRIPTION: This Resolution lays out the direction and focus for energy in Vietnam, to meet the needs of socio-economic development, national defence and security. The Vision to 2045 includes ensuring national energy security, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and adapting to climate change. The intention is to establish a management and risk response system, regularly update scenarios, implement solutions to respond to climate change, promote international cooperation for the same, and the transfer green technology from advanced countries.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation 280/2019 on Latvian Building Code LBN 002-19 "Thermal Engineering of Building Enclosing Structures"
DESCRIPTION: This regulation sets out the Latvian building standard LBN 002-19, which defines thermal performance and energy efficiency requirements for external building envelope structures (walls, roofs, floors, windows/doors, etc.) in new, reconstructed, and renovated heated buildings in Latvia. Its purpose is to reduce energy consumption and heat loss through building elements by specifying design and calculation methods for thermal resistance and airtightness, aligned with the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (2010/31/EU), thereby supporting lower energy demand, improved indoor climate, and reduced CO₂ emissions from buildings.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 42 - Guidelines for the national policy on biofuels and electric energy from biomass
DESCRIPTION:
This law establishes guidelines for the national policy on biofuels, electric energy from biomass and cogeneration. It seeks to improve health, boost agricultural output and productive jobs, improve the security of supply and ease local and foreign investment.

Chapter II charges the National Secretariat for Energy to define a national policy for the production, trade and use of biofuels and biomass (art. 3). The Secretariat will further be in charge of impulse and implement strategic plans on the issue (art. 6).

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Australia's long term emissions reduction plan : A whole-of-economy Plan to achieve net zero emissions by 2050
DESCRIPTION:
This plan sets out a roadmap for how Australia plans to achieve its target of net zero emissions by 2050. The plan is based on five key principles:1. Technology not taxes – no new costs for households or businesses,2. Expand choices, not mandates – we will work to expand consumer choice, both domestically and with our trading partners,3. Drive down the cost of a range of new energy technologies – bringing a portfolio of technologies to parity is the objective of Australia’s Technology Investment Roadmap,

4. Keep energy prices down with affordable and reliable power – our Plan will consolidate our advantage in affordable and reliable energy, protecting the competitiveness of our industries and the jobs they support, and

5. Be accountable for progress – transparency is essential to converting ambition into achievement. Australia will continue to set ambitious yet achievable whole- of-economy goals, then beat them, consistent with our approach to our Kyoto- era and Paris Agreement targets.The plan states that the "wellbeing and prosperity of Australia’s regional communities at its core. It will not impose new costs on households, businesses or the broader economy. Our actions under the Plan will not lead to job losses or place burdens onto regional communities."The plan contains four chapters focused on: Driving down the costs of low emissions technologies, Enabling deployment at scale, Seizing opportunities in new and traditional markets, and Fostering global collaboration. It makes reference to a number of other key policy documents, including the Technology Investment Roadmap.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Fast Start Financing: U.S. Climate Funding in FY 2010
DESCRIPTION: Fast Start Financing: U.S. Climate Funding in FY 2010, Fast-Start Finance Report from United States of America in 2011

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Integrated Power Sector Master Plan 2023
DESCRIPTION: This Plan sets out the long-term Least-Regrets power sector resource plan to meet Ghana's future electricity demand, through optimising existing and future power plants and other energy systems, and transmission capability, and to increase the resilience of the power system to potential risks including climate change. One of the objectives is to meet Ghana's local environmental and climate change commitments, amidst other objectives such as achieving cost-competitiveness in power generation and delivery; meeting local demand and exports; and increasing the resilience in the power system.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law No. 19.772 on Land-use Planning and Sustainable Development of the Coastal Area of the Atlantic Ocean and the Rio de la Plata
DESCRIPTION:
This Law seeks to promote the sustainable and democratic use of natural and cultural resources of the coastal zones of the Atlantic Ocean and the Rio de la Plata, in order to contribute to maintaining and improving the life quality and the social integration of the population in the territory. 

One of the Law's objectives is the adaptation of costal zone interventions to climate change and increased variability.

DESCRIPTION: Philippines Biennial Transparency Report. BTR1

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
DESCRIPTION:
This action plan outlines the current legal and institutional framework around renewable energy, as per the requirements of the EU's Renewable Energy Directive.This document aims to achieve the following:

  1. Assess the current legislative and institutional framework for renewable energy, specifically checking its compliance with the Renewable Energy Directive.
  2. Recommend policy and investment measures necessary to both meet the 2020 target of 30% renewable energy consumption and fully implement the Directive, along with an estimate of the associated costs.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Zambia's Climate Change Gender Action Plan (CCGAP)
DESCRIPTION: The ccGAP is an intersectional document aiming at advancing women empowerment and enabling gender equality while setting climate change response plans. It focuses in priority on sustainable agriculture and food security; Health; Forests, biodiversity and wildlife; Water security, Disaster risk reduction, preparedness and resilience; Infrastructure; Energy; and Tourism. It promotes policy reform and synergy; education and awareness-raising; academic research, sex-disaggregated data, and information dissemination—both for public awareness and to inform policy; and capacity building and training.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Central Bank of Egypt Mandatory Regulations
DESCRIPTION:
The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) issued mandatory regulations through a circular in November 2022 to require banks to: 

·       Set up an independent unit that deals with sustainability and sustainable finance by 1 April 2023; 

·       From 2024, submit periodic reports, including a quarterly report on sustainable finance activities, and a yearly sustainability report by 31 March of each year;

·       From July 2023, engage an environmental consultant certified by the Ministry of Environment to assess environmental risks for major projects seeking funding; and

·       Integrate sustainable finance policies into lending and investment policies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Strategy for the Sustainable Development of the Industry of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2019-2023 and Action Plan
DESCRIPTION: This document was adopted by Decree 502/2019. It aims to improve the dedicated regulatory framework, create infrastructure and conditions for attracting investment in the industrial sector, and introduce industrial innovative technologies.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: German Climate Adaptation Strategy 2024
DESCRIPTION:
The strategy defines measurable goals for climate adaptation in Germany, a total of 33 goals and 45 sub-goals. Most goals are to be achieved by 2030, some by 2050. The objectives are assigned indicators to measure the achievement of objectives. The following applies: No additional bureaucratic burdens or reporting obligations will be created for citizens or companies.

The objectives are assigned to seven clusters that reflect the entire range of adaptation and prevention:

  1. Infrastructure
  2. Land and land use
  3. human health and care
  4. Urban development, spatial planning and civil protection
  5. Water
  6. ECONOMICS
  7. Cross-cluster topics

The strategy aims to strengthen the resilience, i.e. the resilience, of the landscape water balance – this means above all, to restore the ability of the landscape to store water. This requires, among other things, as many unsealed surfaces as possible that can absorb water and healthy, loose soils that can store the water for a long time. This is a sub-goal to the goal of "Preserving available water resources in the long term".

The Adaptation Action Plan IV (APA IV) (Annex 2 to the Strategy) implements the Climate Adaptation Strategy 2024 and defines the measures with which the Federal Government is driving forward Germany's adaptation to climate change and how it is supporting responsible stakeholders in the implementation of measures. It presents the federal government's current and future measures for adapting to the climate impacts.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Act 250/2012 on regulation of network industries, last amended by Act 260/2025
DESCRIPTION: Act No. 250/2012 Coll. on regulation in network industries establishes the institutional and regulatory framework for overseeing key utility sectors in Slovakia, including electricity, gas, heat, and water services. The Act defines the powers and responsibilities of the Regulatory Office for Network Industries, which is tasked with setting or approving energy prices, issuing licenses, and ensuring that regulated services are delivered at reasonable prices and adequate quality. It sets out rules for market functioning, obligations of regulated entities, and mechanisms to protect consumers while maintaining security of supply. Through successive amendments, the Act has been progressively aligned with EU energy legislation, strengthening the independence and competences of the regulator, increasing transparency in price-setting, and adapting tariff methodologies to reflect market conditions and decarbonisation objectives. Recent reforms linked to broader energy legislation updates have further enhanced regulatory oversight, supported the integration of renewable energy sources, and adjusted pricing frameworks to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and improve the efficiency and sustainability of network industries.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Law 2003-010 National Strategy for Disaster Risk Management
DESCRIPTION:
According to the law, risk management and disaster fits into the overall framework of activities relating to civil protection and security. The guiding principles are: guarantee the protection of the population and of the environment; improve the resilience of the population in cases of risks and catastrophes; and develop conditions to reduce the vulnerability of the population - although there is no explicit mention of climate change adaptation.
 
 The law provides mechanisms and measures to safeguard hazards and disasters. The strategy for DRC is based on preventive measures, warning, preparation, management, relief, recovery, reconstruction and development.
 
 The institutional structure for DRM activities includes: the National Council for Disaster Risk Management, a high level co-ordination and strategic decision-making body that is presided over by the Prime Minister and comprised of ministerial representatives; and the National Office for Disaster Risk Management, under the Ministry of Interior. The law calls for the decentralization of DRM responsibilities to the regional, district and commune level.
 
 The SNGRC is currently being revised.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Landfill Methane Regulations
DESCRIPTION:
These Regulations apply to certain privately and municipally owned landfills that have received municipal solid waste.

These Regulations will reduce methane emissions from landfills through a performance-based approach that sets surface methane concentration limits and requires regular monitoring to confirm these limits are being met and to identify and repair methane leaks.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate and Energy Fund Act
DESCRIPTION: The Act supports the development of a sustainable energy system for Austria and the reduction of GHG emissions. Its targets include cutting energy consumption by 25% by 2010 and 45% by 2020. Energy intensity must be decreased by 5% by 2010 and by 20% by 2020. The Fund's activities are focused on three key areas: research into renewable energy systems, development and testing of new transport systems, and acceleration of commercial climate mitigation measures.
KEYWORDS: Energy Demand;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation No. 1398 on Electricity Certificates Regulation
DESCRIPTION: The regulation sets out the incentive mechanism introduced by the Electricity Certificates Act, i.e. the quota system for electricity from renewable sources.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Government Bill (2009/2010: 172) & Government Bill (2009/2010:173) on nuclear power
DESCRIPTION:
Passed by the Riksdag, these laws originating in government bills regulate the conditions for constructing and operating new nuclear facilities. New units are only permitted when they replace existing units (a maximum of 10), whereby the older reactor must be permanently disabled and the new reactor needs to be built on an existing nuclear facility instead of a new location.

The laws reverse the phase-out of nuclear power production, repealing the Nuclear Phase-Out Act and the ban on new nuclear power facilities.

The purpose of the law is to allow old nuclear reactors to be replaced with newer, safer models. It also reflects the recent shift towards new carbon technologies as opposed to a stronger expansion of renewable energies classified as counting towards climate mitigation. The Swedish parliament approved the act under the condition that no direct or indirect public funding may be available for the new nuclear power reactors.

Parliament also stipulated that operators of nuclear facilities and the owners of nuclear power reactors carry unlimited liability in the event of a nuclear accident. Companies are required to hold insurance against third-party claims up to EUR1.2bn (USD1.51bn).
KEYWORDS: Energy Supply;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Action Plan towards the reduction of greenhouse gases emissions
DESCRIPTION:
The Action Plan towards the reduction of greenhouse gases emissions was published by the Luxembourgish government in 2006 to fulfil the country's commitments within the Kyoto framework, and to enable sustainable development in energy-related sectors. The Action Plan defines mitigation measures that constitute a long-term strategy to combat climate change.
 
In the transport sector, the Plan seeks to 1) increase the tax rate on liquid fuels, 2) reform the vehicle tax with environmental criteria, 3) double public transport's modal share to 25% by 2020, and 4) carry out other measures dedicated to "soft mobility". In the building sector, the Plan calls for new legislation over energy conservation and efficiency and a related subsidy scheme. The Plan also promotes renewable resources such as biomass, biogas, hydro and wind, through feed-in tariffs and other subsidy schemes. In the industrial and electricity supply sectors, the Plan calls for a modification of the quota system to reduce greenhouse gases emissions and for enhanced energy conservation.
 
The Plan further proposes 1) to strengthen education and professional training in low-carbon energy technologies and techniques, 2) to participate to several financing schemes from non-luxembourgish entities, and 3) to set up a governmental task force to follow on the Action Plan which is meant to evolve across time through periodic plans for sustainable development and midterm strategies.
KEYWORDS: Energy Demand;Energy Supply;Institutions / Administrative Arrangements;Research And Development;Transport

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Commission Communication on managing climate risks
DESCRIPTION: The Communication presents an urgent call for the European Commission and Member States to move from climate‑risk awareness to systematic and proactive risk management, recognising that increasing temperatures, extreme weather events, and cascading disasters are now material threats to people, ecosystems, infrastructure and the economy. It identifies major risk clusters and outlines four pillars of action: improved governance (clearer responsibilities, stronger coordination at all levels), better tools for risk‑owners (data, modelling, early warning, capacity‑building), harnessing structural policies (spatial planning, critical‑infrastructure resilience, nature‑based solutions) and right pre‑conditions for financing climate resilience (public procurement, investment frameworks, private‑finance mobilisation). The Communication also sets out thematic priorities—ecosystems, water, health, food systems, infrastructure built environment—and proposes concrete EU‑level actions for each, aiming to embed resilience and adaptation into all sectors and ensure that climate risk‑informed decision‑making becomes standard practice across the Union.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: National Energy Sector Strategy (2020-2030)
DESCRIPTION: Following Jordan's 2015-2025 Energy Sector Strategy, the new strategy for the 2020-2030 period aims to further enhance energy security, interconnectivity, efficiency and promotion renewable sources. Recommendations and goals include: an increase in renewables generation from 2400MW in 2020 to 3200MW by 2030; a greater role for storage in Jordan's national grid, to allow maximal usage of renewable generation; expansion of smart meters for electricity users; and expansion of electric vehicles for private and public transport.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Action Plan for the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda
DESCRIPTION:
The Action Plan for the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda serves as a transitional framework to operationalise the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development in Spain, setting the groundwork for a long-term Sustainable Development Strategy (2020–2030). This comprehensive action plan seeks to align national policies with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), fostering collaboration across government levels, civil society, academia, and the private sector. It emphasises immediate measures to tackle pressing issues such as poverty, inequality, and environmental sustainability, while proposing governance reforms and accountability mechanisms to ensure effective implementation.
Climate change plays a pivotal role in this plan, notably through the Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition, which aims to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and build resilience to climate risks. Among others, the plan supports the integration of sustainable energy systems (SDG 7) and urgent climate action (SDG 13), alongside cross-cutting policies on circular economy, water management, and urban development. This holistic approach underscores a commitment to a just transition, ensuring social equity while advancing towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy. By embedding climate considerations within the broader sustainable development framework, the plan positions Spain as a proactive actor in addressing the global climate crisis.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Alternative and Renewable Energy Policy 2019
DESCRIPTION: Pakistan's ARE 2019 sets several overall objectives and some specific targets for the energy sector in the country. The first objective of increasing the share of renewable energy is accompanied by a target of increasing renewable energy generation to 20% by 2025, and then 30% by 2030. Some other objectives of the policy include the indigenization of energy resources and enabling local manufacturing capacity and dispalcement of expensive energy with cheaper renewable sources. The scope of the policy covers almost all sources of renewable energy like biogas, biomass, energy from waste, geothermal, hydrogen, synthetic gas, solar, wind, ocean/tidal wave, storage technologies, and hybrids of any of these.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Malta’s Sustainable Development Vision for 2050
DESCRIPTION: The vision aims to ensure that social cohesion, the protection of the environment, and economic growth move forward in a coherent and mutually beneficial way. It focuses on identifying existing gaps and provides guidelines and targets to effectively address emerging challenges and threats.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Mauritania National Inventory Report (NIR). 2021
DESCRIPTION: Mauritania. National inventory report submitted in 2021

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Regulation No.79 on National Energy Policy 2014
DESCRIPTION: The regulation No.79 on National Energy Policy establishes the policy on Energy Management based on principles of fairness, sustainability and environmental sound aimed to create Energy Independance and national Energy Security. The regulation sets the following policy goals : 1) availability of Energy to meet the national demand; 2) priority of Energy development; 3) utilization of national Energy Resources; 4) national Energy Reserves. The regulation also establishes the following supporting policies : 1) Energy Conservation; 2) Environment and safety; 3) pricing, subsidy and energy incentives; 4) infrastructure and access of people to Energy and Energy Industry; 5) research and development.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Measures for the Management of GHG Voluntary Emissions Reduction Trading (Trial)
DESCRIPTION: These measures allow the Ministry of Ecology and Environment to build a national greenhouse gas voluntary emissions reduction trading market. It lays out rules for project audit and registration; verification and registration of emissions reductions; emissions reduction trading; verification and verification agency management; supervision and management; and penalties.

DESCRIPTION: Colombia. Biennial update report (BUR). BUR 2., Biennial Update Report from Colombia in 2018

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Common Action Framework for Deforestation-Free Cocoa Value Chain (Cocoa and Forests Initiative)
DESCRIPTION:
This Framework sets out the actions for building a deforestation-free cocoa value chain, underlining the crucial role of forests, biodiversity, and conservation in combating climate change, regulating local and regional climate, and providing other essential ecosystem services that support the resilience of the cocoa sector and local livelihoods.

It promotes community-based models for forest protection and restoration, including among other things, the engagement of local communities and producers in awareness campaigns on the status of National Parks and Reserves and Classified Forests and on the critical role played by forests in climate regulation, soil fertility and the water cycle.

The Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) is a joint partnership of the governments of Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, and 35 companies in the cocoa and chocolate sector representing 85% of the world's cocoa trade, aimed at eliminating deforestation from the cocoa supply chain. The ICF complies with the Preservation, Rehabilitation and Extension Strategy of the Government of Côte d'Ivoire. It is an essential component. The Ministry of Water and Forests (MINEF) coordinates the Initiative in Côte d'Ivoire.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Second national climate change adaptation measures (2016-2020)
DESCRIPTION:
The national climate change adaptation measures involve the co-ordination and co-operation of 13 government agencies to implement 87 major projects across 10 sectors: public health, disaster management and infrastructure, agriculture, forestry, marine and fisheries, water, eco-system, climate change monitoring and projection, adaptation business and industry, and publication, education and international cooperation.
Key actions for sectors include:

Public health: establish counter measures to protect the citizen’s lives and health environment from heat wave and air pollution
Disaster management and infrastructure: establish plans for disaster prevention and enforcement of stability of social infrastructure
Agriculture: adaptation of agricultural production system to climate change
Forestry: establish plans for forest health improvement and prevention of the forest disasters such as forest fires
Marine and fisheries: secure stable marine  food product resources and minimize damages from climate change
Water: establish water response system for the flood and drought
Ecosystem: secure biodiversity through the identification of climate change sensitive species.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Gear Change, A bold vision for cycling and walking (Cycling and walking plan for England)
DESCRIPTION:
This document aims fostering walking and cycling in England. Four themes are laid out in the document: 1) better streets for cycling and people, 2) cycling and walking at the heart of decision-making, 3) empowering and encouraging local authorities, 4) enabling people to cycle and protecting them when they do. Physical and mental health is explicitly mentioned as an argument for increasing walking and cycling rates.

Under this plan, the government will build more (protected) cycle lanes, provide cycle training for everyone and bikes available on prescription. It will also create a long term cycling programme, consult to strengthen the Highway Code for safety purposes, support local authorities to crack down on traffic offenses, create low traffic neighbourhoods to improve air quality, focus on areas with poor average health and increase access to e-bikes. 

A budget of two billion pounds has been allocated to this plan. Bike repair vouchers worth £50 will be released under a pilot plan. A scheme to support bike repairers is also considered.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Guiding Opinion on Promoting the Development of the Energy Electronics Industry
DESCRIPTION: This Opinion aims to prompt the development of energy equipment; to focus on core technology research; to train talent; to revolutionise the production and consumption of energy; to accelerate the construction of an "ecological civilisation"; and to achieve the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. To do so, advanced technologies such as 5G/6G, advanced computing, artificial intelligence and the Industrial Internet will be widely used in the energy field by 2030. This would enable the energy electronics industry to become a key force in promoting the realisation of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality. In addition, the Opinion also includes the actions relating to strengthening the overall coordination of supply and demand of energy; promoting coordinated development in the supply chain; and improving the technical innovation support system.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Climate Solutions Package
DESCRIPTION:
In 2019, the Australian government announced the Climate Solutions Package, an AUD 3.5 billion investment to deliver on Australia's 2030 Paris climate commitments.which consolidated a number of existing government programs and policies, and initiated a several new ones. New initiatives include, among others:
  • An AUD 2 billion Climate Solutions Fund, which continues and expands the focus of the government's existing Emissions Reductions Fund.
  • The 'Energy Efficient Communities' programme, aimed to improve energy efficiency standards and labeling, increasing energy efficiency of homes, businesses, and communities.
  • Emhanced investment in pumped storage solutions, e,g. Snowy 2.0 and Snowy 2.0 and 'Battery of the Nation'.
  • Mandating the creation of a National Strategy for Electric Vehicles
  • Support to local communities

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Energy Act (EZ-2)
DESCRIPTION: The Energy Act (EZ-2) establishes the overarching legal framework governing Slovenia’s energy sector, covering the organisation, regulation, and development of energy markets, infrastructure, and supply. It defines the roles and powers of key institutions (including the Energy Agency), regulates energy activities (electricity, gas, and heat), and sets rules for market functioning, consumer protection, and energy supply security, including measures for crisis situations and price interventions. The act also embeds climate and energy transition objectives by promoting renewable energy sources, energy efficiency, and investments in low-carbon technologies, while requiring local authorities to adopt energy planning documents with targets for energy savings and increased use of renewables. Overall, EZ-2 serves as the central instrument for implementing Slovenia’s energy policy and supporting the transition toward a secure, competitive, and decarbonised energy system.

PRINCIPAL_TITLE: Carbon Capture Technologies Program
DESCRIPTION: The Carbon Capture Technologies Program (AU$65 million) aims to accelerate the research, development and demonstration of novel and emerging carbon management technologies to address Australia’s hard-to-abate emissions and residual emissions. Grants will be offered to pilot and demonstration projects that capture, utilise and remove CO2 and have the potential to create new, low-emissions or net-zero industries.
